### On the Formal Cause of Meteors.

How one has fallen into deception in this matter was explained in the preceding sections. Therefore, if the principle of snow is unknown, it is extremely difficult—indeed, truly impossible—to judge it based on its effects alone. Let us see, then, what truth can be drawn from the Holy Scriptures regarding this matter, so that we may better and more correctly judge the aforementioned description given by the Peripatetics <note>The followers of Aristotle, known for walking while they taught</note>. We have it confirmed by the testimony of the Royal Prophet <note>King David, the traditional author of the Psalms</note> that when God sends his word to the earth, his command runs very swiftly:

> *He scatters snow like wool, and frost like ashes; he casts down his ice like morsels; who can stand before his cold?* Psalm 147:16. <note>original: "qui niues dispergit sicut lanam, & pruinam quasi cineres, deiicit gelu suum tanquam frusta, coram frigore eius quis consistat?"</note>

From these words we gather that snow and other frozen meteors <term>meteors: in the 17th-century sense, this refers to any atmospheric phenomenon, including rain and snow, not just falling stars</term> are created from cold by means of the Word of God, or His wisdom. Hence it is said elsewhere that cold comes from the Northern winds; and elsewhere, *By the breath of God ice is congealed*, and *that the mighty God produces ice by his breath*, Job 37:10 <note>The original text cites Job 27, but the verse is from Job 37</note>. This means that God, from the center or the interior, moves and directs his angelic ministers of the winds (or those presiding over the winds), who mix together according to His will to perform His work in the aerial sea, either by freezing or by dissolving. For everything that is done in this world ought to be rightly attributed to God as the First Mover—in the manner of the Sacred Page—and not to the creature (in the manner of the Pagan Philosophers), which is moved primarily by God. Thus it is said: *God breathing, God thundering, God striking, God being angry, God showing mercy, God leading, God inflicting a plague, God distilling the rains*, and so forth.

But truly, how God sends out his breaths, or by what method, or from what place the snow and other meteors constricted by cold come, is quite difficult—indeed, impossible—for human understanding to grasp, unless one is distinguished by the lessons of Divine Wisdom. Hence, it was said by Jehovah himself when questioning Job:

> *Have you entered the treasuries of the snow? Or have you seen the treasuries of the hail?* Job 38:22. <note>original: "Peruenistine in thesauros niuis? aut in thesauros grandinis inspectionem habes?"</note>

By this He seems to hint at how secret and hidden their mystery is. For it is not sufficient to assert with Aristotle that the cause of snow is cold condensing vapor. Rather, other things of greater importance must concur for the investigation of such a mystery: namely, where do such cold effects come from? And if they come from the winds, how are they regulated by God? What kind of vapor is this? Is it from the air thickened above the earth, or does it spring from the earth or not? Where is the seat of its generation?

In the preceding sections, therefore, it was said that snow is created by God’s breath and His swiftly running Word (Psalm 147:16). That the effect of that breath is cold is declared there, for it concludes: *who can stand before his cold?* From this it is clear that the strong northern breaths are stirred by the Word of God along with the gentler Southern ones. From which it follows: *He sends out his word and melts them; as soon as he blows with his wind, the waters flow*, that is, the snows are dissolved. That the substance of snow is drawn from the secret bosom of the air is noted in the question: *Have you entered the treasuries of the snow?* (Job 38:22). Here, by "treasuries," He understands the heavens, according to the passage: *Jehovah shall open his best treasury, the heavens, giving rain to your land in its time*, Deuteronomy 28:12. In this context, by "heavens" He understands the air, since it is the common treasury-chest of the meteors, as was said before.

Therefore, in the bosom of the air and from the consistency of congealed air—serving as the material cause—all such meteors are formed, with the Divine Will acting as the primary efficient cause. For this reason, we say that the breath of the gentle South wind applies the material by positioning the parts of the air for the snow (for it is the nature of this wind to thicken the air), while the coagulating disposition of the North wind, blowing more strongly and with greater dominance, freezes the air thus contracted in a moderate way. And so snow is made, the substance of which is partly frozen and partly ready for dissolution—and the more ready it is, the more force the Southern breath has. The internal act of these things comes from the Word, which fulfills the will of the Father. From this it is clear that Aristotle’s reasoning is most false when he asserts that the matter of snow is vapor exhaled from the earth and water, and likewise that the coldness of the middle region of the air is the cause of coagulation, and the heat of the stars the cause of its elevation. In truth, the matter is the air above the earth thickened by the breaths of the winds; the First Mover is the Word, present everywhere according to the Creator's will, who by his hidden power does these wonderful things, not by mere cold or heat (though these are external effects of His internal operation). Indeed, if this were not so, it would be impossible for snow and hail to remain in the same cloud with fire <note>referring to lightning</note> without the alteration or dissolution of either—for fire's nature is to dissolve frozen things and blunt cold effects. On this matter, it remains written:

> *Snow and hail endured the force of fire and did not melt, so that they might know that the fire burning in the snow and flashing in the rains destroyed the fruits of the enemies.* Wisdom 16:22. <note>original: "Nix & grando sustinebant vim ignis non tamen liquefiebant..." from the Book of Wisdom</note>

From this it is clear that Snow is of a far higher intention and more mystical to the intellect than to be produced in the way proposed and marked out for us by Aristotle. For against his assertion, which says the substance of snow is vapor rising from the elements of water and earth, massed into the likeness of carded wool by the cold of the place where it is generated, we are taught by the Holy Scriptures that the place from which its material is taken is "the treasuries," which He calls the heavens and the air, and not from water or earth. Furthermore, we say according to the testimony of the Sacred Page that the cause reducing the substance of the air into the form of wool is the breath of Jehovah, the effect of which is cold. It is as if one were to say that when God breathes from the northern region, the cloudy substance of the air (which the gentle and relaxed breath of the South wind had thus shaped) congeals into the form of carded wool.

However, how the Divine Will (which Jehovah placed in the elements of the world) acts upon the minds of the angels—who preside over both the constricting and relaxing winds and possess the four corners of the world to make them obedient to His command—acting in the blink of an eye, we shall explain clearly enough in our treatise on the supernatural efficient cause of meteors.

We hasten now to the description of snow according to the sense of the Holy Scriptures, which differs vastly and openly from the opinions of the Pagans.

### Section I. Portion IV. Part II. Book III. Member II.

Snow is a meteor <term>meteor: in this period, the term referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, such as rain, snow, or lightning, not just falling stars</term>, which God brings forth from his hidden treasuries, like wool, according to his will, sending it to the earth either as a blessing or to execute a scourge <note>scourge: a punishment or plague</note>.

->Or thus:<-

Snow is a creature produced from the air or heaven (which is God's treasury chest) by means of the divine breath and cold, like carded wool <note>carded wool: wool that has been combed and prepared for spinning</note>, to fulfill the divine will.

->Or thus:<-

Snow is an imperfectly mixed creature, which the mighty God brings forth from his heavenly treasuries and causes to congeal by his breath, so that whatever the Creator himself commands upon the surface of the earth—whether for a blessing or for punishment and a scourge—it immediately performs and executes.

In these descriptions, it is first noted that Snow is a creature, and consequently not eternal. Second, that the place from which it is drawn is the treasury of God, and that this treasury is heaven or the air, and consequently it is neither water nor earth. Third, that its material cause is the substance of the air or heaven from which it is originally drawn, just as the bones and flesh of a chick were potentially <gloss>potentially</gloss> in the yolk of the egg before they were brought into actuality. Fourth, the efficient cause is explained: namely, that it is the divine breath or spirit; for God acts centrally by ordering through his will, and his Word or Wisdom does his will, like the Son of the Father, and the Angels—as ministers of the Word (since it is their task to carry out the Divine word, as the royal Psalmist testifies)—immediately execute what has been ordered by God. Therefore, it is not correctly said that angels or cold, or any other created thing, perform this or that: but God himself, who is the primary author of action or motion. For that which belongs to God the Creator must not be attributed to the creature: for this is the error of the Heathens, the fountain and origin of Idolatry, who were accustomed to worship the creature instead of the creator in a false manner. Finally, in the last place, the final cause of this kind of meteor is explained: namely, that it is ordained to execute either the creator's blessing or his wrath upon the earth, just like the other meteors.

The Peripatetics <note>Peripatetics: followers of the Greek philosopher Aristotle, known for teaching while walking</note> also place no small difference between the generation of Snow and Hail, falling into this opinion: namely, that hail arises from a warm vapor, which the surrounding cold in the middle region of the air easily penetrates because of its thinness, and condenses it into a cloud. They claim that this cloud is afterwards dissolved and falls drop by drop, and is then compressed into ice by antiperistasis <term>antiperistasis: a philosophical concept where a quality is heightened by being surrounded by its opposite, such as cold intensifying the heat inside a chimney</term> from the penetrating cold as well as the heat of the lowest region of the air, which is why it falls in round and angular fragments of ice. This is their view, in which they state that hail is first procreated from a warm vapor rising from the earth and water; then that vapor is coagulated into a hail-cloud by the cold of the middle region of the air, and finally this cloud, resolved into drops, is at last reduced into innumerable fragments by the cold of that place during its fall.

But Aristotle himself confesses that hail is nothing other than the freezing of rain, caused by cold and wind in the air. And yet elsewhere he seems to assert that hail is generated in clouds very far distant from the earth, saying that the cause of the generation of hail is vapor received into the cavity of a cloud, which vapor he claims is thickened by the coldness of the air.

Bede <note>The Venerable Bede (c. 673–735), an influential English monk and scholar</note> maintains that, just as the North Wind is cold and dry, so by its breath it freezes and constricts the dewy drops descending from heaven, converting them into hail.

And so we see that the Peripatetics themselves, both the Heathens and their Christian followers, are entirely confused and uncertain in their opinions. The reason for this is that they seem to be ignorant of the true internal agent, the central act, and the primordial material cause of meteorological things, by attributing the praise and the name of creation to creatures or effects, and not to God the Creator. They are like fools who think in their hearts *there is no God*, since they perceive all things only as they appear in external vision. But let us now gird our loins for the examination of the above descriptions, which we shall first attempt to complete with the touchstone <note>original: "lapide Lydio" — a reference to the Lydian stone used in antiquity to test the purity of gold</note> of true Philosophy, and then afterwards with the most penetrating fire and light of the divine page.

In their first description, they establish the first matter of hail to be vapor, the second a cloud (which they therefore call "haily"), and the third the resolution of the cloud into raindrops. They posit a double efficient cause: the cold of the middle and also the lowest region of the air, which holds the power of constriction or freezing; and heat, to which they attribute the power of resolution and division.

For the refutation of that Peripatetic opinion, where they claim that vapors rising from the watery element are the origins of clouds, we would refer you to our preceding chapter where we treated the origin of mist and clouds in a more sincere manner. In that place, we left it proven by reasons established both by our own experience and the doctrine of the Holy Bible, that clouds were not composed at all from vapors ascending from the watery or earthy element, but were made by the condensation of air from winds blowing in opposition. And this same thing is undoubtedly the beginning of the substance and composition of the body of hail: namely, the hidden substance of the air or celestial matter, which at times becomes the manifest and visible matter of hail—as sometimes also of snow, rain, or frost—according to the appearance of the divine will.

<meta>This page continues the author’s critique of classical meteorology. ### On the Formal Cause of Meteors.

In the second part of their description, they seem to hesitate, inasmuch as they call a cloud "hail-bearing," even though it has not yet taken on the nature or appearance of hail any more than that cloud from which only rain is observed to gush and be sifted; for they recognize the appearance and form of hail in drops falling after being released from the cloud, and especially following within the cloud. Furthermore, if the matter were as they have dreamed, why by that same reasoning would the raindrops not also be frozen? These are quite often observed to fall along with hail, and they undoubtedly feel and suffer the freezing cold of the place just as much as that substance of hail does. But truly, if there is any difference between a hail-bearing cloud and a rain-bearing one, why is the entire substance of that cloud not converted into ice, since it is certain and approved by all philosophers that the middle region of the air abounds in and is stiff with cold? And consequently, from where did such great heat arise in the cloud that it melts and flows in the middle region of the air—where the effects of a whirlwind are cold—when, conversely, the drops falling from it are frozen again in the lowest region of the air (in which heat predominates due to the various reflections of the celestial rays)?

And again, we see that hail tends to be more frequent in the month of April, and indeed in the summer, than in winter; at which times the temperature of the air overflows with heat, and consequently, 그 region is less suited to freeze liquid drops falling from the clouds. How did it happen (*my Peripatetics* <note>Peripatetics: followers of Aristotle's philosophy</note>) that a very great error lies hidden in this description of yours? This is undoubtedly not the chest or dwelling place of truth. But if you reply with your Master *Aristotle*, that the hail-bearing cloud is at a very great distance from the earth, and that the drops, while passing from the cloud through the space of the middle region, are frozen by the force of the cold of that place—which is increased more through *antiperistasis* <term>antiperistasis: a philosophical concept where a quality, such as cold, is intensified when it is surrounded by its opposite, such as heat</term> in the times of summer and spring—*I answer*: that by this same reasoning the substance of the cloud, floating in the very heart of such a region, ought to be constricted and bound together into a glacial substance by such vigor of cold, so that it could not be reduced into the presupposed liquid droplets easily for lack of dissolving heat.

As for that second description brought forward by *Aristotle*, truth itself forbids us to admit or defend its integrity. For if hail (according to his opinion) were nothing other than the freezing of raindrops produced in the air by cold and wind, we can see no reason why the raindrops descending together with the hail are not, by the same reasoning, converted into hail, since the temperature of the air is equal in coldness. For undoubtedly he himself understands this to be about the lowest region of the air, since he seems to recognize cold winds as the causes acting in the freezing of the drops. But truly (as was demonstrated above), he seems to deny the entrance of winds into the middle region of the air, inasmuch as windy exhalations (as he himself thinks) are not permitted to penetrate there. Is he not also observed to contradict himself in this: that he makes the cause of the generation of hail to be vapor received into the cavity of a cloud, in whose belly he does not blush to assert that it is thickened and frozen because of the coldness of the place and the air?

But what else, I ask, is a cloud than thickened vapor? And if vapor is added to vapor, it must necessarily pass into the same nature of vapor, no differently than water added to water is accustomed to constitute a single and non-diverse form of water. Therefore, if the enclosed vapor is of the same nature as that which encloses it, there will be no reason why, upon the freezing of a part, the whole should not also gradually be frozen. But we have the argument of his own contradiction in this: that in his prior assertion he calls hail nothing other than the condensation of raindrops.

But truly, rain exists after the resolution of a cloud; in the latter assertion, he relates that hail is made not from raindrops, but from the freezing of vapor received into the cavity of the cloud. I commend to your judgments (readers, guardians of the scales of justice) how contrary these two things are.

But we now come to that opinion of *Bede* <note>Bede: an 8th-century English monk and scholar</note>, which we shall pass over lightly since it does not withdraw much from the truth. He makes the *North Wind* <note>original: "Borealem"</note> the efficient cause of hail, and that not unwisely, since cold is derived from it; yet (with his pace) he speaks more of the effect and from the effect than of the internal acting cause. This cause we make triple, differing in dignity and rank: namely, the Creator breathing centrally according to his hidden will; his Word, which does his will; and the angels whose task it is to execute those things which are presented by the Word of **GOD**. Thus **GOD** ordains according to the property of his name, the Word of **GOD** disposes the ordained things in the manner of a royal prince, and the windy angels execute what was ordained by the Word or divine will. The effects of the execution, however, are cold, heat, moisture, and dryness, and those things which follow from them secondarily, such as thickness, ice, snow, and thinness—from which rain, hail, comets, the flying dragon <note>flying dragon: a historical term for a meteor or fireball</note>, the foolish fire <note>original: "ignis fatuus"; a will-o'-the-wisp or phosphorescent light seen over marshland</note>, and other such things arise by various and hidden operations.

But let us bring forward the aforementioned opinions and descriptions of the *Peripatetics*—whether *Pagans* or *Christians*—to the testimony of the divine scriptures, or to the touchstone <note>original: "lapidem lydium"; literally 'Lydian stone', used to test the purity of gold</note>, or the examination of the most penetrating fire, so that we may better see whether there is truth in them or not.

Aristotle, with his sect, makes the vapor attracted upward from the elements of water and earth the mat—

Section I. Portion IV. Part II. Book III. Member II.

The nature of hail. But the mighty God <note>original: "DEVS fortis Iehoua"</note> makes this matter not so easy to discover—specifically, the knowledge of the substance of hail as well as its primordial womb—wherefore He said to Job: *Gird up thy loins, and answer me now: Hast thou entered into the treasures of the snow, or hast thou beheld the treasures of the hail? Job 38:22.* By this speech, God Himself denotes that it is not easy for man to know such mysteries, and that the substance of hail, as well as that of the clouds, snow, rain, lightning, and other such **meteors** <term>In this context, "meteors" refers to any atmospheric phenomenon (rain, wind, snow), not just falling space rocks.</term> is not extracted from the elements of water and earth, but from His own hidden treasures, which we explained in the preceding pages to be the heavens and the air. Therefore, without controversy, Aristotle is mistaken, and the **Peripatetics** <note>The Peripatetics were followers of Aristotle's philosophy.</note> are mistaken, both regarding the source of the hail-meteor and the consistency of its substance.

Furthermore, they ascribe the reason for the shaping and formation of these hail-stones to the cold of the air itself, while the scriptures of truth ascribe all these things to God and His Word, which angels are said to carry out; hence we have it written: *He sendeth forth his commandment upon earth: his word runneth very swiftly. He giveth snow like wool: he scattereth the hoarfrost like ashes. He casteth forth his ice like morsels: who can stand before his cold? Psalm 147:15-17.* From this it is clear that the agent for the procreation of such meteors is God Himself, by means of the Word, from whose cold breaths or **Boreal angels** <note>The North Wind (Boreas) was often associated with cold and divine judgment.</note>, cold is produced as a direct effect; wherefore it is said: *Who can stand before his cold?* He does not say "before the cold," but "before **His** cold," that is, that which arises from His breath. Wherefore it is also said elsewhere: *The mighty God bringeth forth ice by his breath; by the breath of God the frost is congealed. Job 37:9-10.* He does not say that the North wind or the cold brings forth ice or hail, but God by His breath; for when God breathes, the frost congeals. From this it is clear that wind and cold are effects proceeding from God, to whom alone all things produced in the world are to be ascribed. Is it not also found written that Jehovah sent forth hail and sounds <note>thunder</note>, and fire ran along the ground, and that Jehovah God thus sent rain with hail upon the land of the Egyptians? *And there was hail, and fire mingled with the hail, very grievous; and the hail smote all the land of Egypt, all that was in the field, both man and beast; and the hail smote every herb of the field, and brake every tree of the field. Exodus 9:23-25.* In these words we have it denoted that the provider and creator of hail is the mighty God Jehovah, who extracted the material for making them from the "treasures of the hail," which we indicated above to be the heavens and the air. Furthermore, they are arranged in the place of clouds and thunders, and consequently, in their descent they are by no means reduced to such a form by the cold of the place, since in the midst of them fire was kindled, whose nature is to be opposed to cold; moreover, they are surrounded and sent forth with lightning on every side, for Jehovah sent forth sounds, and fire went through the land. Furthermore, they were accompanied by an infinity of rain droplets, whence it is probable that if hail were (according to their opinion) nothing other than drops of rain frozen by the cold on the way down, then no rain would appear, but only hail. Nor is it enough to reply that a stormy tempest of this kind was miraculous and supernatural; for we observe by common experience that rain frequently occurs with hail and lightning. Finally, the "final cause" <note>The ultimate purpose or reason for something.</note> of this meteor is declared by its effect: for it was a scourge and punishment for the Egyptians. Whence it is said elsewhere: *Jehovah cast down great stones of hail from heaven upon them, by which he slew the enemies of the Israelites. Joshua 10:11.* Furthermore, the Royal Prophet teaches us that hail kills the vines in *Psalm 78:47*. And elsewhere: *He smote their vines and fig trees with hail and flaming fire, and brake the trees. Psalm 105:32-33.*

By these things it seems clearly enough explained that God is the prince and author of the manufacture of hail-weapons, and that He Himself does not need the help of vapors from the visible earth or water in this His open work or craftsmanship; for He always has a ready supply of matter for constructing meteors of every kind in His treasury-chest, the Air, which matter He is then accustomed to shape into this or that nature and form according to His inscrutable will. Therefore, in the composition of meteors, the "patient" <note>The passive substance that is acted upon.</note> is the air, while the "agent" is the constricting and freezing disposition and property of the divine name, which is found and marked in that great angel who presides over the sphere of **Saturn** <note>In traditional astrology and cosmology, Saturn was associated with cold and contraction.</note>, to whom Gabriel, the ruler and prince of the Moon, offers moist matter, for dominion over the Boreal region is also ascribed to him. We say, therefore, that two opposite winds—one of which is weaker and provides moisture (that is, damp air), and the other stronger, having a Boreal and constricting power—by their various struggling, dissipate that air gathered and coagulated into a cloudy mass into small fragments. These are whirled around in the violent motion of the opposing blasts by a spiral revolution of the windy air, just as is observed at the meeting of two opposing rivers, where we notice foamy waters rotating and being driven in a circle. This is why, before or during the fall of hail, terrible sounds are often heard in the air—indeed, sometimes a murmur and a crash, and sometimes a noise like that of armed men is perceived from above. And although the Peripatetics think the reason for this arises from the struggle and fight of hot and dry exhalations, or the collision and concussion of contrary vapors in the clouds (since some are hot and dry, while others are moist), it is nevertheless known and apparent to those more skilled in the hidden mystery of Philosophy that all this happens from windy spirits blowing from various regions or corners of the world, by the power of the angels who are the immediate ministers of God presiding over those winds, just as...

### On the Formal Cause of Meteors.

...will be explained more copiously in the treatise on the supernatural efficient cause of meteors. We conclude, therefore, from what we gather from the doctrine and testimony of the sacred pages, that hail is to be described in this manner:

> Hail is a certain hard and icy impression, the matter of which the mighty God Jehovah <note>original: "DEVS fortis Iehoua"</note> extracts from his treasures or his treasury chest—namely, the hidden bosom of the air—and by His cold spirit or breath <note>original: "spiritu seu flatu suo frigido"</note>, separately freezing and compressing it, He forms and conglomerates it into infinite little stones of water in the heavens, which at last, to fulfill His will, He rains down and casts upon the earth, either by itself or accompanied by lightning and rain.

In this definition, the source of its material substance presents itself first: according to the testimony of Holy Scripture, it is extracted from His "treasures," which we explained above to be the heavens or the air. From this, it is clear that the substance of the air is the matter not only of hail, but of all other **meteors** <term>In the early modern period, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomena, including rain, snow, and wind.</term>. Next, it is explained that its **form** <term>The "formal cause" refers to the specific shape or essence that makes a thing what it is.</term> is received from the divine breath or inspiration as the **efficient cause** <term>The "efficient cause" is the primary agent that brings a thing into being.</term>; for it is said that the mighty God produces ice by His breath: *By the breath of God frost is given,* Job 37:10. And elsewhere: *He casteth forth his ice like morsels: who can stand before his cold?* Psalm 147:16. Where by "morsels of ice," hailstones can be understood, and consequently, such hailstones are confirmed to be formed into the shape of watery pebbles by the cold of Jehovah's breath. This extraction of the matter of hail and ice from the dewy bosom of the air is verified elsewhere: *Ice has come forth from the womb of the dew, and the waters are hidden like a stone, and the surface of the deep is frozen.* This can be understood as much regarding the ice in the clouds of the middle region of the air as regarding the surface of terrestrial waters, since clouds are called "the deep" <note>original: "abyssi"</note> elsewhere in the Bible, Job 38:28. Finally, the **final cause** <term>The "final cause" is the purpose or end for which a thing exists.</term> is explained there: namely, to fulfill the divine will. Hence it is said elsewhere: *Cold, ice, hoarfrost, clouds, lightning—whatever God has commanded them to do upon the face of the world, whether for a scourge or for mercy, they perform it immediately.* Job 37. Furthermore, God sent or produced hail from heaven to harm and destroy the men, cattle, herbs, and trees of the Egyptians, Exodus 9. Likewise, Jehovah sent great stones of hail from heaven, with which He slew the enemies of the Israelites, Joshua 10:11. Therefore, we gather from our description that the **material cause** <term>The "material cause" is the physical substance from which a thing is made.</term> of hail is extracted from the air; for in its substance, it is nothing other than air, thickened into a cloudy consistency by contrary winds. Next, we have the formal cause in that it is reduced into the form of watery pebbles, either of a round or angular shape; hence Joshua says, *Jehovah sends great stones of hail from the heavens.* From this, it is also clear that the place where the dense air is reduced into such an image by means of the divine breath is the heaven or the air. Furthermore, the efficient cause is the cold, freezing, and hardening breath of God. Finally, the final cause is, for the most part, punishment and a scourge or penalty: for the earth is rendered far more fertile by rain than by hail, whose nature is rather to harm the fruit of the tree and the crops than to bring them any advantage or profit.

But now we touch upon the third species of such solid meteors: namely, **Hoarfrost** <note>original: "Pruinam"</note>, which does not seem to differ much from the others in respect to its efficient cause, as it is the cold breath or inspiration of Jehovah.

Aristotle, along with the Christians of his sect, defines this as a certain impression from a moist and cold vapor arising from the element of water, not gathered into the thickness of a cloud, which impression is frozen in the middle region of the air by the coldness of the place (in which no heat is present) and the time, and is reduced into the form of hoarfrost.

Others (among whom I name **Bede** <note>The Venerable Bede (c. 673–735), an English monk and scholar.</note>) will have it that this kind of impression is nothing other than frozen dew, which in its descent toward the earth drinks in and receives into itself the nocturnal coldness, by means of which it puts on such a white, hard, and cold appearance as is hoarfrost.

We turn then to that Aristotelian description, and we say that if its first part were true—namely, that the matter of hoarfrost was such a cold and moist vapor springing and exhaling from the nourishments of water and earth—it would follow that the frost would diminish and decrease more and more every day. This is because, in the weather of hoarfrost, the pores of the earth are closed by the freezing cold, so that neither plowshares nor other iron instruments can penetrate it; then, for the most part, the waters are shut up by such tight ice that we see the fish themselves die in great quantities for want of penetrating air. Yet everyone will admit that air is thinner than vapor. Since this is proven false by the effect, we say that Aristotle's opinion regarding the substance or matter of hoarfrost is erroneous, as we do not see the hoarfrost decrease daily from its state, but rather we observe it for the most part growing stronger from day to day, and the earth and trees being more and more clothed in a **swan's beard** <note>original: "barba cygnea"; a poetic description of thick, white frost.</note>.

The same must also be said regarding the material cause of hoarfrost explained in the second description: namely, that it is not of the substance of dew, if we conclude that dew arises and is procreated in the Aristotelian way—that is, from vapor exhaled from the waters and the earth. But that opinion of Bede will be probable if he agrees with us that the entire matter of meteors consists in the power of the air.

But we proceed to the efficient cause of both, which Aristotle believes to be the cold of the middle air, in which he recognizes no heat; Bede, however, says that the coldness of the night is the cause, both of the freezing and of its white form.

### Section I. Part IV. Part II. Book III. Member II.

We, however, in our inquiry into this matter, shall speak with somewhat more specificity. First, we note that Aristotle denied that the substance of the winds could penetrate into the middle region of the air; for this reason, he cannot recognize that hoarfrost is produced by the winds, since he claims it is generated in the middle region of the air due to the coldness of that place. Bede seems to infer that the creation of this "impression" <term>In this context, an "impression" is a physical phenomenon produced by the action of higher forces upon the elements.</term> arises from the cold and the state of the season. We, however, say that the primary, most principal, and internal cause is God alone, who through His Word incites His angelic winds to fulfill His will, both in the heavens and on the earth. Their actions are assigned to God as the central and primary operator, inasmuch as they are the ministers of God, ready to execute those things ordained by God as the First Mover.

Hence it is said that God, sending forth His word, "scatters the hoarfrost like ashes; who can stand before His cold?" <note>original: "DEVS emittens sermonem suum pruinam quasi cineres dispergat, coram frigore eius quis consistat?" cf. Psalm 147:16-17</note> He does not say, with Aristotle, that it is the cold of the middle region of the air, or with Bede, that it is the cold of the night, or with the common folk, that the North winds do this; but rather that God—by means of His Word, from whose breath cold or heat exit as effects according to His pleasure—is not only the efficient cause of hoarfrost, but of all other meteors, and He is the sole and unique cause.

For just as in the world there is but a single **material cause**, which is the universal created spirit of the world, so too is there but one single **efficient and acting cause** upon that matter, which is the uncreated form or light. And although God the Father may be called one agent, and the Son or the Word another, and the Holy Spirit yet another—and consequently infinite creatures which have their powers of acting immediately from them—nevertheless, in the Divinity there is but one Godhead and one Spirit. From this Spirit all spirits are created and acquire their life and actions, not otherwise than how all other parts of the world are filled by the rays of a single sun; yet none of the said rays can be distinguished or separated from the unity of that one sun, as Hermes Trismegistus <note>A legendary Hellenistic figure associated with the "Hermetica," texts combining philosophy, alchemy, and magic.</note> testifies. 

Therefore, whatever is accomplished in growth or in the giving of life by the bright fountain of the sun, we attribute it all to the one sun, and not to any individual ray of it. Thus Orpheus and the other Platonists assigned a particular "god" to every creature in the world, and yet they referred all these particular gods back to the one Jupiter, just as one refers all the rays of the sun expanded everywhere through the world back to the one sun. Hence the Evangelist says, *“All things were created by Him, and without Him was nothing created... in Him was life,”* etc. (John 1). And Saint Paul says, *“From Him, in Him, and through Him, are all things.”* And elsewhere we find that *“the incorruptible spirit of God is in all things”* (Wisdom 12).

Wherefore, the creation of any creature—whether perfectly or imperfectly composed—has been quite deliberately attributed to the primary and unique cause, and not to the effects themselves, thereby excluding creatures from the honor due to the Creator, so that no species of idolatry might follow. Hence Job said: *“By His breath, the mighty God produces ice, frost, snow, and hoarfrost; by the breath of God, the frost is frozen”* (Job 37:9-10). And elsewhere, Jehovah Himself, the creator of all, mocking the ingratitude and folly of man (who is accustomed to attribute the praises of the Creator to created things), addresses Job thus: *“Who has fathered the hoarfrost of heaven?”* (Job 38:29). 

It is as if He were noting the presumption of the Heathens in this question, who shamelessly assert that cold is the progenitor of hoarfrost, rather than the Father of cold and heat; for the Holy Scriptures themselves confess that hoarfrost, snow, hail, and ice are procreated by the breath of the Almighty, and in other places it is stated more expressly that they are produced by God Himself and sent forth from the heavens.

We conclude, therefore, that snow and hail are "impressions" from the air, formed when opposing or transverse winds compress and condense it into the shape of a cloud. These are reduced into this or that form by the divine breath (which produces cold) according to the stronger or weaker predominance of the blowing winds. For example:
*   When the South Wind <note>original: "Austro"</note> blows weakly while the North Wind <note>original: "Borea"</note> is still stronger, soft snows and such clouds are generated.
*   But when the South Wind blows more strongly along with a stronger North Wind, hail-bearing clouds mostly arise.

Furthermore, a strong Northern wind—where the opposing wind either does not blow at all or blows only lightly so that the air is condensed into a cloud—tends to bring forth hoarfrost and ice. I say "hoarfrost" because the North wind, blowing according to the divine will, constricts the moist and moderately dense nature of the air with its breath springing from the **first act** <term>In Aristotelian philosophy, "first act" refers to the initial realization or existence of a power.</term>. From this, the denser part of the air, thus constricted, falls onto trees and herbs. Indeed, when falling upon water, and with that breath assisting and persevering, it immediately results in ice and unites itself with the surface of the water. By this means, the hard form of ice is established and shaped upon the waters. 

This happens because the warm vapors exhaling from the waters and the bowels of the earth cause that frost or ice to appear upon the surface of the waters, and not within the sphere of the water itself. And this glacial crust is strengthened day by day by the addition of new air congealed by cold blasts on the upper part. That crust is hardened through **antiperistasis** <term>A philosophical concept where a quality (like cold) is intensified by being surrounded by its opposite (like heat).</term>, since the cold acts on its exterior surface by constricting and hardening it, while the action of warm vapors exhaling from the earth and water resists it from below; by resisting, it confirms the ice through the long-lasting addition of congealed air gradually falling from the heavens. This is the reason why hot water exposed to the open air in a time of extreme cold is observed to freeze faster than cold water. We have therefore explained here the formula for the procreation of both hoarfrost and ice according to our opinion.

We now proceed to the description of these things according to the intention of the Divine Page.

**Hoarfrost** is a certain meteoric impression, the matter of which is extracted from the air or heaven (the treasury chest of God); its form, however, is such as it possesses in respect to the thinness of the air, mostly [driven] by the breath of God...

# On the Formal Cause of Meteors.

...the northern [wind], as the efficient cause, is produced (for it is said: *who can stand before his cold?*) <note>original: "coram frigore eius quis consistat" — cf. Psalm 147:17. The author attributes the power of the cold wind directly to God's command.</note> which finally, according to the pleasure or will of its creator, to be enacted upon both lands and waters, is poured out from the heavens or His storehouses, either as a scourge or as a blessing.

In this description, we have its **matter**, taken from the lap of the air, which is the treasury of all meteorological bodies; we have its **form**, designated into such a shape as it is by the cold breath of the mighty God Jehovah, mostly from the north; and consequently we have the hidden **breath of Jehovah** as the **efficient cause**; finally, its **final cause** is to fulfill and perfect the command of its creator, whether for benevolence or for punishment. All these parts of our description we have confirmed and established by testimonies derived from Holy Scripture and cited in the preceding sections.

Finally, according to the authority of the sacred writings, it is permitted to define ice in this manner:

->**Ice** is a certain cold **impression** <term>In early science, an "impression" was a phenomenon produced when a celestial or divine force acted upon the lower elements (air, water, etc.).</term>, which, emerging from the womb of dew like a watery stone by divine will, is produced by the cold and mostly northern divine breath, and is coagulated in the open field of the air, and finally, to execute the divine will, by falling downward, is frozen and hardened upon the surfaces of the waters or the deep.<-

The place of birth of this meteorological body, as well as the condition of its substance or matter, are explained by these types of testimonies brought forth by Job: *Ice has come forth from the womb of the dew, like a stone the waters are hidden, and the surface of the deep is frozen, Job 38:28.* <note>The author is quoting a version of Job 38:28-30.</note> Where it denotes that the air, reduced into a moist and dewy substance by the light blowing of the winds, is the **matrix** <term>A "matrix" here refers to a womb or a formative environment where a substance takes shape.</term> from which the substance of ice proceeds and emerges, according to what we have previously reported. Next, its form or figure is explained by the fact that it is reduced into the appearance of a watery or crystalline stone. Then, afterward, the agent or **efficient cause** is explained in another place, where it is found that the mighty God produces ice *by His breath; when God blows, the frost is congealed, Job 37:9.* <note>Original: "flatu suo flante DEO concrescat gelu." This likely refers to Job 37:10 in modern bibles.</note> Therefore, it is clear that the breath of the mighty God Jehovah is the most ancient and primary cause of this birth; for the mighty God produces ice, and the instrument by which He produces it is explained by the fact that He produces it by His breath, and also forms it and reduces it into its icy substance; for by God’s blowing, the frost congeals. Furthermore, that such a breath is mostly from the north we gather from the same chapter 37, verse 9, where it is made manifest that cold comes from the northern winds. Finally, the **final cause** is for the will of the creator, whether to execute punishment or benevolence. Moreover, that it is accustomed to freeze on the surface of the waters is explained both by the place previously cited and by common experience.

### *Correlation to the Microcosm: Wherein we treat those dark, thick meteors, steeped in actual moisture, which are observed to gush from the "heaven" or the corruption of the human air.*

Sect. I. Port. IV. Part. II. Lib. III. Membr. II.

### Relating to the Microcosm, in which we treat very liquid human meteors.

We call these "gross" meteors in comparison to the "superior" ones, which take the form of vapors—specifically those listed in the preceding section. Similarly, these meteors, which are still steeped in sensible moisture or humor, appear to differ in their liquidity and thinness as much as in their thickness, condensation, viscosity, and freezing. Since some are formed from the more liquid part of the watery substance, they are like the "celestial wheels" <note>original: "instar rotis cælestis" — Likely a reference to the circular motion of the heavens or the cyclical nature of fluid transformation.</note>; these are the fluids that arise immediately, and according to the intention of nature, from vapor into drops: of chyle <term>Chyle: a milky fluid of droplets of fat and lymph formed in the small intestine during digestion.</term> in the stomach, of blood in the liver and heart, and of clear, limpid fluid in the ventricles of the brain. By an equal reasoning, we see that vapor in a distillation vessel <term>Alembic: an early chemical apparatus used for distillation, consisting of two retorts connected by a tube.</term>, though barely perceptible—looking like the thinnest smoke—rises into the cap or "head" of the vessel and is converted into dewy drops. In the same way, the vapor arising from food and drink by the power of digestion is turned into dewy drops of chyle that temper the mass of nourishment. This same vapor, through a second extraction in the hollow of the liver, is transformed into reddish drops, much like the smoke of organic wheat which we described in our *Anatomy of Bread and Wheat*. <note>The author likely refers to his own earlier work on the mystical or chemical properties of nutrition.</note> But while nature’s chemistry spends its labor on the juice of nutrients, the power that works in the brain and heart takes and chooses its subject from the clearly invisible air. For that external air, which is drawn into the brain through the mammillary processes <term>Mammillary processes: structures in the brain then believed to be involved in drawing in air or odors.</term>, claims for itself the celestial "marrow" of the air—the quintessence <term>Quintessence: the purest, most concentrated essence of a substance; the "fifth element."</term> suitable for the faculties of the senses and reason—and emits what is superfluous through a certain contraction and expansion <note>original: "systolen & diastolē"</note>. Then, having retained that useful air, it changes it into vapor by the constant addition of its own kind, and from vapor into healthful dews—provided that nature or the attracted air is familiar, benevolent, and healthy to the one breathing it. But if its nature is excessively damp and filled with the worst "seeds" <term>Seminariis: "seeds" or "germs" of disease, a common early modern concept of contagion.</term>, it induces diseases in the brain, vexes that entire region preternaturally, and burdens it with catarrhal clouds. Similarly, benevolent air drawn to the heart passes into benevolent vapors necessary for life; but if it is filled with ill-omened seeds, it usually brings evil and discomfort to the heart and consequently to every member of the body. This happens to people more or less according to their birth, their temperament, and the disposition of the place where the breather lives, and not to everyone equally.

Furthermore, these dewy drops will be converted into rain—that is, catarrhal phlegm in the brain—if the introduced air is affected by excessive moisture. We have this confirmed by Galen <note>Galen: an 2nd-century Greek physician whose theories dominated Western medicine for 1,500 years.</note> in <gloss>Aphorisms 3. 12.</gloss>: *Phlegm flowing from the head to the belly causes a flux,* and elsewhere he says that *phlegm flows down from the head, and in those fluxes the excrements are foamy,* <gloss>Aphorisms 7. 30.</gloss> Furthermore, he admits that phlegm is primarily procreated in the brain, <gloss>Aphorisms 3. 12.</gloss> From this it is evident that it is the state of the air, whether tempered or intemperate, that generates a greater or lesser abundance of phlegm in the brain. Hence it is declared elsewhere *that phlegm is generated especially in the winter time,* <gloss>Aphorisms 3. 20.</gloss> *(when the rains of heaven are also produced),* but in the summer time it is weakened and diminished, *Commentary on the Nature of Man 1. 33 & 35.* It is as if he had said: in the time of phlegmatic air—that is, moist and cold—watery or rainy humor is procreated both in the Macrocosm and in the "heaven" of the Microcosm. This is because, in the air, spirits steeped in southern moisture are breathed everywhere through the atmosphere; these spirits convert the air, or the World’s Mercury <term>World's Mercury: a term from alchemy referring to the volatile, fluid principle of the universe.</term>, into their own moist nature. Consequently, this air (which they must necessarily penetrate) converts and changes both animals and plants into its own nature, by altering their spirits, which are of the same kind as its own, like a son from the same father. This is why fruits and animals nourished by air infected with long-lasting southern moisture are observed to lead more toward phlegm and the nature of rain than those refreshed by Northern or Eastern winds and the like. Consequently, in bodies fit to receive such effects, they usually produce these results in the stomach; as Galen says: *Cold phlegm causes lightness of the intestines,* <gloss>Aphorisms 3. 12.</gloss> *And elsewhere, phlegm in the stomach or intestines causes lightness of the intestines,* <gloss>Aphorisms 6. 1.</gloss> *that is, it induces a lienteric flux <term>Lienteria: a form of diarrhea where food is discharged only partially digested.</term>.* It is as if he said: Phlegmatic air, swelling in food and the surrounding air in the stomach, falls like rain from the stomach into the intestines, and creates a flux like rain from the stomach (as if from the middle region of the air), more or less according to the greater or lesser malignancy of the universal air in that year. From this arise fluid diseases spreading among the people, and various kinds of belly-fluxes. But if this disease is more specific to an individual, it can happen either by reason of food inclining toward the moist and fluid nature of the air, or by reason of a particular body whose imperfection makes it ready and fit to generate such phlegm and to convert the air drawn inside into such a poisonous disposition.

Of the congealed <note>original: "congelatorum" — meaning frozen or solidified.</note> meteors in the Microcosm, some are in its thinner air, others in its thicker air—namely in its "water," which was also once air. The freezing of air in a human being usually produces many "congealed" diseases, appearing both visibly in the flesh and hiding occultly in the body, known only by their effects. Galen himself testifies *that air is as ready to freeze and receive impressions of cold as it is of heat.* *On the Power of Simple Medicines, Book 1, Chapter 18.* And in the book *On the Differences of Diseases*, he acknowledges that all those ailments caused by cold causes are called "congealings."

# On the Formal Cause of Meteors.

...and they take their origin from more violent forces. If we consider frost and hoarfrost in the Macrocosmic <note>Macrocosm: The "great world" or the universe as a whole, which early modern thinkers believed was mirrored by the human "Microcosm."</note> earth, we will perceive that they are nothing other than the freezing of air penetrating everywhere through the pores of the earth, and a formula for constricting and coagulating it into the thinnest ice. By this means, both the air in its own nature and the visible water which the air brought forth are gathered and huddled together into a single earthy mass, both the heterogeneous and the homogeneous.

So also in the Microcosm, or man, the entire fleshy "earth" is affected by stupor and the loss of sensation and motion, as well as by cooling. This is seen in Apoplexy <term>Apoplexy: Historically, a sudden loss of consciousness or paralysis, often what we now call a stroke.</term> (which Galen <note>Galen of Pergamon (129–c. 216 AD): An influential Greek physician whose theories dominated Western medicine for over 1,000 years.</note> defines in *On Affected Places*, Book 3, Chapter 10, and *Aphorisms* 2, 42, by its effect as the loss of sensation and motion in the whole body of the animal), in Carus <term>Carus: A state of profound stupor or deep coma, more severe than lethargy.</term>, Paraplegia, and stupor (which is described in *On Affected Places* Book 2, Chapter 2, as a significant cooling in the human spirit, inducing difficulty of sensation and motion), just as complete cooling entirely removes both sense and motion.

Furthermore, stupor also occurs due to freezing and cooling of the body existing within the porous body of a nerve. Whence it happens that such a nerve (as Galen witnesses in his book *On the Diagnosis of Kidney Affections*, Chapter 3) becomes so obstructed and constricted that the animal spirits <term>Animal spirits: In Galenic medicine, these were refined substances that traveled through hollow nerves to facilitate movement and sensation.</term> cannot be transmitted to the limb which that nerve ought to serve and administer. But regarding these types of diseases arising from the freezing of "human air," I have spoken more abundantly elsewhere. Such types of disease carry with them the evidence of the effect of freezing.

Those conditions which appear visibly as snowy whiteness, due to the internal freezing of "air" or "fumes" (by which both the fleshy earth itself and the parts growing out of it are altered), are graying hair <note>original: "canities"</note> and leprosy. Concerning this, we find it said in Holy Scripture: *Her hand (namely Miriam's) was white as snow*, Leviticus 13:9 <note>The author cites Leviticus 13:9, though the story of Miriam's hand turning white is found in Numbers 12:10; the Leviticus passage describes the diagnostic signs of leprosy.</note>. And elsewhere: *there is a white swelling in the skin and it has turned the hair white.*

But truly, where freezing has occurred in a humor—whether phlegmatic or bloody—diseases are produced there no less dangerous than the others we have related. Something of this kind is accustomed to happen in mortification <term>Mortification: The death of tissue, now known as gangrene.</term>, where the blood is wont to freeze from extreme cold, just as is commonly found in those who live in regions stiff with frost.

Furthermore, in the "falling sickness" <term>Morbus comitialis: Epilepsy. It was called the "assembly disease" because an assembly (comitia) would be canceled if someone had a seizure.</term>, cachexia <term>Cachexia: A "wasting away" of the body, often involving severe weight loss and muscle atrophy.</term>, and similar conditions, we see "glassy" and viscous phlegm (having the form of egg whites) predominate. This is clearly shown in those to whom emetic medicines <note>Emetics: Medicines used to induce vomiting to clear the body of "excess humors."</note> are given. We also frequently observe that in obstructions of the brain caused by cold, a glassy and viscous matter is produced. Moreover, a slimy, sluggish, and melancholic humor is seen to abound in those who suffer from "natural and terrestrial melancholy." It is very easy to judge that this entire process of freezing proceeds from the northern or splenic cold <note>The spleen was linked to the humor of "black bile," which was considered cold and dry, sharing the qualities of the North Wind.</note>, because in that region of the human body resides the terrestrial melancholy, which corresponds in its actions to the quality of the North: consequently, it is freezing and constricting, being cold and dry in its "breath."

Sect. I. Port. IV. Part. II. Lib. III. Membr. II.

## The first small part concerning the origin of springs.

Here, in passing, let me implore the reader's pardon: both in the description of the following and the preceding matters, our muse <note>The "muse" refers to the author's own creative and intellectual inspiration.</note> seems to wander and diverge entirely from that path laid down by us in Book 7 of the *History of the Macrocosm* <note>original: "lib. 7. Physices Macrocosmi historia." This refers to Fludd’s own massive encyclopedia of the universe, published earlier.</note>. I wish for the reader to understand, having been rectified by better judgment, that in that place we spoke in the manner of the **Pagan Philosophers**, and did not pull our description of meteors far from the sentiment of the **Peripatetics** <term>Peripatetics: Followers of Aristotle’s philosophy, known for walking about while teaching.</term>. In this place, however, proceeding with a more sincere style, we intend to agree with the **Holy Scripture** (as it is the unique ark and sanctuary of truth), and to follow and imitate it with the greatest effort and industry. Yet, there is no lack of a "character of probability" in those descriptions of ours expressed in those places—for example, to return to the origins of springs expressed there.

We previously posited that the sole cause of springs was **air**, thrust out from the bowels or caverns of the earth by the force of waters breaking forth abundantly from the clouds; this air, in its upward motion, is usually congealed into drops of water by the coldness of the earth, from which springs can afterwards be gathered and procreated. But truly, it is impossible for **perennial springs** <note>Springs that flow year-round.</note> to arise from this, because the enclosed air cannot be immeasurable or infinite, since the thing located is only as great as the place that holds it; but the earth itself is finite, therefore the air contained in its belly is also finite. And this same thing must be said regarding the second reason—the second theory of the generation of springs—where we said it was possible that the liquid of a spring is produced by the "subtilization" <note>The process of making something thinner or more refined, like turning water to vapor.</note> of the waters contained in the belly of the earth, caused by the heat of the **central fire**. For just as water held in the bowels of the earth cannot be permanent without a new addition from the sea (since it is limited within itself), so too that heat is not able to endure perpetually in the same state and action. However, that experiment of ours depicted in that place can very easily lead toward the sense of the Holy Scriptures, as will be shown more widely in what follows.

But to the matter we are primarily treating in this place (all ceremonies aside), we shall now briskly apply ourselves. We say, therefore, that regarding the origin of springs, the **Peripatetics** (both Pagan and Christian) are greatly deceived. Consequently, we shall show that **Aristotle**, their master, once the matter has been weighed exactly in the scales of justice by true Christians, is to be esteemed a liar, and his doctrine in this matter is to be utterly repudiated. Aristotle, then, along with several of his followers, fell into this opinion concerning the origin of springs: namely, that since the belly of the earth is full of concavities and passages (as these cannot be empty), **vapors** are elevated through them from the earth; when these are resolved into waters on the sides of the caverns, they drip down drop by drop, and thus they form little streams; in this way, they claim springs are procreated. They conclude, therefore, with their Doctor Aristotle, that the matter of a spring is nothing other than vapor resolved and liquefied into water by cold and heat together within the earth—just as clouds, snow, rain, and hail are born in the air from condensed and then liquefied vapor.

<note>The following paragraph is marked with a large vertical bracket in the left margin.</note>

However, so that we may look into that Aristotelian description with sharper eyes and examine each of its members a little more accurately, we must notice with a diligent gaze that they create a double cause for the spring—both material and formal—through that description of theirs. For they make the **remote matter** to be vapor, which they then claim is reduced by nature into the form of flowing water (which they established as the **proximate matter** of the spring). They also posited both cold and heat as the **efficient cause** of the spring; they claim the office of the cold is to congeal the air enclosed in the caverns into vapors, and the office of the heat mixed with the cold is the reduction of those vapors into fluid water.

But truly, let it be permitted to answer them with that worn and tested axiom of the Peripatetics themselves: namely, *it is vain to do by many things what can be done by fewer.* <note>original: "frustra fieri quid per plura, quod potest fieri per pauciora." This is a version of the principle of parsimony, or Occam's Razor.</note> If it is possible for water to be sublimated in its own proper nature through the hidden passages of the earth, from the sea even to the peaks of mountains, then there is no need for air or water to first be contracted into vapor, and for that vapor then to be reduced back into liquid water by congelation. Indeed, it is certain, and consequently possible, that water—without any alteration of its form—can be elevated and raised from the **abyss of the sea** through the occult passages of the earth even to the summits and heights of mountains by a natural instinct, as will be shown more clearly below.

But how sterile and dull is this invention of theirs: that vapors of this kind are resolved into water drop by drop on the sides of caverns, which then later form streams and consequently springs! As if, by this reasoning, those vapors would not rather turn into a watery nature within the veins and porous passages of the earth and thus tend downward again by their own weight in a cycle, rather than moving upward or laterally. Or, if such vapors were condensed in the caverns of the earth, it would be more probable that the greater part of that water would fall back again into the inner reaches of the earth through its pores. But if it were the case that the matter of a spring is procreated from vapors enclosed in the veins of the earth, it would be necessary that such vapors arise either from the cold condensation of the air enclosed in the depths of the earth, or from the resolution of the water contained in its belly through the rarefaction of heat. From this it would follow that the air or water contained in the bowels of the earth is infinite in its quantity, which cannot be (as has been said), for the thing contained is not immeasurable. But if it is replied that the enclosed air is nourished by the open sea, or the water by the common Ocean of waters...

# On the Formal Cause of Meteors.

...and if it is multiplied, let that also be granted. But it does not follow of necessity that where air is contained within the cold earth, vapors and springs are also produced there. For beyond all controversy, it is certain that there is no pore or cavity of the earth that is not filled with air, so subtle and penetrating is the air, seeing as it is the life and spirit of any thing; indeed, not even in water is the thickening and tightening of its parts so dense that it does not have air disseminated throughout its members. 

Furthermore, even if the free passage and succession of air through the pores of the earth were admitted, it would not follow that it would migrate first into vapor, and then afterwards into moisture or fluid liquid. We have demonstrated by experience that if a tube of any substance is passed through a jar full of water, the simple air enclosed in the tube is nevertheless not observed to be easily converted into vapor, much less into water. Much less would the air enclosed in the veins of the earth be so converted, since the dryness of the earth is more opposed to such a function (namely, the condensation of vapor into fluid water) than water is. 

But if the cause of vapor migrating into the nature of water in the caverns of the earth were water itself (which is resolved into vapor by the force of heat), then that labor would be in vain; for it is possible that the water itself, in its whole species or nature, without such a reduction, could be raised from the bowels of the earth (which the abyss of the sea is accustomed to replenish continually) upward to the place of springs through the veins of the earth <term>veins of the earth: a common early modern belief that the earth had a circulatory system of channels similar to blood vessels in a body</term>. And the confirmation of this matter is explained first by these two following clear demonstrations, and then established by the authority of Holy Scripture. As for the first visual experiment, it is depicted in Hero’s *Pneumatics* <note>original: "Heronis spirital." Refers to Hero of Alexandria, a Greek mathematician and engineer whose work on air pressure was rediscovered in the Renaissance.</note>, Book 1, where he treats the bent siphon.

A. B. C. The bent siphon; A. B. is the leg of the siphon in the vessel D. E., which is full of water. The surface of the water in the vessel is at the straight line in which F. G. lies, and the leg of the bent siphon A. B. is filled with water up to the F. G. line. That is, let the part of the leg A. H. be full of water, while the part of the bent siphon H. B. C. is full of air. 

If, therefore, we draw out the aforementioned air with the mouth through the opening C, the moisture will follow at the same time, because a place cannot be entirely empty <note>This refers to the classical concept of "horror vacui," the idea that nature abhors a vacuum.</note>. And if indeed the opening of the siphon C is level with F. G., though filled with water, the siphon will not flow, but will remain full, so that the part of the siphon A. B. C. is replenished with water—even though the part of the water between H. and C. is carried upward against the laws of nature. 

Rather, like a certain balance having an equilibrium, the water will remain drawn upward according to the part H. B. and suspended downward according to B. C. But if the outer opening of the siphon is below the straight line F. G., such as at K, the water flows, because the part of the balance or leg K. B. is heavier than that of B. H.; whence, on account of its weight, it overcomes and draws the water in a fluid motion, first upward from H. to B., and then downward from B. to K. 

But it draws no more than that which tends to the surface of the water A. If that leg is depressed and longer still, namely at L, then that leg will draw to itself all the water between A. and H., by elevating it little by little upward to B, and then falling downward through the leg B. L., it exits through the orifice L; and in this way, it will evacuate that water entirely.

Hence we see that wonderful connection and contiguity which exists primarily between water and air, so that when air is drawn, it is necessary for water to follow, lest a vacuum be admitted—which is quite horrific in the nature of things. And then we see that firm continuity which exists between water and water, so that one part enclosed cannot flow or leak without the other closely adhering to it, either flowing upward or downward, for the reason of the aforementioned admission of a vacuum.

Fludd is citing his own previously published work to show consistency in his physical theories.</note> (where the origin of the winds was discussed by us). Its opening C. does not communicate with the mouth of the vessel A. B., but an outer tube E. F. surrounds it on all sides, so that they are equally distant from each other. The upper part of the external siphon E. G. must be exactly closed and secured, while its lower foot...

### Section I. Portion IV. Part II. Book III. Member II.

...the higher part, namely at **F**, ought to be as far from the bottom of vessel **A-B** as is sufficient for the flow of water to the lower tube, or let it be pierced with holes. With these things thus arranged, if we draw out the air that is in tube **C-D** through the protruding mouth of the interior tube **D**, we shall simultaneously draw the water which is in vessel **A-B**. By this reasoning, all the water of vessel **A-B** will flow out through the orifice of the internal <term>siphon<note>A tube used to convey liquid upwards from a reservoir and then down to a lower level of its own accord. Fludd uses this as a model for how water moves through the earth.</note></term>, which occurs because of the wonderful connection that exists between the air contained in siphon **C-D** and **E-F**. Moreover, the reason for the continuous flow is that the air, due to the interposition of the water, cannot penetrate into the siphon.

From these things, therefore, it is most certain that it is possible—even with the sole assistance of nature—for water to penetrate from its natural place (whether from the belly of the earth or the abyss of the sea) into the bowels of the earth without so many and such great <term>alterations and permutations<note>Fludd is critiquing the Aristotelian idea that water must "change" from air or vapor; he argues it moves simply as water.</note></term>, and this most easily; for we find this same thing in **Art**, which is the closest **"ape of nature."**

But we now approach the testimony of the fountain of all truth, the Sacred Scriptures, against which no contradiction can be made—especially when confirmed by the testimony of the eyes—not even by a fool (since experience is the teacher of fools), and much less by a pious Christian. As the Wise Man <note>Solomon</note> says:

> **Ecclesiastes 1:7.** *All the rivers enter into the sea, and the sea does not overflow; to the place from whence they go out, they return, so that they may flow again.*

Yet the <term>Aristotelians<note>Followers of Aristotle’s physics, which dominated universities at the time but which Fludd viewed as "pagan" and often incorrect.</note></term>, even those who are Christian, do not blush to contradict this most wise man, even though they acknowledge their teacher’s doctrine to be most opposite to that of Solomon. Indeed, with unheard-of audacity, these Peripatetics <note>Another name for Aristotelians</note> delight in publishing this same ethnic <note>pagan</note> doctrine in the Academic Schools. From this, no certainty can be found in natural philosophy among common Christians, and consequently, the truth of science has been so shrouded from us Christians by the dark clouds of the heathens that a fantastic shadow is grasped for substance, and dreams for reality, by those blinded by worldly things. This is the cause of errors in every science; indeed, in Theology itself, which deals primarily with the knowledge of **GOD**, whom the Holy Scriptures have proclaimed to be known through His physical creatures.

How, then, can we arrive at a knowledge of God when we are ignorant of the causes of His creatures? Is it possible to ascend to heaven by Jacob’s ladder unless we first ascend through the elementary steps? Moses saw the "back parts" of God—that is, he saw God in His creatures—and the Royal Psalmist <note>King David</note> said that he knew God himself through His wonderful works. Therefore, how can we arrive at a right knowledge of God if we are ignorant of His works and the mysteries of His creatures? Can anyone be a complete master in <term>Theosophy<note>Divine wisdom or the study of God's internal nature.</note></term> who is ignorant in <term>meteorological<note>In the 17th century, "meteors" included all atmospheric phenomena: rain, wind, lightning, and springs.</note></term> matters and the true, non-imaginary mysteries of the weather? What will you—O theologians, who are so little versed in the true secret of physics—understand by these assertions of the Holy Page?

> *Will you (says Job) send out lightnings, and will they go, and returning say, "Here we are"?* **Job 38:35.** *And David: who makes the winds his angels and flaming fire his ministers.* **Psalm 104:4.** *And again: smoke ascended through the nostrils of Jehovah, and a consuming fire from His mouth; coals were kindled by Him, and bowing the heavens He descended with darkness under His feet; sitting upon the Cherubim He flies, and flies upon the wings of the wind. From the brightness that is before Him, thick clouds pass by, and sending out His arrows He scatters them, and hurling lightnings He pours them out.* **Psalm 18.** *And elsewhere: by His sneezings light shines, from His nostrils smoke comes forth, and from His mouth a flame goes out.* **Job 41:18.** *And elsewhere: Jehovah shall open His best treasure, the heavens, by giving rain to your land.* **Deuteronomy 28:12.** *And elsewhere: Thick clouds are His pavilion.* **Job 22.** *And elsewhere: Thick clouds are the chariot of God. And elsewhere: God spread a cloud for a covering.* **Psalm 104.** *And elsewhere: Jehovah utters hailstones and sounds.* **Exodus 19.** *And elsewhere: The mighty God utters ice by His breath.* **Job 27:9.**

And so on infinitely. If, therefore, you are ignorant of the mysteries of the meteors, and wish to understand them in the ethnic and false Aristotelian manner rather than the sacrosanct way, how [can you know] God and His will...
