### On the Formal Cause of Meteors.

Can you rightly reconcile these two wills? "No man can serve two masters faithfully," says Christ. Those, therefore, who wish to follow Aristotle rather than the **Holy Spirit** (who, by the testimony of Holy Scripture, is the **Teacher of Teachers**) in assertions contrary to the sacred page, are so prone to the **Devil** and immersed in darkness that it is impossible for them to comprehend **GOD** and His light. For when GOD is unknown, all things are unknown; for Christ is all that is, according to holy testimony, and without Him there is nothing. I therefore sincerely advise the Christians of following ages that they should not divert or distort the intention of their Philosophy from the sense of the Holy Scriptures (however much they may be seduced by the vain opinions of the **Pagans**, those rebels against the light). Thus, whatever appears to disagree with the holy context—no matter how much it is confirmed by the Pagans—let us reject it, unless we prefer to speak in that impious and detestable manner of the poet: *I see the better things and approve them, yet I follow the worse.* <note>original: "Video meliora proboque, deteriora sequor" — a famous line from Ovid's Metamorphoses, often used to describe someone acting against their better judgment.</note>

Indeed, this was the case with **Johannes Velcurius** <note>Johann Velcur (1510–1581), a German philosopher and author of a popular commentary on physics.</note>, a man quite famous in natural philosophy, who spoke these words in Chapter 6, Book 3 of his *Physical Commentaries*: *The Holy Scriptures do not plainly agree with the physicists concerning the origin of rivers and springs; for Ecclesiastes Chapter 1 testifies that they flow from the sea through various channels and passages and flow back to their sources, saying: "All rivers enter into the sea, yet the sea is not full; unto the place from whence the rivers come, thither they return to flow again."* But (he says) *the physicists claim the matter is vapor resolved into water, liquefied by cold and heat together within the earth.* And so, having neglected the path of truth, he proceeds to publicly review and teach the false opinions of the Pagans on this matter against his own conscience, as if no true doctrine of physics were to be found in the **Holy Bible**.

But we, treating this matter with greater precision, shall prove that the way expressed by **Solomon** concerning the origin of springs is the only true and authentic one, while that Aristotelian way is vain, fantastical, and bears only a resemblance to the truth. We shall show this by **ocular demonstration**. Specifically, that the matter of springs is actual water, moving immediately from the sea with its aquatic form unchanged, penetrating through the hidden passages of the earth to its very bowels. This water—by the wonderful connection it has with the air through the **Divine Word** operating centrally—is either raised toward the surface from the center of the earth or depressed from the surface toward the center, by virtue of the cold contracting the universal air, or likewise by heat dilating and rarefying it.

This has been more than sufficiently demonstrated by us (almost as if pointing with a finger) in *Part 3, Book 3, Chapter 3* of this work, regarding our **universal experiment**, namely through the logic of the ascent and descent of water in the neck of a **matrass** <note>A long-necked glass flask used in early scientific experiments to demonstrate the effects of temperature on air pressure, acting as a primitive thermometer or weather glass.</note>. For when heat is present and intensified, the water is pushed downward gradually by the rarefaction of the enclosed air, into the "whirlpool" of the sea or earth (that is, into the watery mass). Conversely, in the domain of cold, that water which was previously depressed by heat is raised upward again into the neck of the matrass because of the air's contraction and condensation. And this happens without any change of its form or the alteration of the substance of the water into vapor (according to the opinions of the Pagan philosophers) and then a subsequent reduction back into water. For although I admit it is easier for a light thing to be lifted up than a heavy one, we nevertheless say it is not against the laws of nature for the water itself to be lifted high by the wonderful contraction of the air by cold (since the air is contiguous with the water in an inseparable union), just as you have seen clearly demonstrated in the spiritual conclusions expressed previously.

We believe, therefore, that the essence of a spring, according to the intention of the Holy Bible, should be described in this manner:

> A **Spring** is a flow or gushing of water, produced from the **sea** as the starting point, and through the **bowels of the earth** as the medium, to its upper surface. It is produced by the **Word** operating in the **world-spirit** <term>spiritum mundanum<note>The 'spiritus mundus' or world-spirit was thought to be a subtle substance pervading the universe, through which divine power acted upon physical matter.</note></term> through the effects of heat, either for the health and preservation of man and the creatures destined for man's use, or for punishment and destruction.

In this description of ours, we establish that **water** is the material cause of the spring; the **Divine Word** is the primary efficient cause; and **heat** (begotten from the power of the Divine Word and dispersed everywhere in the air or world-spirit) is the secondary cause. Finally, we have said the **final cause** is either for the preservation of creatures or their punishment, according to the Divine will. In this description of springs, you also have the origin of that water duct—namely the **sea**, which is the primary source and fountainhead of springs and rivers—and the local motion, which occurs through the veins and pores of the earth itself until it reaches the exit or visible beginning of the spring. It is our task to prove all these individual parts of the description and to support them with the testimony of Holy Scripture.

Regarding the **material cause** of the spring, which we have said is water, we have it handed down in express words by the Wise Man (even if ocular experience did not indicate it): *All rivers enter into the sea, yet the sea is not full; unto the place from whence they come, thither they return to flow again.* From which it appears clearly enough that the material cause of a spring is **water and not vapor**, since all rivers are perennial from their sources, the motion of the spring water from the sea to the sea is circular, and its middle motion is through the earth.

Furthermore, that **GOD** is the principal cause producing springs, we have from many other places in the Holy Scriptures. For it is said there: *He sendeth the springs into the valleys, which run among the hills, Psalm 104.* And elsewhere: *When he strengthened the fountains of the deep... wisdom was with him, Proverbs 8:28.* And in Job we find these things written: *He cutteth out rivers among the rocks... and he bindeth the floods from overflowing, Job 28:10.* Here he makes GOD not only the author of springs and streams (which take their rise from springs), but also of His other...

Psalm 104:10.* Here, therefore, you see the final cause explained by the Royal Prophet as being for the benefit of all creatures.

However, we read elsewhere that sometimes springs and rivers are ordained for the ruin of creatures and the destruction of men. Genesis 7:11.* And elsewhere it is said *that GOD, because of the wickedness of those dwelling on the earth, turns the desert into a pool of water, and the parched land into water-springs. Psalm 107:33.* 

Finally, it is right to conclude from these words of the Holy Bible that the sea is the origin from which all springs, and consequently all rivers, are derived. *GOD said, Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place, and let the dry land appear: and it was so. And GOD called the dry land Earth; and the gathering together of the waters called he Seas. Genesis 1.* From this it is clear that the sea is the place originally ordained during creation for waters of every kind; hence it is necessary, according to Solomon’s opinion, that all specific waters proceed from it. But there is also a most powerful argument brought forth by the Wise Man <note>Solomon</note> himself: namely, *because all rivers enter into the sea and the sea does not overflow.* Therefore, it is clearer than the noonday sun that all that water which entered the sea from springs and rivers must have originally flowed out from the sea.

As for what pertains to the generation of temporary springs, you have already seen in the previous sections where they come from: namely, either from an excessive abundance of rain or from the melting of snow.

...whether the bubbling source is a spring, or rather comes from several springs, just as a stream commonly arises from one or a few. Briefly, therefore, in this place—following the doctrine of the most Holy Bible—we shall declare in a few words what a river is, what a stream is, and what a torrent is.

A **River** <note>original: "Flumen"</note> is a gathering of flowing waters which, coming from the sea as if from a primordial source, flows upward through the bowels of the earth from the caverns of springs. By means of many small streams and by divine power, these flow into a single channel. This is ordained according to the will of the Creator to provide for the earth, whether for punishment or for blessing. Once their business is finished, these waters return to their own place—namely the sea—from whence they first came.

In this description of a river, you see that its material cause is water, and in its form, it is fluid and contained within its channels. Its efficient cause <note>The force that brings something into being.</note> is truly divine power—specifically Wisdom itself—by means of which it is said that *Jehovah strengthened the fountains (Proverbs 8:28)* from which rivers seem to gush. Furthermore, we find it written in Ecclesiasticus: *I, Wisdom, have poured out rivers (Ecclesiasticus 24:40).* Finally, we have declared that its final cause <note>The ultimate purpose or goal.</note> is to carry out the will of the Creator, either in punishing or in doing good. We have drawn this also from the sacred source, seeing that God may take away the benefits of healthy rivers because of the impiety of those living there. Thus it was said by the Prophet: *The rivers shall fail, the streams of the embankments shall be thinned and dried up, and the channels of the stream shall be laid bare from their source (Isaiah 19:6).* And elsewhere: *The Lord shall strike from the channel of the river even to the torrent.* And elsewhere: *I have dried up with the sole of my foot all the streams of the embankments (Isaiah 27:12).* And elsewhere: *I will dry up your rivers (Job 37).* And in Ezekiel we find this: *I will make the channels of the rivers dry and deliver the land into the hands of the wicked (Ezekiel 30:12).* Or, he may act beyond the laws of nature by multiplying its waters. Hence King David says: *He turned rivers into a desert, and the flow of waters into thirsty ground, because of the malice of those dwelling therein (Psalm 107:33).* Finally, the wise man testifies in *Ecclesiastes 1* that the universal source of rivers and streams is the sea, from which water passes and to which it returns. Particular springs in the earth are secondary origins, first for streams and then for rivers, since streams arise immediately from the springs of the earth, just as rivers arise from streams. Hence the Prophet says: *The channel of the stream shall be laid bare from its source (Isaiah 19:7).* That many small streams concur to compose a single river is something we are taught even by the experience of our own eyes.

A **Stream** <note>original: "Rivus"</note> we therefore describe as a living and permanent flow of waters, leaping forth immediately from a single spring or from the bubbling sources of several small springs, which then descends into the channel of some river and is made one with it.

The members of this description are so linked with the parts of the preceding one that the logic for both is the same; indeed, a stream stands in relation to a river as a part to the whole, or as a head to a body.

Finally, as pertains to the nature of a **Torrent**, it differs from a river and a stream both in its origin and in its duration. For while those two arise from the sea and from waters penetrating the earth to gush forth as springs—and are consequently for the most part perennial <note>Flowing year-round.</note>—the torrent receives the matter of its flow from the clouds, namely from rains and snows. The Holy Scriptures make mention of this kind of flow in many places, such as when discussing the torrents of *Arnon, Zered, Kishon, Besor, Kidron, Gaas, Cherith, Mamre, etc.* Finally, we are taught that there is a great and distinct difference between these three by these words:
> Stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt, and over their rivers, and their streams, and their torrents, and their pools, and all their lakes of water. <note>A reference to Exodus 7:19.</note>

Of this kind of flow, the consistency of that flowing to the spleen is slimy and earthy, while that passing through the trunk of the Vena Cava is sanguine <note>Bloody.</note>.

### On Manna.

**B**oth the Pagans and those Christians well-versed in Pagan philosophy have admitted that the substance of manna is a certain honeyed dew descending from the sky. However, they also claim that the origin of this same dew arises from the earth and water—vainly nourishing their own imaginary fantasies—namely, that it comes from a very fatty and viscous vapor exhaled from the internal elements of water and earth together with the air, which then falls back upon plants through freezing, like sugar or very sweet flour. In this opinion, the foundations and bases of their philosophy always seem to be established on error, for they derive visible things from other visible things rather than from the invisible. Yet the matter is quite the opposite according to the testimony of Holy Scripture, by which we are taught (as has been frequently alleged before) that we must believe through faith that visible things were first made from those that are invisible. We say, therefore, that Manna is a dense kind of **meteor** <note>original: "Meteori"; in this era, a "meteor" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon like dew, rain, or snow, not just space rocks.</note>, produced by the thickening of the heavenly air when it is soaked with moisture.

> *Does not a certain eminent Philosopher say,* I pray you, consider a simple cloud of water: Would anyone ever believe that it contains within itself everything that the world has—hard stones, salts, air, earth, fire—and yet it appears by itself to be simple water?

So he says. But indeed, in the places cited previously, we have proved clearly enough by reasons established in the Holy Bible that vapors, clouds, and their waters are formed from the condensation of simple air and produced into the world.

We, therefore, according to the laws of holy testimony, have thought it best to describe Manna in this manner:

Manna is a fatty substance of the air which—the gates of heaven having been opened and the divine treasury made manifest—descends from the clouds by divine command in the manner of dew or frost. It grows into a tiny appearance, round like white **coriander seed** <note>original: "semini Coriandri"; a common biblical comparison used to describe the size and shape of Manna.</note>, falling upon the lands to carry out the will of the Creator.

->Or thus,<-

Manna is the heavenly bread, the wheat of heaven, spiritual food, the food of angels, and the very word proceeding from the mouth of **Jehovah** <note>original: "Iehouae"</note>. It descends by divine power from the sky and the clouds in the manner of a dewy rain—either together with the heavenly dew or upon the dew—onto the surface of the earth. It takes a tiny and round form, similar to lumpy frost or coriander seed, curdling there into hardness so that it might serve as food, nourishment, and even medicine for men.

In our first description, you have the **material cause** <note>The physical "stuff" it is made of, according to Aristotelian philosophy.</note> of Manna expressed, insofar as it is described there as being a fatty substance of the air. Then the **formal cause** <note>The "shape" or "essence" that makes it what it is.</note> is expressed in that it is said to grow into a tiny appearance, round like coriander seed. Afterward, we declared its **efficient cause** <note>The "agent" or "force" that brings it into being.</note> to be the divine command—that is, the Power and the Word. Finally, we affirm the **final cause** <note>The "purpose" or "end goal" for which it exists.</note> or occasion of this descent and generation to be the execution of the Creator’s will. All these parts of our description you have confirmed particularly from the most holy pages of scripture in this way: For as far as the material cause is concerned, God says to the Israelites: *Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you, Exodus 16:4.* And elsewhere: *He gave them heavenly bread to eat, John 6:31.* And elsewhere: *He had commanded the clouds from above and opened the doors of heaven, and rained down Manna upon them.* By these it is clearly enough declared that the matter of Manna itself is of an aerial composition, since by the word "heaven" the air is understood, as it is the place of the clouds which Jehovah commanded, etc. Whence the treasury-chest of Manna, in which it is reserved and from which it is fashioned as to its substance, is the air itself. The **form** is also explained by these words: *And in the morning, the dew lay round about the host, and when the dew that lay was gone up, behold, upon the face of the wilderness there lay a small round thing, as small as the hoar frost on the ground, Exodus 16:14.* And elsewhere: *The Manna was as coriander seed, white; and the taste of it was like wafers made with honey.* And elsewhere: *The taste of it was as the taste of fresh oil, Numbers 11:7.* Furthermore, the efficient or creating cause is confirmed by these words:

> I (says Jehovah) rain bread from heaven for you, Exodus 16:4.

And elsewhere: *He had commanded the clouds from above, and opened the doors of heaven, and rained down Manna upon them.* Finally, the purpose of this kind of meteor is explained where it is said:

> He fed thee with Manna... that he might make thee know that man doth not live by bread only, but by every word, etc. Deuteronomy 8:3.

And elsewhere: *Thou feddest thine own people with angels' food, and didst send them from heaven bread prepared without their labor, able to content every man's delight, and agreeing to every taste, Wisdom of Solomon 16:20.* And elsewhere: *He gave them heavenly bread to eat, John 6:31.*

We conclude, therefore, that besides all these things, you have the place of generation for this kind of divine nourishment in our said description: namely, that it descends from the clouds through the opened gates of heaven and the revealed divine treasury. For it is written: *Behold, I rain bread from heaven for you, Exodus 16.* And elsewhere: *He had commanded the clouds from above, and opened the doors of heaven, and rained down Manna upon them, Psalm 78:24-25.*

In the second description also, you have these four causes of the meteor exactly explained. But that material cause is explained in a more hidden way: through the bread and wheat of heaven, through spiritual food, the food of angels, and indeed through the "material word," the efficient cause of which we make Jehovah himself. The place from which it is taken is the heaven and the clouds; the manner of its emanation is indicated, and along with it the formal cause: namely, that it descends in the manner of dewy rain, or together with heavenly dew, or upon the dew to the surface of the earth, curdling into hardness in a tiny and round form, like mounded frost or coriander seed. Finally, its final cause is explained therein by the fact that it serves men as both food and nourishment, as well as medicine.

But I know there will be many who will not hesitate to object that the Manna mentioned by the holy scriptures, by means of which the Israelites were nourished in the desert, was something miraculous and not at all natural...

# On the Formal Cause of Meteors.

...and consequently, they assert that the aforementioned description in no way matches natural Manna, which descends more or less daily with the dew. To them, I truly reply that the substance and form of one hardly differs from the other, although we see one ordered and prepared differently than the other (according to the Creator's pleasure). In this same way, the quails which God sent abundantly into the camp of the Israelites to nourish them did not differ in substance or form from other quails, even though they were brought into that place by divine power and ordained for the sustenance of the Israelites.

And certainly, if anyone knew how to rightly collect the Manna that falls from heaven commonly with the dew—especially in May and also in summer—and how to prepare it by removing the kernel, I believe he would acquire for himself something far more precious than gold and gems, and would possess a most excellent balsam of life. For I have been so instructed by men most skilled in the divine mystery. And Manna of this kind, prepared in such a way and stripped of its external impurities (making the hidden manifest and the manifest hidden), is then called the **hidden Manna** <note>original: "Manna absconditum"</note> which is promised to the victor in the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation 2:17.</note>, seeing as it is a substance in which heavenly grace and the **quintessence** <note>term: "vis quinta" or fifth power; in alchemy, the purest essence of a substance beyond the four elements.</note> are spread and abound copiously from the uncreated rays on every side. 

In this way, we see that the external man has within himself his own internal or spiritual man, which is the temple of the Holy Spirit. Thus it is also said, *the incorruptible Spirit is in every thing (Wisdom 12:1).* But then it is said to abound more in one thing than in another; thus *Christ is said to be all and in all.* But because of our sins, He is crucified in His creatures—or rather, bound and imprisoned. Yet if we, like good Jews and true Israelites, could bind Barabbas and free Jesus—contrary to the custom of the worst Jews who bound Jesus and freed Barabbas—then we would truly know Jesus in His essence: we would become one with Him and be numbered among the elect of God, according to the words of the Evangelist in *John 1.*

As for the final proof of our description, we have it written thus in the Holy Scripture: *He fed you with Manna, that He might make known to you that man does not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of Jehovah (Deuteronomy 8:3).* From this, it is clear that Manna proceeds immediately from the benevolent breath of Jehovah. So also it is said *that the upper clouds by His wisdom drop down the dew (Proverbs 3:20),* and *that His wisdom gives weight to the air (Job 28:25).* It is said, *That by the breath of God frost is produced (Job 37:10),* and *that His word is carried out by the stormy wind (Psalm 148:8), etc.* Furthermore, we read *that He gave them heavenly bread to eat (John 6:31).* And elsewhere: *He had commanded the clouds from above, and opened the doors of heaven, and had rained down Manna upon them to eat, and had given them the wheat of heaven (Psalm 78:24-25).* And elsewhere: *They all ate the same spiritual food (1 Corinthians 10:3).* From these points, it is sufficiently clear that the final description of Manna is also confirmed by sacred testimony.

### On the Ceraunian Stone or Thunderbolt.

The **thunderstone** <note>term: "Lapis fulminaris" or "Lapis Ceraunius"; historically, people believed that fossilized shells or ancient stone axes found in the earth were physical bolts thrown from the sky during lightning strikes.</note>, also called the Ceraunian stone and the lightning dart, is a thing in nature worthy of wonder. The ancients hesitated regarding its origin, nor did the **Peripatetics** <note>note: followers of Aristotle's philosophy.</note> write anything of great importance after considering the matter more accurately. Indeed, philosophers of sounder mind, both ancient and more recent, found it to be of such depth that they believed the origin of such meteors (having considered their wonderful properties again and again) proceeded immediately from the highest God rather than from the craftsmanship of Nature. 

Hence, it is observed that Aristotle and his school—who strive to render a natural reason for this meteor established upon their own fabulous foundations—err in their entire description. It is their opinion that the thunderstone is a sulfurous exhalation mixed with some terrestrial and mineral or metallic matter, reduced into a single mass, usually in a green or blackish cloud. This mass is supposedly gathered into a ball by the surrounding moisture and stuck together like flour with water, and then, by the intense heat coming from the sun and stars (that is, by the power of influences), and partly through **antiperistasis** <note>term: a philosophical concept where a quality is intensified by being surrounded by its opposite, such as heat being compressed and intensified by surrounding cold.</note>, it is transformed from its muddy state into a hard and firm stone, in the manner of bricks, and is driven downward by the violent force of the fire trapped in the cloud.

In this description of theirs, they made the material cause of the stone a lightning-like or sulfurous exhalation mixed with a certain terrestrial mineral or metallic matter and reduced into a single mass—as if to say the matter of the lightning dart is the denser, more compact, and terrestrial part of that exhalation which was raised from the earth into the middle region of the air by the sun's power. Then they explained its form by saying that this slimy mass was transmuted into the appearance of a hard stone by the power of heat, in the manner of bricks. Finally, they placed the efficient cause of this formation in the hidden influences of heaven, namely, stellar heat.

Regarding the opinion of the Peripatetics concerning the matter of the thunderstone, it seems to be erroneous and least consistent with the laws of the Holy Scripture. For (as was explained abundantly in the preceding pages), God is accustomed to produce clouds, and consequently everything that is of the substance of clouds, from the air or heaven and not from the earth. Indeed, this great earth itself which we see is, as it were, the dregs of the waters or the drier part, according to that saying of St. Peter (often alleged before): *the heaven and the earth were first from water and through water by means of the word.*

Therefore it is clear, that both the clouds themselves and those things which are produced in their womb, as the Philosopher says...

### Section I. Portion IV. Part II. Book III. Member II.

...namely salts, stones, flesh, blood, and everything that can be found in the world, are originally made from thin water. But indeed, we have stated that the cloud itself arose from the air or the heavens and not from the earth, which is also confirmed by divine writings in this way:

> Jehovah shall open unto thee his good treasure, the heaven, to give the rain unto thy land in his season. <note>The text cites Exodus 28:12, but this verse is actually found in Deuteronomy 28:12.</note>

It did not say He will open the lands, but the heaven—that is, the air—as if it had said: Jehovah will open the womb or the hidden <term>matrix</term><note>A "matrix" in this context refers to a place of origin or a "womb" where natural phenomena are conceived and formed.</note> of the air, making the hidden part of the air manifest. The Apostle <note>Likely referring to St. Paul in Hebrews 11:3: "the things which are seen were not made of things which do appear."</note> also teaches us in the place cited above that all visible things were previously invisible. From this it is clear that not only visible water, but also the earth, and consequently stone (which is a denser portion of water), comes from the invisible spirit, which is spiritual water. Concerning their "formal cause," I will say nothing in this place, as it is known to almost everyone through visual experience. 

However, we say that the "efficient cause" <note>The "efficient cause" is the primary agent or force that brings something into being.</note> proposed by some is erroneous and entirely false, as it stands opposed to the holy scriptures. For they <note>Referring to the mainstream academic followers of Aristotle.</note> maintain that the heat of the Sun and the stars brought these <term>meteors</term><note>term: "meteors"; in early modern science, this referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, including rain, wind, and lightning, not just falling space rocks.</note> to completion. But the most holy Bible assigns this work not to the creatures, but immediately to the Creator. Although He has placed His "tabernacle in the sun," He does not dwell there exclusively, for He dwells everywhere by His presence, fills all things, and acts everywhere according to His will. For He, who is the eternal fountain of light, is consequently the origin of action, motion, and heat, both in the stars and in the entire universe. Hence St. John says in Chapter 1:

> All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing [made]. In him was life.

And elsewhere:

> The incorruptible Spirit of God is in every thing. <note>original: "Spiritus DEI incorruptibilis est in omni re." Wisdom of Solomon 12:1.</note>

We say, therefore, that the God Jehovah is both the mediate and the immediate efficient cause of a matter of such great importance; for He is the **Alpha and Omega**, and between His prior and posterior acts there is no distinction or separation in essence. For as He is permanent in Himself, so also His actions are permanent. 

But (my good <term>Peripatetics</term><note>term: "Peripatetics"; the followers of Aristotle's philosophy, who dominated the universities of the time and often sought naturalistic rather than direct divine explanations for weather.</note>), if it were true that the influences of the heavens or the stars were the authors of this kind of lightning-filled meteor, I would very much like to know whether there was thunder in the world before the creation of the "host of heaven" <note>The stars, created on the fourth day according to Genesis.</note> or not? And yet we can very easily gather from the sense of the sacred letters that God spoke through thunder even at the beginning of the creation of the world, through the passages we will cite a little further below where mention of thunder will be made; from which it follows that such an opinion is not well-founded. 

And although it has been proven by the experience of those more skilled in Astrology that thunders are heard after certain "aspects" <note>Positions or angles between planets.</note> of certain planets, it does not follow that this happens by necessity. We observe that such effects by no means always follow such planetary aspects. For it is in the power of God alone, to whom it is given to act according to His will—sometimes, namely, by using His planetary instruments, directing His face from His solar tabernacle toward this or that planet (or several at once); sometimes by means of His winds, whose duty it is to obey their Commander. We observe this happening quite often with no celestial cause evidently preceding it. Sometimes it occurs through spirits and fiery or watery demons fulfilling the mandates of the creator, and in infinite other hidden ways, which would be impossible for even the most skilled Astrologer to explore. However, as to how and by what means God operates to produce meteors in the world, we propose to speak in clear words below, where the natural efficient cause is treated.

->Finally, I wish you to briefly receive what a **thunderstone** is according to the intention of the sacred letters.<-

A thunderous weapon is a stony dart or arrow which, like a fiery breath of coals, is ignited by the mouth of Jehovah (as if from passing torches) and is sent down from the clouds, either for the public punishment of the impious or for the hidden benefit of those born of the earth.

That it is a stony dart, arrow, and weapon of Jehovah, we gather from these places:

> Jehovah thundered from heaven, and the most High gave his voice; he sent out his arrows, and scattered them; he lightened, and consumed them. <note>2 Samuel 22:14-15; the text cites 2 Kings 21, following the Vulgate numbering.</note>

Here it is manifest that he understood "thunderous weapons" by the word "arrows," since he speaks of lightning afterward. Similarly elsewhere:

> Bow thy heavens, O Jehovah, and come down: touch the mountains, and they shall smoke. Cast forth thy lightning, and scatter them: shoot out thine arrows, and destroy them. <note>Psalm 144:5-6.</note>

Furthermore, it is said elsewhere: "the shafts of lightnings shall go directly from the clouds, as from a bow well bent," etc. <note>Wisdom of Solomon 5:21-22.</note> Moreover, in other places, these stones are called "little stones" of Jehovah. As for its form, where it is said that it is ignited like the habit of fiery coals from the mouth of Jehovah, like passing torches, it is confirmed by this testimony:

> By God’s neesings <note>An archaic word for "sneezings."</note> (says Job) a light doth shine, and his eyes are like the eyelids of the morning... out of his mouth go burning lamps, and sparks of fire leap out... his breath kindleth coals, and a flame goeth out of his mouth. <note>Job 41:18-21. While this traditionally describes the Leviathan, the author attributes the power behind it to God.</note>

Furthermore, it is clear from these passages already recited what its efficient cause is: namely, Jehovah Himself through His hot and flashing breath. Finally, its purpose is explained in this definition: namely, for the punishment of rebels. Hence it is said:

> Shoot out thine arrows and destroy them. <note>Psalm 144.</note>

And elsewhere:

> He sent out his arrows and scattered them. <note>2 Samuel 22.</note>

But lest anyone should foolishly reply that these words previously cited regarding divine thunder were brought forth by the sacred page and not regarding natural thunder, we respond: this can be understood of *all* thunder. For without this efficient cause, no meteor—not even anything in the nature of things—can be newly produced, neither according to the order of nature nor against the laws of nature; just as we shall make more ample mention in the chapter on thunder and lightning.

### *On worms, lice, birds, and frogs.*

These meteors—even monstrous ones, as well as blood—sometimes descend from the clouds on account of the sins of men. From these things we can understand clearly enough that the air (which is invisible water) is capable of being converted into any nature whatsoever according to the divine disposition: namely into worms, lice, birds, frogs, blood, etc.

### Relative to the Microcosm.

**K. The dark meteors of the Microcosm, which visibly arise from the earth, are:**

1.  **A slow and thick smoke, and this kind is either**:
    *   **Earthy, sooty, and dark**, which stains the external disposition of the body or "human earth" into blackness, as seen in **black morphew** <note>original: "morphea nigra." A skin condition characterized by dark, discolored patches.</note>, **black jaundice** <note>original: "icteritia nigra."</note>, and other spotted skin infections.
    *   **Viscous and watery or humoral**, which grows and turns into a "Vegetable" nature, expressed in **tuberous ulcers**, **moles**, and **proud flesh** <note>original: "carnis superbae." An overgrowth of granulation tissue during wound healing.</note> or spongy excrescences.

2.  **Solid earth altered by smokes, and these are either**:
    *   **Flat**, which further branches into:
        *   **Salty and yet suitable for**: leading to **the Itch** <note>original: "Pruritum."</note>, **Scabies**, **Ringworm** <note>original: "Serpiginem."</note>, **Impetigo**, etc.
        *   **Choleric and suitable for**: leading to **Inflammations** and **Erysipelas** <note>original: "Erysipelas." An acute skin infection, often called "St. Anthony's Fire."</note>.
        *   **Altered by long preparation, such as smoke dispersed through the flesh, from which it happens that the flesh sometimes becomes**:
            *   **Inclined toward the nature of lime, as in**: **Tophi** <note>Small, hard deposits of uric acid.</note> and **gouty chalk-stones** <note>original: "Podagragypsia."</note>.
            *   **Prone to stony hardness, and suitable to be converted into**: **Bony nodes**, **Warts** <note>original: "Verrucas."</note>, and **hard and hunch-backed tumors**.
        *   **Sulfurous and burnt or mortified, producing**: **Gangrene** and **Cancer**.
    *   **Protuberant**: occurring **suddenly and violently like flesh** being **dried and made wrinkled by salt and false fumes, and it produces**: **Psoriasis**, **Hair loss** <note>original: "Alopeciam."</note>, **Dandruff** <note>original: "Porriginem."</note>, and **Leprosy**.
</image-desc>

Sacred Scripture mentions salty earth and salty fumes, dried out together with sulfurous and burnt earth, in many places regarding the Macrocosm. ### CHAPTER XIII.
#### Part One.
##### On the luminous angelic spirit, or animating fiery wind, both hidden and manifest.

**I** believe it is hidden from no one who is even moderately skilled in natural philosophy—or indeed, well-versed in the Sacred Scriptures—that all creatures receive their soul from light and fire. Indeed, that uncreated light <note>The divine light of God.</note> is recognized as animating the universal spirit of the world by its life-giving breath. This is even noted by the poet Virgil in the 6th book of the *Aeneid*:

> *This work, constructed of the vast body of the world,*
> *A divine soul-power rules* ———— And elsewhere:
> *The spirit nourishes from within, and Mind, infused through the limbs,*
> *Moves the whole mass* <note>original: "Spiritus intus alit, totamque infusa per artus / Mens agitat molem"</note> ———— And elsewhere:
> *They say it is driven from within by a soul, by which they think*
> *All things of the world live, and that the world itself leads its life by it.* 
> — Augurellus, Book 1 of the *Chrysopoeia* <note>Giovanni Aurelio Augurello (c. 1441–1524) was an Italian humanist and alchemist; his "Chrysopoeia" is a famous poem about the "art of making gold" through natural philosophy.</note>.

But we also find this confirmed by the Holy Bible: where we read, *In the word was life, and that was the light of men, John 1.* And elsewhere, *the holy spirit of discipline fills the world,* and again, *the incorruptible spirit of God is in all things, Wisdom 1.* Elsewhere, *Christ is all in all*, and again, *he placed his tabernacle in the sun,* and elsewhere, *Christ is the light of the world, and is the beginning, is the word from which all things come and without which there is nothing*. By the Cabalists <note>Followers of Jewish mysticism, which the author integrates into his Christian philosophy.</note>, this hidden principle is called the **Dark Aleph** <note>original: "Aleph tenebrosum"; Aleph is the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, here representing the first cause in its unmanifested state.</note>, but in its manifestation as it gives life to the world, it is called the **Bright Aleph** <note>original: "Aleph lucidum"</note>. Similarly, they called this divine soul dwelling everywhere the angel Metatron <note>original: "Mitattron"</note>, who is considered by some to be the angel Michael, the leader of souls; to him, those more skilled in magic <note>In this period, "magic" often referred to the study of hidden natural laws and divine hierarchies.</note> have assigned the protection and governance of the solar planet—and not without good reason. Moses describes the appearance of such an Archangel with a fiery face, in whom the name of Jehovah is said to dwell; and in the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation.</note> he is described as having a golden girdle girt about his chest, and eyes like flames of fire, holding in his right hand *7 stars, and his face shone like the Sun in its strength, Revelation 1:13.* From this we argue that this angel is the source of light, as he illuminates the 7 stars or planets and seems to bear the image of the Sun itself (whom Plato did not hesitate to call the visible son of God). Similarly, it was said of this angel, *The angel of the Lord descended from heaven and, approaching, rolled back the stone and sat upon it; his appearance was like lightning, Matthew 28:3.* And Ezekiel saw living creatures present before God, *in the likeness of flashing lightning, Ezekiel 1:14.* Is it not also said elsewhere, *Wisdom is brighter than the sun and more precious, Wisdom 7,* and that she is found to be prior to any arrangement of the stars when compared to light? But who is that wisdom? Is it not that uncreated light, the Word or Christ, who is truly the light of the world, the life of creatures, the soul of the world? So it is also said of the person of the great God Jehovah, *before the brightness in his presence the clouds were kindled, 2 Samuel 22.* And certainly, if we contemplate the sacred writings a little more carefully, we will perceive that this universally animating spirit is a soul inclined as much toward destruction as toward generation and preservation. Hence Jehovah said of this same angel or eternal wisdom: *Behold, I send an angel before you to lead you into the place I have prepared; take heed of his face and listen to his voice, do not provoke him, for he will not bear your rebellion, because my name is in him. Exodus 23:20.* From this we argue that just as that spirit was preserving, nourishing, and guiding the life and steps of men, it is likewise fit to be turned into a destructive nature to punish the sins of men. Whence it happened that sometimes, in the form of a pillar of fire, it offered comfort to the Israelites and provided them with every necessity for life, health, and clothing; yet sometimes, by the fiery heat of its face, it punished them with death. Thus it is written in *Leviticus 10:1-2: Fire going out from the presence of Jehovah consumed them, and they died.* For this reason, in such a nature, **the God Jehovah is called a consuming fire, Deuteronomy 9.** And elsewhere, *the spirit of the power of God winnowing, and justice pursuing the unjust, Wisdom 11:21.* And elsewhere, *The wrath of God is kindled and the earth is moved, and the foundations of the mountains are moved and shaken when smoke ascends through his nostrils and a consuming fire from his mouth, Psalm 21:10.* With Jehovah thundering in the heavens and the Most High uttering his voice, he scatters them by hurlng lightnings. And elsewhere: *The wrath of Jehovah is like a consuming fire;* and so in infinite other places, where God, by means of a certain shimmering and flashing spirit proceeding from him, is accustomed at times to act toward the ruin and destruction of both the members of the Macrocosm <note>The parts of the universe.</note> and of men, on account of the sins of the wicked. But conversely, for the preservation of godly men, he benevolently sends forth his illuminating spirit. Hence David said: *Send out your light and your truth; let them lead me to the mountain of your holiness, Psalm 43:3.* And elsewhere, *Let your face shine upon your servant, save me by your kindness, Psalm 31:17.* Such also was that bright spirit which descended upon the Apostles in the form of cloven tongues; indeed, such was that spirit of the God of forms which God breathed into the face of Adam; of which Job also speaks thus: *the spirit of the mighty God made me, and the breath or inspiration of the Almighty gave me life, Job 33:4.* Indeed, such was that Universal Spirit which in the beginning of creation was borne over the waters, imparting to them a fiery vigor and a kind of life. It seems to manifest itself visibly in certain creatures, but only when "clothed" in garments and not in its simple nature; for no one can look upon God in his naked essence and live. We see it in the sun, the stars, and all clearly luminous meteors, and in metals, which are nothing other than an airy or ethereal spirit animated by divine brightness. But for the most part, the brightness of this divine spirit remains hidden and is recognized only by its effect—namely, in animals and plants, and even in water and air. Thus, clearly shimmering meteors—for example, a Comet, lightning, a Will-o'-the-wisp <note>original: "Ignis fatuus"</note>, etc.—even though they seem to be extinguished and consumed, they are not actually consumed or extinguished. Rather, they vanish into the air, and their luminous form is made invisible through expansion. And this is the reason why a comet, a burning spear, "leaping goats," "beams," and lightning <note>These are traditional names for different shapes of atmospheric lights or comets.</note>, etc., produce their hidden effects for a long time after their disappearance—namely, pestilence, famine, war, or fertility—according to the pleasure and inscrutable decree of the Creator. I would not have you believe that there is any extinction or destruction of this divine spirit (whether flashing secretly or openly), for it is in itself entirely free from such suffering; for *the word of God shall remain forever*, however variously it may be disposed in this world according to the will of the eternal Disposer.

What, then, should be thought of that vain opinion of the Heathens <note>Referring to the Aristotelian or Peripatetic philosophers.</note>, by which they claimed that such a spirit—as well as lightnings, comets, and other ignited impressions—were merely hot and dry exhalations, sublimated from the womb of the earth to either the lowest, middle, or highest region of the air? We also affirm (as we have previously regarding the rest) that their assertion is incongruous, for this divine radiance <note>original: "fulgor diuinus"</note> is not absent from the air. Indeed, it is nothing other than a **moist fire** by nature, or a dilated fire, which, by the divine will, contracts to put on the dark and damp garment of **Chaos** and becomes a cloud; or, by making the hidden more manifest, it becomes a luminous mass, as seen in **Comets**; or a luminous spirit quickly vanishing, like a flash of lightning; or something penetrating more deeply, like a thunderbolt. At other times, it is clothed in a body of even greater consistency yet does not burn, such as the *ignis fatuus* <note>The "will-o'-the-wisp" or swamp gas.</note>, **Castor and Pollux** <note>Also known as St. Elmo’s Fire, a weather phenomenon where luminous plasma is created by a corona discharge from a rod-like object in an atmospheric electric field.</note>, or the fire that licks the hair <note>original: "ignis lambens crines"; a classical reference to a harmless, omen-filled flame appearing on a person's head.</note>. And thus we call this spirit a **luminous and animating spirit**, not because it is divine in itself, but because it contains the divine light centrally within it. This light moves the spirit to fulfill its will, no differently than the soul or mind moves the universal spirit, at whose nod the body is subsequently moved.

Furthermore, let it not seem absurd to anyone that I call this flashing, lightning-filled, and thundering spirit "animating and illuminating." For it is most certain that such a spirit—or rather, the central light within it—is of such excellence and of such profound thought in the nature of things that it claims for itself a place equal to the internal agent, the **Angel**, dwelling in the very center of the human soul. This can be gathered from the words of a certain wise man, well-versed in the mysteries of nature and **theosophy**, which are as follows: *God created the angels from the spiritual elements of the fire of the **First Matter** <note>original: "Prima Materia"; the primitive, formless base of all matter in alchemy and Neoplatonism.</note>, which exceeds and surpasses human grasp and understanding. From this arises the "distinction of the individual," that is, a separation such that no one thing is like another; and therefore the Angels are fire, because they have their origin in that essence of spiritual elements. For this reason, they are much clearer and more splendid than spiritual bodies, which a human can hardly admit or comprehend. For by reason of their great subtlety, they can pass through and penetrate all things without any hindrance or corruption of themselves, **like a flash of lightning**.* The soul of man can do the same, which God likewise created from that same substance from which the Angels were created. Thus says that author. From these words, he seems to suggest that the Angels, lightning, and human souls are of the same fiery substance, exalted to the highest degree of creation.

Does this not seem to be confirmed by the sacred page, where it is written: *That fire, proceeding from the sight of Jehovah, killed rebellious men even while their garments and bodies remained untouched? In many cases, it even happens that coins in a purse and swords in their scabbards are melted, while the purse and scabbard remain untouched. Do we not also read elsewhere in the divine context that the Angels, most strong in power, the ministers of God who carry out His word, are *flaming spirits and ministers? Psalm 103:20 and 104:4.* The soul is also a **divine flash of lightning**, breathed into man at the first creation, so that by reason of its subtlety it can do all things, being free from its opaque body. For it is a direct likeness of the Creator, by reason of which it is said that man was created in the **image of God**. Indeed, regarding the divine mind of man, the Apostle has left us this: *Namely, that the same mind should be in us which was in Jesus:* which mind he further explains in the following: *that, being in the form of God, he did not think it robbery to be equal to God.* <note>A reference to Philippians 2:5-6.</note> Regarding the immense power of this divine flashing or radiance emanating from God for the creation of man, that great high priest **Hermes Trismegistus** <note>A legendary Hellenistic figure associated with the origins of alchemy and magic.</note> writes in *Pymander 4*: *Whoever is supported by this nature of God is, by the comparison of their works, held as immortal among mortals; through their intelligence they embrace all beings that are on the earth and in the sea, and if there is anything beyond heaven; and they raise themselves so high as to behold the Good itself, etc.*

From these things, it is right to gather how great is the perfection of such a luminous spirit, exalted by such degrees, for the informing of things—not only those perfectly mixed, but also those imperfectly mixed. For that very matter, which is the inner essence of life and consistency for the angelic and human soul and the lightning-flash, is the very same that informs all things. However, in some, it is more vivid, effective, and free than in others due to the diversity of the species. Thus it is that we see one perfectly mixed creature differ from another, although the internal or central luminous agent is one and the same, about which it is written: *The incorruptible spirit is in every thing, Wisdom 12:1.* Of this uncreated wisdom, the Apostle Paul also speaks: *From Him, in Him, and through Him are all things; to Him be praise and honor.* The rays of this first emanation from the luminous source were esteemed as gods by **Plato**, **Orpheus**, and other Platonists. This is confirmed by sacred scripture, where it is said that GOD fills all things, and elsewhere, *the incorruptible spirit of GOD is in every thing*, and elsewhere, *the Holy Spirit of discipline fills the world*. From this it is clear, according to that opinion of the Platonists, that all things are full of divine rays. However, all these rays are usually referred back to a single uncreated Sun, since His rays can neither be cut off nor separated from Him, for the essence of GOD is indivisible. This uncreated and invisible sun is the divine Word, or the first emanation from the Father of Light, from whom and into whom are all things, inasmuch as He is the Alpha and Omega <note>The first and last letters of the Greek alphabet, signifying the beginning and the end.</note>. From Him, therefore, all forms and lives are derived, and without Him no <term>form</term> <note>In Aristotelian and scholastic philosophy, the "form" is the essential nature or "soul" of a thing that makes it what it is.</note> is given in the nature of things, whether in the heavens or on earth. For it is written: *In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with GOD, and the Word was GOD. This was in the beginning with GOD. All things were made through him, and without him nothing was made that was made. In him was life, and the life was the light of men, and the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it*, etc. John 1. What could be clearer than this? In this it is evidently plain that the Word, which was in the beginning—that is, the eternal emanation—was the author providing form to all created things, since in Him was life from the beginning. Thus, it is evident that just as nothing can happen without Him, so indeed all things are made through Him and persist in Him, by means of that portion of goodness which they received from Him in the first creation. Even if some new creation occurs daily, it must be brought to the perfection of its species through this incomprehensible light. For according to that saying of St. Paul: *From him, in him, and through him are all things*, to whom be praise. We conclude, therefore, that you have here a description of the primary informing luminous spirit, namely Christ, the Word, the eternal Wisdom, the divine Light hidden at the center, the primary emanation, without whose support no creature, and consequently no <term>meteor</term> <note>In the 17th century, "meteor" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, including rain, wind, comets, or lightning.</note>, can live or endure for a moment of time. This, therefore, is the first act, the first form, the first agent, and the central mover and flashing spirit, which informs all things with its life-giving beauty and incorruptible spirit, to whom be eternal glory and immense thanks for His benefits.

# CHAPTER XIII.

## Second Part.

### Concerning the animated aerial body, that is, fire or light of a superior order.

Now truly, we shall reveal what a comet is, as well as those other fiery portents which are observed to appear in the highest region of the air or above it, according to both the Peripatetics <note>Followers of the philosophy of Aristotle.</note> and the truthful judgment of the scriptures. At the same time, we will briefly and yet clearly demonstrate how immense is the discrepancy regarding their origin between the Pagans and those who are truly illuminated and taught by the Holy Spirit.

The Peripatetics (among whom we recognize Aristotle as the chief) agree on this: namely, that the comet itself is a terrestrial exhalation, thick, hot and dry, fatty and viscous, with densely compacted parts and easily flammable. By the power of the stars, it is raised little by little and bit by bit from the bowels of the earth into the highest region of the air. There, being near the sphere of fire, it is spread out due to the disposition and abundance of its material and is set ablaze. Taking upon itself a shape that is either tailed or "bearded" <note>original: "Barbatam"; a common historical term for a comet with a spreading, hair-like tail.</note>, it moves circularly in a long and diffused tract according to the motion of the star under which it is born, or according to the circular motion of the highest aerial region. Many others have made the <term>formal cause</term> <note>The defining essence or shape.</note> of such a meteor various, because it most often brings about drought, the sterility of the earth, and pestilence, and consequently sometimes a change in political government and the place it regards. In their description, they first placed the <term>material cause</term> of the comet as a terrestrial and viscous exhalation, which others want to be in great quantity and conglomerated in the form of very hard pitch. They want to signify its formal cause in that they make this mass either "illuminated" or "tailed" (which has the denser matter in one part and the rest stretched out longer and thinner), or "bearded" (when, namely, the outer parts of such an exhalation appear thinner and more dispersed), for then it creates a bearded star. They made the <term>efficient cause</term> <note>The force or agent that brings something into being.</note> of such a meteor the astral heat, and especially that of the sun, by whose power that exhalation is not only raised little by little from the bowels of the earth to the middle region of the air, but also, having been reduced into a mass in that region (as if in a womb) by the intense cold of the place, it is immediately kindled and illuminated.

However, as far as the cause of the comet and also of other fiery impressions according to the aforementioned intention of the Peripatetics is concerned, we say indeed that their substance or existence—before they were brought into the light—was hidden and lurking in the air as the primordial receptacle and womb of the animating light, and not in the earth, as they have written quite foolishly, as will be seen in the following...

...in the following sections more extensively. Here, however, we shall show that their opinion in this matter is foolish and empty. For first of all, if this were probable, then it would follow that their assertion is most dull-witted, by which they strive to infer that the material cause of wind is a hot and dry exhalation, light in consistency and not at all flammable. They claim that because of this disposition, it is denied passage through the middle consistency of the air <note>In the traditional science of the time, the atmosphere was divided into three regions: the lowest (warm), the middle (extremely cold), and the highest (fiery).</note> because of the coldness of that place, which—through **antiperistasis** <term>antiperistasis</term> <note>A philosophical concept where a quality is intensified or repelled by its opposite; for example, heat becoming more concentrated when surrounded by cold.</note>—drives that hot exhalation downward. But in truth, we do not see this reasoning as being sufficiently fit. If this assertion of theirs were true, then comets and the other meteorological impressions of both the middle and highest regions of the air would be denied passage through that medium even more than the wind would be. You have already seen this proven by many arguments elsewhere, which I will briefly attempt to measure and repeat in this place. The exhalation that produces wind (according to Aristotle's rules) is very light in its substance; therefore, it is more suited in its measure to strive and ascend upward. For just as it is the natural inclination of all heavy things to move downward, so conversely, it is natural for light things to seek the heights. Therefore, such an exhalation is more prone, due to its lightness, to be raised higher than the material of ignited meteors (among which the *Comet* is the chief). The matter of comets is more compact, dense, and viscous, and consequently not as disposed to ascend as the matter of the winds.

Furthermore, he assigns to the windy exhalation a certain disposition—namely, subtlety and thinness—which makes it more inclined by its nature to penetrate through the middle region of the air than the matter of comets and other fiery impressions, which are given a thicker and more compact matter. Just as it is more difficult for comet-matter to be carried upward compared to wind-matter (which is lighter) because of its viscosity and compact disposition, it is certain that it is also more difficult for it to penetrate; for thinner things penetrate where access is denied to thicker ones. Finally, he ascribes to the nature of the windy exhalation that it is not suited to be inflamed or set on fire. From this it is manifest, by his own admission, that it is easier for this exhalation to penetrate through the middle region of the air without great hindrance than it is for ignited meteors. For something that is actually fiery, or closer to becoming fiery, is more repelled and attacked by cold (which is the predominant quality in the middle region of air) and consequently driven downward more than something that has no potential for inflammation. But truly, as the said *Aristotle* testifies, windy exhalations are not at all suited for illumination or for catching fire, whereas on the other hand, those ignited impressions are quite prone and suited to inflammation. From these points, it is likely that those thick, hot, dry, and viscous terrestrial exhalations, being densely compact, are less suited for ascending into the highest region of the air than those thin and non-flammable ones—both because they are raised into the heights with greater difficulty due to their more compact consistency, and also because they can penetrate with greater difficulty due to their thicker and duller composition. Moreover, they are in the closest potential for inflammation; indeed, this material is even accustomed to being inflamed in the lowest and middle regions of the air, as daily experience teaches us. Therefore, without a doubt, either this matter does not ascend from the earth into the highest region of the air, as *Aristotle* thought, or the wind has its origin from elsewhere. Indeed, to use the very same *Aristotelian* arguments: neither the wind nor the comets can spring from the earth, because of the contrariety that exists between them and the cold middle region of the air, whose nature is to attack its opposites, to resist them to the utmost, and to depress them downward toward the earth and the seas.

But without doubt, everyone will ask: if the material for such comets and fiery impressions does not flow out from the earth by exhaling, where then is its source, or from what fountain does its consistency or essence come? To this question, we think we should respond not unadvisedly: the fountain of such impressions is the same as that of the winds and the waters—namely, the heaven or the open air. We shall proceed to prove this by reasons relying on the wings of both true *Philosophy* and holy *theosophy* <term>theosophy</term> <note>Literally "divine wisdom." In this period, it referred to a type of philosophy that sought to understand the natural world through divine revelation and the study of God's workings.</note>. First, among philosophers both recent and ancient, this is a well-worn saying: just as fire is nothing other than the thinnest and most dilated air, so also "thick fire" is the air itself altered into dryness by divine motion. It is for this reason they called the ether <note>original: "ætherem"</note> as if it were *aithe-aer* <note>The author is using a Greek-derived etymology suggesting 'burning air'.</note>, that is, fiery air, or a spirit mixed equally with fire. This species of purest air, although it cannot be discerned by our eyes in its dissipated and subtle nature, nevertheless—if by the will and act of divine wisdom, through the mediation of His angelic ministers, it is gathered into a mass—it will appear in the species and form of a *light-bringing* star (such as a *comet*). Will this seem arduous and difficult to the *Aristotelians*? For even by *Aristotle* himself, their prince, our opinion is supported when he defines a star as being a denser portion of its own orb. It is as if he had said that a luminous star is a part of the ether contracted and condensed by the working of the world's lucid spirit, from which that star acquires its lucid and fiery form. If this is granted by *Aristotle* himself, what will prevent the airy spirit itself, moving in any region of its sphere, from being able to acquire that same visible form through its own condensation? For the star of the ethereal heaven, compared with the consistency of the element of fire or the supreme region of air, is far greater in its simplicity...

# On the Formal Cause of Meteors

...is its nature denser than that of the supernatural substance of the world, and consequently more fit for thickening? We have said that the causes producing such compressions, acting beyond the common laws of nature, are angelic demonic spirits <note>In the 17th-century context, "demons" often referred to spiritual intermediaries or "daemons" in the Greek sense, not necessarily evil beings.</note> who move the winds in every region of the world. Do not both the Platonists and the Aristotelians acknowledge peculiar "intelligences" <note>Spiritual beings believed to govern the movements and influences of the celestial bodies.</note> of the stars, presiding over them, governing, and moving them? They believe that many legions are subject to these intelligences, carrying out the properties of that same star—whether wandering <note>The planets.</note> or fixed—to which they are assigned, exercising their power in the ether and the elements. We read everywhere, both among the ancient philosophers of the greatest insight and in the Holy Scriptures, that demons or angelic spirits mingle themselves with thunder and lightning.

But in truth, we have declared elsewhere that there is one supreme Prince over these angelic spirits, whose commands they are accustomed to fulfill sincerely and beyond which they cannot move even a foot. This Prince is GOD, the Word, and Wisdom, whom angels of every kind are ready to serve. As the royal Psalmist says: *You most mighty in strength, who fulfill his word, hearkening to the voice of his command, his ministers who do his pleasure, Psalm 103:20.* Is it not also said elsewhere: *Who makes your angels spirits (or winds), and your ministers a burning fire, Psalm 104:4?* And yet, nevertheless—just as in great historical deeds we see the glory and the name of victory or triumph attributed to a great leader and commander present at the time, namely Alexander, Caesar, etc.—so also every remarkable deed performed by the invisible army in the heavens and on the earth is mostly referred not to the ministers, but to GOD. Thus it is said: *O Jehovah, do not rebuke me in your anger, Psalm 6:2.* And elsewhere: *A spirit fanning by the power of God and justice pursuing the unjust, Wisdom 11:21.* So the *spirits of the wheels were moved by the presence of GOD to fulfill his pleasure, Ezekiel 1.* So it is said that *GOD struck Job with ulcers and sores*, and yet he performed that through the mediation of Satan. Furthermore, what the seven angels (to whom seven trumpets were given, standing before the face of Jehovah) did by the mere sound of the trumpets is declared everywhere in the Apocalypse. Moreover, it is said: *Behold, I send my angel to keep you in this way*, and yet elsewhere it is said: *GOD went before the Israelites in a pillar of cloud by day and a shining fire all through the night, Psalm 78:15.* And elsewhere: *Wisdom was a covering for the Israelites by day and the light of the stars by night, Wisdom 10:17.* 

We see, therefore, that this same work is attributed to the Angel of Jehovah and to Wisdom, who in effect were the same; for it is said: *Do not provoke him (that is, the angel), for he will not bear your rebellion, because my name is in him, Exodus 23:20.* So also it is said that when lightning appears it is clear, and the spirits are diffused through every region: *and the clouds, when they are commanded by Jehovah to go through the whole world, perform what is commanded of them, Baruch 6:60.* Even the fire sent from above to consume mountains and forests does what is commanded of it; and elsewhere it is said: *The creature of fire, serving GOD who made all things, is sometimes intensified for punishment against the unjust, and sometimes relaxed for beneficence, Wisdom 16:28.* And elsewhere: *Whirlwind, cold, ice, frost, clouds, rain, and whatever lightning GOD commands these to do upon the surface of the orb on earth, whether for a scourge or for doing a benefit, they make it ready at hand: Job 38.* And yet elsewhere it is said *that GOD makes a weight for the wind (or the air), Job 28 & 38. That GOD makes sapphire clouds by wisdom, and overturns the bottles of heaven according to his will. He begets the drops of dew, and produces ice and hoarfrost; he gives snow like wool, scatters his ice like morsels, and binds the waters in thick clouds.* 

It is said elsewhere that he performs all these things by his Word, whose role it is to do the will of the Father. Hence it is said in the place cited above: the clouds scatter their light, which illumines all things round about wherever the will of the Governor drives them, for everything he had commanded them upon the face of the world, whether for a scourge or for showing mercy. And elsewhere: *When GOD shall distill the drops of water, which shall pour down rain for his calamity, Job 36.* And elsewhere: *The spirit or breath of the nostrils of Jehovah works wonders.* And elsewhere: *By the sneezings of GOD light shines, and indeed his eyes are like the eyelids of the morning; from his mouth proceed torches, as if his breath kindled coals and a flame came out of his mouth, Job 41:18.* And elsewhere: *Jehovah, descend, bow your heavens, and touch the mountains so they smoke; send out your lightning and scatter them, Psalm 144 v. 3.* And elsewhere: *Jehovah shall thunder from heaven, and the Most High shall give his voice; he sent his lightning and consumed them.* And elsewhere: *GOD makes the clouds his vehicle or his chariot, who walks upon the wings of the wind, who makes his angels winds and his ministers a burning fire, Psalm 104:3.* 

From these words it is most evidently clear that GOD is the leader and orderer; but in truth, he mostly works through his ministers in the nature of things and executes his will, both according to the laws of nature and extraordinarily and prodigiously—that is, beyond the custom of nature. He always acts primarily through his Word or Wisdom, which fulfills his commands and takes the place of the divine will, and secondarily through angels of many orders differing in dignity. Whence it happened that this Wisdom (which the sacred page calls the "first creature" <note>original: *primam creaturam*</note> *Ecclesiasticus 24:9* <note>The text cites Eccl. 9:1, but the "first created" Wisdom is usually associated with Ecclesiasticus/Sirach 24 or Proverbs 8.</note>)—that is, the first emanation or outgoing from the Father—was identified by the Kabbalists <note>Followers of Jewish mysticism (Kabbalah), which influenced many Renaissance Christian thinkers.</note> as that great Angel Metatron, in whom the name of Jehovah resides. The Platonists said this was the "Soul of the World" <note>original: *animam mundi*</note> informing all things, which St. John confirms in Chapter 1, saying: *by it (namely the Word) all things were made, and without it nothing; in it was life, etc.* 

The primary minister of this Word is the Archangel Michael, who has the protection of souls in his guardianship; he who waged war against the great angel of darkness with his followers, obtained the victory, and in a glorious manner is always said to stand before the face of Jehovah. At his command, therefore, all other angels offer obedience, and are said to receive life in no other way than the creatures of the world receive it from the Sun (over which this same angel presides). Hence, as was said before, the winds are called "sons of the Sun," by whose breath all other meteors in the world are procreated. Therefore, the actions of all... are subject to the command of Jehovah.

Therefore, it should not seem strange to any Christian that I have said that the winds (whose internal principles are angelic spirits) are the authors of every meteor, in whatever sublunary region it may be produced, and consequently of the comet itself along with its brothers. For we have demonstrated elsewhere, in the chapters on the winds, that winds are familiar to both the ethereal and sublunary regions (contrary to the vain assertions of the Peripatetics <note>Followers of Aristotle’s philosophy.</note>).

The matter of Comets, therefore, is a denser part of its own sphere—namely, the fiery sphere—coagulated into one by the opposing blasts of fiery demons, just as a cloud is forced together by the opposing reasons of the aquatic angelic spirits. If fiery demons interpose themselves in this action, they bring forth thunder and lightning together according to the will of the Creator. But truly, it is right for one versed in the secret mysteries of Philosophy to know that it is not possible for either clouds, thunder, or rain to proceed from the element of fire or the supreme region of the air. Hence it happens that, because of the fiery disposition of the place, instead of dark clouds, fiery meteors are sometimes, though rarely, found there. These are not as massive as the bulk of clouds, since the thinness of the region’s consistency cannot produce such a mass in its condensation. Furthermore, the winds are not violent in that region—indeed, they are scarcely sensible—since they find little or no resistance there due to the thinness and dryness of the region's consistency. And this must be considered above all: that fiery spirits always mix themselves with the substance of their own nature and illuminate it, in the manner of that royal spirit who placed his tabernacle in the sun. These bright spirits receive their splendor from that bright fountain reigning invisibly everywhere, and especially in its solar tabernacle, from which the bright force of life is not only flashed upon the stars and every other bright creature on all sides, but is also attributed to the angels themselves. It is their duty to accommodate the lights received from the fountain of light to their own proper spheres, from which they are afterwards imparted and rained upon the elements. These are the lights which the elementary demons receive and drink in, and according to the divine will, pour out into the elements either visibly or invisibly. These outpourings include light, motion, and those Aristotelian "influences." Having considered these things, we thus descend to a general description of comets and any fiery impressions:
