# On the Formal Cause of Meteors

...measure? Job 28:25. By these words, he seems to suggest that God sometimes creates winds out of the air by thinning it, and at other times creates waters and clouds by condensing it; He establishes the laws for the rain and a path for the lightning of the thunders, and even the dense bodies of fiery impressions. For in truth, the "meteors" <note>In this period, "meteor" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, including rain, wind, and lightning, not just falling stars.</note> of the upper region of the air are, as far as their physical bodies are concerned, nothing other than spiritual clouds. These do not dissolve into rain like the lower clouds, but finally vanish into the air like "spirit of wine" <note>Original: "spiritus vini," referring to highly distilled alcohol or ethanol.</note> that has been many times refined; though it is visible in its mass, once the glass is opened, it vanishes invisibly into the air and is gradually resolved.

In the same way, we see that the clouds in the higher part of the middle region, which are saffron-colored, never dissolve into rain, but are accustomed to return and be transformed into subtle and invisible air, from which they were originally derived; hence they are called dry and sterile clouds. In quite the same manner, the air in the highest region—placed and gathered there by the power of fiery demons <note>The author uses "demons" in the older sense of spiritual intermediaries or "daemons," rather than purely evil spirits.</note>—is sometimes reduced into such clouds, though they differ greatly from the others in clarity and purity. Job seems to confirm this very thing with these words: *Now men do not look at the light when it is bright in the higher clouds, which the passing wind has cleansed, Job 37:21.* From this, we also think it worthy of observation that the wind performs its office even in the upper regions of the air, contrary to the opinion of the Peripatetics <note>The "Peripatetics" were followers of Aristotle's philosophy, who generally believed the upper atmosphere was unchanging and lacked such weather patterns.</note>. From these facts, it is clear that the matter or consistency of the body of any fiery meteor is air, compressed in a certain dry way—that is, by the breaths of fiery spirits—to execute the divine will, and contracted into one visible mass according to the specific type of impression.

Secondly, we have expressed the **formal cause** of the same in a general way: namely, that it is a visible airy body, animated and inspired by a lucid and flashing spirit. This was clearly illustrated in the pillar of fire that went before the Israelites at night, and the star that guided the three Magi of the East and showed the place where the Savior of the world was born.

Thirdly, we have made the **efficient and informing cause** twofold: namely, the primary cause, which is Wisdom herself; and the secondary or assisting cause, the angelic ministers, whom we also call demons. Regarding the primary office in this work, we read these things in Holy Scripture: *GOD by his wisdom fits the weight for the winds (or the air) and weighs the waters by measure. He makes statutes for the rain and a path for the lightning of the thunders, Job 28.* From this it is clear that Wisdom is that greatest Angel under whose command are the fiery, airy, and watery angels alike, as she has the power to rule and dispose of the air, the waters, and the flashing fires. Furthermore, it is written: *Who has made the sapphire clouds of wisdom? Job 38:37.* And elsewhere: *the upper clouds by wisdom distill the dew, Proverbs 3.* And elsewhere: *GOD went before the Israelites in a pillar of cloud by day, and by a shining fire all through the night, Psalm 78:14.* Or as we find in the Book of Wisdom: *Wisdom was a covering for the Israelites by day and a starlight by night, Wisdom 10:17.*

Indeed, if I were to say that a fiery meteor is the "tabernacle of Wisdom," fortified by her fiery ministers—which either looks upon the sins of men with a threatening eye and pursues them with threats in her wrath, or gazes kindly in her mercy—you will perceive that this deviates very little from the sense of the Sacred Letters. For it is written: *Wisdom was a covering for the Israelites by day, and a starlight by night, Wisdom 10.* Here, therefore, she mercifully looked upon the Israelites from her tabernacle, which was the pillar of fire; this is one of the primary types of fiery impressions. So also from such a tabernacle—namely, the body of a comet—Wisdom shone forth and directed the Magi, or wise men of the East, with her light to the place where Christ the Savior of the world was born.

But it is also written that fire, coming out from the presence of Jehovah (or Wisdom, or the Angel in whom was the name of Jehovah), hidden in the pillar of cloud or fire, killed the sons of Aaron and they died, *Leviticus 10:2.* And elsewhere it is said: *The wrath of Jehovah was greatly kindled, and fire went out from Jehovah, and consumed those two hundred and fifty men who offered incense, etc., Numbers 16:35.* And from this, Jehovah is called in his wrath a *consuming fire: Deuteronomy 4:24.*

And so it is certain that GOD is accustomed not only to kill sinners visibly by fire sent from a fiery meteor, but also to wound and stir up a foul pestilence among men by its invisible dispersal through the mediation of His angelic instruments. By such a fiery scourge, seventy thousand men of the Israelites died invisibly, as the Angel of GOD struck and smote them, *2 Samuel 24:16.* Thus we also see that the substance of a comet, dissipated invisibly through the air, frequently produces plagues, famine, and drought upon the earth, as is declared by the effect.

But I would have you understand that there are undoubtedly very many comets and other fiery impressions in the air which are entirely invisible to men, both in their origin and their effect. These, beyond all controversy, are the causes of various epidemic diseases, as described more fully in the chapter *On Invisible Lucid Meteors*. We say, therefore, that GOD, through the mediation of His flaming angelic ministers (among whom we recognize Wisdom as the prince and primary), is the efficient cause not only of every fiery meteor, but also of watery ones and every other kind. And although the Peripatetics and many others ascribe such an office to the stars, the element of fire, and the coldness of the middle region of the air, it is the mark of a true Christian to attribute acts of this kind to the "Act of acts"—namely, to give to God what is from God, and by no means to arrogantly credit them to created things. From a lack of such consideration, a monstrous perversity of idolatry arose among the heathens, along with a neglect of the true worship of God. To this error must be attributed the fact that almost every barbarian nation set about fashioning and establishing a new God for themselves.

...he seems to declare in his speech: for the sun and the moon and the stars are indeed bright and sent for the benefit of mankind. Likewise, when lightning appears, it is clearly seen; and the spirit <note>In this context, "spirit" refers to the wind.</note> blows in every region, and the clouds, which are commanded by God to travel through the whole world, perform what has been commanded of them; fire also, sent from above to consume mountains and forests, does what has been prescribed for it. However, these things are not similar to any of those in their appearance or powers; wherefore it should neither be thought nor said that they are gods, since they can neither render judgment nor do anything for men. Knowing, therefore, that they are not gods, do not fear them. Thus he says. <note>The author is likely quoting from the "Letter of Jeremiah" found in the Apocrypha/Deuterocanon, which argues against idolatry by showing that natural forces obey God while idols do nothing.</note> By these words he seems to hint that every created thing is to be referred to the craftsmanship and dignity of the Creator alone, and not to the vain qualities of creatures, which proceed immediately from the divine act. But we shall discuss these things more abundantly in the part where we deal with the "efficient cause" <note>The "efficient cause" is the primary agent or force that brings something into being.</note>.

We now ascend to the particular descriptions of the fiery meteors of the highest order, which, as they are accustomed to vary in their form and figure, so they seem to claim for themselves various descriptions. And although the followers of Aristotle <note>The "Aristotelians" or Scholastic philosophers who followed the teachings of Aristotle.</note> have divided the Comet into two species—namely, the "hairy" and the "bearded"—we, in this matter, instructed by the learning of others well-experienced in the mysteries of philosophy, conclude that there are many more species of them. Each of these seems to claim a peculiar name for itself because of its different appearance when it shows itself. Specifically: 

*   They call one a **burning lance**, since it is stretched out in length and is quite thick in size.
*   Another they call **Xiphias**, which is a shorter lance, and at its tip turns more into a point <note>original: "mucronem," referring to the sharp point of a sword; Xiphias is Greek for "sword-shaped".</note>.
*   A third they call **Mercurial**, which is bluish, very small, and equipped with a tail.
*   A fourth they say is a **soldier**, for it is the color of Mars <note>Red or reddish-orange.</note>.
*   A fifth they name **Aurora** <note>The Dawn.</note>, as it exceeds the brightness of all the stars.
*   A sixth they call the **Rose**, and this bears an impressed human likeness.
*   A seventh is the **Tenaculum** <note>Tongs or Pincers.</note>, which stands as if erected upon a fiery base and is wondrously tailed, with its tail appearing to be carried upward.
*   An eighth they frequently call **Black**, being endowed with a dark color, a short tail, and very little "hair" <note>Referring to the luminous trail or coma.</note>.
*   A ninth is the **Ceratian**, which is called "horned" from the shape of its heat and appearance.

To these are also added three others, which are not as permanent as the rest: the first is called, because of its resemblance in appearance, a **Burning Beam**; the second **Flying Sparks**; and the last is called a **Chasma** <note>A Chasm or Gap.</note>; in which appearance the sky seems to open with a sudden light appearing beneath the clouds, so that a terrible abyss seems to be present. You will find the likenesses of all these meteors depicted and visually described in our "meteorological mirror," and in the places most suitable to their generation.

# CHAPTER XIII.
## Third Section.
### Concerning the fiery meteors of the middle region.

Among the fiery meteors of the middle region of the air, we make the primary ones flashes of light, lightning, and thunderbolts. The latter two rarely happen without a tremendous crashing sound (which is called **thunder**), so that thunder seems to be nothing other than an effect between a "luminous or fiery soul" acting strongly, and a dense, vaporous, and cloudy or watery spirit resisting perversely. But in truth, just as we see in man that some necessary organs are required to produce his voice and speech, so indeed Sacred Scripture testifies that the Creator of the world himself speaks to his creatures in many ways and through many means: namely, through thunders, through visions, through dreams, etc., about which we will speak more widely below. For first, we shall speak in a succinct discourse on what the Heathens <note>Referring to the Pagan Greek and Roman philosophers.</note> thought about the stupendous and profound origin of such meteors, so that we may afterwards transition to the sense of the Sacred Page with a better method.

And although in the preceding pages the luminous soul informing those meteors was discussed by us clearly enough, we will nevertheless in this place put forward a few things concerning the three species of flashes, which differ among themselves only by degrees of material thickness. Aristotle maintains that the general material cause of such luminous meteors is a hot and dry exhalation, raised from the earth into the middle region of the air by the power of the stars. There, partly by the strong collision and clashing of clouds among themselves, and partly through <term>antiperistasis</term> <note>The intensification of a quality (like heat) when it is surrounded by its opposite (like cold).</note>—namely, because of the intense cold of that place—he says that this matter, thus raised and compressed and enclosed in the "belly" of a cloud, is ignited, and because of its earthy and compact disposition, it tends downward. From this, thunder consequently makes that noise or roar, which arises from the extinction of such an ignited exhalation in the water of the cloud. This, I say, seems to be Aristotle's intention in the second book of his *Meteorology* and elsewhere, as well as that of his followers, both Pagan and Christian. And in truth, Aristotle seems in some way to be excused in a matter of such difficult resolution, since not only he, but also almost all other philosophers seem to have doubted and differed from one another (not being at all consistent with themselves) regarding the origin of lightning and thunder. For Empedocles thought that the thunderbolt and the flash were fire intercepted from the rays of the sun descending downward. But Anaxagoras thought that this fire was a portion of the <term>ether</term> <note>The "upper air" or the substance of the heavens.</note> falling from on high into the concavity of a cloud, in which it is struck; and he says the brightness of this light leaping out from the cloud is called a flash, or lightning, or a thunderbolt, which through the effect of its piercing makes the thunder.

<meta>This page continues the investigation into the causes of "fiery meteors," specifically lightning. ### On the Formal Cause of Meteors.

Others maintain that lightning proceeds from hot and dry winds within clouds that are tightly compressed and hemmed in; they say these winds scorch and ignite the clouds, from which a rumbling arises. There are even some who refuse to believe lightning is generated by fire at all, but rather through the "imagination" <note>In this context, an optical illusion or reflection.</note> of shimmering water, which is seen at night in the clouds through the brightness of the stars. But Aristotle seems to rightfully refute this opinion, because lightning is seen during the day under the rays of the sun. Finally, the operation of nature in this regard is so marvelous that some, plunging themselves more deeply into the mysteries of God and nature and diligently considering the admirable power and operation of the flash, have judged it to be not a work of nature, but the highest immediate effect of God—a group among whom every true Christian ought to be numbered. But we shall first hasten to the examination of that Aristotelian definition.

He [Aristotle] says that its material cause <note>The "material cause" refers to the substance out of which something is made.</note> is drawn from the earth, and he makes the "acting cause" in its elevation an Astral power. However, he identifies the "efficient cause" <note>The primary agent that produces an effect.</note> that ignites it as the external and accidental collision and shaking of the clouds, occurring simultaneously with the cold of that region acting through <term>antiperistasin</term> <note>original: "antiperistasin"; a Greek philosophical term referring to the intensification of a quality when surrounded by its opposite, such as heat becoming more intense when compressed by surrounding cold.</note> in its illumination. Finally, he accounts for its downward motion by explaining that a portion of its matter is terrestrial, and consequently heavy and compact.

But as for its material cause and the seat of its "matrix" <note>The "womb" or place of origin where a natural phenomenon is formed.</note> from which the lightning is produced, we are taught by the Holy Bible that these are far different than what that man Aristotle supposed. In the book of Ecclesiasticus it is found written: *Look upon the rainbow, and bless him that made it; very beautiful it is in the brightness thereof. It encompasseth the heaven about with a circle of glory, the hands of the Most High have displayed it. By his commandment he maketh the snow to fall apace, and sendeth forth swiftly the lightnings of his judgment. Through this the treasures are opened, and the clouds fly forth as birds. By his great power he maketh the clouds firm, and the hailstones are broken small. At his sight the mountains are shaken, and at his will the south wind bloweth. The noise of his thunder maketh the earth to tremble, so doth the northern storm and the whirlwind... Ecclesiasticus 43.* <note>The author is quoting from the Latin Vulgate version of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 43:11–17.</note> From these words of the wise man, we gather not only the material cause of thunder and lightning, but indeed of almost all other meteors—the bright as well as the dark—and even the formal, efficient, and final causes. Likewise, the "hidden matrix" from which the matter of all these things arises is explained there. For as far as the matter of meteors is concerned, he seems to indicate it primarily there, as well as the matrix, where he says: *the treasures are opened, and the clouds fly forth etc.* From this it is clear that the "treasury of Jehovah" is the matrix of all meteors, and indeed the matrix of matter itself. Hence it is said elsewhere: *Jehovah shall open unto thee his good treasure, the heaven, to give the rain unto thy land, Deuteronomy 28:12.* And elsewhere: *He bringeth the wind out of his treasures, Psalm 135.* From which it is clear that by "the heavens" he understands the open air in which the clouds are suspended; whence it is also found said elsewhere: *God makes a weight for the winds, and he weigheth the waters by measure, when he made a decree for the rain, and a way for the lightning of the thunders, Job 28:25.* From these things it is evident that just as air is contained in air (no differently than the contents within a container), so indeed the air becomes the matrix and sanctuary—or treasury chest—of meteors procreated from air in various forms.

Hence, in a further passage, he seems to acknowledge that each of these is a "gathering of the spirit," that is, of air. Their formal cause is also elicited from the aforementioned description—namely, the Iris or heavenly rainbow—where it is said: *Look upon the rainbow, and bless him that made it: very beautiful it is in the brightness thereof, it encompasseth the heaven about with a circle of glory.* Furthermore: *the snows, lightnings, mists, clouds, hailstones, winds or the breathing South wind, the thundering voice with its motion, the Northern storm etc.* do not lack their own formal differences (by which one is usually distinguished from another) in their very naming. The "Efficient" is also indicated therein, where it is said: *the hands of the Most High have opened it*, and elsewhere, *Bless him that made it*, and, *it encompasseth the heaven about with a circle of glory.* And: *by his commandment he hastened the snow, and he hasteneth to send forth the lightnings of his judgment, and therefore the treasures were opened*, and, *in his greatness he placed the clouds, and by his will the South wind blew, Psalm 135:7.* <note>The author blends several scriptural citations here to emphasize divine agency over nature.</note> and so in the rest, and elsewhere: *Jehovah maketh lightnings with the rain.* Finally, the "final intention" or purpose of the generation of these meteors is that they may fulfill His will; hence it is said there: *In his will the South wind blew*, and elsewhere you will find it written: *that the whirlwind, cold, ice, clouds, rain, lightnings etc. whatsoever God commanded them to do upon the face of the world in the earth, whether for a rod, or for terror, or to perform mercy, he causeth it to be ready, Job 38.* <note>Referencing Job 37 and 38.</note> And in the prophet Baruch it is found: *The clouds, commanded to go through the whole world, obey and perform the command itself; when the lightning appears, it is seen clearly, and the wind itself blows through every region; and when the clouds are commanded by God to go through the whole habitable world, they perform what is commanded; and the fire sent from above to consume mountains and forests does what is commanded, Baruch 6.* <note>A reference to the Letter of Jeremiah, often included as Baruch Chapter 6.</note> From these things, therefore, it will be permitted to express the description of lightning in this manner:

-> Lightning is a certain fiery air, which is brought forth from the treasury chest of God (or the heavens) by divine power, and is sent out to perform the will of the Creator here on earth, whether benevolently or malevolently. <-

# On the Formal Cause of Meteors.

...before his brightness the clouds passed away, and the Lord thundered from heaven, etc. Psalm 17. <note>Psalm 17 in the Vulgate is Psalm 18 in modern Bibles.</note> Finally, the purpose of thunder and lightning is declared there: namely, that it exists as much for judging the people as for providing food in abundance.

->Or thus:<-

Thunder is the voice of the Most High, mixed with flame and lightning, issued and ordained by God to disturb the wicked. In this form, the **formal cause** <note>The "formal cause" refers to the essential nature or "shape" of the phenomenon—here, the sound and light.</note> is the crash or voice with lightning; the **efficient cause** <note>The "efficient cause" is the agent that brings something into being.</note> is Jehovah Himself; and the **final cause** <note>The "final cause" is the ultimate purpose or goal.</note> is to serve as a scourge for the wicked.

This is confirmed by the preceding passage: *The Lord thundered (says the royal Psalmist) from heaven; the Most High gave His voice, with hail and coals of fire; and He sent out His arrows and scattered them; He multiplied lightnings and troubled them. Psalm 17.*

->Or thus:<-

Thunder is the voice or sound proceeding from the throne of God, sent forth by the Divine Will from the hollow of a cloud into the open air to execute His purpose—whether for evil or for good—both in the heavens and on the earth.

In this case, the formal cause is the voice or sound; the efficient cause is the lightning of God; and the final cause is either for a blessing or a curse.

It is confirmed thus: In the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation.</note> it is written, *From the throne proceed lightnings... Revelation 4:5.* And elsewhere: *Will you send out lightnings, and will they go, and returning say, "Here we are"? His lightnings shone forth to the world, etc. Psalm 97:2-4.* And elsewhere: *The clouds gave a voice; for indeed your arrows passed through, etc. Psalm 76:17.* Where by "arrows," he seems to mean lightnings in this context. Hence it is also written elsewhere: *The shafts of lightnings shall go directly, and as if from the well-curved bow of the clouds, Wisdom 5:21.* By this, he seems to hint that the clouds "gave a voice" because the lightnings passed through and penetrated them.

->Or thus:<-

Thunder is the voice of God in an elevated cloud, surrounded and covered on all sides by the force of waters, before which fire goes forth and ignites everything around it.

Hence Job says: *Will you lift up your voice in a cloud, and will the force of waters cover you? Job 38:34.* And elsewhere: *Clouds and darkness are round about Him; fire shall go before Him and shall inflame His enemies round about. Psalm 97:2.*

->Or thus:<-

Thunder is the voice of God, at which He provides a multitude of waters in the heaven, and creates lightnings and rain. Hence it is written: *At His voice He gives a multitude of waters in the heaven, and He lifts up the mists from the ends of the earth; He makes lightnings into rain, and brings forth the wind out of His treasures. Jeremiah 10:13.*

->Or thus:<-

Thunder is the sound of a multitude of waters, or the voice of the clouds, brought about by God's flashes of light shining upon the whole world.

->Or thus:<-

Thunder is the sound of a multitude of waters, fearing and disturbed at the sight of Jehovah, or a voice or crash echoing around which the clouds are accustomed to give. This voice is issued or produced immediately by the flashes of light proceeding from the throne of God and breaking out from the clouds (which are the tent of Jehovah), in order to execute the Divine Will.

In this description, the **material organ** of such a voice is the waters—as if they were fearing and disturbed—wherefore they are accustomed to give out a voice, sound, or crash because of the penetrating power which the bright and shining sight of God, the worker of wonders, produces. Hence it is said: *Before the brightness in His sight the clouds passed away, hail and coals of fire; the Lord thundered from heaven, and the Most High gave His voice. Psalm 17.* And elsewhere: *The waters saw you, O God, and they feared; and the depths were troubled. A multitude of the sound of waters; the clouds gave a voice; the voice of your thunder was in a wheel. <note>original: "in rota." This likely refers to the rolling sound of thunder or a whirlwind.</note> Psalm 76:17.*

The **formal cause** is also described in this: that it happens with a crash and with flashes of light.
The **efficient cause** appears to be the lightnings, or rather the fiery sight of God animating the lightnings themselves and directing them toward the goal ordained by God. Thus, lightnings are like the instruments of God in His wrath, just as a sword is the instrument of a man who strikes; we say such a man struck with a sword, and not the sword itself. Therefore, we say God Himself is the only actor in these matters, the father of the thunders themselves, who sends out lightnings like His arrows from His throne, according to that passage in the Apocalypse.
The **final cause**, moreover, we have established to be the fulfilling of the Divine Will.

->Or finally, in this manner:<-

Thunder is the voice, or speech, or eloquence, or sound proceeding from the mouth of Jehovah, which is directed under the whole heaven with light over the borders or edges of the earth, after which a sound roars, or God thunders with the voice of His excellence; and it cannot be tracked when His voice is heard, He who thunders wonderfully with His voice.

We have this confirmed by the words of the Holy Scriptures: *Hear with trembling the voice or speech, or (as another interprets it) the eloquence proceeding from His mouth; He directs that eloquence and light under the whole heaven...*

### Section I. Portion IV. Part II. Book III. Member II.

...light over the ends or borders of the earth. After him a sound roars; he thunders with the voice of his majesty, and it is not tracked down when his voice has been heard. God, thundering with his voice, does wondrous things, etc. Job 37.

Therefore, against the foolish opinions of the Pagans <note>original: "Ethnicorum" — referring here to non-Christian classical philosophers like Aristotle or Seneca</note>, it is demonstrated that neither exhalations nor vapors, nor the sun with the stars, nor the earth or water, nor the elements, nor even created nature itself, but God Himself—who is the worker of all wonders—is the immediate **efficient cause** <note>The "efficient cause" is the primary agent or force that produces an effect.</note> of these marvels. We have this confirmed by Holy Scripture, lest we, like the Pagans, falsely attribute these things to nature, its elements, or things made of elements, which are to be attributed first and before all else to the Creator; for in doing so, we might unexpectedly cast ourselves into foul idolatry along with them.

But it may be objected by some that these types of thunder of which the Holy Scriptures speak were miraculous and not at all natural. Both modern and ancient philosophers fall into this way of thinking: namely, that thunders are sometimes "natural" and sometimes "supernatural." They act as if the things performed in the moisture of the world's nature do not happen as immediately from God as those things which occur according to the season of the year or the hot weather of the air, or those which happen in winter or for other hidden reasons. Yet it cannot be unknown to a true Christian that God is everywhere, and has His dwelling both in the elements themselves and in the things composed of them. For in the highest heaven He is clothed with light as with a garment; in the midst of heaven He placed His tabernacle in the Sun; in the lowest region He made the thick cloud His tent. Indeed, as Job testifies: Jehovah answered him out of the whirlwind. Furthermore, He is also in the earth, for "the earth shall bring forth a Savior." He speaks in the Prophet and through the mouth of the Prophet; indeed, God uses every part of this world as His instrument <note>original: "organo"</note>, and speaks in various ways according to the variety of the instrument. In the simple spirit of the world, His voice is neither heard nor understood except by those who are enlightened or stirred by the spirit; He speaks in the angels and through the mediation of angelic instruments, but most often He speaks to mortals terribly in His wrath—that is, in thunder. Whence Job says: *Listen with trembling to the voice going out from His mouth under the whole heaven, and the light over the borders of the earth. Job 37.*

Therefore, those philosophers are quite unsound of mind who distinguish thunders into "vain and brute"—meaning those which seem to signify nothing—and "prophetic and significant." It is as if thunders ought to be called vain, brute, and signifying nothing simply because the intention of God (who produced nothing in the world in vain) was not revealed to those philosophers during their creation. O, how hidden are the mysteries of God, and how concealed from the knowledge of profane men! Nor indeed can I praise the skill of Cicero in this matter, who in his book *On Divination* <note>original: "De Divinatione"</note> seems to deny—quite thoughtlessly—that any kind of divination can arise from the observations of lightning; he makes such study vain and empty. And yet we are taught the opposite by the Holy Bible, where it is found written: *That the great God, surpassing our knowledge, spreads out the clouds like His tent at His pleasure, and lightens with His light from above; He covers also the depths of the sea, for by these He judges the people, and gives food to many mortals. In His hands He hides the light, and commands it to come again, etc. Job 36.* From these things it is right to gather that God sends lightning to execute justice upon mortals, and also turns lightning into rain for the benefit of mortals. Whence it is said elsewhere: *When He utters His voice, there is a multitude of waters in the heavens; He causes the clouds to ascend from the ends of the earth; He makes lightnings for the rain, and brings forth the winds out of His treasures. Jeremiah 51:15.*

From this it is clear that there is no thunder except that which is the voice of Jehovah. Hence the Royal Psalmist speaks generally of thunder in these words: *The voice of Jehovah is upon the waters; the voice of the glorious, strong God thunders; the voice of Jehovah is upon many waters; the voice of Jehovah is powerful and in His majesty; the voice of Jehovah is full of beauty; the voice of Jehovah breaks the cedars, even the cedars of Lebanon; and He makes Lebanon and Sirion skip like a calf; the voice of Jehovah divides the flames of fire; the voice of Jehovah shakes the desert; the voice of Jehovah makes the deer give birth and strips the forests bare; truly, in His temple everyone speaks of His glory, etc. Psalm 29.* Here the King mentions both the terrible voice of Jehovah and the peaceful one.

We conclude, therefore, that it is the greatest folly of any Christian—indeed, an irrecoverable madness—to place such great faith in the vain and lying opinions of the Pagans, who toss about empty words concerning thunder. These men try to persuade people that thunders and lightnings are merely incidental things, born from a natural imbalance <note>original: "intemperie"</note> of the heavens and not sent by God at all. Thus, looking only at the effect, they delight in falsely taking it for the efficient cause. That is, they wish to attribute to the creatures what belongs to God, the Creator of every thing. In this way, they continue not only to chatter thoughtlessly but to blaspheme impiously, leading men to idolatry, just as if someone were to attribute the life of a man to his body rather than to his soul. Therefore, I want you to know that I have not written in this place recklessly, but diligently and supported by good foundations; other philosophers who have peered deeper into the hidden mystery of Jehovah seem to agree with me. For considering the wonderful operation of the lightning-bolt, they judged it not a work of nature, but an immediate effect of the Most High God.

### On the Formal Cause of Meteorological Phenomena.

...you might think [these things] are produced by a harsh imbalance of the air. I would wish that you listen to this warning of ours, and not reject it as futile or hold it as nothing, if we prove that lightning and thunder proceed directly from God; for in such a duty of mine, I shall provide not only solace to you in your tribulation, but also give glory and honor to God my creator.

Know therefore that the "wise" of this world—those followers of the Pagan philosophers <note>original: "philosophorum Ethnicorum asseclæ" — specifically referring to the followers of Aristotle and other non-Christian Greeks</note>—rave, have raved, and in their obstinacy will continue to rave. Indeed, they do not concede that God works all things in all, and that His Word moves, stirs, and preserves all things. Instead, they ascribe it to "created nature," pretending that God acts out of necessity through intermediaries—namely, through secondary and tertiary causes. Thus erring, they are further unwilling to understand that God operates solely through His Word, and not through other necessary means; and thus He works by no means through those causes alleged by them, but only within them as if they were instruments.

But you, who are nourished on the Holy Bible and governed by the law of Christ, I persuade you to conceive of this—and to turn it over within yourselves forever—that God created the first substance, namely water, as something damp or moist through His Word. And this very substance remains moist even today, after the lapse of so many thousands of years. Again, from this water, the heaven and the earth (as Saint Peter witnesses) were created by means of the Word. Furthermore, in the heavens He produced the light, the sun, the moon, and the stars, the day and the night, and all other created things by the utterance of His Word, and He imposed upon them their services. Therefore, all those things perform their duties according to that Word. Where, then, is the "nature" of the Peripatetics <note>The Peripatetics were the followers of Aristotle, known for explaining the world through physical laws rather than direct divine action.</note> which is supposed to carry these things out? There is clearly nothing anywhere except the one and only Word of God, which works these and all other things, according to that saying of the Evangelist:
> *All things were made by the Word, and without Him was nothing made; in Him was life, etc. John 1.*

From this it is clear that without Him, nothing can exist or act. Insofar as the air is a part of the heavenly substance, it follows that it was made by the Word and "swims" (as it were) in the Word, as the Word embraces all things and is moved and governed by the Word of God itself. Nay, even within the Word—as if in the treasury chest of God, and that a universal one—it has its own particular chests, from which various species of meteorological phenomena are produced. These He has placed under the protection and governance of various angels and spirits (who were also created from the air and in the air through the Word), as it is right to gather from various passages of Holy Scripture to be cited by us below. By their administration (as the Word moves and works), all meteorological phenomena are produced in the air, and all storms wonderfully arise which are accustomed to happen to the world. Hence it is said, that He made His angels winds, and His ministers a flaming fire, etc. Therefore, at the beginning of the world, God created the angels together with the air, who perform and execute their task and office in the air regarding the direction of storms, rain, snow, hail, frost, clouds, lightning, thunder, fire, chasms <note>original: "chasmatum" — likely referring to celestial phenomena like auroras or "gaps" in the clouds</note>, thunderbolts, waters, heat, cold, moisture, dryness, and many other things of that kind. And this very thing is done today by His Word; all of which will be clearly declared by us in our following Portion, where we shall deal with the **efficient cause** of meteorological phenomena.

This is indeed unknown to the Pagan philosophers and their Christian followers, for in their mouths and writings a lying and false spirit has claimed a seat for itself. From this, their ignorance and the vanity of their philosophy has arisen. Nor is it a wonder, since they have known neither God nor His most holy Word; indeed, scorning the Holy Scripture or reading it very little, but dwelling only on their own ravings, they are accustomed to sew lie upon lie. If those Christian disciples of the Pagan Peripatetics had read the Holy Bible with the same zeal with which they turned over the false Aristotelian books and volumes, they would have found the truth about the air and storms: that it is not at all the way they wrote in their books filled with imaginations. Rather, they would see that God has His own particular treasure-houses in the open air for these species already mentioned, from which He produces winds and storms; and that the air swims and consists in the Word of God, and is led by the angels appointed for this, as the Word of God directs, when, where, and how God wills. Whence David said:
> *The angels of God, most mighty in strength, doing His word, listening to the voice of His word, ministers doing His pleasure. Psalm 103.*

We also read of the prince having power over the air <note>A reference to Ephesians 2:2, usually interpreted as the devil, but here used to discuss the spiritual hierarchy of the atmosphere.</note>. And although this very thing proposed by us in this discourse might seem trivial to some, it is nevertheless arduous and of the greatest importance, insofar as it also concerns the divine honor. It is vital that the children of God know and understand truly and fundamentally that the reason for storms and other operations relating to them happen not by their own motion, nor by chance, nor even in such an imaginary way as the Pagans posit and feign in their writings. Instead, they proceed and arise from Divine Providence and from the chests of the divine treasuries, and are sent down from above into this lower world. Thus, if ever dangerous storms arise, people may call upon God, that He might wish to mercifully turn away that danger of the storm, and in its place grant a benign rain, and at once defend, protect, and preserve the fruits of the earth together with men and cattle from all evil; and furthermore, to consider all things whatsoever that can yield to the honor of God.

I would have you consider how immense is the difference between the books of the Pagan philosophers and the fountain of all truth, and that by adhering to their testimonies, it is necessary that you depart from the fountain of all truth. For there is in truth no truth, except in God alone; for
> *God Himself is the only truth, and he who remains in truth remains in God and God remains in him, and thus he will be made like a divine being in God, and*

Finally, how the angels are merely ministers and, as it were, the organs of God in such wonderful operations—no differently than a flute is the instrument of music through which a musician produces his melodies (that is, he acts harmoniously by his breath)—and how God alone is the mover in these things to execute His will in this lower world, will be clearly explained (God willing) in the portion of this treatise where we deal with the efficient cause of meteors.

### CHAPTER XIII.

#### Part Four.

->*On the ignited meteors of the lower aerial region of a certain consistency: namely*<-
->*the evening redness of the sky, the "Assub" <note>original: "Assub" — an Arabic-derived term used in medieval and Renaissance science to describe shooting stars or meteors</note> that quickly appear*<-
->*and disappear, falling stars, the Will-o'-the-Wisp <note>original: "Igne fatuo"</note>,*<-
->*or the fire that licks the hair, and*<-
->*Castor and Pollux <note>A phenomenon now known as St. Elmo's Fire, often seen on the masts of ships</note>.*<-

The Prince of the Peripatetics <note>Aristotle</note> and others who follow his doctrine count the appearing and disappearing *Assub* among those eleven ignited "impressions" <note>A technical term in older physics for atmospheric phenomena</note> which they are accustomed to mention. To their number we may also, not unwisely, add the evening redness, as there is no great difference between it and the appearing and disappearing *Assub*. These men maintain that the appearing and disappearing *Assub* is produced from a thin exhalation hidden in the clouds, a part of which sometimes appears and sometimes vanishes. But we, in truth, say that such suddenly appearing and disappearing luminous impressions proceed from more hidden causes: namely, from the secret will of God and the hidden operations of His Word and His angelic ministers. It is their task to present and fulfill divine commands through such visible instruments, whether for blessing or for bane, upon the lands and the waters. From this we also draw from the Holy Scriptures that 
> the clouds scatter their light, which surveys all things in a circuit wherever the will of the Governor drives them, to do everything He has commanded them over the face of the orb of the earth, whether as a scourge, or for performing kindness and mercy. (Job 37:11-13)
Here he seems to understand not only lightning, but every luminous meteor produced around the clouds, which the Creator is accustomed to produce in His wisdom in a wonderful and sometimes prodigious manner. Hence David speaks thus: 
> How magnificent and ample are the works of God; You have made them all in wisdom. (Psalm 104:24) 
And elsewhere: 
> Remember the wonders He has performed, His miracles and His judgments. (Psalm 105:5) 
By His wisdom, I say, or by His Word, all these things are produced in a wonderful manner; it is His role 
> to bind the waters in His thick clouds, so that the cloud is not rent under them. (Job 26:8) 
For God by His wisdom not only adjusts the weight of the air, and weighs out the waters by measure, and makes decrees for the rain, but also prepares a path for the lightning of the thunder and indeed for every luminous meteor.

The same must also be thought regarding the evening redness, in which, nevertheless, the nature of the "animating light" and the "animated body" differ in consistency. For in the evening redness it is denoted that nitrous spirits <note>In 17th-century chemistry, "nitrous spirits" were thought to be volatile, life-giving or explosive components of the air</note> dispersed everywhere in the air—which were rendered invisible due to expansion or hiding—now appear in the open air through condensation. These spirits are observed to appear in the heavens along with the warm breath of the winds. We also see this in the chemical extraction of the spirit of salt nitre <note>Nitric acid</note>, where such a redness appears in the receiving vessel. This appearance is caused by a compelling fiery breath; and from this it happens that, unless the artist watches cautiously, the receiver may be shattered into infinite pieces (at great danger to the artist) due to the violence of the winds enclosed within it, which we have occasionally perceived. We have also frequently observed that after such appearances in the sky, more robust winds are produced in the air. But the operator of such an operation is a God-like wisdom.

Falling stars in the upper part of this aerial region come from a small portion of that same light, but of a denser substance, from which comets and other ignited impressions of the higher regions arise. These have hidden operations within themselves (however much they may be disparaged by men) and produce slow and almost imperceptible effects, according to the will of Him who is accustomed to create nothing in vain.

Furthermore, the Will-o'-the-Wisp, which is accustomed to lick the hair of animals, as well as Castor and Pollux, are secret lights produced in thicker air, governed by the local spirits <note>original: "daemonibus" — here meaning guiding spirits or intelligences of a specific place, not necessarily evil demons</note>, and ordained to fulfill the pleasure of the Creator. Indeed, none of these things have been produced in the world idly or pointlessly by this most wise and eternal Nature, which inhabits and fills every place. It would be an infinite and perhaps tedious discourse to explain all these things at greater length; therefore, since it shall suffice to have spoken a word concerning their formal cause, I shall conclude this chapter in a few words.

# CHAPTER XIV.
## Section One.
### On meteors of both a thinner and a thicker terrestrial consistency.

There are certain bright, manifest, and visible meteors of the macrocosm <note>The "Great World" or the universe as a whole, reflecting the "microcosm" of the human body.</note> whose consistency is more corporeal, claiming for themselves a terrestrial disposition; in their nature, they tend toward melancholy and <term>adust bile</term> <note>original: "bilem adustam" — in ancient medicine, this refers to "scorched" or overheated humors, associated with dark, dry, and earthy qualities</note>. Some of these are of a thinner constitution, having the form of a thicker smoke, by which earth, sand, and stones are tinted into various appearances—namely yellow, black, red, white, and so on—and these smokes are accustomed to rising from the winds and the "vessels" of the earth. There is also another species of such meteors that is even more corporeal, thick, and gummy, being either sulfurous or bituminous, etc. We shall say a few words regarding what philosophers—both the ancient Pagans and their Christian followers—think about the generation of these terrestrial meteors, so that we may later compare their opinion with the fountain of all truth.

As for the **sulfurous meteor**, they considered it to be a certain metallic matter, cooked and bound together by the heat of the sun and the heavens from an unctuous and subtle earthy and fiery substance.

As for **bitumen**, they maintain it is born in the earth from putrefied, oily humors.

We, however, say that bituminous substances are nothing other than the effects of sulfur, just as ashes are the effects of ignited coals, as we shall discuss more extensively in a further demonstration below; but let us return to the point.

In their description of the sulfurous meteor, we see that they made its "material cause" a certain oily and subtle earth and a fiery substance, in which specific part they also expressed the "formal cause." They posited the "efficient and ripening cause" to be the solar and celestial heat.

But indeed, we have said elsewhere that the internal spirit—not only of the "external man" but also of the visible earth and every thing constituted by it—comes from the universal air of the world. It is from this air that all things were procreated from the beginning in respect to their consistency. We say that the parts of the universal air of the world are linked to one another in such a connection and continuity—whether they are enclosed in the earth, in man, or in any other thing—that it is necessary for a single part of that same whole to be felt by the whole, and for a disturbance in one part to be felt by another. From this it is clear that the sulfurous disposition of the mundane air <note>The spirit or life-force of the atmosphere.</note> is also the cause of that sulfurous nature in both the earth and in man. Therefore, a metallic nature of this kind undoubtedly proceeded originally from the mundane air, and this by divine ordinance and will, through the execution of the influences or <term>daemons</term> <note>original: "dæmonum" — in this context, mediating spirits or angelic agencies that govern the physical world, rather than "demons" in the modern sense</note> presiding over the celestial bodies, who are governed by the Word, in which their life resides.

Finally, we are taught that sulfur is produced in a marvelous way from the "chest of the air" by the wisdom of GOD according to His pleasure—created as if from nothing and then poured out and emitted into the earth as if from the treasury of the heavens—in that GOD sent down sulfur and fire from heaven upon Sodom and Gomorrah, and overthrew the cities with all their inhabitants, and everything that thrived in them (*Gen. 19*).

From this same treasury, GOD is accustomed to bringing forth His lightnings and thunders, and very often emits His fire from heaven, just as we read happened in the times of Moses and Elijah. However, concerning the occult and mystical reason for procreating such meteors, we shall speak more extensively (GOD willing) in our treatise on the "Efficient Cause of Meteors." As for the procreation of bitumen, it is most certain and proven by experience that it is generated by the mixing of earth with burnt sulfur, or rather by the embrace of the viscosity of the one with the other. This can be seen to this day from the result at the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah; for the lake there, called the **Dead Sea**, is said to abound with this kind of gummy species, which is carried to distant places to be used in place of mortar for buildings, and is not infrequently used among physicians.

# Correlative to the Microcosm.

<image-desc>A complex branching tree diagram (logical chart) that categorizes the "Luminous Meteors of the Microcosm." The diagram uses a hierarchical structure to link atmospheric phenomena to human physiological and pathological states.</image-desc>

Luminous Meteors of the Microcosm are either:

*   **Manifest or perceptible**, to whose composition two things concur, namely either:
    *   **The fiery or choleric spirit**, animating and illuminating the aerial humors of the Microcosm, and this is either:
        *   **Flashing, Coruscating, Lightening, or Thundering**,
            *   From which various forms of hot <term>intemperatures</term> <note>Disturbances of the bodily humors</note> and different types of filth in inflammations and diverse fevers appear.
        *   **Of the Superior region**, namely the "body" of this region or order consists of:
            *   **Comets, Pillars, Straw-like flashes**, and other fiery portents
            *   Which were first dispersed into the aerial Great World <note>Macrocosm</note>, and then afterwards drawn into the aerial Microcosm through inhalation and spread through nourishment; their consistency is very subtle.
        *   **Of the Middle region**, namely that of:
            *   **Thunders, chasms**, and other things of that kind.
            *   And this portion is of a moderate consistency.
    *   **The animated aerial body of the Microcosm**, or that portion of the condensed air of the Microcosm illuminated by the "seeds" of the scattered meteors of the Great World; it is of the order of:
        *   **The Face:**
            *   Long-lasting redness, compared to the redness of evening.
            *   Red color that appears and disappears quickly, as seen in those feeling shame or anger, and in other light "irradiations" that appear and vanish in the manner of light flashes <note>original: "coruscationum"</note>.
        *   **The Aerial region**, such as:
            *   Internal fumes, or those created in the internal aerial spirit of the Microcosm, such as the fantasies that tend to appear as fiery ghosts even when the eyes are closed (both in the healthy and the sick). Such dreams or fiery visions also seem to appear during sleep.
        *   **The Inferior and more dense region**, and these are of a consistency that is either:
            *   **Terrestrial**, tending toward a "scorched" <note>adust</note> disposition, and are of a consistency that is:
                *   **Of a Thicker nature:**
                    *   Either **Sulfurous**, such as all thick inflammations, and likewise leprosy, dry scabies <note>An itchy skin disease</note>, etc.
                    *   Or **Bituminous**, such as all <term>gummata</term> <note>Soft, tumor-like growths</note> or excretions arising from the flesh.
                *   **Of a Thinner consistency**, which is either:
                    *   **A Humor**, which is yellow or "scorched" bile <note>original: "bilis flaua seu adusta"</note>.
                    *   **A Smoke**, from which comes yellow jaundice <note>original: "icteritia flaua"</note> and yellow <term>morphew</term> <note>A skin condition causing discolored patches</note>.
*   **Hidden.** See Book L.

Just as in the Great World <note>Macrocosm</note> there is a difference between a spirit that is flashing, coruscating, lightening, and thundering—which is usually a matter of degree, of "more or less"—so that they seem to be like steps of luminous splendor sent forth from the clouds by a divine mystery; so indeed are there such degrees of fiery spirit in the aerial medium of man himself. By means of these spirits, febrile diseases of various kinds present themselves in action, and are visibly perceived in the serum of the blood or in the urine. Among these, a "daily fever" <note>original: "febris diaria"</note> can be rightly compared to a quick flash of light <note>coruscation</note>, and every "intemperature" that is barely perceptible can be compared to a flashing spirit, or otherwise as is related below.

-># On the Formal Cause of Meteors.<-

Those fiery meteors of a higher nature—that is, those belonging to a more eminent place, such as the various types of comets—occupy a more sublime position in the aerial middle of man, namely within the spirits of life <note>In the medical philosophy of the time, "spirits" were subtle substances that carried life force through the body</note>. Thus it happens that they not only lethally affect the "seeds" of such meteors dispersed in the macrocosmic air <note>the atmosphere of the world</note> and inhaled by the human spirit, but because of the sublimity of their location, they even penetrate the essence of life itself. From this arise plagues, pestilential fevers, and all contagious diseases. Hence, experience also teaches us that the appearance of a comet usually indicates decay and a morbid disposition not only for humans but also for plants and fruits; for this reason, prognostications of plague and famine are commonly made. Furthermore, we see that the minimum duration for a comet's appearance is seven days, which is the same amount of time in which pestilential diseases—especially the plague and pestilential fevers—usually reach their end; for the "crisis" <note>the turning point of an illness</note> of a very acute disease is measured by a continuation of this kind.

In the human air, therefore, three distinct regions are perceived: a place compared to the highest region of the air, where similar contents are produced; a place likened to the middle region with its own corresponding meteors; and the lowest place assigned to thick spirits and humors. The solid body of man corresponds to the Earth. Just as the Earth is subject to many accidents—namely sulfurous flames, hot waters, and other such things—so too do gums similar to amber <note>likely referring to resinous bodily secretions</note>, sulfurous inflammations, and other similar conditions occur in the human body.

# CHAPTER XIV.

## Third Part.

### On the luminous meteors of the macrocosm formed from the air.

We shall explain in the following sections how the South Wind <note>original: "Auster"</note>, together with its neighboring winds, makes the air thick and dense, corrupting it and rendering it putrid. This rarely occurs without clouds; nevertheless, even without the manifest appearance of clouds, it makes the air so dense—though not perfectly obvious to the senses—that for this reason it causes objects to appear smaller to the eye than they truly are. These winds produce meteors that are sometimes hidden and sometimes visible and manifest. These, in turn, are rendered useless by the dissolution caused by the blast of the opposing wind, whose role is to annihilate and scatter the Southern influences. From this, their malignant seeds <term>seminaria: hidden "seeds" or origins of disease, a concept predating modern germ theory</term>, invisibly dispersed in the air, partly enter the fruits and food of men, and are partly drawn from the air through the windpipe <note>original: "asperam arteriam"</note> to the heart. This easily infects the human spirit—specifically the "aerial" spirit within us—from which plagues and putrid diseases usually follow, especially in those who are not well-fortified by their own nature against these opposing blasts. Hence it is that some are poisoned by these contagious seeds, while others remain healthy and immune from their malignancy by divine will. 

For this reason, it is found written that when God came from the south <note>original: "meridie"</note> with the splendor of light—that is, with lightning—the plague went before Him, and a burning coal <note>original: "anthrax", referring to pestilential sores or burning fever</note> went forth at His feet; and where He stood, He measured the earth, and beheld and drove asunder the nations, as seen in Habakkuk 3:2-6. From this, it is clear that although by divine mandate such luminous meteors are sent from the South to punish the wicked, He does not usually strike everyone with them, but only some; hence it is said that He "measured the earth." The Royal Prophet <note>King David</note> also speaks in these words: *Thou shalt not be afraid for the terror by night; nor for the arrow that flieth by day; nor for the plague that walketh in darkness or the night; nor for the destruction that wasteth at noonday—or as Jerome interprets it, "from the noonday demon" <term>daemon meridianus: a traditional term for the spirit of pestilence or spiritual sloth associated with the heat of the day</term>—the plague shall not come nigh thy dwelling, for He shall give His angels charge over thee, Psalm 91.* In this discourse, by "plague in the south," he understands those pestiferous seeds which are hidden invisibly in the air as if by a dark mist. 

Through the first example, therefore, we see how God, hastening from the south and surrounded by lightning, thunder, and clouds, made the plague and contagious diseases His messengers, with which He is accustomed to disturb nations and peoples rebellious to Him. That God produces all meteors, whether as a scourge or to show kindness to the inhabitants of the earth, Job seems to suggest with these words: *The whirlwind, the cold, the ice, the frost, the clouds, the rain, the thunder and lightning; whatever God commands these to do upon the face of the world on the earth, whether for a scourge or for the benefit of the inhabitants of the earth: Job 37:8-13.* Regarding this kind of stormy spirit acting invisibly but sensibly in the air, the wise man says: *the power of the spirit, or the spirit of power or virtue, shall stand against the wicked, and like a storm or whirlwind shall scatter them.* That such spirits are the destroying angels or ministers of God, we shall show later in its proper place.

# CHAPTER XIV.

## Fourth Part.

### Concerning the "Meteors" of the Macrocosm that are Secretly Luminous and of a Thicker Consistency.

<note>In this context, "meteors" refers to any phenomenon occurring in the air or rising from the earth, including vapors, fumes, and gasses. "Secretly luminous" refers to the author's belief that these substances contain a hidden, vital light or spirit.</note>

The secretly luminous meteors of the Macrocosm <note>original: "Macrocosmi meteora occulte lucida"</note>, gushing forth from the earth and waters, arise either:

- **According to the nature of the place**, and these are either:
    - **Terrestrial**, such as fumes:
        - Vegetable, animal, and mineral; in their natures smelling either good or bad; sulfurous, such as that poisonous vapor leaping out of the earth into the **Cave of the Dog** <note>original: "antrum canis"; a famous volcanic grotto near Naples where carbon dioxide pooled on the floor, suffocating dogs but leaving humans unharmed</note> at the Promontory of Pozzuoli.
        - Bituminous, like the vapors rising from the territory near the **Dead Sea**; or from the lake of Sodom and Gomorrah.
    - **Aquatic**, which affect the air either:
        - **By infecting it malignantly**, such as the fumes of:
            - **Lake Avernus** in Pozzuoli <note>A volcanic crater lake once believed by the Romans to be the entrance to the Underworld</note>.
            - The **eastern marshes** near Alexandretta <note>original: "Scanderon"; a port city in modern Turkey known historically for its pestilential marshlands</note>.
            - The unhealthy sulfur of **hot springs** <note>original: "thermarum"</note>.
        - **By affecting it healthily**, such as the "eastern waters."
- **Accidentally**, and that in two ways, namely either:
    - **By Art** <note>meaning human skill or technology</note>, flowing forth such as fumigations:
        - Foul and stinking.
        - Poisonous.
        - Pleasant and healthy.
    - **By Chance**, happening namely:
        - From the eruption of vapor from a putrid and poisonous place.
        - From the **breaking of glass**, as happens quite often in **chemistry** <term>chimia: here referring to alchemical or early chemical laboratory work</term>.

## The Correlation.

### The hidden, luminous meteors of the Microcosm <note>The "Microcosm" refers to the human body, viewed as a miniature reflection of the entire universe.</note>, gushing forth from the "earth" and "waters" [of the body], are either:

- **According to the nature of the thing or the place**, and these are either:
    - **Terrestrial**, such as fumes:
        - Of **vegetables, animals, or minerals**, whether taken internally or smelled from without, producing both good and bad effects.
        - **Sulfurous**, such as the poisonous vapors in those afflicted by leprosy and the "venereal plague" <note>original: "lue venerea"; a common historical term for syphilis</note>.
        - **Bituminous**, which specifically harden into gums or painful stony deposits <term>tophos: gouty or chalky deposits in the joints</term>; even when these are dissolved, they return into a state of smoke, either resolving the disease or making it worse.
    - **Phlegmatic and aqueous**, and these are either:
        - **Infecting with disease**, such as the fumes of:
            - **Lakes**, as seen in those suffering from dropsy <term>hydropicis: edema or swelling caused by excess fluid</term>, internal abscesses <term>empyematicis: collections of pus, usually in the lungs</term>, and bilious, flowing tumors.
            - **Consumption**, arising from the corrupted humors of the stomach <term>phthisis: a wasting disease, historically associated with tuberculosis</term>.
            - **Putrid marshes**, as seen in virulent and rotten ulcers, "moist" scabies, weeping pustules, etc.
            - **Corrupted hot springs**, as in bilious fistulas <note>An abnormal passage or hole in the body</note> or those infected with bile.
        - **Conferring health**, such as that chylous <note>original: "chilosus"; relating to chyle, the milky fluid of digestion that carries nutrients to the blood</note> and natural humor.
- **Accidental**, such as all fumigations, whether created by art <note>i.e., medicinal incense or professional treatments</note> or occurring by chance.

So great (as has been declared before) is the regard of the spirit of the worldly air for that of the human, and so close is the relationship, that the latter can in no way live or be sustained without the former. From this, therefore, it happens that the fumes arising from the terrestrial air—whether animal, vegetable, or mineral—possess such an affinity with the similar humors and human spirit in the body, that they are most easily connected with them. Indeed, they frequently convert the body's humors into their own nature. We see this just as we see the air of a bedroom changed from its prior condition into the nature of specific scents when sulfur, frankincense <note>original: "olibani"</note>, or civet <note>original: "Zibetique"; a musky perfume from the civet cat</note> are burned. 

In the same way, we sometimes observe the air infected with poisonous odors to the destruction of mortals. This is apparent in those who are infected by the plague, or smallpox <term>variolae</term>, or measles <term>morbilli</term>, or consumption, or even bleary-eyedness <term>lippitudine: an inflammatory condition of the eyes</term>. By the meeting of these "aerial spirits" with the air of a room, the worldly air is quickly infected; from this, it follows that the air itself then tends to infect others staying in that same place.

# THE THIRD MEMBER
## OF THE THIRD BOOK
### CHAPTER XV.
#### Particle I.
##### *On the Meteors of the Macrocosm arising from simple elements.*

<note>In the 17th century, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, including rain, wind, and lightning, not just falling space rocks.</note>

- **K. Macrocosmic Meteors arising from simple elements are either:**
    - **Peaceful.** See [section] N.
    - **Tempestuous or stormy**, and these arise either from:
        - **Winds, both manifest and hidden**, and of this kind there are three species:
            - **Prester** <note>original: "Prester"; a term from antiquity for a fiery whirlwind or a waterspout accompanied by lightning</note>, which is a rain or a flood of fire from wind that is:
                - Smoky,
                - Sulfurous,
                - Thundering.
            - **Ecnephias** <note>original: "Ecnephias"; a sudden, violent wind bursting from a cloud</note>, from many hidden and invisible winds blowing downward together with great force and violence.
            - **Whirlwind** <term>Turbo: a rotating wind-storm</term>, which is twofold, namely either:
                - **Not ignited**, from the meeting of two contrary winds blowing violently and rotating in circles, tending upward from the earth in their motion.
                - **Ignited**, called **Typhomania**, which rolls like a burning wheel over the earth and in the air; it is a certain species of Prester, named "Typhon" from burning <note>original: "Typhon ab incendendo dicta"</note>.
        - **Winds and waters together**, such as a sea storm or those of lakes.
        - **Winds and earth together**, such as:
            - Earthquakes
            - Chasms <note>original: "Hiatus"; openings or rifts in the ground</note>
        - **From all elements together**, namely:
            - **Wind**:
                - Hidden,
                - Manifest and flashing, such as **Thunder**.
            - **The water of a cloud**,
            - **Earth or a thunder-stone.** <note>The "thunder-stone" or ceraunius was historically believed to be a physical object that fell during a lightning strike.</note>

The <term>Peripatetics</term> <note>Followers of Aristotle’s philosophy</note> claimed that the matter of the Prester, the ignited whirlwind, and lightning or thunderbolts was the same: namely, an exceedingly hot and dry exhalation that is grand and abundant. They say this is ignited by the heat of the sun through agitation, friction, collision, and strife. But we, contrary to their doctrine, say that the matter of both the Prester and the ignited whirlwind is a sulfurous wind or air, produced from the **TREASURY OF GOD** <note>A common mystical reference to the "Aeterial" or "Aerial" heaven where God stores the elements of nature</note> or the aerial heaven by the Divine Will. We hold that its efficient cause is **Jehovah** Himself, and not a solar creature; and that their purpose is mostly for the punishment of the wicked, though sometimes the ignited whirlwind is created by **GOD** even for the benefit of the elect <note>A reference to the biblical "whirlwind" that took Elijah to heaven or the pillar of fire</note>.

Thus, supported by the authority of the Sacred Scriptures, I proceed to describe both the Prester and the whirlwind.

A **Prester** is a great rain, and as it were a flood of fire and sulfur, which **Jehovah** is accustomed to send down sometimes from the heavens—as if from His treasury (whose nature is to manifest the hidden part of the air in whatever form according to His will)—onto a portion of the earth as a scourge for the wicked.

In this description, we define the material cause of the fiery whirlwind <note>original: "presteris"</note> as a fiery or sulfurous rain; however, we establish its efficient cause as Jehovah Himself, as He who creates it as if anew from nothing, or brings it forth from the treasury of God, or from the invisible treasury of the air. The formal cause <term>Formal Cause: In Aristotelian philosophy, this refers to the "pattern" or "essence" that makes a thing what it is.</term> is explained by the fact that it is called a rain that is not watery, but fiery and sulfurous. Finally, we have expressed its "end" or purpose in that it is usually produced for the punishment and destruction of the wicked.

By the testimony of the Holy Scriptures, we can prove all these causes of the fiery whirlwind in this manner. First, we find these words written by the Royal Psalmist: *Jehovah rains down burning coals, fire, and sulfur upon the wicked, and a wind joined with various fiery whirlwinds. Psalm 11:6.* <note>original: "prestere"</note> Here the Prophet expresses the matter as well as the form, and even the efficient cause and the purpose. He describes the matter in that he mentions *coals, fire, and sulfur*; and in these words, he also distinguishes the fiery whirlwind from other watery rain by a sufficiently clear form. Then afterward, he identifies the efficient cause not as the sun—which is merely a creature—but as Jehovah the Creator, who acts directly in all things. Finally, he establishes the purpose: that He may torment the wicked and affect them with death. Concerning the effect of this kind of meteor, David writes elsewhere: *As fire burns the forest, as a flame sets the mountains on fire, so pursue them with your tempest, and terrify them with your whirlwind.* Here the Prophet seems to take the fiery whirlwind as a species of whirlwind <term>Turbo: a rotating wind-storm or hurricane</term>. Similarly, Moses describes the effect of this kind of meteor in these explicit words: *The land is so burnt with sulfur and salt that it can neither be sown nor sprout, nor can any herb grow upon it. Deut. 28:12. And it is said elsewhere, nor can any herb grow upon it. Deut. 29:23.* Finally, in Genesis, the parts of our aforementioned description are confirmed in plain and open words: *Jehovah (says the Text) sent down from the heavens a rain of sulfur and fire upon the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah, which overthrew the cities and the entire plain, and all the inhabitants and the offspring of the earth, because of the wickedness of those living there.*

Therefore, it will be most clearly apparent to a wise person who diligently considers these things we have brought forward how vain is the opinion of the Pagan philosophers <note>original: "Ethnicorum Philosophantium"; likely referring to Aristotle and his followers</note> and those Christians who follow them in this matter. Furthermore, when the text says "from the heavens," it understands the "heavens" to be the inner chambers of the air, which we declared in the preceding pages to be the storehouse or treasury of all meteors. This is confirmed by these words of the priest: *Jehovah will open to you his best treasury, the heavens, giving rain in its time. Deut. 28:12. And it is said elsewhere: Have you entered the treasuries of the snow? Or have you inspected the treasuries of the hail? Job 38:22.* And so it is with the rest; it is certain that God has His own treasuries for every species of meteor, and that they are brought from hidden power into manifest action at the Creator's pleasure. Certainly, this dispute of ours concerning the investigation of such a meteor should not seem irrelevant to the wise, in which, contrary to the opinion of the philosophers of this age, we attribute its generation to the Best and Greatest God, Jehovah, and not to accidental causes in nature, or created things such as the sun and stars, etc.

For since it is certain, and confirmed by the sacred text, that the world—by means of such a fiery flood <note>original: "diluvio igneo"</note>—shall be deprived of its present form, destroyed, and purified at the time of the Last Judgment, we believe it must be diligently considered among the learned of the Christians that the error of such Pagan philosophers should be driven into exile from the Christian state, beyond the Hyperborean mountains <note>A mythical land in the far north; here used to mean "total banishment."</note>, and delivered to the perpetual oblivion of good men. Specifically, the error is that the cause of such a meteor (by which the world must perish in the end, that is, be changed and purged from its prior form through purification) is said to arise from the earth by means of the heat of the sun and stars, rather than from God, the father of all wonders, to whom be praise and glory. Was it not for this reason said *that the Son of Man shall come from the east to the west, in the manner of lightning and consuming fire? Matthew 24.* <note>The text incorrectly cites Matthew 27.</note> So also Jehovah is called a *consuming fire, before whose sight nothing can endure, for the mountains melt like wax, etc. Deut. 4.* And yet the Peripatetics <note>Followers of Aristotle's philosophy</note> and the Christians who follow them insist that such power arises solely from "imaginable exhalations" <note>Aristotle's theory that weather is caused by dry and moist vapors rising from the earth.</note>, but back to the point.

Since the matter of the whirlwind <note>original: "turbinis"</note> or Typhon is the same as that of the Fiery Whirlwind <note>original: "Presteris"</note>, though it is observed to be sent from the heavens in a different form and smaller quantity, we therefore attribute the following description to it as well, by the consensus of the Holy Bible. And first, we divide it into the fiery or inflamed whirlwind, and the non-fiery whirlwind which rotates dust, straw, and sometimes larger things in a circle.

We describe the inflamed whirlwind from the holy testimony thus:

An inflamed whirlwind is a fiery wind, rolled into a ball or wheel, which, coming forth by divine power from its inner chamber—from both the northern and southern regions, and also the southwest—has sometimes become the vehicle of Jehovah. From this "tent," as it were, it pleases Him to appear to the saints, to speak to them, sometimes even to snatch them up to Himself into heaven, and most often to send out His vengeance upon the wicked. In this, the material cause is wind or fiery air; the formal cause is that inflamed air rolled into a wheel. The place is its inner chamber—that is, the cloud appropriate for its generation; the efficient cause is the power of Jehovah, by which it is brought forth from His own treasuries. The end or purpose is that it might be the seat of the divine essence, and a kind of tent from which He is accustomed to speak with His saints at times, and frequently to pour out punishments upon the wicked. We have also expressed the regions of the world from which it is most often accustomed to come. And all these things we defend by the authority of the sacred context.

*Out of the inner chamber (says Job) comes the whirlwind, and cold from the scattering winds. Job 37:9.* That is, from the north, as
