Jerome interprets it thus. And in Isaiah we read: *As whirlwinds from the South <note>original: "ab Aphrico"</note> it comes.* Isaiah 21. And elsewhere it is written that Jehovah shall blow the trumpet, and shall go in the whirlwind of the South. Zechariah 9:14. From these passages, the quarter of the world from which it is mostly sent forth is explained. But Ezekiel has it thus: *Behold, a whirlwind came out of the North <note>original: "ab Aquilone"</note>, and a great cloud, and a fire infolding itself, and a brightness was about it, and out of the midst thereof as it were the color of amber <note>original: "electri"</note>, and out of the midst thereof the likeness of four living creatures, and this was their appearance; they had the likeness of a man.* Ezekiel 1:4. In these words, he denotes that the matter of the whirlwind is wind; the quarter of the world from which it comes is the North; and its form is described by a great cloud, a fire infolding the wind, and by a brightness surrounding it. By the "appearance of amber" <term>Amber (Electrum): In this context, it refers to a gleaming alloy of gold and silver or a translucent fossil resin, used here to describe the divine radiance.</term> in the midst of the fire, the throne of God is expressed, together with the spirits in the wheels; and by the likeness of a man, or the son of man, the essence of Jehovah is understood. From this vehicle, therefore, He addresses the Prophet. Hence it is clear how Jehovah does all these things by the mediation of His angelic spirits, at whose nod all things they do are performed. Job also testifies that God is accustomed to speak to the elect from a whirlwind, as when Jehovah answered Job out of the whirlwind. Job 38:1. Finally, regarding the purpose of such a weather phenomenon, it is certain that it exists both for the benefit of men—namely, when God chooses to converse vocally with His elect—and also when He snatches men away from the society of mortals by way of transfiguration. Thus, Enoch is said to have been snatched from the company of mortals and to have walked with God; and of the taking up of Elijah we read: *Behold, a chariot of fire and horses of fire parted them both asunder, and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.* 2 Kings 2:11. That God alone was the actor in this matter is written previously in these words: *When the Lord would take up Elijah into heaven by a whirlwind...* 2 Kings 2:1. But in truth, God most often creates such an impression for vengeance and punishment on account of the disobedience of men. Whence it is written: *He shall be visited of the Lord of hosts with thunder, and with earthquake, and great noise, with whirlwind and tempest, and the flame of devouring fire.* Isaiah 29:6. And elsewhere it is said: *A wind of the power of God blowing, and justice pursuing the unjust.* Wisdom 11:21. And elsewhere: *As the fire burneth a wood, and as the flame setteth the mountains on fire, so persecute them with thy tempest, and make them afraid with thy whirlwind.* Psalm 83:15. And elsewhere: *A whirlwind catches the wicked man by night,* or as Jerome interprets it, *A parching wind shall take him.* Job 27. And elsewhere: *The spirit of power shall stand against the impious, and like a storm or a whirlwind of wind it shall scatter them.* Wisdom 5:24. Finally, in Jeremiah we read: *Behold, the whirlwind of the Lord goes forth in fury, a falling tempest: it shall rest upon the head of the wicked.* Jeremiah 30:23. By which we may see that the fiery whirlwind is very frequently created in the wrath of Jehovah as a scourge for men.

We describe a whirlwind that is windy and not at all ignited in this manner:

A windy whirlwind, yet not subject to ignition, is a certain invisible spirit proceeding from the divine inner chamber <note>original: "penetrali"</note> of the Deity, which, being sent onto the earth, executes the will of the Creator either for good or for evil.

*Out of the inner chamber,* says Job, *comes the whirlwind: and cold from the scattering winds.* Job 37. Job also understands this species of whirlwind where it is said: *They were as stubble before the face of the wind, and as ashes which the whirlwind scattereth.* Job 21:18. Hosea also understands it where he says: *As the dust snatched by the whirlwind from the floor...* Hosea 13:3. The Royal Psalmist also understands this kind of wind where he speaks in these words, Psalm 107:23-29: *They that go down to the sea in ships, these see the works of Jehovah and his wonders in the deep. For he commandeth, and raiseth the stormy wind <note>original: "spiritum turbinis"</note>, which lifteth up the waves thereof... Then they cry unto Jehovah in their trouble, and he bringeth them out of their distresses. He maketh the storm a calm, so that the waves thereof are still.* Thus he speaks. In this discourse, he seems to understand that tempestuous wind which is invisible and not at all ignited.

### CHAPTER XV.

->Second Part.<-

->On the Storms of the Sea or of Lakes.<-

We are taught everywhere in the Holy Scriptures that a stormy tempest of any kind depends upon the divine will, as He who claims empire for Himself over both soul and spirit. Whence He is called the Lord God of soul and body, the strong God of spirits. Numbers 16:22. Nor indeed is there any storm which is not performed by the angelic ministers of God, at the Word or the divine will inciting them. Whence the Royal Prophet says: *Angels of God, mighty in strength, that do his commandments, hearkening unto the voice of his word, doing his pleasure.* Psalm 103:20. And elsewhere: *Who makest thy angels winds or spirits, etc.* Psalm 104:4. And indeed, the most horrifying of all storms is that of the sea, in which the waves like mountains seem sometimes to be raised to heaven, and then suddenly are observed to be thrust down as if into the abyss of the pit <note>original: "Barathri"</note>.

The Peripatetics <term>Peripatetics: Followers of Aristotle's philosophy, known for walking about while teaching. They favored natural, material explanations for physical phenomena.</term> and other followers of ethnic <note>i.e., Pagan</note> philosophy attributed the cause of this kind of storm to the winds—not ineptly, but in this agreeing with Holy Scripture. But in truth, concerning the origin of the winds—namely, their material and efficient cause—they have judged poorly and incongruously. For they falsely asserted that the material cause was a hot and dry exhalation breathed out from the earth, while simultaneously claiming the efficient cause was not Jehovah, through the mediation of His angels, but the sun, the stars, and the cold temperament of the middle region of the air.

We, however, disagreeing widely with those others, say that the **material cause** is drawn from the treasury of God—that is, from the heavens or the air—and we call the **internal agent** a certain angelic spirit, which the spirit of Jehovah animates and is accustomed to stir in the waves to fulfill His will. From this, we describe a **Sea Storm** based on the authority of Holy Scripture in this manner:

A **sea storm** is a disturbance of the sea by a spirit of the whirlwind (which Jehovah stirs by His word to fulfill His will in the waters); that is, a lifting of its waves even to the heavens, and a sudden sinking of them down to the abyss, by which the soul of the sailor melts in distress, and all his wisdom is swallowed up, and finally—unless Jehovah in His mercy makes the whirlwind stand in silence—he is swallowed by the surging waters and thus perishes because of his sins.

In this description, we perceive the **material cause** of the storm to be the sea waters, and the **efficient cause** to be Jehovah himself, who disturbs the waters through his minister—namely, the whirlwind. The **form** of such a storm is depicted by the waves being raised upward everywhere, as if to heaven, and then depressed down to the lowest abyss. Finally, the **end** <note>The "end" or "final cause" refers to the purpose or goal of a phenomenon.</note> of such an operation is explained as this: primarily, to show those who "go down to the sea in ships" that the vigor of the human soul or the power of worldly wisdom is confounded and brought to ruin when the spirit of divine power opposes it; and secondly, to show that it is in God’s hands either to impose silence on that turbulent spirit and return it to rest along with the waves (when it pleases Him to have mercy on the sailors), or to stir and animate it until the ungodly are submerged. And we have this confirmed by the testimony of the Royal Psalmist, from whom we receive this discourse:

> *They that go down to the sea in ships see the works of Jehovah and his wonders in the deep. For he commandeth, and raiseth the stormy wind <note>original: "spiritum turbinis"</note>, which lifteth up the waves thereof. They mount up to the heaven, they go down again to the depths: their soul is melted because of trouble. They reel to and fro, and stagger like a drunken man, and are at their wits' end <note>original: "omnis sapientia eorum absorbeatur"; literally: "all their wisdom is swallowed up"</note>. Then they cry unto Jehovah in their trouble, and he bringeth them out of their distresses. He maketh the storm a calm, so that the waves thereof are still. Then are they glad because they be quiet; they praise Jehovah for his goodness, and for his wonderful works to the children of men, etc. Psalm 107:23–31.*

These words of David seem to include all the members of our aforementioned description. Furthermore, that the "Father of Storms" is the God of Hosts, acting through the winds, seems to be declared elsewhere in these words: *Thou breakest the ships of Tarshish with an East Wind <note>original: "Euro"</note>. Psalm 48:7.* Similarly, that it is in His power to restrain the waves of the sea and lakes, and to make the turbulent spirit be silent and the waves rest, is gathered from the authority of Job, where it is said: *He stilleth the sea by his power, and by his understanding he smiteth through the proud waves <note>original: "percutiat eleuationem"</note>. Job 26:12.*

We conclude, moreover, that this same thing which has been said regarding waves and storms ought also to be understood regarding the waves of lakes, ponds, rivers, and so forth.

# CHAPTER XV.
## Part Three.
### On Earthquakes and Their Occurrences.

The opinion of the Pagan philosophers, and especially the **Peripatetics** <term>Peripatetics: Followers of Aristotle, who taught while walking about. They generally sought naturalistic and physical explanations for weather and geology.</term>, is that the **material cause** of an earthquake is various vapors trapped within the earth's cavernous belly and passages. They claim the **efficient cause** is the resistance and struggle of these vapors against one another, by which they expand themselves and make a path by violent eruption from the caves or dens of the earth, and thus, according to the lightness of their natures, they strive upward with a sudden motion. From this they conclude that in such a violent eruption from the earth, the mass of the earth is either shaken entirely or in part, causing it to tremble. They also claim that a plague usually follows this commotion of the earth because of the "malignancy" of the fumes breaking forth, by which they firmly assert both the air and the waters are corrupted.

If their opinion were fortified by any probability, a stronger faith might be attributed to it by wise men; but, oh, the faith of God and men! Who, endowed with any prudence and properly practiced in the contemplation of God's wonders, has dared to say and assert that such a massive weight could be vibrated and shattered with such a light—and even such a universal—trembling, roaring, and disturbance by mere smoke hidden in its bowels? Or if smoke were the material cause, who, I ask, is the actor in so stupendous a matter? Is it the battle of vapors among themselves? And if it is their battle, who is the primary agent within them? But truly, it is no wonder that these Pagan philosophers, and their Christian followers, have erred in the causes of effects, since they were ignorant of Jehovah himself and His Word, by whom and through whom all things were made and brought into the light. 

We, however, affirm that there is an **aerial spirit** in the earth, by means of which the entire terrestrial mass lives and is continued in its being—not unlike how we see the human body preserved in its state and being by its own internal air. This spirit cannot persist unless it absorbs and draws in a small portion from the mundane spirit <note>the surrounding atmosphere</note> every moment. Indeed, we see, instructed by the testimony of Holy Scripture, that Jehovah by His look alone strikes fear into the clouds and waters, and disturbs the abyss itself. *Psalm 77:16–17.* From this comes the multitude of the sound of waters and clouds; indeed, it is said elsewhere that the waters were afraid at the voice of His thunder. *Psalm 104:7.* And elsewhere, that the clouds

...the clouds passed away in his sight. In a very similar manner, the Creator is also accustomed to act in the terrestrial air, when the earth seems to tremble and be shaken as if by fear—namely, by the mere voice and gaze of Jehovah. Hence it is said, *the earth is shaken and moved; the foundations of the heavens are moved and shaken when his wrath is kindled against it; smoke rises from his nostrils, and fire from his mouth devours; coals are kindled by him. And bowing the heavens, he descended with darkness under his feet, and he sits upon the Cherubim and flies, etc. 2 Samuel 22:8.* <note>original: "et concutitur & mouetur terra... 2. Sa. 22. 8." This is a paraphrase of David's song of deliverance, describing a theophany where God's presence causes a cosmic upheaval.</note> From this, it is clear that there is a spirit or smoke emitted by God which is the cause of the disturbance and shaking, not only of the open air and its clouds—whence come thunder, sound, and trembling in the air—but also in the aerial spirit enclosed within the earth. This aerial spirit, by the angelic breath or smoke proceeding from Jehovah, is sometimes ignited like lightning in a cloud; but once ignited, it is forced to burst forth from the earth with a massive trembling, just like the spirit ignited in a cloud bursts from the cloud's caverns, not without an immense disturbance and shaking of the watery mass collected in the form of a cloud. For undoubtedly the matter stands thus: just as *God made his angels winds, and his ministers a burning and flashing fire, Psalm 104:4,* so indeed these "windy" ministers, both visible and invisible, perform their duties in executing the divine will, both in the enclosed spirits and in that universal open air. We say, therefore, that just as the mundane spirit <note>The "spiritus mundanus" or World Spirit was believed to be a subtle substance pervading all nature, acting as the medium for God's influence.</note> is the vehicle for the ministers of God, through whom and in whom He works whatever pleases Him, so it is necessary that the wondrous nature of these operations proceeds immediately from the divine essence, which exists in these ministers like an uncreated soul or a reigning divine word. Thus, we do not say that this or that flute produced the melody, but rather the flute-player. Therefore, although God uses angels as instruments to produce an earthquake, as well as the disturbance of the air and clouds in thunder, nonetheless that entire operation is to be ascribed to God as the immediate actor. Hence Job says: *God moves the earth from its place so that its pillars tremble; he removes mountains, etc. Job 9:5.* And elsewhere: *When God looks upon it, the earth trembled; and when he touches the mountains, they smoke. Psalm 104:32.* Therefore, we must confess with that same Prophet that *the lowest footprints of the earth are in the hand of God, Psalm 9:5,* and consequently, that the earth is governed by Him alone—that is, it either rests or is vibrated according to His good pleasure. And although its shaking is sometimes ascribed to the presence of an angel, it is nevertheless certain that wherever the angel of God is present, there also Jehovah Himself is present; for in the angel is the great name of God—that is, His ineffable Word. It is for this reason that Dionysius <note>Dionysius the Areopagite, an early Christian theologian who wrote extensively on the "Celestial Hierarchy" of angels.</note> quite wisely calls the Angels *Agalmata*, that is, the clearest mirrors gazing upon the light of God, which is His emanation. For this reason, it is written: *Behold, there was a great earthquake; for the angel of the Lord descended from heaven, and his countenance was like lightning. Matthew 28:2.* By these words, he wished to imply that by the sight of the flashing essence of an angry God within the angel of Jehovah, the spirit of the earth was so agitated and moved that it violently erupted from the bowels of its own mass.

We conclude, therefore, that by the authority of the preceding passages, it will be permitted (I believe) for us to make a description of an Earthquake in this manner:

**An earthquake occurs when the spirit and, as it were, the soul of the entire terrestrial mass—disturbed by the gaze of Jehovah or the breath of His angry angel, and incited and agitated by expansion—is forced to burst violently out of its terrestrial body into the open air, like a massive sigh or groan, or like ignited air from a cloud (not without the shaking and ruin of mountains, cities, temples, and royal buildings, the slaughter of men, and frequently an ensuing plague); by its impetus, the terrestrial mass trembles and is moved, and the open air is infected and poisoned by its malignancy.**

-> Or thus: <-

**An earthquake occurs when the terrestrial spirit, incited by fear and dread at the sight and breath of Jehovah kindled in wrath, causes its own earthy body to tremble and move, just like the spirit of a man struck by unexpected fear.**

In the first description, we made the "terrestrial spirit" (or the earth's internal spirit) the material cause of the earthquake. For we see this in the distillation of **spirit of nitre**: <note>A reference to early chemical experiments with nitric acid. The "agitation" of chemicals in a flask was often used as a microcosm to explain earthquakes.</note> the internal spirit of the nitrous mass, because of the vehement agitation of the fire, leaps out of its body, sometimes destroying the vessel receiving it and shattering it into a thousand pieces, not without a horrific sound. Similarly, the air itself enclosed in a dense cloud is animated, illuminated, and agitated by expansion by the spirit or the mere gaze of an angry Jehovah; hence it happens that, with a great disturbance of the clouds, it pierces and splits their sides with violent force and exits with trembling and noise to execute the will of the Creator. Of this kind, then, was that once-famous earthquake on the **promontory of Puteoli**, <note>Puteoli (modern Pozzuoli) near Naples, an area of high volcanic activity.</note> which occurred arriving with sulfurous flames, lightning, and tremendous thunder; and that one not many years ago, which is said to have happened with the ruin of the little town of **Plurs** <note>Piuro (Plurs) in Italy was destroyed by a massive landslide/earthquake in 1618, a famous disaster in the author's era.</note> in Italy and the subversion of a very high mountain near it, with "typhonic" flames rising from the caverns of the earth and mountain, at the same time as lightning and thunder were sent from on high.

Concerning those earthquakes that proceed from a spirit that is *not* ignited, the Holy Scriptures have written in abundance, and the experience of men still living testifies to them; therefore, we do not intend to say more words about them in this place.

We have already discussed thunder, clouds, lightning, and the thunderstone <note>A "thunderstone" (lapis fulminaris) was a historical term for prehistoric stone tools or meteorites believed to fall from the sky during storms.</note> at great length above.

### Corollary.

We have said in the preceding sections that the spirit of both the earth and of man—and indeed of any other thing, whether animate or not—is so bound in its substance to the open spirit of the world (which we call the air), that the disposition of the parts is suddenly changed into the disposition of the whole (unless some matter of greater weight prevents it). From this, it is clear that the seeds of <term>meteors</term> <note>In this context, "meteors" refers to any atmospheric phenomena like wind, rain, or lightning, not just space rocks.</note> created in the air of the <term>macrocosm</term> <note>The "Great World" or the universe.</note>, which are dispersed everywhere in that air through dissolution, very easily penetrate by successive turns into that same air. Through a certain magnetic inspiration, they are introduced into the particular air of both the earth and the human body (and other living things). There, according to the appetite of their own nature, they are accustomed to produce the same or at least similar effects in the air enclosed within bodies as they manifest in the open air. For example: following the appearance of comets, a plague or pestilential fever usually ensues in the highest region of the human spirit—namely, the vital spirits—from which <term>petechiae</term> <note>Small purple or red spots on the skin caused by minor bleeding.</note> or purple spots arise. The appearances of lightning and <term>chasms</term> <note>A term for atmospheric openings or "gaps" in the clouds through which light or fire appeared to pour.</note> very often generate putrid diseases; and so it is with the rest, as demonstrated in the following table.

On the Formal Cause of Meteors.

## CHAPTER XVI.

### First Section.

### On the Rainbow, or the celestial arch.

By the **Peripatetics** <note>Followers of the philosophy of Aristotle.</note>, the **Iris** <note>The rainbow.</note> is said to be an arc of various colors in a dewy, opaque, and concave cloud, appearing to the eyes of observers from the reflection of the rays of the sun positioned opposite it. They say it cannot be otherwise than arched or semicircular in its shape, although it is certain, and proven by experience, that according to the testimony of Holy Scripture, an arch of this kind sometimes encircles the heaven, as is demonstrated to the eye in our **meteorographic mirror** <note>Likely a diagram or scientific instrument created by the author to simulate atmospheric effects.</note>.

In this description of theirs, they define the **material cause** <term>material cause</term> <note>The physical substance something is made of.</note> from which or in which it is made as the dewy, opaque, and concave cloud; they explain the **Formal cause** <term>formal cause</term> <note>The "form" or essential nature that makes a thing what it is.</note> by saying it is a multi-colored arc; and they make the **Efficient cause** <term>efficient cause</term> <note>The force or agent that brings a thing into being.</note> the solar rays, from whose reflection it appears to the eyes of those watching.

But we, from the text of the Holy Scriptures, conclude that the Rainbow can be described by a **Christian Philosopher** in this manner:

> The Rainbow is the circle or bow of GOD, very glorious in its splendor, which the hand of the Most High has so extended, and placed in the clouds on a rainy day, that it might be a sign of the eternal covenant which He Himself struck with every living soul that lives in the flesh; namely, that there shall no longer be a flood to destroy the whole earth.

->Or thus:<-

> The Rainbow is an arch shining among the clouds of glory on a rainy day, which GOD made with His own hands, and He has encircled the heaven with the circuit of His glory, so that it might be a sign to every living soul of the flesh that the universal flood has been restrained.

In these descriptions, the material cause is seen to be a certain glorious spirit, manifesting itself in its splendor in the misty clouds of heaven. The Formal cause is expressed by saying it is a glorious arc in its splendor, placed in the clouds on a rainy day; or that it is an arch shining among the clouds of glory, encircling the heaven in its circuit. Furthermore, we have described its efficient cause by saying that it was made and placed or impressed in the clouds by the hands and, as it were, the finger of the Most High. Finally, although its general effect is to produce rain, nevertheless its chief purpose and the first of all was that it should be a sign of the covenant between GOD and all flesh, that a universal flood would not come hereafter: as if by this power of His, GOD restrains the clouds from excessive rain, or that its appearance and presence is a sign of remembrance and commemoration of the promise made between GOD and the earth.

From this it is clear that the glorious and shining splendor, which the Heathens <note>Referring to non-Christian philosophers, specifically the Greeks.</note> say arises from the rays of the sun as a multicolored thing, we say proceeds from GOD and His throne full of glory. Indeed, we say with the Holy Bible that GOD Himself in His person and glory—dwelling not only in the glorious solar body, but also present everywhere in the spirit of the world—made this wonderful sign and adorned it with the reflection of His glory.

And although it is certain that solar rays seem to be present in such an operation, nevertheless a power far more potent than solar rays undoubtedly concurs in the formation and generation of such a meteor: namely, the wonderful splendor of God, which is either hidden or manifested according to His will, as was said regarding the procreation of other meteors. For certainly, if dewy clouds and solar rays were the sole cause of such an impression, hardly a day would pass without us seeing a rainbow or celestial arch, since dewy clouds are frequent everywhere in the sky. Furthermore, we have shown elsewhere that GOD is the father of the clouds and of every beautiful flash of lightning, and that each of them has a treasury from which they are drawn by divine command, according to that saying of the wise man: *Look upon the rainbow, and bless Him that made it: very beautiful it is in the brightness thereof. It compasseth the heaven about with a circle of glory, the hands of the Most High have bended it. By His commandment He maketh the snow to fall apace, and sendeth swiftly the lightnings of His judgment. Through this the treasures are opened, and clouds fly forth as birds. By His great power He maketh the clouds firm, and the hailstones are broken small. At His sight the mountains are shaken, and at His will the South wind bloweth. The noise of His thunder maketh the earth to tremble: so doth the Northern storm and the whirlwind, etc. Ecclesiasticus 43:11-20.* <note>The Latin text cites verse 15, following the Vulgate numbering.</note> By which he seems to imply that neither the Sun, nor the stars, nor anything else, but GOD alone is the efficient cause of the rainbow as well as the cloud and all other impressions. Furthermore, regarding their claim that the Rainbow is made by the reflection of the sun in the concavity of an opaque cloud; experience teaches us that this is false, since it usually occurs in misty air, in the inner part of the lowest region of the air, and sometimes appears no further than three hundred paces from the eye. This is shown because we can discern the shining Rainbow between a mountain and sometimes a wood placed before the eye, as if descen-

[shining] brightly; <note>The Latin text begins with "dentem," the second half of the word "splendentem" (shining) from the previous page.</note> from which it happens that, contrary to the opinions of the **Peripatetic Philosophers** <note>Followers of Aristotle.</note>, it is not required that the rainbow be formed in the concavity of an opaque cloud. Indeed, it is very often observed to appear in air that is sufficiently dense yet diaphanous and transparent: through which, and by means of which, it is possible to discern a mountain or a forest. And it seems that the Sacred Text deals with this misty air when it is said by the Wise Man:

> *Ecclesiasticus 50:8. Like the rainbow shining among the clouds of glory.* <note>original: "Arcus refulgens inter nebulas gloriæ"</note> *And concerning such a cloud—namely, misty air—other testimonies of Holy Scripture seem to speak; the Rainbow therefore appears to manifest among dense clouds, and to the eye, in misty or dewy air.*

And although several Philosophers, and indeed experts in optics, wish to discuss and debate the variety of the Rainbow's colors in their own fashion—saying that the diversity of colors arises from variations in both the cloud and the light, and that thin water in a dewy cloud, otherwise bright air, and dark clouds must all concur for the procreation of different colors—they claim that all these things, when irradiated by the sun, provide different colors: namely, crimson, green, yellow, citron, red, glaucous, or blue. (Aristotle seems to treat these matters in Book 3 of his *Meteorology*). Nevertheless, if we wish to consider the matter a little more accurately, we see that it behaves differently than they imagined. These colors of the rainbow are often produced without those specific mediums and in a different subject entirely, as **Roger Bacon** <note>13th-century English philosopher and friar known for his emphasis on empiricism.</note> teaches in his book on *Experimental Science*, and as common experience also shows.

For in many lower things, colors of this kind are observed to appear: if we take hexagonal stones <note>Likely quartz crystals or basalt.</note> from **India** or **Ireland**, and if we hold them against the rays of the sun penetrating through a window or some hole into a shadow or shaded air, we will perceive near the rays all the colors of the rainbow in the same order in which they are arranged in the celestial arch. Therefore, it is certain that colors of this sort can be produced without the aforementioned mediums (clouds); thus, it does not seem to follow that these colors are brought to light solely because of the reflection of solar rays in a concave and opaque dewy cloud.

Nor does it follow of necessity that the solar rays striking a surface directly are the sole cause producing such a variety of colors. For, according to the testimony of **Roger Bacon**, if an operator takes the said hexagonal stone and turns himself toward a somewhat darker place, applying the stone to his half-closed eye, he will immediately discern the said colors of the rainbow in the air. There are, therefore, some who believe that colors of this kind are procreated by a specific property of that stone; but truly, this is false. These colors appear in a similar way using either a crystal or a well-polished glass body reduced to a triangular form <note>A prism.</note>, appearing in both shaded and luminous air.

Furthermore, such colors sometimes appear on the oars of a boat when they are wet with dew and droplets are dripping as they are lifted from the water; the same happens when water is violently thrown against the rays of the sun. Nor is it necessary, as has been said, to have the presence of the sun for such an appearance, since it often happens that even at night—in the absence of the sun—these colors are observed to appear around a candle. Yet, we admit that it is necessary for light to be present, without which we cannot discern anything colored, much less colors which cannot be seen without a colored object. But as pertains to the "subject" in which these colors are visible, we say it can be the air itself imbued with light; for I remember lying in bed in the morning and for a long time perceiving these colors indistinctly in and near the solar rays.

Wherefore, without a doubt, the **efficient cause** <term>efficient cause</term> <note>The agent or force that brings something about.</note> of these wonderful colors is more occult and hidden than can be easily grasped by the Heathen Philosophers, or indeed by those followers of theirs among the Christians of this age. For **GOD**, who is all and in all, and who fills the worldly spirit everywhere with His brightness (though it be invisible), is the cause of such a wonder in nature: He who is accustomed to reveal Himself to men through signs, through colors, through lightnings, and infinite other ways.

In moist nature, this light is called the "Voice of Light," or the **Word**, by **Hermes Trismegistus** <note>Legendary Hellenistic figure linked to alchemy and wisdom.</note> in *Pimander 1*; standing by moist nature, it nourished it. And another, immersing himself deeply in the mysteries of nature (*On the Art of Chemistry, ch. 9*), says that this hidden nature is a certain infinite power, procreating like from like, increasing and nourishing all things, and for this reason possessing the names of all things within itself; having no color, yet participating in and effecting all colors; the fertile mother of all qualities and things. From this he concludes that this nature is **GOD**, and GOD is that uncreated nature—the created/creating/nourishing moist nature which the **Platonists** <note>Followers of Plato's philosophy.</note> recognize as the **Soul of the World** <term>Anima Mundi</term>, existing invisibly in its whole and in every part, just as the human soul exists in its body.

**Zoroaster** <note>Ancient Persian prophet/philosopher.</note>, with whom **Heraclitus of Ephesus** <note>Pre-Socratic Greek philosopher known for the doctrine of change and fire.</note> also seems to agree, calls this "Invisible Fire," from which all things are generated. Others among the **Hebrew Doctors** <note>Scholars of Jewish mysticism or theology.</note> hold it to be that fiery vigor which the **Spirit of Elohim** <note>The Spirit of God.</note>—which is the fiery love that moved over the waters—produced in them, and consequently dispersed everywhere, though invisibly, in the world. For as **St. Peter** testifies:

> *2 Peter 3: The heavens and earth existed before out of water and through water, consisting by the word of GOD.* <note>original: "Cæli & terra erant prius de aqua..."</note> *That is, by the primary emanation from the throne of divinity, through which all things were made and without which nothing was made (John 1).*

Does not the Wise Man also treat clearly of the nature or invisible light of this spiritual sun when he breaks out into these words?

> *Wisdom 7: Wisdom is a spirit having all virtues in itself, simple and yet manifold, looking into all things, containing all intelligible spirits, more mobile than all mobile things, and reaching everywhere because of her purity; for she is a certain emanation of the clarity of almighty GOD, sincere, more beautiful than the sun, and compared to the light, she is found prior to every arrangement of the stars, etc.* <note>original: "sapientia est spiritus omnes in se habens virtutes..."</note>

From this it is clear that to this spiritual sun and light, rather than to the physical sun, must be attributed the origin of the rainbow as well as all other meteors...

# On the Formal Cause of Meteors.
<note>In early modern science, "meteors" referred to all atmospheric phenomena, including rain, wind, and rainbows, not just falling space rocks.</note>

...operation, which they derive either from the sun or the stars, seeing as they obtain and possess their vigors and properties from this root of light. Wherefore we have it written, *How wonderful and vast are all the works you have made in wisdom*, Psalm 104:24. <note>original: "Opera mirabilia & ampla quæ fecisti omnia in sapientia," Ps. 103. 24. in the Vulgate.</note> *And elsewhere, by his spirit he has adorned the heavens*, Job 26:13. *And elsewhere, GOD by his wisdom adjusted the weight of the air, and weighed the waters by measure, making statutes for the rain, and a path for the lightning of the thunders, etc.* Job 28:25. From these things it is right to gather that this holy spirit of discipline, which fills the world and is found everywhere in the heavens, though invisible, sometimes renders itself visible through media, as in the matter of the sun, the rainbow, and other meteors. For although it is a simple spirit in itself, it is nonetheless manifold in respect to the variety of its operations and appearances. 

But what need is there for more words? We have this expressly designated in the sacred scriptures, namely Ecclesiasticus 43:11-12: *Look upon the rainbow, and praise him who made it; very beautiful it is in its brightness. It encompasses the heaven with a circle of glory, the hands of the Most High have stretched it out.* <note>original: "Vide arcum cœli, & benedic eum qui fecit illum..."</note> So also we read elsewhere that the appearance like a bow, when it is in a cloud on a rainy day—which was the appearance of brightness all around—was the presence of GOD and his ministers in the cloud; similarly, this same thing is explained in the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation.</note>. Hence also it is found elsewhere, like a rainbow reflecting among the clouds of glory, where "clouds of glory" seem to denote a certain glorious actor in the construction of that bow. 

But indeed, the following text not only clearly depicts the <term>Efficient Cause</term> <note>The agent or force that actually brings something into being; in this case, God.</note> of the Rainbow, but also seems to denote its primary purpose: *I will set my bow (says Jehovah) in the clouds, and it shall be a sign of a covenant between me and the earth. And when I cover the sky with clouds, my bow shall appear in the clouds of heaven, and I will remember my covenant which I made with you, and with every living soul that breathes in the flesh, and there shall no more be the waters of a flood to destroy all the earth; and my bow shall be in the clouds, and I will see it, and I will remember the everlasting covenant, which was established between me and every living soul of all flesh that is upon the earth.* Genesis 9:12-16. From this speech it is clear that the **matter** of the Rainbow is the air in the clouds; the **subject** in which it appears is the cloud; the **form**, however, is openly indicated in what was said: that the bow of heaven is very beautiful in its brightness and has encompassed the heaven in a circle. The **Efficient cause** is God, as he is said to have made it. The **End** <note>Final cause or purpose.</note> is hidden: that it may be a sign of the restrained flood. Therefore it is certain that the spirit of GOD, expanding itself everywhere, though invisibly, both in the heavens and on the earth, is the author and actor of this glorious creature, who composes, alters, and changes all things according to His will, both in shape and in color, and performs all things—in which action He uses His creatures, the angels, as instruments. 

And since the reasoning for the colors and shape of the heavenly bow is treated in an optical manner by those skilled in optics and the science of perspective, we shall explain below, both with words and with a visual demonstration in our "Meteorographic Mirror," what they themselves think in their art concerning the generation of the Rainbow.

In the art of <term>Chemistry</term> <note>Meaning Alchemy in this context.</note>, those more skilled say that their "mystical sulfur" shines like a Rainbow through the waters, and this with almost all the colors found in the Rainbow. They say that it is the bow of the Rainbow itself because it is in the midst of pure, liquid, and flowing water, and in the midst above the earth; therefore they express the entire property of sulfur and its natural likeness through the Rainbow. For the rainbow is not seen in the mundane sky except when the sun is shining, which rain is also accustomed to follow; for when mists or opaque clouds come, the Sun itself and the rainbow are hidden together. In the very same way, the Rainbow is not seen in the "sky of the chemists" unless the "central sun" is shining, which is the incorruptible spirit dwelling centrally in pure sulfur; this bow also, in a similar fashion, is accustomed to follow the "Microcosmic rain." But when mists or opaque clouds come, the Sun itself and the rainbow are similarly hidden. A certain man most experienced in that secret writes these things (On the Art of Chemistry, chapter 13). 

And certainly it should be known that just as the incorruptible spirit of GOD, giving life to all things and acting as the soul of the world, is said to be in the whole and in every part, so it acts in a particle according to its action in the whole. And although it belongs to Jehovah alone to create worlds anew—to whom (*as Solomon testifies*) *wisdom was present as a master worker, composing all things in the creation of the world*, Wisdom 9:10—nevertheless, through the mediation of this wisdom (which Jehovah is accustomed to send to man so that she may be present and labor with him), man is given certain knowledge of the constitution of the world and the power of the elements, and the beginning, middle, and end of times, and the variety of seasons and the positions of the stars, etc. Wisdom 7:17. For this glorious central spirit, freed from elementary impurity by human labor and industry, is accustomed to reveal the practice of the divine mystery to man, according to the words of the wise man in the place cited above. Therefore, all these things are perfected by God alone, the worker of wonders, whether they happen in the accustomed course of nature or beyond human expectation and the foreknowledge of common astrologers, by means of the **wonderful word**, in whose power are all things.

# On the Formal Cause of Meteors.

### CHAPTER XVI.

#### Part Two.

## *Regarding the peaceful terrestrial meteors of the Macrocosm, moist in nature.*

<note>In the 17th century, "meteors" referred to any natural phenomenon occurring in the atmosphere or on the earth's surface, including clouds, rain, springs, and even marshes.</note>

**Peaceful terrestrial meteors of the Macrocosm** <note>the Great World or Universe</note>, **of a more moist constitution, are characterized by either:**

*   **Coldness**, such as those that are:
    1.  **Marshy or swampy**, being earth that is corrupted and muddy.
    2.  **Inundated with many small springs**, contaminated by waters that are fresh, acidic, <term>aluminous: containing alum, a bitter mineral</term>, salty, or containing other such minerals.
    3.  **Deeply hollowed out** by stagnant waters.
    4.  **Gathering together** into a muddy mass.
*   **Heat**, such as:
    1.  **Marine marshes**, or land made swampy by the flow of salt waters, which are corrupted and made unhealthy by them.
    2.  **Marshes or swampy land** infected with either bitter or sulfurous waters, whether protruding outward or hollowed out into the depths.

## Correlative to Man.

The **peaceful terrestrial Meteors of the Microcosm** <note>the human body</note>, which are of a more moist constitution, are characterized by either:

*   **Coldness**, similar to marshy lands, namely:
    *   **Abscesses** <note>original: *Apostemata*; localized collections of fluid or inflammation</note> resembling:
        *   **Stagnant marshes**, such as **Dropsy** <note>original: *Hydropesia*; the abnormal accumulation of fluid in the body</note>:
            *   **General** <note>affecting the whole body</note>, such as:
                *   **Anasarca** <note>severe, widespread swelling of the skin</note>.
                *   **Leucophlegmatia** <note>a condition of pale, dropsical swelling associated with excess phlegm</note>.
            *   **Localized**, such as **Ascites** <note>fluid accumulation specifically in the abdominal cavity</note>.
        *   **Muddy and silty marshes**, including:
            *   **Oedema** <note>swelling caused by fluid trapped in the body's tissues</note>.
            *   **Acrochordons** <note>original: *Acrochordines*; small, fleshy skin tags or hanging warts</note>.
            *   **Lupiae** <note>cysts or "wen," usually soft and painless swellings on the head or neck</note>.
            *   **Struma or scrofula** <note>a swelling of the lymph nodes, typically in the neck, often associated with tuberculosis</note>.
    *   **Ulcers** that are cold and cause very little pain.
    *   **Pustules** that are watery and <term>serous: resembling or containing the clear part of the blood</term>, such as **Phlyctenae** <note>small blisters or vesicles filled with clear fluid</note>, which are small pimples.
*   **Heat**, similar to marshy ground, under which are categorized:
    *   **Abscesses**, such as:
        *   **Phlegmon** <note>an acute, spreading inflammation of deep skin tissues</note>.
        *   **Miliary herpes** <note>a skin eruption characterized by many small, millet-seed-sized spots</note>.
    *   **Pustules**, such as:
        *   **Epicyclide** <note>a specific type of skin eruption or pimple</note> arising from **choleric blood** <note>blood mixed with yellow bile, thought to be hot and dry</note>.
        *   **Others** originating from:
            *   **False phlegm**.
            *   **Bilious blood** <note>blood dominated by bile</note>.
    *   **An itchy vapor**, which is false, nitrous, and bitter, containing some burnt earthy components, from which arise **scabies** <note>a contagious, itchy skin condition</note> and **moist itching** <note>pruritus</note>.

# A BRIEF EXPLANATION AND ELUCIDATION OF THIS OUR METEOROGRAPHIC MIRROR OR SPECULUM.

<image-desc>A complex hierarchical logic tree (Ramist diagram) classifying the components of a 'meteorographic mirror.' The chart branches from left to right using curly brackets to divide concepts into binary or ternary sub-categories, covering theological actors (Divine Spirit, Angels) and material subjects (Spiritual and Corporal elements, including meteorological phenomena and living beings).</image-desc>

In this mirror or meteorological Reflecting-Glass, two primary things present themselves to be noted: namely, worldly
* **Action** which comes from the part of the primordial form, in which two things must be considered:
    * **The Author & Actor** who is the simple, unique, and only divine spirit, who is either:
        * Outside all things, and is the fount of divinity called *Ein Sof* <note>original: *Ensoph*; a Hebrew Kabbalistic term for the Infinite or God before manifestation</note> or infinity.
        * Inside all things, as one who is disseminated everywhere from the *Ein Sof* fount through ten shining breath-holes <note>original: *spiracula lucida*; a reference to the ten Sephiroth or divine emanations</note> of diverse properties, and fills all things.
    * **The Organs** in and through which he acts immediately, namely the Angels.
* **Passion** <note>In this context, "passion" means the capacity to be acted upon—the receptive or material side of nature.</note> which comes from the part of matter, in which we observe two types of subjects:
    * **Spiritual things**, and these are:
        * Primary, which are either:
            * Empyrean Angels <note>Angels of the highest, fiery heaven</note>
            * Demons
                * Olympic <note>Celestial or planetary spirits</note>
                * Elemental.
        * Secondary, which are:
            * Ether.
            * Air.
            * Wind.
    * **Corporeal things**, and these are either:
        * Elements.
            * Water.
            * Earth.
        * "Elementated" things <note>Things composed of the elements</note>, and these are mixed either:
            * Imperfectly, such as "meteors" <note>In the 17th century, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomena, including rain, snow, and lightning.</note> that are:
                * Ignited.
                * Watery.
                * Smoky.
            * Perfectly, and these are:
                * Animals.
                * Vegetables.
                * Minerals.

-> Of all these things, the perfection and end is Man. <-

***

Look here (most welcome Reader!), what others have attempted to express with much speech and a subtle style of teaching—namely, the science of meteorology—I desire to offer to your gaze by this almost short and brief picture, and by a method of visual demonstration. In this, as if in a most polished mirror, we have outlined the whole condition, form, and position of any "meteor," and indeed the optical logic of certain phenomena (by which some such impressions appear in the sky as they are not in reality). Therefore, I would like you to briefly receive the intention of making this mirror, the explanation of its parts, and the knowledge of distinguishing the regions in the Hemisphere one from another.

By two parallel lines rising above the Horizon, drawn circularly from east to west and outlining the hemisphere, we intend to represent the cavity of the stellar heaven at the edge of the ether. And therefore we have assigned to the Sun and the Moon multiple stations or positions in the interstice, or space between the two parallel lines signifying the heaven. For it seemed impossible to us that any demonstration in this mirror depending on the Sun and the Moon could be referred to a single site or place, and also in one part of the picture various types of impressions <note>Atmospheric effects or phenomena</note> cannot be depicted. Therefore, we call that whole space—containing the two semicircles starting from the east and ending in the west with parallel lines—the "heaven," in which we have placed the Milky Way, the Sun, and the Moon. Moreover, the lowest semicircle refers to the image of the earth itself, from which a multiform view toward meteorological objects is usually made.

Every place interposed between the ethereal heaven and the earth denotes the vast seat of the air or the extension of the world-spirit, in whose capacity, as a common medium, the whole institution and logic of our purpose seems to be included and contained. This general place is also divided into three parts by two curved lines forming an arc, which the common folk are accustomed to call the "regions of the air," neglecting their dimension, about which common philosophers seem to contend too much. We, however, think that the lower region of the air does not exceed the highest mountains in its dimension or extension.

# A Lucid Explanation

...we have considered: but truly, we believe the upper region to be most vast and exceedingly spacious. We think the region situated between these two—the middle—is moderate in its dimension between those extremes. Within these regions of the air are included the principal arguments of our intention (as has been said); we have thought this must be considered by you first and placed before your eyes, especially regarding the various seats and positions of the meteors.

In the upper region, we have ordained that the divine action and the organs or ministers—in and through whom all things in these lower parts, and indeed in the heavens above, are perfected—be distinguished according to the strength of our understanding. Concerning these ministers, as they are the beginnings of all things (both perfectly and imperfectly mixed), we shall speak briefly and lightly in this place, descending from the peak of the mirror to the base. We do this because mention has been made of them abundantly in both the preceding and following sections, to the honor of **GOD**, the creator of all, and for the education of man, who is the goal and perfection of all things.

All things created in the world—whether they are simple or arisen from simples (such as Angels, who are a kind of "otherness" <note>original: *alteritas*</note> and forged from two; stars; and also, among the sublunary bodies, the imperfectly mixed ones which are composed in and from the air; and finally the perfectly mixed, such as animals, vegetables, and minerals)—are composed of a shining form, whether it be apparent or hidden, and matter as the subject. Of these two, the role of matter is to suffer <note>original: *pati*; in the sense of being passive or receptive to change</note> and the role of form is to act. Without these qualities, nothing in the world could exist or reach the goal of perfection toward which all things tend. Thus, in the first place, we must especially consider what is the source and beginning in the motion of continued action, from which various acts are rained down and disseminated everywhere through the world. Then, we must consider what the immediate ministers or organs of the primary actor are, through which and in which he acts or pours out the acts of his emanation. After that, we think it must be considered with diligent intuition what the principal subjects in the world are—both in the ethereal heaven and in the air—as the air is the place where all kinds of meteors (our primary focus here) are usually procreated; and finally, in the water and the earth, around which the aforementioned acts of God are observed to act and move.

In the first or upper place, we find God himself in the immense and infinite dimension of his divinity, described as if by letters—since he can never be depicted by an image or comprehended in his infinity by the human mind. It pleases us to signify or express him there through the word *Ensoph* <note>original: *Ensoph*; the Hebrew Kabbalistic term *Ein Sof*, meaning "The Infinite" or God before manifestation</note> along with the Kabbalists and more Secretive Theologians. This word signifies Infinity, which they asserted to be the unique fountain of life and divine essence—an infinity, indeed, without which nothing lives and nothing is, for all things proceed from the One. This unique fountain (into whose secrets it is not possible to penetrate) they quite wisely make into a double spring, namely natural and spiritual, from which the living waters proceed. These descend by way of emanation, first through a stream into the shining parental gate called *Elion Cheter* <note>original: *Elion Cheter*; Hebrew *Elyon Keter*, meaning the "Supreme Crown"</note>, which is the highest crown; and then afterward into the Son, *Hochma* <note>original: *Hochma*; Hebrew *Chokhmah*, meaning Wisdom</note> or Wisdom. Hence the royal Psalmist says, *with thee is the fountain of life*. From this, it is right to gather that **GOD** in his innermost essence is outside all things and beyond the cavity of the world, nor can he be grasped by the sharp edge of the mind. Nevertheless, through his various breathing-holes <note>original: *spiracula*</note> which are the *Sephirotic* <note>original: *Sephiroticæ*; referring to the Sephiroth, the ten attributes in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself</note> enumerations or shining gates, he scatters and disseminates various shining emanations—distinct from one another in property—downward everywhere through the cavity of the world. These emanations, as they take on a worldly spirit, are accustomed to take on the names and properties of Angels. The first three of these, out of the ten, are ordained for the fashioning of the world's regions, the heavens, and the elements: the first, the Crown, is ascribed to the Father; the second, called Wisdom, to the Son; and Prudence <note>original: *prudentia*; likely referring to the third Sephirah, *Binah*, or Understanding</note> to the Holy Spirit. This the royal Prophet also seems to prove in this speech: *by the word of the Lord the heavens were established, and all the power of them by the spirit from his mouth*. Here, the Lord is the Father, emitting the word or wisdom, by means of which heaven and earth were created out of the waters (as St. Peter testifies), and by the spirit from both of them, all power is in them. However, the seven other emanations are received and, as it were, soaked up by the seven remaining Angelic spirits. By means of these, the said Angels are informed; they act and operate according to the property of the Divine name from which they are rained upon into those worldly subjects, wherever they are disposed throughout the spacious world. And these are those angels who are said to preside over the Seven Planets, concerning which we will speak more broadly below.

As for those angelic or spiritual receptacles or organs, which are ordained by God to receive the types of divine influxes, we shall explain them in a few words for the better understanding of the readers, in this manner: describing the channels of the influxes, the orders of angels who receive them first, and finally to which spheres of the celestial region they lead them by virtue of their office.

First, therefore, it must be known and observed with a diligent intellect that from the infinite fountain of immense divinity, called *Ensoph*, ten shining emanations (according to the intentions of the Kabbalists) flow through as many channels differing in property. These are poured out and emanate everywhere into the world according to the will of God, first into ten various orders of Angels and saints. From these, again, ten Archangels (counting the soul of the Messiah among them), created by **GOD** for this business—namely, each one of them receives any of those emanations as shining influxes from any order. For almost all Theosophists agree in this: that as the orders of Angels [above... <note>original catchword: *superio-*</note>]

# Of the Meteorographic Mirror

The higher beings receive light, or a lucid emanation, directly from **GOD** and thus emit and manifest it to those of the lower orders; for this reason, the Angels are called mirrors <note>original: *specula*</note>, as they are capable of receiving the light of **GOD**. On this point, Dionysius, Basil, Isidore, Gregory, and others all agree. Similarly, just as the more "secret" theologians <note>referring to Kabbalists</note> have observed ten distinct hidden properties in **GOD** through a serious study of the Holy Bible—perceiving various names of **GOD** attributed to them by the prophets and patriarchs—so too is a specific Angel assigned to each of these emanations. Each Angel has a primary duty concerning that specific property of **GOD** for which they were destined from the beginning. For it is a general principle among the secret theologians, Kabbalists, and others—with whom Dionysius also seems to agree—that no angel is permitted to undertake a work belonging to another. 

But truly, because the office of the Angel Metatron <note>the highest archangel in this system, often associated with the presence of God</note> was so universal—concerned with the formation of the world, the division of darkness from light, the quickening of the world, and the motion of the heavens—he is believed to be that "first wisdom" created before every creature (as the wise man says). Through his mediation, all things were afterwards made; hence, he contains within himself the total perfection of the angelic nature, no differently than all the solar rays are said to be contained within the sun.

We proceed, therefore, to a clear demonstration of this matter, as you have it depicted in the uppermost region of our Meteorographic Mirror in the following manner:

The **first emanation** gushing forth from the eternal fountain of divinity, according to the benevolent property of **GOD** prone to kindness, is called **EHIEH** <note>Hebrew: "I AM"</note>. This name of **GOD** regards eternity and the entire wheel of time—namely the past, present, and future. The channel, or lucid gate, or <term>Sephira</term> <note>a divine emanation in Kabbalistic thought</note> of this fountain of divine grace is **Cheter**, or the **Crown**. This is the root of the entire Sephirotic tree, from which gate the emanation of life and essence flows into the order of the **Seraphim**. This is the highest order of the First Hierarchy. These angels, as Isidore testifies, are "fiery," kindling others with a burning heat and love. They possess that remarkable brightness through this most lucid outflow, which is full of the gift of love and concord; this order is the very source of Charity. Next, this lucid influence is received by Metatron, the first and greatest of all Angels, who directs it into the highest sphere of the ethereal heaven, called the <term>Primum Mobile</term> <note>The "First Mover," the outermost sphere of the traditional cosmos which drives all others</note>. By its power, he animates all the heavens in the entire world, rotating them from the east to the west, and from the west back to the east in a natural day. Thus, he seems to animate the entire world-spirit by his motion and light, which is why the Platonists call him the **Soul of the World** <note>original: *anima mundi*</note>.

The **second emanation** is called **IAH**, also from a benevolent property. For by means of this divine name, form is dispersed through the entire spirit of the world. The channel through which it passes, and the lucid gate through which it exits, is called by the Kabbalists **Hochma**, that is, **Wisdom**, through which all things were made. This emanation directs the fountain of its light to the order of the **Cherubim**, who are therefore said to abound in the fullness of knowledge and the gift of wisdom and understanding. This order entrusts that downward-tending emanation to the guardianship of the Archangel **Raziel**, who is made the guardian and director of this outflow. He directs it into the eighth sphere, or the sphere of the fixed stars, through the middle of which passes that zone or belt of heaven called the **Zodiac**. Judging by the etymology of the name <note>likely connecting the Greek *zoe* (life) with the Zodiac</note>, this spirit or emanation acts primarily toward quickening and animation through its power. This influx also generates various meteorological "impressions" in the air.

The **third emanation**, or divine flow, is called **ELOHIM**. The channel or branch in which it moves, and the lucid gate from which it exits, is called **Binah**, or **Prudence** <note>often translated as "Understanding"</note>. From here it descends into the lowest order of the first hierarchy, namely the **Thrones**. This indicates a property of **GOD** that is severe and full of judgment. From this order, the Archangel **Zaphkiel** (or as others prefer, **Oriphiel**) receives these descending flows and conducts them into the **Sphere of Saturn**. Hence, just as Saturn is a heavy, fixed, and melancholy planet, it is said to pour down severe effects of judgment and punishment upon the lower world. For this reason, it is called the **Greater Malefic** <note>original: *Infortunium maius*; an astrological term for a planet that brings significant difficulty or bad luck</note> by astrologers. Occasionally, sad and dark effects are produced by it—such as thick clouds, foul mists, and thin, dry rains—sometimes mixed with thunder, in the manner of the separation of the fiery element from chaos.

The **fourth emanation** from the source of the **Ein Sof** <note>original: *Ensoph*; the Infinite or Boundless Godhead</note> is called **EL**, which indicates Mercy in this property of **GOD**. Thus, its channel or lucid gate is named **Chesed**, that is, **Clemency** <note>or Mercy/Kindness</note>. This influx of divine light is sent into the highest order of the middle hierarchy, called the **Dominions**. Through this, power is given against malignant spirits, as well as the benefits of life and benevolent breezes, which are led into the **Sphere of Jupiter** by the Archangel **Zadkiel** (or as others prefer, **Zaccariel**). This is the reason why the planet Jupiter is filled with such benevolence toward the human race and living creatures; thus, it is called the **Greater Benefic** <note>original: *fortunium maius*; the planet of great good fortune</note> by astrologers, just as Saturn is called the Greater Malefic. Among the meteors it occasionally produces in the air are whitish clouds mixed with redness, which tend to resolve into either light rain or wind.

The **fifth emanation** is named **ELOHIM GIBOR**, a name of **GOD** that implies severity. The channel or gate from which it flows from the source of the Ein Sof is called **Geburah**, that is, **Punishment**. This emanation passes downward into the middle order of the third hierarchy, which is the **Principalities**...

# A Lucid Explanation

...of power and dominion over rebels, compelling them by force and arms, as it were, toward the true worship and reverence of God. The Angel to whom this influence is entrusted by this order is the severe *Samael*, who leads it into the sphere of **Mars**. From this sphere, fiery influences and the "seeds" of wrath are sent down into the lower world. By the power of such influences, the air is seen to fill with saffron-colored clouds, which occasionally release thunder, lightning, and tempests; indeed, according to the opinion of astrologers, comets and "fiery impressions" <note>A traditional term for meteorological phenomena like meteors or lightning</note> originate here. Furthermore, it happens that because of the infected and malignant heat of this Martial influence, fevers, plagues, and hot diseases are sometimes observed to be brought upon mortals; for this reason, Mars is called the "Lesser Misfortune" <note>original: *Infortunium minus*</note> by astrologers.

The Sixth Emanation is called **ELOAH**; being most full of every shining virtue, it has for its channel *Tipherith*, which signifies grace, beauty, and clarity. This influence directs its power into the lowest order of the middle hierarchy, which is the **Powers** <note>original: *Potestatum*</note>. Their role is to subject wicked angels or spirits to themselves, doing so by force and power, as Gregory says. This order commits that influence to the power and custody of **Michael**, that great Angel who made this emanation his own internal spirit; by its virtue, he subjected the Dragon and all his company to himself. This Angel, therefore, leads this influence into the sphere of the **Sun**, which he governs, from which he later pours it out liberally into the lower realms. Upon contact with this influence, life is multiplied in growing plants, generation occurs on land and in the sea, and all things are refreshed by the solar grace and beauty.

The Seventh outpouring is called by the Kabbalists **IEHOVAH ZEBAOTH**. Its channel or Sephirotic gate is called *Netzeth* <note>Netzach</note>, that is, *Triumph*, through which this emanation goes forth. It descends into the highest order of the lowest hierarchy, which they call the **Virtues** <note>original: *Virtutes*</note>, in which the divine virtue shines forth. For as *Isidore* says, the angels of this order receive illumination, purification, and perfection from the orders of the middle hierarchy. The commentator *Archangelus* <note>Likely Archangelus of Borgonovo, a Christian Kabbalist</note> in his *Commentary on Kabbalistic Dogma* seems to assert that influences are directed from *Tipherith* into this order, which may indeed seem likely because of its lucid, clear, and beautiful condition—being a place where the light of **GOD** shines wonderfully. But we follow Dionysius and Isidore here. This influence is received from this order by the good Angel **Anael**, and is carried down into the sphere of **Venus**. By his presence and virtue, good influences—pleasing to the human race—are scattered everywhere through the sublunary air, water, and earth. By his presence also, thin clouds and sometimes light, sifting rain are created. This is also why this planet, namely *Venus*, is called the "Lesser Fortune" <note>original: *Fortunium minus*</note> by astrologers.

The Eighth emanation is called **ELOHIM ZEBAOTH**, after its property, and it has for its gate or Sephirotic channel *Hod*, that is, *Praise*. This descends into the order of **Archangels**, from which it is remitted to the Archangel **Raphael**. He leads it into the sphere of **Mercury**, who is (according to the poets) the great messenger of Jove. From there, it is later sent into the sublunary region, where it occasionally creates rapid winds in the air, which are not infrequently associated with heavy showers and rains. Moreover, this influence is observed to act in various ways within man: specifically, it grants good sense, makes the intellect sharp, and the memory fertile.

The Ninth is called **SADAI** <note>Shaddai</note>, whose shining gate is *Iesod* <note>Yesod</note>. Descending through this, it passes into the order of **Angels**, from which it is committed to the guardianship of **Gabriel**. He directs it into the sphere of the **Moon**, which rains down moist and cold influences into the air, water, and earth, creating various and multiform "impressions" within them, namely winds, rains, and other such things.

Finally, the Tenth is called **ADONAI**, that is, "Lord." Its channel is *Malchut* <note>Malkuth</note>, that is, "Kingdom," from which this emanation descends into the sphere of souls (as the Kabbalists maintain), led by the soul of the **Messiah**. From there, it is finally carried down into the elements, where, for the most part, severe effects are produced on account of man’s disobedience.

At this point, I would have you know in passing that, according to the intentions of the Magi and Kabbalists, each of the aforesaid angels is a great Prince. They possess much liberty and power to dispose of these gifts of **GOD**, or these properties of His, either mercifully or severely according to His will among the creatures of this sublunary world. Their powers seem to increase according to their common and natural (or usual) disposition in the annual course, within the dominion of their planets and signs, and consequently in their ordained times—namely, the years, months, days, and hours—and in the elements, parts of the world, and the winds appropriated to them.

And certainly, to speak more truly, the dominion belongs neither to the signs nor the planets themselves; rather, it is a matter of a more abundant divine efflux, which reaches them more at one time than another according to the divine will. Consequently, the Angel or "Intelligence" of a planet or star is like its internal spirit moving it, whose central soul is that very emanation of divinity. The Angel is continually intoxicated by this emanation as if by divine nectar. Therefore, it is incorrectly said by those skilled in Magic that the Angels act under the dominion of a sign or planet; rather, it is that the sign and planet become stronger or more powerful according to the greater or lesser strength of their Intelligence in the divine emanation it receives. Furthermore, it must be understood that every one of these powerful Angels (seven of whom are said to stand before the face of God) dominates many legions, through which they are accustomed to act both in heaven and in the elementary region.

# On the Efficient Cause of Meteorological Phenomena.

Here, therefore, you have the sole and unique efficient cause of meteorological phenomena <term>Meteors: In the early modern period, this term referred to any atmospheric phenomenon (rain, snow, wind, lightning), not just falling stars.</term>, designated with its various instruments according to the varying nature of their emanation.

### In the empty space.

In the left part of the empty space, you have a triangle depicted and divided into several squares; the title inscribed on this triangle is as follows:
*Meteorological forecasting through the aspects of the planets among themselves and to the moon.* ☌. ✳. □. <note>These symbols represent the astrological "aspects" or angles: conjunction, sextile, and square.</note> In this triangle, at the margin of the left side, you will find these letters: V, Æ, A, H, which stand for Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter. <note>original: *Ver, Æstas, Autumnus, Hyems*</note>

Furthermore, in the right part of the empty space, you have a double mystery described within a single sphere: namely, the "gates of heaven," and then the "openings of the great valves" <note>A reference to the biblical concept of the "windows of heaven" opening to release rain or divine influence.</note>; regarding all of these, because ample mention was made in the 1st book of the 3rd section, *On the Celestial Efficient Cause of Meteorological Phenomena*, we do not intend to speak further in this place. Therefore, for a fuller explanation and exposition of these two mechanisms, I refer you to that book of the third section.

Concerning all that space that lies between heaven and earth, and the types of meteorological phenomena found in each of the specific regions of the air:

***

**Classification of Meteorological Phenomena Sketched in the Aerial Space of the Graphic Mirror:**

*   **Those that are seen and truly exist; these are either:**
    *   **Fiery phenomena**, categorized by their region:
        *   **Highest region:**
            *   **Comets**, of which there are various types: Horned <note>original: *Ceratias*</note>, Black, Tongs, Rose, Dawn, Soldier, Mercurial, Sword-shaped <note>original: *Xiphias*</note>, and the Spear.
            *   **The Chasm** <note>An opening or "gaping" in the sky, often referring to auroras.</note>
            *   **The Beam** <note>original: *Trabs*; a long, horizontal streak of light.</note>
            *   **Flying Sparks.**
        *   **Middle region:**
            *   **Lightning bolt** <note>original: *Fulmen*</note>.
            *   **Flash of light** <note>original: *Coruscatio*</note>.
            *   **The Prester** <note>A whirlwind or "fiery spout" associated with thunderous storms.</note>
        *   **Lowest region:**
            *   **Falling spark.**
            *   **Shooting stars.**
            *   **Leaping goats** <note>original: *Capræ saltantes*; a term for flickering, atmospheric lights.</note>
            *   **Will-o'-the-wisp** <note>original: *Ignis fatuus*</note>.
    *   **Watery phenomena**, categorized by their region:
        *   **Middle region:** Clouds, Rain, Snow, Hail.
        *   **Lowest region:** Vaporous air, Mist, Dew, Hoar-frost, Ice.

*   **Those that exist but are not seen, such as the winds, which are either:**
    *   **Common winds:** Occurring at fixed times, or generally from the four quarters of the world.
    *   **Sudden winds:** Such as the Whirlwind or the *Ecnephias* <note>A violent, sudden storm or hurricane breaking from a cloud.</note>.

-># Clear Exposition<-

**Things that seem to be and are not**, the explanation for which is drawn from the science of optics; and these are:

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
