# Section I. Portion IV. Part II. Book IV. Member I.

...[God] created GOD, the sun, the moon, the stars, and other things for the service of all the nations under heaven (*Deuteronomy 4*). It does not say that He created the Sun by His word and then afterwards created the other stars from the sun; rather, by His own word, according to His own specific arrangement and will, He created the sun separately along with the rest. For this reason, He made each of them different from the others in shape, property, and position; thus it is said that He counted the number of the stars and called them all by their names—our great Lord, who is of many strengths and virtues. By this, the Prophet <note>Likely referring to King David in the Psalms or Moses in the Pentateuch.</note> seems to hint that He assigned various names to them based on their various properties and virtues. We are persuaded of this because in the linking of the words, he says, "our Lord is great and of many virtues." 

So too, Adam is said to have given names to the beasts of the earth and the birds of the heaven—names which were undoubtedly not frivolous or empty, but suited to the property of each. By these things, we are reminded that all the stars in heaven were created distinctly from the sun, and yet on the same day—indeed, in almost the same moment—not otherwise than the earth and every species of plants and animals, though distinct from one another. These received from the supreme Creator a soul and a bodily existence distinct from the others; for in His word alone is the life and existence of every thing. And just as we see that the earth is illuminated at intervals and by turns from the solar face (which gives rise to the day in each hemisphere), so we are taught by daily experience that the moon receives its waxing and waning from the Sun’s brightness. Yet, it is certain that both the earth and the moon exist in themselves and in their own proper natures even when solar light is absent.

But here, finally, a twofold question may arise: do all the stars in Heaven receive their visible light from the Sun or not? And then, is any star altered or strengthened in its action or influence by its aspect <note>The angular relationship between two celestial bodies in astrology.</note> or by the shining virtue of the Sun? To both questions together we say (as has been reported by us before) that Cicero and others assign a proper light and splendor to all stars, with only one exception <note>Presumably the Moon.</note>. However, the greater crowd of philosophers maintains that the stars have very little proper light or beauty of their own from their creation, but they frequently say that they are kindled and illuminated by the Sun; for this reason, *Heraclitus* <note>A pre-Socratic Greek philosopher known for his doctrines on change and fire.</note> called the Sun the fountain of heavenly light.

But regarding our own opinion, we say either that this last opinion of the philosophers appears false and inconsistent, or that the history told by Eusebius <note>Eusebius of Caesarea, a 4th-century historian, who recorded various accounts of an eclipse occurring during the Crucifixion.</note> regarding the universal eclipse of the Sun is far from the truth and a mere fable. In that history, he tells that the day was turned into a dark night, so much so that the stars were seen in the sky. Therefore, if this eclipse was that universal one during the passion of our Lord Jesus Christ in that very hour—as he himself seems to imply—in which there was no intervention of the moon <note>A solar eclipse usually requires a New Moon, but the Crucifixion occurred at Passover, during a Full Moon, making the darkness "miraculous" rather than a standard eclipse.</note>, it follows that this was a true failure of solar light. Consequently, the Sun, which had no light in itself to give, could not give light to the others as they likewise failed; yet even in that same failure, the bright stars showed themselves to the eyes of men.

In any case, it is likely that although some of the stars may have had sparks of light for their own ornament at the moment of their creation, they nevertheless receive a notable and excellent splendor from the solar rays (when not suppressed by any failure of their own), not otherwise than can be seen in the globe of the earth and the moon. But truly, since the supreme activity of every thing—whether greater or lesser—is discerned in the increase or decrease of its light, it is certain that the force and virtue of any of the wandering stars <note>The planets.</note>, or indeed even the fixed stars, becomes more fit and inclined to pour out such and such influences (whether simple or fixed) upon the lower regions through the conjunction of rays, or through opposition, or through the trine, square, or sextile aspect <note>Various astrological angles: trine (120°), square (90°), and sextile (60°).</note>. For example, the Sun coming together with Saturn produces sad, melancholic, and heavier effects, both in the higher elements and on the earth itself. For this reason, at such a time, the demons or angels of Saturn will have stronger effects in the elements, because the great angel *Metattron* <note>Metatron, often associated with the presence of God or the highest celestial scribe.</note> or *Michael*, the Prince of the entire heavenly host, who is the presiding officer of the sun, seems to assign dominion to the prince of the globe of Saturn—namely, *Caphieli* <note>Also known as Cassiel, the angel of Saturn.</note>—over both the ethereal and elemental world; and so it is with the others.

Furthermore, the various effects of the Sun as it runs through each house <note>The signs of the Zodiac.</note> are observed very clearly every year; for example, when passing through Aries, it is accustomed to bring about dry and violent winds (the kind that usually blow in the month of March), and so it is with the others.

However, the essential cause of this effect is the will of GOD, dwelling in the solar organ. By His gaze and intuition alone—or by the ray sent out to the center of a star or some organ—and along with that divine spark reigning in it, which assigns life and being to the whole composite, it is immediately and joyfully received with obedience, as if by a messenger and brother of the same uncreated parent from whom that spark of light was derived. Hence, like rejoices in like, and nature delights in nature; whereby the whole nature of the stellar body, and the spirits <note>original: "dæmones" — here used in the classical sense of intermediary spirits or intelligences, not necessarily evil beings.</note> ordered for the service of that star, are suddenly snatched up to fulfill and perfect the will of the Emperor in the ordinary course of the world. This occurs whether it be in producing winds, or in drawing forth and bringing out rains, hail, snow, frost, or rime from the treasury of GOD, or finally in generating lightning, thunderbolts, thunder, comets, and other fiery meteors, both manifest and hidden. We have expressed a model of this assertion here, for the better understanding of the readers' capacity, in the production of winds; in which demonstration the ray of the will...

# On the Efficient Cause of Meteors.

Thus it is said that **GOD** has placed his tabernacle in the sun, <note>This refers to Psalm 19:4, which in the Latin Vulgate tradition was often interpreted as God setting His dwelling place in the solar disk.</note> and for this reason it is said elsewhere that every thing claims as much of **GOD** for itself as it is capable of receiving light. <margin>Jehovah <note>original: "יהוה"</note></margin>
In the aforementioned demonstration <note>Referring to the woodcut image.</note> we therefore have an image of three persons of one essence: namely, the fountain of the divine essence as the Father, existing outside of all things; the Word or emanation from the fountain, as the Son, existing both within and outside all things (insofar as he is not divided from the Father, and by whom the heavens were made firm); and the Holy Spirit of discipline, flowing into all virtues or forms from every side. The Spirit, while arranging his tabernacle in the sun, is nevertheless not confined within the sun; he is in all things and outside all things, insofar as he proceeds from the fountain and the emanation simultaneously, yet his essence is not divided from them, as it is an indivisible essence in all things.

And in this way you have it demonstrated how **GOD** gives life and inspiration and all things to everyone, and by what reason *in him we live, move, and have our being,* as in Acts 17. Similarly, how *there is one God the Father, from whom all things come,* in 1 Corinthians 8. It is not that we are born from the sun, but that man—the Lord of all creatures—is adorned in his own spirit with such an inspiration as the sun, which is the fullest vessel of the glory of the Most High. Indeed, all remaining creatures, although they have not received this divine gift in the same measure as the sun and man, are for this reason both called "sons of God."

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the Sun’s role as the vessel of divine light, shifting from its general governance of the universe (the Macrocosm) to its specific influence and counterpart within the human being (the Microcosm). # Concerning the Efficient Cause of Meteors.

## CHAPTER XVII.

->*That **GOD** created the microcosmic sun as well, by whose rays—illuminated by **GOD**—He is sometimes accustomed to perform miracles beyond the laws of nature, and greater ones than that macrocosmic Sun, which was established for the ordinary reckoning of the year and seasons. Finally, that the Sun of the invisible, everywhere-present One (by whom those other suns are illuminated) performs even greater things.*<-

---

From what we have stated above regarding the properties of the sun, it has been clearly explained that **GOD** made the sun for the power of the day (Psalm 136:8); that is, so that it might look upon all things with its illumination, and similarly so that the days might be separated, as well as light and the years. Nevertheless, this was accomplished by the Lord through the science operating within the sun (Ecclesiasticus 33), as He is the one who placed His tabernacle within it (Psalm 19). Furthermore, we have also said that worldly things are revived, multiplied, and heated by means of the sun’s central virtue. We have already expressed above—and will explain a little more extensively below—how both the earth and the heavens and the air are affected by its various properties according to its different aspects, namely, how they are sometimes disturbed and agitated by every kind of meteor. <note>In the 17th century, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomena, including rain, wind, lightning, and snow, not just falling stars.</note> All these things are so regular and ordinary in the course of nature that we would say they are produced not miraculously, but according to the paths of nature. Thus, not only Astrologers (by the varying positions of the stars) but even common people and farmers are accustomed to predict and foresee these worldly accidents through diverse observations.

But truly, since **GOD** established the temple of His Holy Spirit in the external part of man—in whose body, though it be base, Jesus is said to dwell—He acts by His own particular and proper breath, just as He placed His tabernacle in the worldly sun. Therefore, without a doubt, **JEHOVAH** acts as wonderfully in man through His wisdom (dwelling in man's internal spirit) as He does through that wisdom dwelling in the solar spirit of the world. For the **WORKS OF GOD** which He performs in wisdom are everywhere wonderful. Nevertheless, we shall find, if we look into the matter a little more accurately, that the delights and pleasures of wisdom are with the sons of men (Proverbs 8).

Whence, in man and by means of his "organ" <note>Referring to the human body and soul as a musical instrument or tool for divine action.</note>, He is accustomed to bring forth far greater things than in the worldly sun. Indeed, this virtue of His is so excellent above that of the world, that the worldly sun is observed at times to show remarkable obedience to it. Thus Joshua said—or rather the Word of **GOD**, or this Holy Spirit of discipline dwelling in Joshua: *“Sun, stand still over Gibeon; do not move,” and the Sun stood still in the middle of heaven* (Joshua 10), <note>original: "Sol sta contra Gabaon, ne mouearis, & Sol stetit in medio cœli"</note> and it did not hasten to set for the space of an entire day. Furthermore, by the prayer of Hezekiah, his spirit was so pleasing before **GOD** that the Sun was compelled to retreat in its natural course and return against the laws of nature (Isaiah 38).

Furthermore, although it is within the power of the sun to produce clouds and winds, and that in the ordinary way, it is within the power of the illuminated spirit to produce even greater things. For when the heavens were like brass and no rain was granted by God to the children of Israel, by the virtue of that spirit reigning in Elijah, a small cloud like a man’s hand rose out of the sea, and immediately the heavens were darkened with clouds and wind, from which came a great rain (1 Kings 18:41). So also, lightning descending from heaven by the virtue of Elijah destroyed the captain with his fifty men (2 Kings 1:12). So too, by that spirit operating in Moses, thunders and hails were sent from heaven; for when Moses extended his staff toward heaven, **Jehovah** sent hail and sounds, and fire ran along the ground (Exodus 9). And by the virtue of that spirit in those three chosen and illuminated men cast into the fiery furnace, all the violence of the fire was taken away, so that it did not burn them at all. And by this most powerful spirit in Christ, the stormy tempest of the sea was mitigated in a moment, demons were cast out of human bodies, diseases miserably afflicting the wretched were cured, the dead were called back to life, fish and loaves were multiplied, water was changed into wine, and finally—which is the miracle above all—the madness of death and the devil was suppressed, the mortal body was made incorruptible and immortal, and at last the worldly and celestial sun itself was compelled to suffer at the passion of that body and be deprived of its light.

Hence it was that the Philosopher <note>Commonly referring to Aristotle.</note> confessed in the second book of the *Ethics* that man is of such excellence and sublimity that he is, in a way, the end of all things. And Hermes Trismegistus <note>A legendary Hellenistic figure associated with a syncretic blend of the Greek god Hermes and the Egyptian god Thoth, credited with foundational texts on alchemy and philosophy.</note> says that man is a great miracle, an animal to be adored and honored, for he passes into the nature of **GOD**, and is as if he were **GOD** himself. And Zoroaster says: you must ascend to the light itself and to the Father’s rays, from whence the soul was sent to you, clothed in much mind. And in another place, Hermes Trismegistus says: you must ascend above the heavens and be far from the choirs of demons. And Pythagoras says: if you, leaving the body, pass into the free ether, you will be an immortal **GOD**. But the Holy Scriptures describe this more clearly, saying: *He who adheres to **GOD** shall become one spirit with Him*, and elsewhere: *At last we shall be transformed into the same image.* Finally, as pertains to the other acts and wonderful operations of the illuminated human mind, from which it is manifest that the internal man is more excellent in dignity and efficacy than the worldly sun...

...and he is to be preferred because of that most holy gift, namely that God-like breath <note>original: *spiraculum scilicet Deiforme*</note> which was imparted to him by the Creator.

Hence, we also read in scripture that all creatures were ordained by the Creator for the use of humans; and we are told by a holy priest <note>Likely referring to a Church Father like Basil or Ambrose</note> that the sun was created on the fourth day specifically to serve the man who was to come. We could discuss infinite matters concerning these things here, but since the Holy Scriptures are filled with them everywhere, we shall return to the power of the said illuminated spirit in its "aerial house." This spirit is present everywhere throughout the world and fills all things, according to that saying of the Prophet: *To you, the Seraphim and Cherubim do not cease to cry out: Heaven and earth are full of the majesty of your glory.* <note>This is the "Sanctus," a hymn based on Isaiah 6:3 used in Christian liturgy.</note> Therefore, it also works everywhere according to its good pleasure, commanding its angels as ministers who carry out its word and will—whether to produce fiery, windy, cloudy, or snowy meteors <term>meteors: in the 17th century, this referred to any atmospheric phenomena like rain, wind, or lightning</term> to fulfill its desires. This happens sometimes from its tabernacle in the Sun, sometimes from the human tabernacle, and often from that vast worldly spirit which it fills everywhere, saying "Let it be," and it is done. That is to say, by darting a ray of its will toward this or that region of the world, the angel having dominion over that quarter is immediately moved and sends forth its windy legions to fulfill the commands and will of its most high Lord. Hence the royal Prophet says: *Angels of God, most mighty in strength, doing His word, hearkening to the voice of His word, hosts or ministers doing His pleasure. (Psalm 103:20).* And elsewhere: *Who makes your angels winds, and your ministers a burning fire. (Psalm 104:4).* Regarding this, Baruch also says: *The wind that blows through all regions obeys God in its blowing.* But we shall speak more extensively on these matters below.

### CHAPTER XVIII.
#### *How the wisdom of God is the first author and actor of the winds, both in the Microcosm and the Macrocosm.*

In the preceding chapter, we stated that angels are sometimes winds and sometimes burning flames. However, we shall declare more fully in the following section how that Great Angel—who is the emanation or brightness of the Almighty's power—is the great Lord over these angels and governs them to carry out the Father's will in the form of winds. Truly we read *that God, or Divine Wisdom, bowed the heavens and descended, with darkness under His feet; and He ascended upon a Cherub, and flew or glided upon the wings of the wind (2 Samuel 22:10-11 and Psalm 104).* From this discourse, it is clear that just as the Seraphim are ministers burning with fiery love and serving before God, so too the Cherubim are aerial ministers through whose action or motion in the air the winds are produced. Hence it was said that *He ascended upon the Cherubim and flew upon the wings of the wind,* which refers to the aerial spirits existing under the power of the Cherubim and having authority in the air. Therefore, the winds are said by the Prophet *to carry out the commands of God (Baruch 5:60).* 

We described this matter more fully before: how the will of God, included in the word "Let there be" <note>the Latin *Fiat*</note>, moves and is sent forth with the utterance of the Word to any creature. When it joins with the spark of that Word or Spirit inhabiting that creature (both for its formation and preservation), it carries that creature away entirely to fulfill the will of the Creator without any resistance. This cannot be otherwise, because God is the sole actor in every creature. Thus it happens that a creature, whether spiritual like the angels or corporeal, is always ready to fulfill the will of God—that is, to carry out His Word and consequently His pleasure, according to the passage cited above: *Angels of God, most mighty in strength, doing His word, hearkening to the voice of His word, that is, doing His pleasure by the word. (Psalm 103:20).* 

And therefore, these intelligences are called "winds" insofar as the air is disturbed by their breath and motion through the divine will; it is said to move from that quarter of the world from which these angelic spirits carry the Spirit of Wisdom, at whose nod they are moved wherever or whenever He wishes. Hence it is said: *By His will the South wind breathed (Ecclesiasticus 43:17).* But elsewhere he says in even clearer speech: *He who assigns a weight to the air (or wind), and weighs the waters by measure, establishes a law for the rain, and a path for the lightning of the thunder.* By this speech it is denoted that God, by His wisdom, fits the air in its light nature and, by agitating it through His ministers, produces the winds. By compressing it to a denser degree, He procreates clouds, from which rain later arises. Also, by another adaptation and shaping of the air, He produces the lightning and the thunder; for His flame-vomiting ministers are the formal causes of the inflamed air, just as they themselves are called winds in their invisible nature, which are heard but not seen. 

From this, it is certain that the internal act of the winds or angels disturbing the air comes immediately from God—that is, the ray of the divine will joined with His own ray, which is of the same essence. For this reason, it is necessary that they be moved and incited with all their effort to fulfill the divine will. Consequently, the truly efficient cause of winds, thunders, rains, comets, and other such meteors is referred to God and not to the creatures themselves, who indeed do not know how to move unless they are moved by God. *For in God we live, in God we move, and we are (Acts 17:28).* For it is God alone who is rightly said *to work all things in all (1 Corinthians 12).* And although this act is sometimes assigned to the creature, that speech must be understood as referring to that incorruptible spirit which acts primarily and centrally in every thing; for since this spirit, according to the assertion of the Wise Man...

...wisdom is present in every thing <note>original: *Sap. 12. 1.* referring to the Wisdom of Solomon: "For your incorruptible spirit is in all things."</note> of this world, and since this spirit is more mobile than any other thing <note>original: *Sap. 7. 8.*</note> and, as he says in another place, where he also acknowledges it to be a certain pure emanation of the brightness of the Almighty, we are bound to believe that this spirit, just as it was the first acting force in the world, so also it moved first in every particle of the world, in no other way than the first movable thing in the world received its action from this spirit. Thus, in the leading of the Israelites through the desert, it is sometimes said they were led by the direction of an angel, and sometimes with JEHOVAH going before and occasionally directing them, with a pillar of fire by night and a shadowing cloud by day; and yet, in truth, it was Wisdom alone covered in a created garment, whence she herself said, *My throne is in a pillar of cloud*, and Wisdom was a covering by day and the light of the stars by night <note>original: *Sap. 10. 17.*</note>. So also it is commonly said that the sun illuminates and warms, and by the Cabalists <note>Practitioners of Kabbalah, a Jewish mystical tradition that heavily influenced Renaissance thinkers.</note> this duty is attributed to the angel Michael who presides over the sun—or, more truly, it is attributed to divine wisdom. Wisdom, establishing a tabernacle in the sun—that is, revealing itself abundantly and primarily in that worldly organ, and acting centrally in it and from it—truly performs those things attributed to the sun: namely, it warms by its own motion (as it is more mobile than any other thing) and illuminates by its own super-eminent splendor, which is far more excellent than the brightness of the sun or stars. In Wisdom <note>original: *Sap. 7.*</note> consists the power of the elements, the beginning, middle, and end of times, the solstices, the changes and varieties of the seasons, the circuits of the years, the positions of the stars, the forces of the winds or spirits, etc. Therefore, it is evident that it is the spirit of wisdom itself, or the emanation of the brightness of the Almighty in the sun, and not the sun as a mere creature, which does all these things in the world. In the same respect, it is neither the Sun by its own property (though the winds are called the children of Titan and Aurora <note>A reference to Greek mythology: Titan (the sun) and Aurora (the dawn) were the parents of the winds.</note>), nor the Angel Gabriel presiding over the Northern quarter, nor Uriel ruling that of the South, who makes the wind, nor the spirits Egin or Anaymon <note>Traditional names for "Kings of the Winds" found in medieval and Renaissance occult grimoires.</note> who are subject to them, nor the air itself which is the consistency of the wind, but Wisdom herself, who by her look alone does all things according to her pleasure. *God* (says David) *is in the heavens themselves; he does whatever pleases him* <note>original: *Pfal. 143.*</note>. And elsewhere: *Whatever he wills he does in the heavens, on the earth, through the seas, and all the abysses* <note>original: *Pſ. 135. 7.*</note>. The reason is constant: namely, because Wisdom herself is the only truth, emanating from the source of all truth, and all things were made and informed by this light, in which alone there is life. From this it is clear that, just as all the sparks of the divine light are not divided from one another in essence—for there is only one and individual essence in the Deity, although its property is threefold—so indeed it is necessary that all sparks or rays gushing from a single source should be of one will and effort with it. Hence they seize the creature they inhabit and rule in every way, like created organs for those things which are to be perfected either in the heavens or on the earth, according to the will of the Father who is in the highest heavens and above all imagination. Hence it is said in the person of Christ, the true Wisdom: *I came down from heaven to do the will of the Father who is in heaven.* We proceed thus to our subject: we say that the winds are not improperly, but indeed most properly, said to proceed and be derived from the mouth of Jehovah—that is, from the immediate act of divine wisdom—and that they do not come to us mortals vainly or by chance, but to perform the pleasure of Him who sent them. To confirm the first part of this assertion, we have the Holy Scripture speaking in various places in this manner: *The wind (or spirit) blows where it wishes, and you hear its voice, but you do not know where it comes from or where it goes* <note>original: *Ioan. 3. 8.* (John 3:8)</note>. By which words it seems to argue that the spirit is received by the spirit of the breather, and that this breather is God-like, because it is said to breathe according to its own will; finally, that the end of this motion in the air or the place toward which it tends is hidden and known only to the breather. Nevertheless, it is certain that it was created to perform the commands of the breather, as the Prophet has it <note>original: *Baruch. 3.*</note>. That it is the spirit, as it were, of the breather is gathered from this, because we find these things written: *By the blast of your nostrils the waters were heaped up... you blew with your wind and the sea covered them* <note>original: *Exod. 15. 8.*</note>. And in another place: *God breathes out his wind, sending forth his word* <note>original: *Pſ. 147. 13.*</note>. From these words we can conclude that God, by means of his word, excited the soul of the wind to complete the will of the Father; for the ray or aspect of the divine will is sent forth to the minister presiding over the wind, and uniting itself to the ray of the creature, it suddenly seizes it to complete His will. In the same sense it is said that *by the breath of God frost is produced* <note>original: *Iob 37. 10.*</note>; that is, by the breathing of the divine will, the North wind is incited by its minister Gabriel to produce and create frost, whence in the preceding verse he said: *from the inner chambers comes the storm, and cold from the North star,* etc. So also elsewhere it is said that the *wind proceeding from Jehovah scattered the quails snatched from the sea* <note>original: *Nu. 11. 31.*</note>. But this is best declared by the appearance of that almighty spirit to the Apostles, in which it is said that *suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled the house where they were sitting, and there appeared to them divided tongues as of fire, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit* <note>original: *Act. 2. 2.*</note>. Here, then, we have the soul and reason of the winds: the disturbance and motion of the air, as it is the most mobile of all mobile things; whence in its motion, by dilating the air, it shakes and pushes it more or less, by reason of its own act. This act is also the spirit of spirits, inspiring, moving, and agitating all things; thus it is said that Adam heard the voice of Jehovah walking through the garden *to the wind of that day* <note>original: *Gen. 4. 2.*</note>. And elsewhere: *Behold, Jehovah passed by, and a great and strong wind, breaking the mountains and shattering the rocks before Jehovah* <note>original: *1. Reg. 19.* (1 Kings 19)</note>. And elsewhere it is said that *Jehovah flies upon the wings of the wind* <note>original: *Pſ. 18. 8.*</note>, as if one were to say that He, flying in the air, sometimes seizes the air with Him in the manner of a wind. ### Section I, Portion IV, Part II. Book IV. Member I. 194

This is created by the agitation and action of the Word, or divine wisdom, acting like a sun in the center of the world. This happens immediately <note>without any intervening physical steps</note>, with no sublunary <note>earthly or below-the-moon</note> causes coming between them, as the *Peripatetics* <note>Followers of Aristotle’s philosophy, which emphasized physical cause-and-effect</note> and the Christian philosophers of our own century have falsely believed.

We conclude, therefore, that nothing is clearer or more certain than that the winds are both ordained by God and procreated within His wisdom; and finally, they are sent out into the open air of the world to execute the will of the Creator. This is indicated in the Sacred Fountain <note>the Bible</note> in express words in this manner: the *Psalmist* says, *God brings forth the wind from his treasuries* <note>original: "Deus depromit ventum è thęſauris ſuis"</note>: Psalm 135:7. And elsewhere: *He directed the east wind in the heavens and by his power brought in the south wind*, Psalm 78:26. Job also says that *God made a weight for the winds*, Job 28:25. And Moses: *God sent a wind so that the waters might subside*, Genesis 8. And elsewhere: *Jehovah brought an east wind into the land all 그 day, etc.* Exodus 10, and *He sent a strong west wind, etc.* And elsewhere: *A wind went forth from Jehovah and scattered quails from the sea toward the camp*, Numbers 11:31. And so it is in other passages, from which it is clear enough that all winds come immediately from God; they can by no means move or blow unless they are animated and incited by Him. 

Here it must especially be noted that God emits His ray, which produces these worldly blasts, from His various "organs." For instance, sometimes it comes from a dense cloud, as in a *storm-cloud* <note>original: "Ecnephia"</note>, a *whirlwind* <note>original: "prestere"</note>, or a tempest; and also blasts derived from His lightning, for when lightning or thunder has more or less finished during the day, winds are very often accustomed to follow. Furthermore, it is also said that God flies upon the wings of the winds in the time of thunder, as will be discussed more fully below. Sometimes He accomplishes the effects of His will through the human "temple" in the form of wind, or in the suppression of winds: *Then*, says *Matthew*, *Jesus, rising, commanded the winds and the sea, and there was a great calm*, Matthew 8. Similarly, from the spiritual temple of *Elijah*, He emits His ray to bring clouds and winds into the sky. 

From this, therefore, the infinite power of the illuminated man is declared, which is accustomed to operate against the foreknowledge of Augurs, soothsayers, and Astrologers. Regarding this spirit of the illuminated man, *Daniel* speaks thus: *The King asks about a mystery; the wise men, magi, soothsayers, and diviners are unable to show you what is to come; but there is a God in heaven revealing mysteries*, that is, in both the *Microcosmic* <note>the world of the human being</note> and *Macrocosmic* <note>the universe at large</note> heaven. From this spirit, *Daniel* explained the dream and performed many other miracles, which the wise men of this world could not understand by their own prudence. 

Finally, He is accustomed to emit His power from His excellent *Macrocosmic* organ to constantly govern the nature of the world, preserving it according to the laws ordained by Him in the beginning. Thus, the worldly spirit is rotated by His internal spirit, which is also gathered from these words of the wise man: *The sun, surveying all things in its circuit, the spirit moves on and returns to its circles*, Ecclesiastes 1:6. Furthermore, we gather from these words of the *Prophet* that this spirit, which emits the winds from the four quarters of the world, is one and not many, even though it is said to blow from different places: *Come, spirit, and breathe upon these slain, that they may live again*, Ezekiel 37. By these words, he indicates that there is only one breather, or infusing spirit, though the winds are various—but let us return to the point. 

We see, taught by experience, that different ordinary winds are agitated every year by the worldly sun, according to its varying positions. It is observed every year that in the hottest time of summer, when the sun enters the first part of Leo, the Dog Star <note>original: "canicula"</note> rises; this is usually preceded for eight days by those North winds which they call *Prodromos* <note>original: "Prodromos," meaning forerunners</note>, because they run before the *Etesians* <note>seasonal Mediterranean winds</note>. For two days after the rising of the Dog Star, those winds called *Etesians* begin, which are North winds lasting for eight days. So too, the setting of the constellation of the *Pleiades* <note>original: "Vergiliarum"</note>, which occurs 44 days after the autumn equinox, begins the Winter, which the wintry North wind <note>original: "Aquilo"</note> usually accompanies. Note also that the South winds follow the *Etesians* and last until the rising of the star *Arcturus* (which rises eleven days before the autumn equinox). Furthermore, in the spring, the West wind <note>original: "Favonius"</note> is said to blow more frequently from the western corner in the early part of the season, and the East wind <note>original: "subsolanus"</note> from the east around the rising of the *Pleiades*, which rise in the 26th degree of Taurus; and so on with the others. 

In these things, we see how the worldly winds are excited in a customary manner from different quarters of the world by grace of the sun’s rays. The sun receives its rays in different ways upon different objects in the heaven—both by its own property and by the various methods of reflection, as well as by the diverse mixing of celestial natures. All these objects, animated and made "pregnant" as it were by the solar rays, rain down forces into the sublunary air that differ from each other in nature and condition. This happens by the Creator's annual decree placed in the sun, whose internal spirit—acting as the rector and governor of the entire world—acts in various ways upon the world's spirit. Thus, the various natures within it, weighed in the equal scales of the Creator's justice, might be respected and preserved. In this way, the various species of things in heaven, on earth, in the sea, and in the air are generated, multiplied, sustained, and altered by corruption according to the Order of Nature. All these actions in the world depend on the Word of the Lord, who *placed his tabernacle in the sun*—that exalted and eternal spirit, I say, creating the heavens, stretching them out, establishing the earth and what sprouts from it, giving breath to the people upon it, and spirit to those who walk on it, Isaiah 42:5. Of Him it is said: *God does according to His will both in the powers of heaven and in the inhabitants of the earth, and there is none who may resist His hand or say, "Why have you done this?"*, Daniel 4. 

That all these things which seem to be ejected by the Sun are the works of God, and not of any other creature, we gather from these words of the holy Priest: *The strongest God, who is truth, turns the heaven in a circle*, 3 Esdras 4. Similarly, the wise man says: *The appearance of the heaven is the glory of the stars, illuminating the world in the highest, God, etc. has circled the heaven in the circuit of his glory, the hands of the Most High have opened it, etc.* Ecclesiastes 43 <note>Sirach/Ecclesiasticus</note>. Consequently, every influence from the heavens, every structure on the lands or in the sea, or every imperfect mixture in the air, is undoubtedly from God (with no subordinate cause placed in between), who is the author of all things, from whom, in whom, and through whom all things exist, as the *Apostle* <note>St. Paul</note> holds.

# On the Efficient Cause of Meteors.
<sig>Bb 2</sig>

Therefore, I leave it to you—elevated as you are on the more precise wings of doctrine and the knowledge of truth—to consider how ridiculous the schools of the Peripatetics <note>Followers of Aristotle’s philosophy, who emphasized physical cause-and-effect over spiritual origins</note> are, when they devise so many fantastic efficient causes for the winds: namely, a hot exhalation seeking the heights, the heat of the sun lifting and calling it up from the earth, and the intense cold of the middle region of the air.

---

### ->*A Relational Argument to Man, in which it is proved that GOD is also the sole and unique author of the winds to be produced in the Microcosm.*<-

Not without reason was man called **the microcosm** <note>original Greek: ὁ μικρόκοσμος, meaning "the little world"</note> by the Philosopher, insofar as he possesses the greatest likeness and analogy to the great world <note>the Macrocosm, or the universe</note>. For man enjoys the same elements as the world, which are accustomed to act and be acted upon through similar actions and passions, both in the one world and the other. Indeed, it seems that the lesser world <note>man</note> received the parts of its substance and being from that greater world, if we consider the matter a little more accurately; for in time and order, the greater world preceded the lesser. Whence *Hermes Trismegistus* <note>A legendary Hellenistic figure associated with ancient wisdom and alchemy</note> did not hesitate to repeatedly call man "the son of the world," just as the world is "the son of GOD." And indeed, if we carefully weigh the words of the Prophet, we shall find them pertaining to the Philosopher’s proposition; for in the resurrection of the bones, he speaks thus: <margin>Ezekiel 37</margin> **"Come from the four winds, O spirit, and breathe upon these slain, that they may live." Ezekiel 37.** By these words, he seems to imply that life comes from that spirit which God bestowed upon the world for its existence and vivification. However this may be, it is a certain and well-worn truth that just as God created the one by His own breath of life, so He also created the other. That is, just as the Spirit of the Lord, which moved upon the waters in the great world, provided them with fiery vigor and created and animated its humid spirit, so indeed, for the creation of man, He breathed the breath of life into the created spirit of man, whence man was made into a living soul. **"I," says God, "creating the heavens and establishing the earth and those things which sprout from it, give breath to the people who are upon it." Isaiah 42:5.** <margin>Isaiah 42:5</margin> From these things we gather that the life not only of the world but also of man took its beginning from the wind, or divine inspiration.

Furthermore, just as we see the common spirit of the world divided into four elements, so too we see that not only the human spirit (which we also call air) but also the body participates in these elements. In fact, we see that the air of both the one world and the other enjoys its own proper sun: for the heart performs its duty in the human spirit no differently than the Macrocosmic sun does in its own. But truly, we see with open eyes that just as man’s first power was from the inspiration of Him who "set his tabernacle in the sun," and man received the parts of his constitution from the air and elements of the world, it is necessary that there be a continuous relationship both between the incorruptible spirit in the sun and that in the heart—seeing as both are but a single thing in essence—and also between the air of the world and that of man. Both are from one and the same fountain, and both enter into this same common duty toward each other: namely, that the luminous spirit of the Creator may fly upon the wings of either wind or spirit, and be carried as if in a vehicle or chariot. 

And just as in the world that aerial spirit is divided into three regions, one of which is placed before another in dignity and purity, so indeed is this spirit in man divided: into the **animal and intellectual spirit** in the brain (referring to the highest heaven, the Empyrean or Angelic spirit of the world); the **vital spirit** in the heart (compared to that ethereal world of the sun); and the **natural spirit** in the liver (having respect to the sublunary <note>earthly</note> region of the world). 

From this it arises that there is such great proximity—nay, even continuity—between these two spirits and luminous souls (which are in effect of one essence governing them), that in later times the Microcosm <note>man</note> cannot exist without the assistance and presence of the former <note>the world</note>. For this reason, Heraclitus said not foolishly: "If you take the Sun out of the world, what is our little body?" If the soul is absent, no pulsating vein is drawn there, no vital breath, no breathing at all. And this is why the Philosopher <note>Aristotle</note> thought that man could not be generated by man unless the sun assisted, etc. Whence his axiom: **The sun and man generate man.** <note>original Latin: "Sol & homo generant hominem." A famous Aristotelian principle suggesting celestial influence is necessary for biological reproduction.</note> 

For this reason, therefore, man (since we are now dealing with his sympathy with the mundane spirit) is said to live as long as he breathes. Therefore, antiquity rightly ascribed the **spirits**—which the more excellent of the physicians estimate to be the "innate heat" moving the body, exciting the senses, and nourishing thoughts and minds—to the venerable Sun. The Sun moves all things as an instrument and is the organic cause of all living things through that incomparable spirit that inhabits its center. These spirits, according to the testimony of Homer, are said to be present in us daily in such a way as the mundane Sun, the Prince of planets, breathes out, moves, irradiates, and prepares, cooks, and refines through the middle of the sublunary air. 

Which air alone (I say), because according to the testimony of Hippocrates <note>The "Father of Medicine"</note> and even experience itself, whatever its quality may be, we are compelled—willingly or not—continually and necessarily to breathe in. By the help of the lungs, we draw it through the mouth and the windpipe, and from there we send it out again into the left chamber of the heart (which is very full of the spirits that animate the body and restore and cherish the animal power); moreover, we receive it into the brain through the nostrils, and into the entire body, which is altogether "conspirable" <note>capable of breathing together</note>, through the junctions and pores of the arteries. It is from this, therefore, that according to the state of the air in the sky and the sun in the air, we also find our own spirit disposed everywhere in the blood, the viscera, and wandering through the flesh—for example, according to the motion and temperature of the air depending on the sun and the entire face of the heaven on a given day...

The author is specifically linking human moods and health to the movements of the winds and divine light, drawing on both classical poetry and Kabbalistic theology.</meta>

Sect. I. Port. IV. Part. II. Lib. IV. Membr. I.

...more in one than in another, we shall feel our **spirits** <note>In this period, "spirits" refers to the subtle fluids believed to circulate through the nerves, connecting the soul to the body</note> either more dull, slower, and more prone to melancholy, or sharper, lighter, and more inclined toward joy. This is something that can be seen and noticed not only in humans, but even in the **animals** themselves. For it is natural for beasts and birds to be cheered by clear air and a bright sky, to sing and, as it were, to smile; but they become saddened and seem to groan under a dark, gloomy, and cloudy sky when rain is coming. This is confirmed for us by the following speech of the poet:

> But when the storm and the shifting moisture of the sky
> Have changed their paths, and Jupiter, damp with the south winds,
> Condenses what was just now thin, and thins what was dense,
> The appearances of their minds are turned, and their hearts now conceive
> Other motions—different from when the wind drove the clouds.
> From this comes that chorus of birds in the fields,
> The happy cattle, and the crows exulting from their throats.
> <note>original: "Verum ubi tempestas & cœli mobilis humor / Mutauere vias..." — a famous passage from Virgil's *Georgics*, Book I, describing how animals sense changes in the atmosphere.</note>

From this it is clear that the spirits of men are refreshed by the brightness of the world’s light. On the other hand, the sublunary world <note>the Earthly realm below the moon</note> itself seems to be refreshed and rejoice at the bright gaze of the sun. Because of the presence of divine glory—which is most full of divinity in the sun—every spirit, both in the world and in the creatures within it, is irradiated, exults, is stirred, and seems to leap with joy. For there is a perpetual appetite in matter to be shaped by the beauty and the bright presence of the Creator. Thus, the more it is deprived of Him by gloomy darkness, the more it is disturbed; it seems to approach the boundaries of **privation** <note>The state of being "without" light or form, often associated with chaos or non-existence</note> and, consequently, to distance itself from the bright act of the Creator. Yet, as **Augustine** and others testify, the more light something has within itself, the more of God it seems to claim for itself. 

It is for this reason, therefore, that in gloomy, thick, and dark air, the lower world seems to mourn, to be disturbed, and to be saddened. Through a "consensus" and a close "kinship" (so to speak), the spirit of man also seems to fall ill and be disturbed. Thus, even in bodies that have not strayed far beyond the limits of health, they seem to be affected by sadness, heaviness, and an unexpected sort of grief—as if one were to say that when God hides the splendor of His face, both the spirit of the world and the creatures of that world are affected by the sickness of grief and sadness. Indeed, we read this very thing in the express words of the Prophet: *All creatures look to God; when God gives to them, they gather it; when He sends forth His spirit, they are recreated; when He hides His face, they are troubled; when He takes back their spirit, they expire. Psalm 104.* <note>The author is quoting the Vulgate version of Psalm 104 (Psalm 103 in the Catholic tradition), which emphasizes nature's total dependence on God's breath/spirit.</note> This discourse applies both to the visible light which takes its origin from God (and is the visible image of the invisible light) and to that invisible light from which we primarily received our life and Being.

But I shall gird myself more closely to the matter at hand. I say that if such a relationship exists between the spirits of both worlds <note>the Macrocosm and Microcosm</note>, and if the life of both is an inspiration, or a breath and life-giving wind proceeding from the mouth of the Almighty—and if the disturbances of one follow the disturbances of the other—then it must follow that various agitations of the winds or air in the one produce similar effects in the other. 

Regarding the **microcosmic winds** <note>internal bodily "winds" or gases</note> and their four quarters corresponding to those of the greater world, we have spoken clearly in our treatise *On the Mystical Anatomy* <note>Latin: *De anatomia mystica*, one of the author's specific works on the spiritual nature of the human body</note>. There, we not foolishly compared the **Spleen** with the northern region, the **Liver** with the southern, the region of the chest (where the seat of the **Heart** is) with the corner of the **East** where the Sun rises, and finally the quarter of all the **viscera** <note>internal organs/intestines</note> with the **West**. Therefore, we do not intend to say more about them in this place. 

But as for what concerns the present purpose: it is certain that just as the benign property of God produces gentle and beneficial winds both in the world and in man for the life and recreation of both the elements and the things made of elements, so too <term>Ehieh</term> <note>Hebrew "I Am," representing the highest divine name</note> graciously rains down benevolent influences and breaths through the bright gate of <term>Cheter</term> <note>The Hebrew Sephirot "Keter" or Crown, the first emanation of God</note> (the Crown), inclining toward fiery love in the world, through which the world was created. Likewise, <term>El</term> <note>The Hebrew name of God associated with Mercy</note> rains down warmth and moisture upon the world's creatures through His bright gate <term>Chesed</term> <note>The Sephirot of Mercy or Loving-kindness</note>, by way of the sphere and star of **Jupiter**. He pours out benevolent breaths of life, which is why Jupiter is called a benevolent planet in the procreation of living things and the preservation of their lives. 

So too, the solar influences from the gate of <term>Tiphereth</term> <note>The Sephirot of Beauty, associated with the Sun</note> distribute the heat of life everywhere to creatures. These are breathed out, and by them the world is wonderfully refreshed. Hence we see spring winds produced by the breathing of benevolent winds—sometimes blowing through the earth with a suitable dryness (as in the month of March), and sometimes moistening the fields with pleasant and fertile rains (as in the month of April). By their breath, both the earth of the **Macrocosm** <note>the universe</note> and the entire mass of the **Microcosm** <note>the human body</note> are purified and receive the necessities of life. Even the western and eastern winds greatly favor human life; they are observed to breathe utility into both plants and other living things. These benevolent breaths are expired by God, who is full of mercy and clemency in His beneficial property. For this reason, the blood is usually renewed in the springtime. Such breaths are accustomed to occur in every season according to the good pleasure and mercy of God toward men, by which they live healthily and mostly escape diseases.

But indeed, in His other property contrary to this one, He is noted to act contrarily. In His anger, He is observed to act severely with the sublunary spirit, as well as with the waters, the earth, and their creatures, because of the sins of men. Whence it happens that, when He expires the effects of His property in His name <term>Elohim</term> <note>The Hebrew name of God associated with Judgment/Severity</note> through the bright gate of <term>Binah</term> <note>The Sephirot of Understanding, often associated with the restrictive or "feminine" aspect of God</note>, into the sphere of...

Saturni, <note>catchword: "...of Saturn"</note>

<meta>This page continues the discussion on how celestial spheres and divine attributes influence both the Macrocosm (the universe) and the Microcosm (the human body). ### On the Efficient Cause of Meteors.

...of Saturn, from which they are afterwards rained down into the elemental region, it is customary for the world and the world's creatures to be dealt with severely. This occurs by God turning his face away from his creatures, binding the heavens with thick and dark clouds, fostering winter chills and their effects, and conversely, stirring up and agitating the actions of human life. This is why the northern blasts procreate cold winds, which are most opposed to the life of mortals and induce stupor and insensibility. Furthermore, sometimes Jehovah, in his wrath, pours out fiery breaths and burning spirits by the power of his name <term>Elohim Gibbor</term> <note>Hebrew: "God the Mighty," associated with divine judgment</note> from the fiery gate of <term>Geburath</term> <note>The Sephirot of "Severity" or "Strength" in Kabbalah</note> through the sphere of Mars, under the guidance and leadership of <term>Samael</term>, a fiery angel who is malignant to the life of creatures. From this follow lightnings, flashes, and hot, scorched winds; and because of such emissions from Jehovah, he is called a "consuming fire," both in the greater and the lesser world. Furthermore, the ultimate extremity of severity in God is seen in the property of his name <term>Adonai</term> <note>Hebrew: "Lord"</note>, which sends down the influence of his will from the bright gate of <term>Malcuth</term> <note>The Sephirot of "Kingdom," representing the physical manifestation of divine will</note> through the body and sphere of the Moon. From this, in the great world, come floods, inundations, and vehement rains; and in the Microcosm <note>the human body</note>, such diseases as dropsy, catarrhs, and other watery ailments. Here, therefore, is the occasion for diseases both cold and hot, joined with dryness or humidity, as shall be spoken of in their proper places.

In the property of his clemency, therefore, the first which is called <term>Ehieh</term> <note>Hebrew: "I Am," the highest and most merciful name of God</note>, moved by mercy, he is changed into the condition of a Father; and in this sense it was said: *The Lord God said this, creating the heavens, extending them, establishing the earth and those things which sprout from it, giving breath to the people, and spirit to those walking upon it, Isaiah 42:5.* In this speech, the Prophet shows that God, in his first property, created and generated the world, as it were, and then afterwards the other creatures, both vegetable and animal, and especially man, by his breath or spirit. In the manner of a father, he looks upon his children with clemency and, as it were, fatherly love, and preserves them by the continuation of that same breath, or the "breath of life." Furthermore, with respect to this property, it is said that God created all things that they might exist, and he made the nations of the earth healable; there is no medicine of destruction in them, nor the kingdom of the underworld upon the earth, for he did not make death, nor does he delight in the perdition of the living.

In the second property of his benevolence toward created things, by reason of which he is called <term>El</term> <note>A Hebrew name for God often associated with kindness and grace</note>, he treats his creatures benevolently. Moved by mercy, he is accustomed to take away those curses from them with which he sometimes afflicts them for their sins, as is clear in the recovery of Miriam from her leprosy. Moses inclined God to this cure with prayers through the name <term>El</term>, saying: *El, na, rapha, na, la, El*, that is, *God of grace, heal, I pray, her.* In this sense also David said, *Heal me, Jehovah, for my bones are troubled, Psalm 6:3.* In this place, he also seems to imply that the medicine of Jehovah is his grace, mercy, and kindness; hence he says elsewhere, *I cried out to you and you healed me, and kept me alive, lest I should go down into the pit, Psalm 30:10.* And elsewhere: *Your mercy is from the heavens; O how precious is your kindness and mercy, when the sons of men take refuge under the shadow of your wings, Psalm 25.* And the Apostle says that *mercy and grace far surpass the nature of sin, Romans 5:20.* And in another sense, *Your visitation preserves my spirit, Job 10:12.* Hence Jupiter is called the "fosterer of human nature." Finally, in his third property—namely, that by which the influence of graces and beauty rains into the sphere of the Sun through the bright gate <term>Tiphereth</term> <note>The Sephirot of "Beauty" or "Harmony"</note>, that is, grace and beauty—it is read that *the Sun is the giver of glory and grace, Psalm 84:12.* And elsewhere: *the fountain of life is with you, Psalm 36:9.* Hence the Sun is called by philosophers the "author of life" and the "father of multiplication" among the worldly organs. Furthermore, from the name of God <term>Sadai</term> <note>Shaddai, meaning Almighty or Sustainer</note> through the bright gate <term>Iesed</term> <note>Chesed, the Sephirot of "Mercy" or "Loving-kindness"</note>, that is, redemption, we have the benevolent influences of redemption and salvation, of which property the King understands when he says: *You shall save both men and beasts, etc., Psalm 36.*

In the first of the properties tending toward severity, from which he is called <term>Elohim</term>, and which passes through <term>Binah</term> <note>The Sephirot of "Understanding," often associated with the feminine and the restriction of light</note>, he pours down punishments and slaughters upon the earth. For in this, God is accustomed to exercise his power by punishing the wicked, and the ministers in this property are those angels called *Bene Elohim*, that is, the sons of Elohim. <term>Elohim</term>, therefore, signifies the earth and dread, and its place in the world is the north wind, from which all evil comes. Such influences pass through the sphere of Saturn, which is why this planet is called the "greater misfortune" by astrologers. In this property, God pursued the Egyptians with palpable darkness and similar plagues, and also when Jehovah sent down great hailstones from heaven, with which he slew the enemies of the Israelites, *Joshua 10:11.* By the same reasoning, he produces earthy and stupid effects in man, as well as melancholic and fearful ones, through those angels. Hence it was said that Miriam appeared white with leprosy—an evil which he later healed in his mercy by changing the name <term>Elohim</term> into <term>El</term>. And elsewhere: *Jehovah struck the men of Ashdod with hemorrhoids, 1 Samuel 5:5.* And in this property, it is said that Jehovah, meeting Moses on his journey, wished to kill him, *Exodus 4:24.* And elsewhere: *I will cause terror to rule over you, with consumption, Leviticus 26:16.* Similarly, in this property, he poured his evil spirit into Saul by taking away the good spirit which he had granted him in <term>El</term> or grace; and in infinite other instances. Similarly, in such a disposition of his, joined with that of <term>Elohim Gibbor</term>, he is described in such a form of terror in the persecution of the unjust: *Smoke went up in his wrath, and fire broke out from his face; coals were kindled by him. He bowed the heavens and came down, and darkness was under his feet. And he mounted upon the Cherubim and flew; he flew upon the wings of the winds. He made darkness his secret place, and dark waters in the clouds of the air his tabernacle round about him. At the brightness in his presence the clouds passed, with hail and coals of fire. And the Lord thundered from heaven, and he sent out arrows and scattered them; he multiplied lightnings. Psalm 17.* <note>Original: Psalm 17; in modern Bibles, this is Psalm 18:8-14.</note>

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the "Efficient Cause of Meteors," specifically focusing on how divine severity and the alignment of the planets (Mars and Saturn) manifest as fiery weather events and disease in both the Great World (the universe) and the Small World (the human body).</meta>

#### Section I. Portion IV. Part II. Book IV. Member I.

<margin>Psalm 17.</margin> With these words, the Prophet denotes and describes perfectly a "mixed virtue"—namely, the fire of Mars combined with the horrific and fearsome darkness of Saturn. This refers to the property of <term>Elohim Gibbor</term> <note>Hebrew: "God the Mighty," the divine name associated with the power of judgment</note> and the gate of <term>Geburah</term> <note>The Sephirot of "Severity" or "Strength" in Kabbalah</note> joined with that of <term>Binah</term> <note>The Sephirot of "Understanding," often associated with the restrictive influence of Saturn</note>. This occurs in the severe property of the second order, by which He is called <term>Elohim Gibbor</term>. When this power sends its outflows through the bright gate of <term>Geburah</term>, it takes on a fiery nature and is called a "consuming fire." Its ministers, who carry out this property, are fiery angels, of whom the Psalmist speaks when he says <margin>Psalm 104.</margin> that *He makes his angels winds and his ministers a burning fire*. <margin>Job 38.</margin> Hence Job also says: *Will you send lightnings and they shall go, and returning say to you, "Here we are"?* In this sense, the aforementioned Prophet speaks elsewhere: <margin>Psalm 18.</margin> *He rained down upon the wicked coals of fire, fire and sulfur, and the spirit of storms is the portion of their cup.* And elsewhere: *Smoke rose from the nostrils of Jehovah, and fire from His mouth, etc.* and by hurling lightnings, He scatters them. Furthermore, in another place, he describes how God, in a state of burning heat, is accustomed to afflict the impious through his fiery ministers. <margin>Psalm 79:5.</margin> *Will you be angry forever?* (says David) *etc. Pour out your heat upon other nations that do not know you, for the consumer has consumed Jacob.* Where by "the consumer," he understands a minister or angel of God who brings affliction. <margin>Psalm 17.</margin> And elsewhere: *He multiplied lightnings, and you threw them into confusion.* Similarly, He sent a rainy flame of sulfur and whirlwinds <note>Original: *presteres*, referring to fiery or pestilential whirlwinds</note> into Sodom and Gomorrah for their sins. <margin>Genesis 19.</margin> And elsewhere: *Fire coming out from the presence of Jehovah killed the sons of Aaron, and they died before Jehovah*. <margin>Leviticus 10:12.</margin> And elsewhere: *Fire going out from Jehovah consumed those 250 men who offered incense*. <margin>Numbers 16:35.</margin> And elsewhere: *The burning wrath of Jehovah shall remain in this place and shall not be extinguished*. <margin>2 Kings 22.</margin> Moreover, it is said that the vindictive angels of fiery disposition are the ministers in this action: <margin>Baruch 4:35.</margin> *Fire from Jehovah will be sent into Babylon for a long time, and it will be inhabited by demons for a long duration.* 

But it must also be observed that this fiery property of God works sometimes visibly and sometimes invisibly upon disobedient men. Finally, this malignant fire frequently works within the <term>macrocosmic</term> <note>The Great World or the Universe</note> spirit toward the disturbance or total destruction of that "smallest world" <note>The human being, or Microcosm</note>. We gather this from many passages of Holy Scripture. <margin>Wisdom 19:13.</margin> *By the force of lightnings* (says the Sage) *punishments come upon the wicked.* And elsewhere, the holy page speaks thus of the human spirit corrupted by the vindictive fire of God: *The wrath of Jehovah was kindled against Israel, and that plague was stayed so that it did proceed no further; there were those who died by that plague, 24,000.* <margin>Numbers 25.</margin> Furthermore, elsewhere: <margin>Job 6:4.</margin> *The arrows of God are plagues, whose poison the human spirit drinks up.* And elsewhere: *Let the plague cling to you until it has consumed you.* And elsewhere: <margin>Deuteronomy 28:12.</margin> *Jehovah will strike you with wasting, and with a hot, burning, and scorching fever, and with drought, and with blight, and they shall pursue you until you perish,* and so on in the rest. 

By these examples it is sufficiently clear that just as lightnings are subtle and fiery winds sent by God to exercise His will here on earth, so too are febrile and pestilential winds in the "human air" <note>The internal spirit or atmosphere of the human body</note> very similar to them in nature, operation, and effect. The reason is readily apparent: namely, because the <term>Microcosmic</term> air is the son of the <term>Macrocosmic</term> air, and is thus linked to it by a natural bond, so that one (the Microcosm's air) cannot live, exist, or remain without the other. Hence Hippocrates, Galen, Avicenna, and all those most skilled in medicine, posit that a change in the world's air caused by winds leads to a change in the human air, both in sickness and in health—as they have explained at length in their books on Epidemic diseases, on the *Ephori* <note>Medical overseers or specific disease categories</note>, and on flatulence. Hence we also read in Isidore that the Northern Wind <note>Latin: *Septentrionalis* or *Boreas*</note> makes the air pure and clear, hardens bodies, and closes the pores; therefore, it purifies the humors, makes the human spirit clear, aids digestion, rectifies pestilential air, and assists the power of generation. For this reason, Aristotle holds that if the wind is northerly during conception, the infant will be male; if southerly, female. <margin>Book 5, Chapter 1.</margin> And Constantine says that the North Wind represses bad humors, but likewise occasionally induces dryness of the chest, coughing, and roughness of the lungs; it makes the limbs numb and is heavy for the consumptive, and this is because of its cold and dry disposition.

Similarly, the [South] winds <note>The text likely means the Southern winds here, as it describes the opposite of the North</note> make the air thick and cloudy, open the pores, multiply rains, and sometimes thunder, corrupting the air, etc. And Bede recognizes that the South Wind <note>Latin: *Australis*</note> acts in the air and the human body just as it does with the heaven and earth of the world; hence he says that it opens the pores of the body, hinders the power of sensation by thickening [the humors], and induces a heaviness of the body. In this, he seems to agree with Hippocrates, who also arrived at this opinion: that this wind dulls the hearing, makes it difficult, affects the head, and does not bind or confirm the humors, but rather dissolves them, calling them forth from the interior toward the exterior, and brings pestilential diseases, along with many other things which are more fully discussed in our Preternatural History of the <term>Microcosm</term>.

We conclude, therefore, that since three spirits are reckoned in this world—namely, the divine (which is primary), the mundane (the world's), and that of the creatures—and since these spirits are derived successively from one another (namely, the secondary is stirred either peacefully or violently by the motion of the first, just as a body is moved sweetly or violently by the soul), and again the third by both, it is necessary to believe that all these spirits, when put into action, are considered and held to be blasts and winds. Yet this is the greatest difference between these spirits: the first is uncreated, splendid, animating the others primordially, the light of the world, and the breath of life; the two lower ones are air, blast, and spirit, of a moist and foreign nature;

## CHAPTER XIX.

### *That clouds, snows, hails, frost, and other such dark meteors are procreated in the air by the winds of God, and how God is the sole and unique author and actor in their creation.*

That God is the actor and origin not only of the Winds but also of all other <term>meteors</term> <note>In the 17th century, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, including rain, snow, and rainbows.</note>, and that He works through various organs of the world for their procreation, the wise man demonstrates to us most clearly and with truly golden words: *The beauty of the height is the firmament, the appearance of heaven in a vision of glory. The Sun when it appears, announcing at its rising: an admirable vessel, the work of the Most High. At noon it parches the earth, and who can endure its burning heat? As one keeping a furnace in a work of heat, so is the Lord great who made it, and at His word it hastened its course. And the moon in all things in its season shows the time and the sign of the age. From the moon is the sign of the feast day, a light that wanes in its consummation; according to its name it is marvelously increasing in its consummation, a vessel of the camps on high, shining gloriously in the firmament of heaven; the beauty of heaven is the glory of the stars, the Lord illuminating the world on high; at His holy words they shall stand for judgment, and they shall not fail in their watches, etc.* <margin>Ecclesiasticus 43:1-12</margin>

By these words, the wise man primarily denotes that the stars are the sole organs of heaven, by whose mediation He illuminates all things and operates upon lower things for the procreation of every kind of meteor. Hence he calls the sun an "admirable vessel," because in that which is called "the work of the Most High," it is recognized as a creature and not the creator. However, he explains there how God acts through the sun: namely, by heat and burning, by which the "human furnace" is preserved in the work of its heat—that is, all things are generated, preserved, and finally, having been led through the circle of nature to the period of a new generation, they perish; that is, they are deprived of their preceding form. Furthermore, he himself, with the lunar organ, distinguishes the seasons of the year into days and months. 

Finally, he concludes that it is not the sun, but the Lord in the sun or any other star who is the beauty of heaven, according to that saying: *By His spirit He adorned the heavens with the glory of the stars,* <margin>Job 26</margin>. Whence it is said, *The Sun giving grace and glory,* <margin>Psalm 84:12</margin>, and the "illuminator of the world"; thus He is handed down as the Light of the world by which the world was made, *John 1*. Therefore, by the mediation of visible organs or instruments of this kind in the world, God produces His meteors in the sublunary world, which the said wise man seems to confirm immediately in the following verses: 

*Behold the rainbow, and bless Him who made it; it is very beautiful in its brightness. It has encircled the heaven in the circuit of its glory; the hands of the Most High have fitted it. Therefore the treasures were opened, and the mists flew out like birds; He placed the clouds in their greatness, and the hailstones were broken. At His sight the mountains were moved, and by His will the South wind breathed. The voice of His thunder struck the earth, the storm of the North wind and the gathering of the spirit; and like a bird lighting to sit, He scatters the snow, and pours out the frost like salt upon the earth. The cold North wind blew, and the crystal froze in the water, etc.* <margin>Ecclesiasticus 43:12 onward</margin>

By these words it is clearly indicated that God is the author of all meteors in general: namely, the rainbow, snow, hail, mist, cloud, wind, thunder, lightning, storm, the gathering of spirits, frost, ice, etc. We say that the generation of clouds is ordained by God according to the order of mundane nature, and then God mostly operates from His "solar tabernacle," and also by the mediation of other celestial...

We say, therefore, that the Name or Word of God primarily moves the winds, which in their external form are nothing other than moved air, but their internal nature is the clarity of the Almighty, by which they are animated, governed, and disposed according to the will of the Creator to carry out God’s commands. He moves the first part of Himself in the angel, who, obeying His will, is first moved in the air in the form of wind with his legions, and then fits the air into the nature of wind or the thickness of a dense cloud, from which they more widely receive the laws of rain, or He brings it back into the property of lightning. And yet it is not the angel, but God or Wisdom in the angel, who is most rightly said to do all these things, since He is the true and sole actor in these matters.

## CHAPTER XX.

### *On the single efficient cause of flashes, lightning, thunderbolts, and thunders, and likewise concerning the actor of sulfurous smoke and flames.*

As the creator of all makes his angels Winds, so also he makes his ministers a burning fire or flame, as witnessed by the royal Prophet, Psalms 103 and 104. <note>Psalm 104:4</note> Now, we call lightning and flashes the air itself, animated by a presence and clothed in their fiery form. We gather this from the consequence of such speech as: *God fits a weight to the air, and weighs the waters by measure; and he makes a way for the lightning of the thunders, where he is seen to fit the air in its weight so that through it, as through a medium, his fiery spirits may make their way to fulfill the will of the creator.* <note>original: "Deus aptat pondus aeri... facitq; fulgetro tonitruum viam suam." A paraphrase of Job 28:25-26.</note> Job seems to hint at this in another place: *The clouds scatter their light, which illuminates all things round about, wherever the will of the Creator drives them for everything he commanded them upon the face of the world, whether for a scourge or for mercy, Job 37:11-13.* <note>The author cites Job 28:25 in the text, but the passage is from Job 37.</note> And elsewhere: *Behold, God extends his light over the clouds, and covers the roots of the sea, Job 36:30.* And elsewhere: *Will you send forth lightning bolts, and will they return and say to you, "Here we are"? Job 38:35.* Are we not also made more certain of the efficient cause of lightning from these words: *Fire going out from the presence of Jehovah killed the sons of Aaron, Leviticus 10:2*? <note>original: "Ignis exiens à conspectu Iehouæ, exanimauit filios Aaronis"</note> And elsewhere: *Fire going out from Jehovah consumed 250 men who had offered incense, Numbers 16:35.* Finally, in the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation</note> we have it that *lightnings, voices, and thunders proceeded from the throne of God.* By these things it is clearly denoted that flashes and lightning proceed immediately from God, and that this discourse should be understood in this way: Namely, the divine Essence, in its wisdom or emanation, agitates its likeness in fiery spirits (by means of which a fiery angel exists and remains, such as appears in the air during the time of lightning: for the incorruptible spirit of God is in every thing, but more abundantly in angels). It urges and moves a part of itself (I say) to perform those things which are ordained by the moving Father. These fiery spirits, in their motion, disturb the air, massing and constricting it into thick clouds; and conversely, spirits of an opposite nature, breathing from a contrary quarter of the world, wage an impetuous war, violently breaking out from that damp embrace and the thick prison surrounding them. Indeed, those fiery or watery spirits or demons do not do this of themselves, but God is accustomed to effect it by the ray of his twofold essence acting within them. And this is the reason that many thunders are heard at the same time, rising from different corners of the world; whence Daniel says: *the four winds of heaven fought upon the great sea, Daniel 7:2,* that is, in the open air. By "winds," the Prophet here understands the angelic intelligences who preside over the four corners of the world. But concerning these, God willing, we shall discourse more clearly in the second book of this member. But we also have other testimonies of the sacred page everywhere dispersed through it to prove this our single efficient cause of all things: specifically that God alone (with no other subordinate efficient cause mediating) is the author and actor in thunder, lightning, and all other luminous meteors whatsoever. For in one place it is said: *Smoke went up in his anger, and fire from his face burned; coals were kindled by him, etc. At the brightness in his presence the clouds passed away, hail and coals of fire; and the Lord thundered from heaven, and the Most High gave his voice, etc. Psalm 18:8-13.* <note>The author cites Psalm 17, following the Vulgate numbering.</note>

<meta>This page continues the author’s refutation of Aristotelian meteorology.
