<header>Section I. Portion IV. Part II. Book IV. Member II.</header>

[Angels] on earth are of great importance as caretakers, seeing as they are accustomed to being present for individuals, and indeed to care for every single creature, whether animal, vegetable, or mineral. St. Paul discusses this leadership in various places, and mention is made of Archangels and Angels everywhere throughout the sacred pages.

From these sources, it is clearly established that each of these hierarchies has a special relationship to a person of the Holy Trinity: namely, the **supreme** hierarchy relates to the divine essence; the **middle** relates to the emanation, or the Son, as it concerns the monarchy and economy of the heavens; and the **lowest** hierarchy has respect for sublunary <term>Sublunary: the earthly realm "below the moon," subject to change and decay</term> things, since it is present in the lower forms and virtues and is seen to administer them.

It is in this sense that the royal Psalmist [David] seems to speak in very few words, saying: *By the Word of the Lord the heavens were made firm, and all their powers by the spirit from his mouth;* <note>original Latin: "Verbo Domini firmati sunt caeli, & spiritu ab ore eius omnes virtutes eorum;" see Psalm 33:6</note> where the Lord, or the Father, created the heavens through the Word, or the Son, and every virtue and influence through the Spirit proceeding from both.

According to the division of the ancient Hebrews, however, we see the same orders of angels—both in number and effect, though varying in specific names—following the series of the "Bright Gates" or *Sephirot* <term>Sephirot: the ten attributes or emanations in Cabala through which the Infinite reveals itself</term>, or the numerations of the Cabalists <term>Cabalist: a student of Jewish mystical interpretation of the Bible</term>, through which various influences of divine properties descend to lower things. For as we have declared elsewhere, the influences of *Keter* <note>The "Crown," the highest Sephiroth</note>, over which the divine name *Ehieh* <note>Hebrew: "I Am"</note> presides, descend through the order of the **Seraphim** according to the doctrine of Dionysius. Likewise, according to the sense of the ancient Hebrew Doctors, God—as *Ehieh*—is said to bestow the gift of being through the angelic order of the *Haioth Kadosh* <note>Hebrew: "Holy Living Creatures"</note>; He distinguishes Chaos through the *Ophanim* <note>Hebrew: "Wheels"</note> of the *Elohim*; and He provides the forms of universal matter through the *Aralim* <note>Hebrew: "Mighty Ones" or "Thrones"</note> of *Jehovah*, and so on for the rest, as will be clearer in what follows. Other Hebrew Doctors have applied almost the same names to these angelic orders, though changing the sequence: namely, *Chasmalim, Cherubim, Tarshish, Aralim, Seraphim, Malachim, Ophanim, Issim, Elohim*, to which they also delight to add the *Bene Elohim*, who oversee both good and evil Daemons (of which more below). They have fished all these names out of the sacred fountain of the holy pages. For Ezekiel speaks of the *Chasmalim* <note>Ezekiel 1:4, often translated as "glowing amber"</note>. Genesis, Exodus, and the Psalms mention the **Cherubim**. Ezekiel also names the *Tarshish* <note>Ezekiel 10:9, often translated as "beryl"</note>, though common interpretation offers "angels" or "messengers" in its place. Ezekiel also holds the name *Ophanim*; just as *Issim* <note>Hebrew: "Men-like spirits"</note> is expressed by Solomon. They took *Elohim* from the first book of Kings, where the Medium of Endor said to Saul: *I saw Elohim ascending from the earth*, that is, "gods" or "spirits" according to the common edition. Regarding the good *Bene Elohim* <note>Hebrew: "Sons of God"</note>, Job mentions them; while Moses and Job in another place mention the evil ones.

It is not irrelevant to note that although only nine orders of angels are recorded by the wise or the more secretive theologians, there is an innumerable multitude of individuals within each of those species, which they have named "armies." They divided each of these orders, primarily according to the partition of the celestial Zodiac, into twelve parts; the first member in this division they called *Mizaloth* <note>Hebrew: "Constellations" or "Mazzaroth"</note>. Then, they partitioned each of these twelve members into thirty portions, which they called **Cohorts**. This subdivision they called *El*, which consequently contains thirty cohorts under it for each of those twelve, making a total of three hundred and sixty cohorts of Angels.

Afterward, they assign another subdivision which multiplies that 360 by 30, producing the number 10,800; this subdivided member they call a **Legion**. They multiply this number again by 30, producing what they call a *Rihaton*, consisting of 324,000. Further, they multiply this number by 30 again, and the resulting number they call a *Chitton*, which is composed of 9,720,000. Finally, they multiply that product by 30 again, and the resulting number will be 291,600,000. From all these, the total sum is one million, six hundred and fifty-five thousand, one hundred and seventy-two, <note>The author's total here (1,655,172) does not mathematically follow the geometric progression described; he is likely referencing a specific Cabalistic sum found in mystical texts like the *Sefer Raziel*</note> according to the doctrine of the Cabalists, who made all these angels "ministering spirits," about whom more will be clear in the following pages. The Platonists, however, maintain that there are as many legions of lower daemons as there are stars in the heaven, and they say there are as many daemons in any legion as there are stars in the sky. Some Cabalists strenuously defend the idea that angels do not only agree with men in many natural things but also in number, asserting that there must be as many humans to be saved as there were rebellious angels who fell from heaven in the conflict and fight between Michael and Lucifer; and again, that there will be as many damned as there were angels on Michael's side who won the victory over the fallen angels.

But whatever the opinion of the Cabalists and Platonists may be regarding the number of angels, we also gather from the sacred letters that there are many myriads of angelic spirits, as seen in several places: *The chariots of God* (says David) *are two myriads, many thousands of angels; the Lord is among them as in Sinai, in the holy place. Psalm 68, v. 10.* <note>Psalm 68:17 in modern numbering</note> Furthermore, Christ speaks of many legions of both his Father and of Satan. Augustine and Gregory maintain that the number of good angels transcends all human grasp; to which, conversely, correspond innumerable unclean spirits—there being as many in the lower world as there are pure spirits in the upper world. Certain theologians have also confessed to having received this from divine oracles. And in the *Porta Lucis* <note>Latin: "Gate of Light," a famous Cabalistic text by Joseph Gikatilla</note> it is held that from the earth all the way to the firmament there is no lo-

# On the Efficient Cause of Meteors. <note>original Latin: "De Causa Meteororum Efficienti." In the 17th century, "meteors" referred to all atmospheric phenomena, including wind, rain, and lightning, not just falling stars.</note>

...not empty, but everything is full of forms. From these, some are pure, some are capable of grace, others are foul, harmful, and tempters; etc.

### Classification of Celestial Spirits (C)

**Angels or celestial spirits (also called "Olympics") assigned to the stars:**

*   **To the Fixed Stars:**
    *   **Of the signs of the Zodiac:**
        *   **Of several signs:** Namely, the four <term>Triplicities: groups of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water)</term>.
        *   **Of one sign:**
            *   The **Whole** sign.
            *   A **Part** of the sign: either <term>Decans: ten-degree segments of a zodiac sign</term> or <term>Quinaries: five-degree segments of a zodiac sign</term>.
    *   **Outside the Zodiac:** For there is no star in Heaven that does not have its own intelligence.
*   **To the Wandering Stars (the Planets):**
    *   **Princes (Presiding spirits):**
        *   Saturn: **Otiphiel** or **Zaphkiel**
        *   Jupiter: **Zachariel** or **Zadkiel**
        *   Mars: **Samael** or **Gamael**
        *   The Sun: **Michael**, under whom four others preside (over the seasons, the years, and as guardians of the Sun).
        *   Venus: **Anael**
        *   Mercury: **Raphael**
        *   The Moon: **Gabriel**, to whom many legions of lower spirits are subject, assigned to the <term>Mansions of the Moon: 28 divisions of the lunar cycle</term>.
    *   **Inferiors (who obey the princes in the aforementioned spheres):**
        *   Saturnine spirits,
        *   Jovial spirits,
        *   Martial spirits,
        *   Solar spirits,
        *   Venereal spirits,
        *   Mercurial spirits,
        *   Lunar spirits.

Celestial spirits <note>original: "Dæmones." While we often think of 'demons' as evil, the author uses the term in the older sense of 'daimon'—a guiding spirit or supernatural power.</note> are called "mundane" <note>of the world</note> by the more mystical theologians. Furthermore, they are also called "Olympics," those who dwell in the firmament and its stars. Their duty is to decree fates and to administer fatal events to those below, according to the will and permission of God. Thus it happens that neither an evil spirit nor an evil fate can harm one who "dwells in the help of the Most High." <note>original Latin: "in adjutorio altissimi," a reference to Psalm 91:1</note>

Moreover, it is decreed for each of these spirits to bring about that which the star to which it is attached has portended. However, they can bring nothing from potentiality into action without divine permission; for God alone is the one who grants them the ability and the effect. As the Creator of all, it is granted to Him that the super-celestial, the celestial, the sublunary, and indeed even the infernal realms must obey and submit.

Regarding the spirits presiding over the fixed stars, those who hold their kingdoms in the Zodiac preside over either the triplicities—namely the Fiery, Airy, Watery, or Earthy.

Others are placed in charge of individual whole signs, namely: **Malchidael** over Aries, **Asmodel** over Taurus, **Ambriel** over Gemini, **Muriel** over Cancer, **Verchiel** over Leo, **Hamaliel** over Virgo, **Zuriel** over Libra, **Zarachiel** over Scorpio, **Advachiel** over Sagittarius, **Hanael** over Capricorn, **Cambiel** over Aquarius, and **Barchiel** over Pisces. Indeed, the names of the angels of any sign are usually derived from the harmony they have with the name of the sign they oversee. Thus, from *Aries* comes **Ariel**; and likewise **Telechiel**, **Suriel**, **Tommiel**, **Sartamiel**, **Betuliel**, **Masniel**, **Acrabiel**, **Chefitiel**, **Gediel**, **Deliel**, and **Dagymiel**. It is as if we said in Latin letters: Ariel, Tauriel, Geminiel, Cancriel, Leoniel, Virginiel, Libriel, Scorpiel, Sagittariel, Capriel, Aquariel, and Pisciel. 

In any case, it is certain that each of these signs has its own peculiar prefect or angel. The <term>Cabalists: followers of Jewish mysticism</term> believe that John intended this in the Book of Revelation, where, in his description of the Heavenly Jerusalem, he mentions the twelve gates of the city. By these twelve gates, he understands the twelve celestial signs (which Plato calls the "gates of heaven"). The Apocalypse says that an angel is present in each of these gates, for it explicitly assigns twelve angels to the twelve gates of the heavenly city. And just as there are three Eastern signs, three Western, three Southern, and three Northern according to the doctrine of the astrologers, so the revelator [John] recognizes and assigns three gates to the Eastern region, the same number to the West, three to the South, and likewise three to the North.

#### Section I. Portion IV. Part II. Book IV. Member II.

Furthermore, the *Kabbalists* <note>Followers of Jewish mysticism (Kabbalah) whose ideas were widely integrated into Renaissance Christian magic.</note> assign a lower angel to all the decans <note>original: 'decuriis'. These are ten-degree segments of the zodiac, also called 'faces' by astrologers.</note> of the signs, and even to the "quinaries" which are the five-degree half-parts of a face. According to their opinion, every angelic "triplicity" <note>A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element: Fire, Earth, Air, or Water.</note> also enjoys its own angelic prefect.

*Abbot Trithemius* <note>Johannes Trithemius (1462–1516), a famous Benedictine abbot, cryptographer, and occultist.</note> testifies in a specific treatise dedicated to the *Emperor Maximilian* that every planetary sphere possesses a prince-spirit or "intelligence." Through the mediation of these spirits, the world is governed in succession. By their agency, all things that exist in the heavens and the air, as well as those that live and grow upon the earth, are fated and arranged according to the will of the Creator. 

The superior Prince or prefect destined for the governance of Saturn is called **Zabkiel** by the Magi (as some would have it), while others call him **Oriphiel**. He is followed by **Zadkiel** or **Zachariel**, who presides over *Jupiter*. Then there is **Zamael** or **Samael** (or as others prefer, **Camael**) over *Mars*; **Michael** over the *Sun* (though some make **Raphael** its prefect); **Haniel** or **Anael** over *Venus*; **Raphael** over *Mercury* (though some attribute **Michael** to it); and **Gabriel** over the *Moon*. 

It seems that *John* in *Revelation 1* refers to these spirits ruling the planets when he says: 
> *And from the seven spirits who are before the throne of GOD, etc.* 

*Raphael* also understood this when he said to *Tobit*: 
> I am Raphael, one of the seven angels who stand before Jehovah. <note>original Latin: "Ego sum Raphael vnus ex angelis 7. qui astamus ante Iehouam." This refers to the Book of Tobit, an archetypal text for angelic lore.</note>

And *Gabriel* said to *Mary*: 
> I am Gabriel, who stands before God. (Luke 1)

And elsewhere, it is said to *Daniel*: 
> Behold, Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me. (Daniel 10:15)

*Zachariel* was also the good angel of the *Prophet Zechariah*, of whom he writes: 
> The angel who spoke in me went out, and said to another angel: "Run," etc. (Zechariah 2)

These princes or prefects have many cohorts of lower spirits under their jurisdiction. These spirits are constantly sent down into the lower realms by way of "influence" to carry out the will of their leader (according to God’s commands). This influence is more abundant depending on the dominance of the star in heaven which they are said to inhabit. These lower angels or demons take their general names from their star; just as we say "Frenchman," "Englishman," "Spaniard," or "Italian" to mean a man born in France, England, Spain, or Italy, so too do we call the inhabitants of those planetary spheres **Jovials** (of Jupiter), **Saturnines** (of Saturn), **Martials** (of Mars), and so on.

The angels under the command of the Great Archangel *Gabriel*, however, tend to vary in nature and disposition according to the varying position of the lunar sphere within the signs of the *Zodiac*. Astrologers call these positions "mansions." There are 28 mansions in total, and therefore the angels governing them are called by various names, which we list here in order: *Geniel, Enediel, Amixiel, Azariel, Gabiel, Dirachiel, Seheliel, Amnediel, Barbiel, Ardestel, Neciel, Abdizuel, Jazeriel, Ergediel, Ataliel, Azeruel, Adriel, Egibiel, Amutiel, Kyriel, Bethnael, Celiel, Requiel, Abrinael, Aziel, Tagriel, Alheniel, Amnixiel*. All of these have great power over the various changes of water and air, as well as the alterations of earthly things.

Finally, according to the doctrine of the *Kabbalists*, there are other angels to whom the four watches of the night are committed (of which Christ speaks: *And if he comes in the second or third watch of the night, etc.*). Others are placed over the four "watches" of the year, according to those four solar stations occurring in Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn <note>The spring equinox, summer solstice, autumn equinox, and winter solstice.</note>.

### Concerning the Efficient Cause of Atmospheric Phenomena.
<note>original: "De Causa Meteororum Efficiente." In the 17th century, "meteors" referred to all atmospheric phenomena, including wind, rain, and lightning.</note>

...of this world, from which the principal winds are observed to blow, and for this reason they are called the **Cardinal Winds**, as we have previously declared. Therefore, from among the Good Angels, the Doctors of the Hebrews attribute the care and dominion of the Eastern Wind to **Michael**, and to **Raphael** that of the West; the former is called the *Subsolanus* <note>The "under-the-sun" wind, or East wind.</note> and the latter *Favonius* <note>The gentle West wind or zephyr.</note>. To **Gabriel** is given the prefecture of the North and its principal wind, and to **Uriel** the governance of the South.

And it should be known that although four spirits or demons are assigned to the office of the cardinal winds—namely, **Oriens** for the direction of the East wind, **Paymon** for the West, **Egyn** for the North, and **Amaymon** for the South—who also have many legions or cohorts of demons serving under them to execute their malice—nevertheless, these evil angels (who have been given the power to harm the sky, the earth, and the sea) are subjected to the dominion of the aforementioned good angels. Thus, without their permission and leave, or rather the will and word of GOD shining through them, they can do no evil in the lands, in the water, or in the air, as will be more clearly seen in the following discourse.

But the Doctors of the Hebrews, most skilled in secret Theology, seem to distinguish this with even more expressive words. For *Rabbi Tedacus Levi* <note>Likely Todros ben Joseph Abulafia (1225–1285), a famous Spanish Kabbalist.</note> in his *Book on the 10 Numerations* <note>A treatise on the ten Sephirot, the divine emanations in Kabbalah.</note>, after he had spoken clearly enough concerning the four Cardinal winds, continues thus: "From those four winds," he says, "He created angels who are prefects over them by day and by night. For Michael, who is of the side of Clemency, is the official <note>original: 'Mamona'. This likely refers to an 'appointed official' or is a corruption of a Hebrew title like 'Memuneh'.</note> over the Eastern wind until midday; and until nightfall, Raphael, who is also of the side of clemency, rules the western wind. Then Gabriel, in the power of judgment and severity, is prefect over the northern wind during the middle of the night and two measures of the world; while Noriel presides over the South." These are his words. And the *Book of Secrets* <note>original: 'Liber Arcanorum', likely referring to the *Sefer HaRazim*.</note> acknowledges that these presidents have many species or legions under them. To this *Joseph Castaliensis* <note>Joseph Gikatilla (1248–c. 1305), a major Kabbalistic writer.</note> in the book called *The Gate of Light* <note>original: 'Porta lucis', or *Sha'are Orah*.</note> seems to agree, saying that from the earth to the firmament there is no empty space, but all is full of forms—some of them pure, some capable of grace and mercies, and below there are many foul, harmful, and tempting images, all dwelling and flying in the air. elsewhere *Joseph Castaliensis* has these words: "From the earth even to the firmament there is no empty place, but the whole is filled with species—some for peace, some for war, some for good, some for evil, some for life, and some for death; and all that is in the lower habitation in which we are." And all these spirits are animated by the good angelic winds if they are good, or by the evil if they are bad. From this it is clearly evident that those winds, which among the Peripatetics <note>Followers of Aristotle’s philosophy, who focused on physical rather than spiritual causes.</note> and even us common folk are considered natural impressions, are referred to the orders of spirits when considered in occult philosophy. Hence it is also read in the Sacred Page: > The spirit of storms which fulfills his word, *Psalm 148*. And elsewhere: > Who makes your angels winds, etc. *Psalm 104*. Furthermore, the *Apocalypse, chapter 7*, makes mention of the Angels in whose power is the force of the winds.

The four elements of the sublunary region, as they are diverse in nature, also claim for themselves diverse leaders and prefects appointed to them by God. Under their command exist great crowds of spirits or demons. Those who are under the command of the **Seraphim** are endowed with a fiery nature, and for this reason, by natural inclination, they choose the fiery element for their homeland. But if they descend further down outside its limits (which often happens in the domain of Mars in the heavens), they produce thunder, flashes, lightning, and other things of that kind in the air, because of the conflict that the watery spirits have with them. By a similar reasoning, we see in the human body that the bilious or sanguine humor, when outside its natural place and seat, putrefies and disturbs the "human air" with hot "meteors" <note>An analogy comparing bodily vapors/fevers to atmospheric storms.</note> and induces diseases. The same that has been said of fiery spirits is to be understood of the aerial, watery, and earthy spirits, who serve their own leaders and, by natural effort, choose that element for their homeland over which their prince has dominion. Hence they are called aerial, watery, and earthy spirits, because they participate more in such natures.

Finally, according to the doctrine of the Kabbalists and the Doctors of the Hebrews, we understand that there are 72 strong angels of the whole earth, by whose assistance Moses is said to have divided the Red Sea. For these are called by them the Angels of Division, and they say that God divided the earth according to the number of these angels. Hence we read in the book called *The Gate of Justice* <note>original: 'Porta Iustitiæ', likely another reference to Gikatilla's work or a similar Kabbalistic text.</note> that all nations were left and delivered into the power of seventy prefects—that is, the Princes of the angels. These are said to be familiar to men and to be the presidents of the seventy-two regions of the earth, as *Reuchlin* <note>Johann Reuchlin (1455–1522), a German humanist who introduced Greek and Hebrew studies to his peers.</note> holds, who in the third book of *On the Art of the Kabbalah* sets out to list their names according to the opinion of *Rabbi Solomon* and others in this manner:

**Vehuiah, Jeliel, Sitael, Elemiah, Mahasiah, Lelahel, Achaiah, Cahetel; Haziel, Aladiah, Lauiah, Hahaiah; Lezalel, Mehahel, Hariel, Hakamiah, Louiah, Caliel**, and so on for the rest, as it is permitted to find in the place cited before. <note>These are the names of the Shem HaMephorash, the 72-fold name of God derived from Exodus.</note>

And so you have all the kinds of good angels distinct and divided according to the partition of the world. Nevertheless, those skilled in magic seem to refer these to the Sacred Letters, since they symbolize with them. The Holy Letters are said to be symbols for created things and, consequently, for the angels who are assigned to those created things, as we shall declare below.

## Chapter IV.

### *On the Difference Between Wicked and Malignant Demons.*

Just as God, who is the Emperor of light, is the Emperor of goodness, so also the Devil, who is the great Prince of darkness, is the author and worker of evil. From this it follows that just as God employs good angels as his ministers—who are thereafter called angels of light—so, conversely, the Devil has many troops of demons under his command. These are divided into legions, to whom it is given to invade and harm the airy spirit <note>The "airy spirit" refers to the vital, invisible substance believed to permeate both the atmosphere and the human body.</note> of both the Macrocosm <note>The "Great World" or the universe at large.</note> and the Microcosm <note>The "Little World" or the individual human being.</note> in a malignant manner. Therefore, relying on these matters confirmed by the authority of many trustworthy writers, I shall attempt to distinguish the multitude of Evil Demons <note>original: "Cacodæmonum"</note> in the following way:

**Evil demons are maliciously active around:**
- **Spirit only**
    - Of the Macrocosm (A)
    - Of the Microcosm (B)
- **Both spirit and body at once**
    - Of the Macrocosm alone (C)
    - Of the Microcosm alone (D)
    - Of both together (E)

The entire composition of both the world and man consists of spirit and body. However, since the universal spirit of both worlds is divided into three regions (as has been frequently declared by us before): First, there is the Empyrean heaven <note>The highest, most spiritual part of the heavens.</note>, which is the seat of the good angels. From this place, the malignant angels, on account of their ambitious rebellion, were banished as if into exile to the dense and lower region of the universal spirit. To this upper region of the worldly spirit corresponds the intellectual or rational spirit in man, which is the angelic seat of the mind.

Next, in the world, there is the middle seat of this universal spirit, which is called the ether. In this region, the Olympic Angels or Demons <note>These are spirits associated with the planets and the stars, thought to govern the laws of nature.</note> act; they are called the "distributors of Fate" because they pour down both malevolent and benevolent influences (according to the pleasure of the supreme creator) into the region of the elements. It is from these that the sublunary demons—both good and evil—receive their powers in action and their various dominions. From this it is clear that Satan, who is the Prince of the air, can do nothing without permission and various influxes, according to the diverse arrangement of any Sephirotic numbering <note>Refers to the ten *Sephirot* or divine attributes in the Kabbalah, here used as "gates" of light or influence.</note> or "luminous gate." To this middle region of the world's spirit corresponds the vital spirit in man, which sometimes inclines toward higher things and sometimes toward lower and fleeting matters.

Finally, the sublunary spirit of the world is that which (by divine permission) the great Prince of darkness commands. To this corresponds the natural spirit in man, which Paul seems to call the *animal soul* <note>original: "animam animalem." This refers to the lower, instinctual soul focused on physical survival and desires rather than spiritual truth.</note>, whose appetite is occupied with the flesh and its pleasures. Hence it is said that the *Prince of the air has power, and works in the children of disobedience*, as will be seen below. However, who the orders of Evil Demons in the elementary air are, and what their conditions are, may be gathered from the following members of the demonic division.

**Evil demons exercising their powers in the sublunary spirit of the world (namely, the air) differ in dignity, as some are:**
- **Principalities or Spirits of a superior order**
    - Emperor
    - Kings (F)
    - Dukes (G)
- **Subjects or those of an inferior condition, and subject to the aforesaid leaders, who are divided from one another into cohorts and legions (H).**

Just as in the Empyrean Heaven one may find Principalities, Archangels, and Angels of a benign condition, so indeed Lucifer, having once been cast down from that throne with his angels, has similar ministers under him, distinguished by rank and dignity. We also have this confirmed by the Apostle <note>Referring to St. Paul.</note>, whose authority is this: *Put on (he says) the armor of God, so that you may be able to stand against the deceits of the Devil, for our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against Princes and powers, against the rulers of the world of this darkness, against spiritual wickedness in high places, etc. Ephesians 6:12.* By these words, he clearly teaches that the Devil, as if the highest king and emperor of wickedness and malignancy, has under him his own ministers eminent in condition, whom the Apostle calls "Princes and powers," "rulers of the darkness of the world," and "spiritual wickedness." Hence, also elsewhere, the said Apostle says, *You have walked according to the age of this world...*

# On the Efficient Cause of Meteors.

<note>"Meteors" in this historical context refers to all atmospheric phenomena, including rain, wind, lightning, and clouds, not just falling stars.</note>

...of this, according to the prince of the power of this air, who now works in the children of disobedience: etc. Ephesians 2:2. From this, it seems to be concluded that he is the commander of the entire air; and the mages and those more skilled in hidden theology <note>original: "Theologia occulta"</note> (such as Agrippa, Book 3, Chapter 18) seem to verify this same point regarding the words of the Apostle, saying: That this Prince is called *Meririm* by the Hebrews, that is, the mid-day demon, a scorching spirit and a demon raging at noon, under whose command are the powers of the air. These spirits mingle themselves with thunder, lightning-bolts, flashes, and other impressions of the air. From this, it happens that they corrupt the air with their malignant breaths and, consequently, are accustomed to bring forth pestilential diseases, famine, infertility, and infinite other inconveniences to the world: as has been declared more widely in the history of the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation</note>, and will be declared more clearly by us below. 

From these testimonies of the wise, therefore, we gather what the sacred scriptures understood concerning this supreme King of Evil Demons <note>original: "Cacodæmonum"</note> in those passages already cited by us: *God shall come from the South, his glory covered the heavens, and the earth is full of his praise; his brightness shall be as the light, there his strength was hidden; death shall go before his face, and the Devil shall go out before his feet.* <note>A paraphrase of Habakkuk 3:3-5</note>. Yet others interpret this as: *The plague went before him, and a wasting pestilence in the south,* etc. In this discourse, the Prophet seems to hint that God, in His wrath, uses the Devil as His minister, with whom He goes out from the south—which is the contagious and deadly region of the world—where the air is contaminated by corrupt breaths. And hence it is that this commander of the dark air is deservedly called *Meririm*, or the demon scorching in the noon-day, by whose malignant blasts the entire region of the elements is intoxicated and contaminated when God permits; and he is also called Satan by the Holy Bible and by the Cabalists.

The Kings or Royal Evil Demons immediately serving under the command of Satan are four, namely:

| King (Royal Demon) | Cardinal Direction & Winds | Associated Element |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Oriens** (also called **Uriens** or **Samael**) | Eastern Regions and Winds | Element of Fire |
| **Amaymon** (also called **Azazel**) | Southern Regions and Winds | Element of Air |
| **Paymon** (also called **Azael**) | Western Regions and Winds | Element of Water |
| **Egyn** (also called **Mahazael**) | Northern Regions and Winds | Element of Earth |

It is a dogma of the Cabalists that every one of the prefects of the good angels is a great prince, and has enormous power over the demons subjected to them—whether they be overseers of the stars of the Zodiac, or of the wandering stars <note>The planets</note>, or of the corners of the world, the winds, and the elements. This liberty and power is assigned to them at certain fixed times, years, months, days, and hours in the quarters of the world, the winds, and the elements. Each of these Princes also has several orders of inferior demons under them, as will be seen more fully below.

Both the Royal Evil Demons and the princes of the good angels have dominion over the Corners, Winds, and Elements of the world, as it is their task to present and execute the severe commands of God the Creator upon these lower things. This happens in the same way that the Principal Good Angels are accustomed to act kindly and according to divine mercy toward creatures. Therefore, according to the doctrine of the Cabalists and Hebrew doctors, just as four leaders are counted in the army of God who preside over the corners of the world, its winds, and the four elements—namely **Michael, Gabriel, Uriel, and Raphael**, who (by God’s mercy) govern all things in the sublunary world <note>The world below the moon, i.e., Earth</note> kindly through their good legions—so, by a contrary reasoning, four vengeful standard-bearers are said to carry the banners in the army of Satan. These are **Samael, Azazel, Azael, and Mahazael** (whom others call **Oriens, Amaymon, Paymon, and Egyn**). These are kings and prefects of the evils of corruption and death, just as the four aforementioned royal good angels are most opposed to them by nature and office. But truly, since the mercy of God is said in the sacred letters to excel His severity, the Creator has indeed assigned greater power and virtue to His good Princes than to His malignant ministers; indeed, He gave them dominion over those malignant and devastating spirits or angels. This is best denoted by these words of the Apocalypse, chapter 7: *I saw four Angels standing upon the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth...*

And I saw another angel ascending from the rising of the Sun, having the seal of the living God, and he cried with a loud voice to the four Angels to whom it was given to hurt the earth and the sea, saying: Do not hurt the earth, nor the sea, nor the trees, until we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads. <note>This is a translation of Revelation 7:2–3.</note> From this, it is to be gathered more clearly than light, first: that there are four royal angels, to whose command the four corners or cardinal points of the world are assigned, as well as the powers of the winds blowing from them. Secondly: that these royal demons <note>original: "Dæmones regales"</note> are malignant and harmful, as it is in their power to hurt and afflict with evil the earth, the sea, and the creatures within them. Furthermore, that this good Prince is Michael is declared by the direction from which he ascends—namely, from the rising of the sun—and because he is that leader who is said to have obtained victory against the Dragon and who daily offers holy souls to God. 

Furthermore, Daniel also understood these Cardinal Angels when he said: *Behold, the four winds of heaven strove upon the great sea.* <note>Daniel 7:2</note> And by "winds," the gloss <note>A "gloss" refers to a traditional marginal commentary on the Bible.</note> interprets the four angelic intelligences who preside over the four corners of the world. In the first chariot were red horses, in the second chariot black horses, in the third chariot white horses, and in the fourth chariot dappled and strong horses.* And I said to the Angel, *What are these, my lord?* And the Angel answered, *These are the four winds of heaven, which go forth and stand before the Ruler of all the earth; the black horses went forth into the North country, and the white followed them, and the dappled went forth toward the South country. But the strongest went out and sought to go and walk to and fro through all the earth,* etc. <note>Zechariah 6:1–7</note>. 

By this, he seems to suggest that under the name of winds are understood the Angels presiding over them along with their legions. Similarly, by "mountains of brass," he seems to mean great clouds rushing together from various regions of the world, which he calls "brazen" because they are flashing on all sides with light and lightning. In this, the Prophet Ezekiel seems to agree with Zechariah: *Behold, a whirlwind came out of the North, a great cloud, and a fire infolding itself, and a brightness was about it, and out of the midst thereof the likeness of four living creatures... and the living creatures ran and returned as the appearance of a flash of lightning,* etc.

Hence the Apostle says: *You walked according to the Prince...* <note>Ephesians 2:2</note>

...of the power of this air, etc. Ephesians 6. By this, he means Satan, who is the prince or emperor of the air, under whose Empire there are (according to the doctrine of the Hebrew Doctors) four kings or standard-bearers, who are said to carry the wide sails of Satan. These are the kings previously cited, whom the Apostle calls in another place the Princes, Powers, and lords of darkness in this world (Ephesians 2:2). Under their command are legions of a fourfold nature, corresponding to the four triplicities <note>Groups of three zodiac signs associated with one of the four elements: Fire, Earth, Air, or Water.</note> of the Zodiac. Each of these has three Princes; for example, in the fiery triplicity, there is a prefect for Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius. Their influences in the elementary kingdom are committed to the custody of Samael, if they are ill-affected, or Michael, if they are well-affected. It is for this reason that, according to the twelve prefects of the celestial signs, our Savior mentions legions of angels, saying: *Do you think that I cannot now pray to my Father, and he shall presently give me more than twelve legions of angels? Matthew 26:53.* We have spoken previously of these twelve prefects of the signs and the lords of the four triplicities, who are related to the gates of the heavenly city—namely, three in the east, and just as many in the west, as well as in the south and the north—along with the angels who are their guardians. By a similar reasoning, the wicked angels are also organized into legions; thus, when Christ asked the Demon, *What is your name? he answered, My name is Legion, for we are many. Mark 5.* <note>The OCR cites Mark 8, but this event occurs in Mark 5.</note> From this we can note that the substance of a demon is exceedingly minute, like a solar atom <note>original: "atomi solaris"—referring to the tiny specks of dust visible in a sunbeam, then considered the smallest particles of matter.</note>, and consequently, there is an infinite multitude of demons flying everywhere in the air. This is also confirmed by the Hebrew Doctors in express words; it is their opinion that from the earth all the way to the firmament there is no empty space, but all is full of forms—some of them pure and capable of grace, while below there are many foul, harmful, and tempting images dwelling and flying in the air. Similarly, in the *Gate of Light* <note>original: "Porta lucis," the Latin title of Joseph Gikatilla’s *Sha'are Orah*, a fundamental Kabbalistic text.</note>, it is held that there is no empty space from the earth to the firmament, but it is entirely filled with species: some for war, some for peace, some for good, some for evil, some for life, and some for death; and all this is in the lower habitation in which we exist, as Joseph of Castalla <note>Joseph Gikatilla.</note> reports. From these accounts, it is evident that the number of demons, both bad and good, in this elementary region where we breathe is infinite to us. Some are of the nature of the East, others of the South, some Western, and others Northern, in respect to the regions of the world and the triplicity whose temperament and condition they share.

Furthermore, they are also named from the nature of the planet by whose influences they are chiefly animated and quickened: some are called Saturnine, others Jovial [of Jupiter], Martial [of Mars], Solar, Venereal [of Venus], Mercurial, and Lunar. This is because they are subjects of the Angels or Intelligences presiding over the Planets. Thus it happens that when Saturn predominates in the horoscope or celestial scheme, because his influences are then abundant, the spirits in the elements that share his nature tend to predominate, and so it is with the others.

Finally, each of these is called by a general name based on the element in which it naturally participates and in which it commonly and most willingly lives, as if in its own fatherland. In this, many who are most skilled in the mysteries of demons agree. For first, the Cabalists and Hebrew Doctors say that the demons are squalid and most foul enemies to the human race, which is why, in their opposition to the good angels, they are called Angels of the contrary strength. Yet they admit that some of these wander through the highest region of the air, and these they call **fiery**; those who are accustomed to wander closer to us they call **airy**; those who terrify the land they name **earthy**; those who inhabit lakes and rivers and often shake the sea they call **watery**; and finally, those they call light-shunning and dark, they place as **subterranean**. Psellus <note>Michael Psellos, an 11th-century Byzantine philosopher and author of *De Operatione Daemonum*.</note> also seems to confirm this from the confession of Marcus, saying that only six kinds of these demons are found in the elementary region:

*   The first is **fiery**, which is seen to wander about the sublime region of the air.
*   The second is **airy**, which wanders near to us.
*   The third is **watery**, which plunges itself into fluids, namely lakes, ponds, rivers, and the sea.
*   The fourth is **earthy**, which for the most part occupies itself around the earth.
*   The fifth is **subterranean**, which is accustomed to dwell under the earth.
*   The sixth and last is **light-shunning**, inscrutable, and dark.

These types of Evil Spirits [Cacodemons] are said to hold God, the Angels, and even men in hatred; we shall soon speak more extensively of their properties and conditions.

## *On evil spirits acting upon the human spirit.*

<image-desc>A classification diagram. On the left is the text "Evil spirits <note>Original: *Cacodæmones*</note> who act upon the human spirit are distinguished into six grades <note>Though the text says "six," the author lists eight distinct points below.</note>, of which:" followed by a large curly bracket spanning eight numbered points on the right:</image-desc>
> The First infects with idolatry and vain or false worship, and lures one to adore it.
> The Second contaminates with lies, deceives with false whispers, and leads into error.
> The Third inflames with anger and fury, and finds ways to kindle various passions in them.
> The Fourth fills one with vengeance, retribution, and cruelty.
> The Fifth mocks with illusions and false miracles.
> The Sixth ignites with the discord of wars and the heat of devastations.
> The Seventh slanders, spies, and accuses before the sight of God.
> The Eighth casts one into errors and danger through temptations and snares, and defiles with despair.

The first grade of evil spirits <note>Original: *Cacodæmonum*</note> infesting the human spirit is the order of those called the "false gods" <note>Original: *pseudothei*</note>; for it is their nature to falsely attribute the name of GOD to themselves, and to entice the human spirit to their cult and adoration through false and deceptive demonstrations. Their prince is thought to be *Beelzebub*, that is, the "old god," who is so bold that he did not hesitate to tempt the spirit of the Savior of the world himself, saying, *if you will fall down and worship me, I will give you all these things. Matthew 4.* To this grade also belonged the gods of the Midianites, who, through the daughters of Moab (with whom the people of Israel committed fornication), seduced that people from the worship of the true God, and persuaded them to adore them and offer sacrifices or burnt offerings. *Numbers 25.* Such also was the spirit of the Oracles, namely the Delphic Apollo, and others.

The second grade comprises those who are accustomed to introduce and whisper falsehoods into the spirits of men; of this order was that lying spirit which, by divine command, entered into the mouths of the Prophets of Ahab: *1 Kings 22.* Similarly, it includes that spirit which strikes terror and dread into the spirits of men, of which it is written: *Behold, I will send a spirit upon him, and he shall hear a rumor, and return to his own land. 2 Kings 19.* The prince of this order is called *Python* (that is, the serpent) by those skilled in magic.

Those of the third grade are they who inflame the human spirit with the love of iniquity, anger, and the flame of fury. To perform this office more easily, they invent games, such as cards, dice, and other such things by which men are moved to passion and anger. Such was that demon named *Theuth*, whom Plato says was the teacher of games, specifically of dice; the Hebrews establish their prince to be *Belial*, which is interpreted as "without a yoke," disobedient, or a transgressor.

The fourth grade or order is that which not only drives the human spirit toward vengeance and retribution, but has itself become the author of Divine vengeance. The royal Psalmist <note>Referring to King David, the traditional author of the Psalms.</note> seems to show a precaution against the invasions of such a demon into the human spirit with this discourse: *Cease from anger, and forsake wrath; fret not yourself in any wise to do evil, for evildoers shall be cut off. Psalm 37:8.* And the wise man says: *Be not hasty in your spirit to be angry: for anger rests in the bosom of fools. Ecclesiastes 7.* And elsewhere: *Make no friendship with an angry man; and with a furious man you shall not go. Proverbs 22:24.* Furthermore, that he is an avenger and a minister executing God's vengeance is indicated by this passage cited from Holy Scripture, where such a demon is called: *A spirit venting the power of God and pursuing the unjust with justice. Wisdom 11:21 <note>Douay-Rheims citation; in modern bibles this is Wisdom 11:20.</note>.* And of him elsewhere: *A spirit of power and a spirit of virtue shall stand against them. Wisdom 5:24.* The Kabbalists and Mages identify their prince as *Asmodeus*, that is, "one who executes justice."

The fifth grade consists of those who deceive with illusions and false miracles. The magicians of the Egyptians required the assistance of these when, attempting to work against Moses, they performed so many illusory miracles in the presence of Pharaoh. Evil mages <note>Original: *Cacomagi*</note> and sorcerers implore such aid in their business. Finally, the mages themselves affirm their Prince to be Satan, of whom it is said in the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation.</note> that he seduces the whole world, performing great signs, and making fire descend from heaven to earth in the sight of men, to seduce those dwelling upon it.

The **sixth grade** is said to disseminate discord, war, devastation, and desire through the human spirit; the Prince of these is called **Apollyon** <note>original: "Apollyon", from the Greek for "Destroyer"</note> in the Book of Revelation, and by the Hebrews **Abaddon**, which means "the exterminating and devastating one." To this order also belonged that Angel standing between heaven and earth, whom Jehovah sent to lose and destroy Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 21:15), and the one who slew every man of great strength in the camp of the King of Assyria (2 Chronicles 32).

The **seventh grade** is accustomed to slandering, spying upon, and accusing spirits in the presence of Jehovah. The magi call him **Astaroth**, which means "the spy," and in Greek he is called the **Devil** <note>original: "Diabolum"</note>, which means "the slanderer and false accuser."

The **last grade** <note>the eighth</note> attempts to deceive the human spirit through temptations and snares, leading it into error and despair. The Prince of such demons is said to be **Mammon**, whom they interpret as "Greed" or "Desire."

### On Demons acting wickedly upon the spirit and physical members of the Macrocosm. <note>The "Macrocosm" refers to the great world or the universe, as opposed to the "Microcosm" of the individual human being.</note>

**Demons act, sometimes malevolently, upon the bodies and spirits of the sublunary macrocosm <note>the world beneath the moon</note> by the Divine Will; from which there arises in:**

*   **The Thick Air:** Inflammation from fiery winds <note>original: "prestere"</note> and flashes of lightning; disturbance from windy whirlwinds; gloom from mists and thick vapors; the evening redness, and so on.
*   **The Cloud:** Blazing fire; burning coals and small stones; dark gloom; hail and snow; thunder.
*   **The Sea:** Disturbance of the waters; the rising and falling of waves; the agitation of the internal spirit <note>of the water</note>.
*   **The Earth:** Trembling and shaking; fire and destruction from fire sent down from heaven; gaps and fissures; flooding and submersion; dryness and sterility.

The schools of Theologians recognize that the sixth grade of **Evil Spirits** <note>original: "Cacodæmonum"</note>, according to their own division, consists of those who are **aerial powers** <note>original: "potestates aereæ"</note>. However, we include all the previously mentioned grades in this order, since it is not our intention to define any separate species that is not encompassed under one of the aforementioned winds, or the cardinal governors of the world, or the four Elements. But because all these demons are powers of the air itself, or sublunary spirits, we therefore say that the remaining evil spirits—whether they are occupied with man or any other thing in the world—are included under their command. 

The school of Theologians therefore recognizes that these aerial powers mingle with thunder, lightning-bolts, and flashes of light, corrupting the air and bringing about pestilences and other evils. The Book of Revelation seems to affirm that their Princes are those **four angels** holding the four winds, in whose power it is to harm the sea and the earth. Their Prince they identify as **Meririm**, that is, the "sweltering spirit" or the "demon who rages at Midday." But **Paul** calls him the "Prince of the power of this air, who works in the children of disobedience." 

And a certain wise man, deep in the mysteries of God and nature, speaks in these words in his treatise *On the Revelation of Divine Majesty*: *"Together with the air, God also created by His word angels and spirits, who perform and execute their task and office in the air regarding the direction of storms, both bad and good—rain, snow, hail, frost, clouds, lightning, thunderbolts, thunder, 'thunder-stones' <note>original: "lapidis ceraunei", referring to prehistoric stone tools once believed to fall from the sky during storms</note>, fire, chasms, comets, floods of water, heat, cold, moisture, dryness, and many other things of this kind; and this very thing still happens even today through His word."* 

Regarding all these matters, those secular "wise men" or philosophers write books for themselves that are wonderfully foolish; in these books, not even a single point—let alone a whole letter—is true. Instead, whatever has flowed from their brains onto the pen and paper is all that can be read in them, which is absolutely nothing but pure, unadulterated lies. Indeed, the very "spirit of the mouth" in those wise men is entirely lying and false, yet they still wish to be called wise. This happens solely because they know neither God nor His most holy Word. Thus he spoke.

Sect. I, Port. IV, Part. II. Lib. IV. Membr. II.

The lowest region of the Macrocosm <note>The "Macrocosm" refers to the great world or the universe, as opposed to the "Microcosm" of the individual human.</note>, being subject to various passions and changes, is observed to have its airy spirit distinguished into various degrees of corporeality. Before any of these degrees are reached, both the external body and its internal spirit are afflicted and driven by the angelic spirits or ministers of God—namely, those of the wind as well as those of the burning flame. For David confessed that *God makes his angels winds, and his ministers a burning fire (Psalm 104:4).* And in the preceding psalm: *That the angels of God, most mighty in strength, carry out the word of God, listening to the voice of his command, and that they are the armies and ministers of God doing his pleasure, etc. (Psalm 103:20-21).* In this discourse of the royal Psalmist, we are taught that there are three principal orders of angels: the first and superior order, receiving the outpouring of God directly, is accustomed to effect—that is, to receive and send forth—the word of God; the second order listens to and observes that word as if issued by the supreme Commander, and then commits that mandate to the legion assigned to its dominion for execution; the third order is that which immediately performs and carries out the pleasure of the Creator.

More recent theologians also seem to admit this same point: namely, that the superior orders of Angels receive light or emanation directly from God, which they afterwards impart and communicate by flowing into the lower orders.

Moreover, God uses some of these Angels to carry out the effects of his wrath and vengeance; these we therefore call "malignant" and "cacodemons" <note>original: "cacodaemones", from the Greek for "evil spirits"</note> in relation to ourselves, yet they are nonetheless necessary ministers of God. Thus, God used Satan as his minister to tempt Job. So too was that destroying Angel of Jehovah, whom David saw with raised eyes standing between heaven and earth with his sword drawn in his hand and stretched out against Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 21). And also that one whom Jehovah sent to cut down every man of great strength in the camp of the King of Assyria (2 Chronicles 32). Such also was that evil spirit from Jehovah which possessed Saul, and so on. He also uses others in his kindness, who are called "good" and "benign" spirits; such was the Angel who appeared to Elijah in the desert and offered him food, and the one whom God sent before Moses and the Israelites to keep them on their journey through the wilderness (Exodus 33). And that Angel who redeemed Jacob from all evil (Genesis 48). And the angels who met him on his journey (Genesis 32). Finally, all those angels whom God sends before the righteous (Genesis 24:7). Similarly, by the ministry of good angels, the spirit of the Macrocosm is governed kindly and peacefully, just as it is disturbed by the dominance of tumultuous spirits, through which even sublunary <note>The "sublunary" region refers to the Earth and its atmosphere, the area "below the moon" where change and decay occur.</note> bodies are seen to fall ill.

The first embodiment that occurs between simple air and a perfectly mixed body is the "breath-like" or "cloudy" air, in which various preternatural impressions are produced by evil spirits: namely, inflammation from fire-blasts <note>original: "prestere", a term for a fiery whirlwind or lightning-producing storm</note> and lightning, disturbance from winds and whirlwinds, gloom from clouds and thick vapors, evening redness, and so on. Regarding the intemperance of the air from such fire-blasts, Holy Scripture speaks thus: *Behold, a whirlwind came out of the North, and a great cloud, and a fire infolding itself, and a brightness was about it, and out of the midst of the fire as it were the appearance of amber, and out of the midst thereof the likeness of four living creatures... and the spirit was in the four wheels, etc. (Ezekiel 1).* By these words the Prophet wishes to imply that the soul of both that cloud and that fire-blast was that spirit—or rather the charioteer of that chariot—and that the Lord who was carried in it was Jehovah himself, as we can gather from that entire chapter. And Isaiah says: *By the Lord God of hosts shall it be visited with thunder, and with earthquake, and great noise, with storm and tempest, and the flame of devouring fire (Isaiah 29:6).* And Jeremiah says: *Behold, the whirlwind of the Lord goes forth in fury, a rushing tempest; it shall rest upon the head of the wicked (Jeremiah 30:23).* And the royal Psalmist: *Upon the wicked he shall rain snares, fire, and brimstone, joined with a stormy whirlwind (Psalm 11:6).* And elsewhere: *As the fire burns a wood, and as the flame sets the mountains on fire, so persecute them with thy tempest, and make them afraid with thy whirlwind (Psalm 83:14-15).* And regarding the whirlwind, Isaiah says *it comes from the South (Isaiah 21:1).* And Zechariah: *The Lord God shall blow the trumpet, and shall go with whirlwinds of the south (Zechariah 9:14).* And Job says: *Out of the south <note>original: "penetrali", literally "the inner chamber", often interpreted as the south in biblical contexts</note> comes the whirlwind, and cold from the scatterers (Job 37:9)*—that is, from the spirits or demons who, by their blowing, carry out the will of God from the North. We conclude, therefore, that its internal part is a stormy spirit of God, effecting the word and will of God, as the Prophet David acknowledges. Whence the Wise Man also says: *The spirit of the power of God shall stand against the wicked, and like a whirlwind of wind shall scatter them (Wisdom 5).*

Furthermore, clouds are the vehicles of God which are carried and animated, and are seen to be moved with violent motion in the air and preternaturally disturbed by the angels of God and his presence. In his presence, angelic ministers always stand and assist. Hence the Prophet says: *He ascended upon the Cherubim, and flew upon the wings of the winds, and he made darkness his secret place; round about him was his tabernacle, dark waters in the clouds of the skies. At the brightness that was before him his thick clouds passed, hailstones and coals of fire. The Lord also thundered in the heavens, and the Highest gave his voice; hailstones and coals of fire. And he sent out his arrows, and scattered them; and he multiplied lightnings and discomfited them, etc. (Psalm 18:10-14).* In this discourse, the Prophet clearly teaches that the ministers of the Lord are the Cherubim and the winds—as if he had said, the angels listening to his voice, and the winds or angelic spirits, fiery ministers, carrying out his pleasure, as he confesses elsewhere. And elsewhere he says: *The waters saw thee and were afraid, the depths also were troubled. The clouds poured out water, the skies sent out a sound; thine arrows also went abroad. The voice of thy thunder was in the whirlwind; the lightnings lightened the world; the earth trembled and shook (Psalm 77:16-18).* And elsewhere: *The waters shall be afraid at the voice of thy thunder (Psalm 104:7).* Finally, with even more expressive words, David reveals all of this in the following: *O Lord, clothed with light as with a garment, stretching out the heavens like a curtain, who lays the beams of his chambers in the waters, who makes the clouds his chariot, who walks upon the wings of the wind, who makes his angels spirits, and*

### On the Efficient Cause of Atmospheric Phenomena <note>original: "De Causa Meteororum Efficiente." In this period, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, such as rain, wind, or lightning, not just falling stars.</note>

...your ministers a burning fire, the Abyss like a garment is his covering, the waters shall stand upon the mountains; at your rebuke they shall flee, at the voice of your thunder they shall be afraid. *Psalm 104:2.* By these words, it seems to be proven that Jehovah is the prince and supreme commander, who has his tabernacle in the clouds, whom angels—both fiery and windy—serve, and that the clouds seem to be troubled, to fear, and to roar at the sight of his splendor, and finally to behave in a supernatural manner. The third step in the progression from the invisible nature of the air to a perfectly mixed body is water, whose primary element is the sea; this, along with rivers and lakes, is either rendered peaceful by the good spirit of Jehovah, or is disturbed by the evil spirit of Jehovah and stirred up to the harm of sailors. Hence the royal Psalmist says: *You break the ships of the ocean with the East wind (Psalm 48:8); that is, with a vehement blast sent by the divine will through Samael <note>In certain mystical traditions, Samael is an archangel often associated with severity or the East wind.</note> or the East.* And elsewhere: *You who trouble the deep of the sea (Psalm 65).* And elsewhere he acknowledges that the sea is stirred by the rebuke of Jehovah, and that the sea, seeing Jehovah, fled away. *Psalm 114:3.* And Job says: *By his power the sea is stilled, and by his understanding he has struck down pride. Job 26:12.* From this, one may see that it is God’s role both to disturb and to restore quiet to the sea or the element of water. But the royal prophet expresses this best and in the most lucid words elsewhere, saying: *Those who go down to the sea in ships, they see the works of Jehovah and his wonders in the deep; and he speaks, and makes the spirit of the whirlwind blow, and lifts up its waves; they mount up to the heaven, they go down even to the depths, so that their soul melts in distress; they are tossed and stagger like drunken men, so that all their wisdom is swallowed up. Then they cry out to Jehovah in their trouble, and he leads them out of their distress; he makes the whirlwind stand in silence, and their waves are still; they celebrate the mercy of Jehovah and proclaim his wonders to the sons of men. Psalm 107:23-31 <note>The source text cites this as verse 33, but the passage corresponds to verses 23–31.</note>.*

Here, therefore, you see first that Jehovah is the commander of all powers, and the first actor and operator of all things; secondly, that in his severity he deals severely with the elements of the world because of the sins of men; and then thirdly, that he acts through his angelic ministers, who are always ready—according to their own office, whether good or evil—to carry out the commands and pleasure of the Divine. For he says: *And he makes the spirit of the whirlwind blow.* But through the repentance of men and their cries for mercy, he makes the tumultuous whirlwind stand still. Here, moreover, the spirit of the whirlwind is an angelic wind, executing the severity of God upon the sea; which, at Jehovah’s command, acts upon the internal spirit of the sea and lakes in an insane, tumultuous, and furious manner—no differently than that evil spirit of Jehovah acted upon the internal airy spirit of Saul himself, or the demon called Legion in that possessed man, which by the power of Jesus was cast out and entered into the swine; or as in those vexed by the worst epilepsy, who swell with a great swelling and cast foam from their mouths; or in those affected by that rabid disease called <term>Lycanthropy</term> <note>A delusion where a person believes they have changed into a wolf.</note>, who are tossed and carried here and there in a violent manner. Thus does that violent spirit act with its legions in the sea, and lakes, and ponds, etc.

Finally, since the earth is the denser part of water, we have now arrived at it, which we say is also sometimes tossed and struck by the evil spirits of God. Hence the Sacred Page says: *The earth is shaken and moved, the foundations of the heavens are moved; it is shaken when his anger is kindled against it. 2 Samuel 22:8.* And elsewhere: *God moves the earth out of its place, so that its columns tremble; he removes the mountains. Job 9:5-6.* And elsewhere: *At the sight of God the earth trembled, and at his touch the mountains smoke. Psalm 104:32.* But indeed, in such an act of God, he himself uses spiritual ministers destined for that work, who, at the command of the angelic prefect, shake the earth, produce huge chasms in it, vomit fires from its bowels, and are accustomed to perpetrate many other terrifying things on the earth. Hence also, when God was angry at the impiety of the Jews, it was said: *Behold, there was a great earthquake, for the angel of the Lord descended from heaven, and his appearance was like lightning, etc. Matthew 28:2.* Sometimes also through his avenging angels, Jehovah sends down fire and sulfur upon the earth, by which it is subverted and treated supernaturally. *And Jehovah (says Genesis) sent down upon Sodom and Gomorrah a rain of sulfur and fire from the heavens, and subverted the city and the entire plain, and all the inhabitants, and the growth of the ground, etc. Genesis 19:24.* But that Jehovah used his angels in such a business is explained in that very context. And elsewhere it is said: *The land is burnt with salt and sulfur, so that it can neither be sown nor sprout, nor can any herb grow in it, etc. Deuteronomy 29:23.* Which indeed Jehovah produced through the mediation of his ministers for the inhabitants of the earth because of their sins. And elsewhere: *Jehovah will cause your rain to be powder, or dust shall descend from the heavens upon you until you are destroyed. Deuteronomy 28:24.* Furthermore, in another place the Psalmist says: *He turns a fruitful land into a salt waste, because of the wickedness of the men dwelling in it; conversely, he turns a desert into a pool of water and a parched land into springs of water, etc.* By which he seems to argue that in his severity God renders the earth as dry and sterile as it is suffocated by an excessive flood of waters, because of the sins of men; which the <term>Cabalists</term> <note>Mystics who study the Jewish tradition of the Kabbalah, often focusing on the hierarchy of angels and the names of God.</note> and those versed in the deeper mysteries of God hand down as being done by him through his ministers.

For just as they have assigned angelic prefects to the elements—namely, Seruph to fire, Cherub to air, Tharsis to water <note>The original Latin text repeats "igni" (fire) for Tharsis, but Tharsis is traditionally the angel of water; the translation corrects this for clarity.</note>, and Ariel to the Earth, who are good leaders—so indeed under them act four malevolent spirits: namely, Samael from the fiery part, Azazel from the airy part, Alzael from the watery part, and Mahazael from the earthy part; under whose command (as was said before) are many orders of inferior demons. Therefore, both fiery and bright tempests with such comets proceed from fiery angels; likewise, atmospheric impressions from airy angels; as from the watery ones come those which disturb the waters; and it is the role of earthy spirits, as <term>Psellus</term> <note>Michael Psellus, an 11th-century Byzantine monk and scholar whose works on demonology were highly influential in the Renaissance.</note> testifies, to cause openings in the earth and shake the foundations, and to send forth flame-vomiting winds from below.

There is no doubt that Evil Spirits <note>original: "Cacodæmones"</note>, as deadly enemies to mankind, afflict both the human spirit and body in the same way they afflict the air, water, and earth in the Macrocosm <note>the universe at large</note>. For since man is a "son" of the World in respect to his composition, and since man himself is considered to be the ultimate end of all created things, it follows that these wicked demons are ordained by God for the punishment of sinning men, just as the good angels are ordained for obedience, protection, and prosperity. 

However, all these spirits, being ministers of God ordained for the punishment of the world and of men, are able to achieve nothing unless it is permitted to them by God. This is clearly shown by the example of Job (Job 1, 2) and the Demoniac whom Christ liberated (Matthew 8:31). Hence the Demon said to Christ, *If you cast us out, send us into the herd of swine*, and He said, *Go*. Therefore, when God curses a man or a people, then these destroying angels are ready to carry out the will of God. 

In this way, when God cursed the people for the sin of David, the destroying angel was immediately present to destroy Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 21). Furthermore, at the word of Jehovah, an angel was ready in a moment and struck down every man of valor in the camp of the Assyrians—namely, 185,000 men (2 Kings 19). Thus we see that the immediate inflictor of the plague is the destroying angel of God, who is also called the "Waster" and the "Exterminator" in other places. 

But truly, just as the sin of man is the occasion for disease and death, the devil is not only ready for the infliction of evils, but—in order to be let in for such duty and execution—he is accustomed to invite man to sin with hidden allurements. For Evil Spirits of this kind, especially those of an airy nature, are familiar with our own external or "aery" spirit due to their composition. They can very easily insinuate themselves with hidden whispers and drive the human faculty of imagination <note>original: "sensum phantasticum"</note> and incite it toward that which will seem evil in the eyes of God. 

Once this is done, the demon then has power over the man's airy spirit and his body; however, he cannot penetrate into the "human heaven" (the temple of the Holy Spirit), for he is an exile from heaven. Adam mourned this cunning of the devil too late, for having been led by the allurements of the serpent, he fell from heaven into the sphere of sin. Indeed, even the Royal Prophet <note>King David</note>, however wise and spiritually elevated, could not safely escape the devil's deceits; caught in those snares, not only he but the entire people were vexed with a plague for that same sin. Do we not read this in express words on the holy page: namely, that the Devil incited David to number the people of Israel, so that...

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the spiritual causes of affliction. While the previous page categorized different types of diseases based on their elemental nature (Aereal, Aqueous, Fiery, etc.), this page explains the theological and mechanical process by which God uses both good and evil angels as ministers to enact these physical and mental states upon humanity.</meta>

# On the Efficient Cause of Meteors. <note>In early modern science, "Meteors" referred not just to falling stars, but to all atmospheric phenomena and "vapors" that influenced both the weather and the human body.</note>

...in this way, would he bring a plague upon him? (1 Chronicles 21). Yet, even when a human sins, it is not within the power of a destroying angel to afflict him with evil, unless **GOD**, setting aside His mercy and putting on the cloak of severity, has said: "Let it be done," or "Let him be struck." Thus, in Exodus we have this pronounced by **GOD**: *I am about to send all my plagues upon your heart, and upon your servants, and upon your people in all the earth* (Exodus 9:14). And elsewhere: *The Lord will make the pestilence cling to you, and the Lord will strike you with consumption, and with a burning fever, and with inflammation, and with fiery heat, and with drought, and with blight, and with the "royal disease" <note>original: "morbo regio," traditionally referring to jaundice or scrofula</note>, which shall pursue you until you perish. And the Lord will strike you with the boils of Egypt, and with hemorrhoids, and with the scab, and with the itch, of which you cannot be healed. And the Lord will strike you with madness, and blindness, and astonishment of heart, so that you shall grope at midday as a blind man gropes in darkness. And he will strike you with a malignant ulcer in the legs and knees, such that you cannot be healed* (Deuteronomy 28).

Once these things are pronounced by **GOD**, as if by a decree, the evil Angel stands ready with his subordinates to carry out what **GOD** has spoken. Thus it is said that the devil struck Job with a most terrible ulcer from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head (Job 2). And yet, Job said in this adversity: *the arrows of the Almighty are heavy within me; my spirit drinks their poison; the terrors of GOD, drawn up in battle array, war against me* (Job 6:4). And elsewhere: *You have lifted me up to the wind, you have made me melt away in substance* (Job 30:22). From these examples, one may see that where a destroying angel is permitted to afflict a man with disease, that entire work—though performed through a ministering agent—is ascribed to God, who afflicts with disease through evil angels, just as He restores health through good ones.

Evil angels do not afflict with disease, nor do good ones bless a man with health, by their own power; rather, both health and sickness come from **GOD** through the angels. From this it follows: *If you diligently attend to the voice of the Lord your God, and do what is right in my eyes, I will put none of the diseases upon you which I brought upon the Egyptians, for I, the Lord, shall be your creator <note>or "healer"</note>* etc. (Exodus 15:26).

This means: "I will bring it about and command that the good angels—such as **Raphael** <note>The name Raphael literally means "God heals"</note>, along with his angels—shall cure you, or my word through the angel," etc. Hence the name Raphael is as if we said "God healing."

We conclude, therefore, that it is **GOD** who strikes and who heals, but He does this through His ministering angels, whose role is to do His pleasure. Thus, there is no evil demon who can strike without the permission of the good ones, nor can a guardian angel grant permission or cease his protection (for everyone has their own good guardian angel) except by God’s command. Concerning the types of these spirits and their contrary conditions, mention was made where it was said: "that the good spirit of the Lord departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord troubled him." Wherefore his servants said: *Behold now, an evil spirit from God troubles you* (1 Samuel 16:15).

Thus it is also manifest that evil angels, or **Cacodaemons** <term>Cacodaemons: literally "evil spirits" or "bad demons" (from the Greek kakos and daimon)</term>, are the instrument of **GOD** in His severity, just as the good ones are in His mercy. David also confesses this in plain speech: *He cast upon them the fierceness of His anger, indignation, and wrath, and trouble, by sending evil angels among them; for He struck all the firstborn, and spared not their cattle from death* etc. (Psalm 78:49). From these words it is clear enough that although Moses speaks of "the destroyer" or a destroying angel, nevertheless many angels or Cacodaemons were assisting in that work. **Artesius** <note>Likely a reference to an earlier medieval or Renaissance medical authority</note> declares the aptitude of demons, by which they have power over men abandoned by **GOD**, in these words:

> "There are certain infirmities in which the devil joins himself when a humor <term>Humor: one of the four vital bodily fluids (blood, phlegm, black bile, yellow bile) that determined health and temperament</term> departs from its proper balance and disturbs health itself. This happens most especially in infirmities arising from **cholera** <note>Yellow bile</note>. The reason is this: the Devil's internal nature is fire, and his external nature is air; therefore, by God's permission, he can easily join with the human 'air' <note>The "spiritus" or vital breath within the body</note>."

So he says. But the role of good angels is to bind the elements in harmonious peace, as they are the children of concord. Therefore, when these angels, by the divine will, vacate their office, it happens that the evil demons—who are the offspring of discord—suddenly invade and attempt to turn human harmony into dissonance. Thus it is clear that demons, according to their elemental natures, are accustomed to procreate various diseases in the human body.

For this reason, **Albohali** <note>Abu Ali al-Khayyat, an 8th-century astrologer/physician</note> says that **Melancholy** comes from a demon. And **Alzarabius** <note>Al-Zahrawi/Albucasis, a famous medieval surgeon</note> says that ailments invade men from the transgressions and curses of demons who are called **Alhabinables** <note>A corrupted Arabic term for certain harmful spirits or influences</note>. And **Psellus** <note>Michael Psellos, an 11th-century Byzantine scholar</note>, from the revelation of Marcus, says that "aerial spirits" or demons bring harm to men by approaching the "phantastic spirit" <term>Phantastic spirit: the faculty of imagination (phantasia) in the soul, believed to be composed of a subtle, airy substance</term> that dwells within us, because of the similarity between their two natures. By this means, the words of disturbances and pleasures sound within us; they do not emit a voice through percussion and sound, but send forth their discourses without sound. They speak into the ear in a silent manner, whispering, and they present various colors to the imagination according to their will, insofar as they are airy—for air is capable of all colors. From this, their phantastic essence transmits figures, colors, and whatever forms they themselves wish into our very animal spirit. Thus they cause us much trouble, suggesting desires and plans, representing forms, stirring up memories of pleasures, and frequently inciting images of passions in those who are awake and those who sleep. Sometimes, by tickling our thighs and groins, they suggest and sharpen insane and wicked loves. These spirits disturb the soul with a certain art and sophisticated fraud.

But indeed, the watery and earthy demons devise nothing with wisdom, nor do they perform anything with cunning, except for what is troublesome, and they harm in the manner of a **Charonean spirit** <note>A spirit of the underworld or the dead, named after Charon the ferryman</note>. It is the property of these spirits to corrupt whatever they come near, whether it be a four-footed beast, a man, or a bird.
