### Section I. Portion IV. Part II. Book IV. Member II.

These spirits suddenly harm and sometimes destroy the bodies and minds they agitate, perverting the natural faculties. They often kill both men and beasts through fire, water, or by casting them from heights. Such spirits do not attack out of a simple will to do harm—though they are indeed the most bitter enemies of humanity—but rather out of a greed for life-giving heat. They invade both humans and animals, especially those spirits who dwell in deep, freezing, and moistureless places. Because they contract extreme cold and "burning" dryness in those depths, they flee from it and seek out animal heat, which is moderate and mixed with pleasant moisture. They especially favor human heat, as it is more tempered. 

Thus, when they invade bodies, they disturb them significantly by clogging and filling those passages where the **animal spirit** <note>In early medicine, the "animal spirit" was a subtle fluid believed to travel through the nerves to facilitate sensation and movement.</note> resides. Once the animal spirit is constricted by the density of these demonic bodies and shaken from within, the physical body begins to vibrate and shake. Their principal powers fail to function correctly, resulting in sluggish and erratic movements. 

If one of these invading demons is of the subterranean type, it convulses and destroys the person it has occupied, crying out through them, using the victim's breath and voice as if it were its own instrument. If the demon is **light-shunning** <note>original: "lucifugus"</note>, it brings on a profound lethargy, stifles the voice, and makes the obsessed person appear as if dead. This type is the most earthly of all, being exceedingly cold and dry; therefore, wherever it creeps in, it blunts, numbs, darkens, and destroys all vital animal power.

Consequently, this kind is called the "mute and deaf" spirit, and it does not depart from those it occupies unless repelled by divine power—namely, through prayer and fasting. **Psellus** <note>Michael Psellus (c. 1017–1078) was a Byzantine scholar whose work "On the Operation of Demons" was a primary source for Renaissance demonologists.</note> learned these things from the observations of Mark, who lived in the desert for a long time to learn the duties and properties of demons by conversing with them.

We conclude, therefore, that demons tend to induce diseases that match their own nature and elemental disposition. Thus, fiery demons cause fiery diseases, aerial demons cause windy or respiratory ones, aqueous demons cause watery ones, and earthly demons cause sluggish and "earthy" conditions. However, they sometimes mix together, producing a **hybrid disease** <note>original: "morbum... spurium"</note>, as will be explained more fully below.

**Evil Spirits** infect the spirit and body of both worlds <note>Referring to the Macrocosm (the universe) and the Microcosm (the human body).</note> by corrupting either:

        *   **Meteors** <note>The term "Meteors" here refers to any atmospheric phenomenon, such as comets (fiery) or clouds (aqueous).</note> (Fiery, such as a comet; or Aqueous, such as a cloud.)
        *   **Water.**
        *   **Earth.**
2.  **Water.**
3.  **The Earth.**

The various sects of physicians acknowledge that when the mind or spirit is disturbed, the body is also disturbed, and vice versa. This is also a well-worn and proven fact in the **Macrocosm** <note>The "Great World" or the universe at large.</note>: when the air of a place or region is corrupted, the water and earth are also corrupted, as are the creatures—especially the humans—living there. Holy Scripture agrees with this, saying:

> *And the Lord shall strike you with corrupt air, etc.* <note>original: "aere corrupto"</note>

And elsewhere:

> *The Lord will strike you with consumption, and with a fever, and with cold, and with burning heat, and with parching heat, and with corrupt air, and with blight, etc.* (Deuteronomy 28:22).

And Solomon, in the passage where he reveals the method of curing diseases through prayer, speaks these words:

> *If there be a pestilence or if corrupt air arises, or blight, or mildew, etc.* (1 Kings 8:37).

From these it is evident that the ministers of God are permitted to corrupt the air, as it is their role to execute the Lord's decrees. For they are accustomed to scatter the seeds of contagion through the open air, a fact which the Royal Prophet <note>King David, the traditional author of the Psalms.</note> seems to verify in this discourse:

From this discourse it is clear, first, that the air is infected by the **Noonday Demon** <note>original: "dæmonio meridiano." In the Latin Vulgate, Psalm 91:6 refers to a specific demon of the midday, often associated by theologians with spiritual sloth or sudden plague.</note> and its legions; and second, that God appoints good angels to preserve men from the evil ones.

The School of Theologians seems to infer nearly the same thing as the Prophet when they define the sixth rank of **Evil Spirits** <note>original: "Cacodæmonum"</note> as those called **Aerial Powers**. These spirits mingle with thunder, lightning, and thunderbolts; they are said to corrupt the air and, by this means, bring about pestilences and other evils. The poisonous dregs of these worst-disposed elements, turned toward malignancy, are those springs from which those four contagious and poisonous rivers of the infernal kingdom seem to gush. ## II. On the Efficient Cause of Meteors.
<note>In this period, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, including rain, wind, lightning, and rainbows, not just falling space rocks. The "efficient cause" is the active force or agent that makes these things happen.</note>

ready at a moment to execute divine commands: From this it happens that, by the divine will, they are found everywhere suddenly and as if in the blink of an eye, for the help and assistance of men, just as the divine mind intends. But truly, although they are said to move, they are not considered to be contained within a physical place in a "definitive" sense—seeing as they are not, in themselves, long, wide, dense, or rare, but are instead intellectual beings. However, insofar as they take up a body for themselves, they are said to be "circumscribed" <note>To be "circumscribed" means to be limited by physical boundaries or occupy a specific volume of space.</note>, as is found everywhere in the Holy Scriptures. Therefore, although they are near and present, in their simple nature they are said to work everywhere as God wills. Furthermore, their existence in a place is distinguished from that of God and other creatures. According to theologians, God is said to be in a place, but not "definitively" like angels and spiritual creatures, nor "circumscriptively" like physical things; rather, He is said to be present to all things in a threefold way, as **Gregory** <note>St. Gregory the Great (c. 540–604), a prominent Father of the Church.</note> holds: namely, **by presence** <note>original: "praesentialiter"</note> so that He may set forth good to them; **by power** <note>original: "potentialiter"</note> through influence; and **by essence** <note>original: "essentialiter"</note> through the intimacy of His essence; and in this way, He is said to fill all things. An **Angel**, in its separate nature, is said to be in a place definitively but not circumscriptively, insofar as it works everywhere, even though it is near to any given thing by presence. Thus we say the **Sun** is in a bedroom through the flow of its rays into that place, although at the very same moment the solar essence is not denied its place in the heavens, in the waters, in the air, and throughout the entire hemisphere of the earth. 

But here a question arises that is not easily solved, namely: Do the super-celestial and celestial angels penetrate and descend personally to these lower regions? Or do they, while remaining in heaven, tend to care for these lower things through their "effluxes" or outflows alone? In the resolution of this doubt, the wise men most skilled in the mysteries of the **Intelligences** <note>"Intelligences" was a common term for the angels who were believed to move the celestial spheres.</note> seem to differ. For we receive from the **Cabalists** <note>Followers of Kabbalah, a school of Jewish mysticism that heavily influenced Renaissance thought.</note> that although the 72 angels (who have the power to divide the whole circle of the earth into 72 parts or regions, over each of which a specific angel from the 72 previously numbered presides) dwell in the super-celestial world, they nonetheless care for these lower things—namely, various kingdoms through various influences. From this we see it happen that one region differs from another as much by the condition of the sun or soil as by the character of the people. Hence **Photinus** <note>Likely referring to the Neoplatonist philosopher Plotinus (c. 204–270), whose work focused on "Intellect, Ideas, and Being."</note> says in his book *On Intellect, Ideas, and Being*, that this sensible world is determined by only one place, but he affirms the "intelligible world" is everywhere; and consequently, he intends that the intelligible world surrounds, orders, preserves, and penetrates this world of ours. Hence the wise men of the Cabalists assert that there is no herb or plant on earth that does not have a **star** in the firmament which strikes it with its influence and cries out to it, as if with a hidden and Angelic voice, "grow and multiply after your kind." In this, the Holy Page <note>A common way to refer to the Bible.</note> seems to agree with them, breaking out in these words: *Do you know the laws of heaven: if you have placed a prefect, or president, or executor on the earth?* <note>original: "Num nosti leges caelorū: si posueris praefectum vel praesidē vel executorem in terra" — a paraphrase of Job 38:33.</note> by which it indicates there are presidents, though the manner of their intimate operation is quite difficult to grasp. 

The **Apostle** <note>St. Paul.</note>, however, seems to disagree with the aforementioned Cabalists in this matter, saying that although all angels are ministers of God and assist Him, they are nonetheless sent at the good pleasure of the Prince; and though they are sent, they always assist God, according to that spoken by **Christ**: *Their angels always see the face of the Father* (Matthew 18). So also there was the angel who is personally said to have descended from heaven, and rolled back the stone of the tomb, and sat upon it, whose appearance was like lightning and his clothing like snow (Matthew 28). Similarly, **Raphael** appeared to **Tobit**, **Gabriel** to **Daniel** and **Mary**, and we have infinite other examples in the Holy Bible of the real appearance of Angels and Archangels in this world. 

However, unless I am mistaken, this controversy of theirs can be removed and contracted into one: that just as the image of the sun is in the heavens, while its light and brightness are here on earth, so also the person of an angel can be where it wills, and the "rays of its power"—which are indivisible from its essence—can be everywhere. Therefore, without a doubt, an angel appears personally and cares for bodies, and yet it is accustomed to transfer itself really and essentially wherever it is commanded by God, but in such a way that it can look back upon and presently care for the office assigned to it by God at creation. So also a **candle**, led into this or that part of the dark air, does not cease to look upon and illuminate the entire darkness of the place. Furthermore, it is to be trusted that just as heaven is everywhere, and God is also present—namely everywhere in the vast spirit of the world, in water, and in every point of the earth—so indeed every single angel is accustomed to claim for itself the privilege of ubiquity. But wherever it is not in its distinct essence, there the rays of its essence are nonetheless accustomed to be poured in; this operation is properly called **influence** <note>term: "influence" (Latin: influentia). In historical science, this was a physical/spiritual "flowing in" of power from stars or angels into the earthly realm.</note>, about which the Cabalists have spoken so many and such great words, and which can no more be divided or distinguished from the essence of the angel than solar rays from the sun—but back to the point.

Regarding the senses of angels, the wise men well-schooled in the Cabala say (**Reuchlin**, Book 3 of *The Art of the Cabala* <note>Johannes Reuchlin (1455–1522) was a German humanist who pioneered the study of Hebrew and Kabbalah among Christians.</note>): that what tongues are to our minds, ears are to the angels; and just as divine spirits speak with the tongues of angels, so human spirits listen with the "ears of their minds." Hence it is that a non-signifying voice <note>A "non-signifying voice" refers to sounds or names (like those used in ritual magic) that do not have a standard dictionary meaning but carry spiritual power.</note> can do more in **magic** than a signifying one. Any voice is powerful in magic insofar as it is formed by the voice of God, because that in which nature exercises magic is the voice of God. But that voice of God is not like that of a man, but like the word of **Jehovah**, which (witnessed by Jehovah) is in the angel; thus the voice of the angel is mixed from the divine will (or the "luminous word") and the angelic nature (or the "spiritual and aerial organ"). Therefore it is established that this becomes very hidden and familiar to the mind alone. But truly, at times, having taken up a body, they are accustomed to strike our ears with an articulate voice, as we find everywhere in the Holy Page.

### Section I. Portion IV. Part II. Book IV. Member II.

It is also a characteristic of theirs to occasionally take on various appearances and forms that are visible to our physical eyes. This is why they sometimes appear in human form, sometimes as fire, and at other times they take on the form of air and wind. Not infrequently, they are perceived in the appearance of a river or water, or they may be clothed in the likeness of birds, gems, or precious stones. Some even dwell within the human spirit. Thus, the Prophet <term>Zechariah</term> <note>A Hebrew prophet (c. 520 BC) whose visions are recorded in the Old Testament.</note> saw an angel coming out of him who spoke to another angel. Sometimes they are seen in the shapes of letters and characters, or occasionally in the sound of a voice, and so it is with many other types of visions which are contained abundantly in the sacred scriptures. The more esoteric <note>original: "secretiores"</note> theologians seem to support this assertion of ours.

The reason why they are so suited and ready to take on any form is because, as spiritual and aerial substances of singular purity, they possess within themselves all "intelligible forms" <note>In the philosophy of the time, "intelligible forms" were the pure mental concepts or blueprints of things, independent of physical matter.</note>. Consequently, all intelligible forms are compatible with them. From this, it follows that they are filled with these species and images—that is, every form of intelligence and every physical likeness that is shaped by intelligence shines through them. This is not unlike how every color is reflected in the air, or every object in a mirror. However, those objects in the air or a mirror come from the surrounding environment, whereas this angelic impression comes from their very center and according to their own will and pleasure, as <term>Psellus</term> <note>Michael Psellus (c. 1017–1078), a Byzantine monk and philosopher known for his writings on demons and spirits.</note> seems to suggest.

As for the disposition of the good angels, it is certain and proven by holy writings that they are contrary to the evil ones in their nature, and they are ready and prone by natural inclination to accomplish whatever is good.

->*The Passive Nature of Angels*<-
<note>The original Latin title is "Angelorum Passio." In this context, "passion" does not mean emotion or suffering, but rather the capacity to be acted upon or to receive influence from a higher source.</note>

Angels do not suffer from physical weight or force, since their outward nature is the purest, most subtle, and lightest spirit, as is excellently declared by the words of the Evangelist <term>Luke</term> in his final chapter. Rather, we say that angels "suffer" insofar as they receive the influx of divine light in abundance. That is to say, their spiritual bodies are perfectly prepared to receive the impressions of divine light, which they then later impart and communicate to lower beings by divine command. However, the holy scriptures teach us that the evil angels do suffer and are tortured because of the dense and dark mass of their substance, for their place is the infernal lake; but we will discuss them a little further below. Furthermore, insofar as the good angels are subject to the rule and commands of God, they are thought to undergo the signs and impressions of the divine will—but in a peaceful manner, for they are said to serve God without any compulsion.

->*The Common Property*<-

We call it a "common property" of a good angel when it concerns not only themselves but universal things, whether uncreated or created, in this world. This is properly called their "office" or duty, both toward God the creator of all things and toward His creatures; for an angel is a nature that stands in the middle between creatures and God.

The supercelestial angels of the higher order worship God and the unique Creator as a most firm and stable unity. They are occupied solely with Him and are not said to preside over physical bodies in the world or the administration of lower things. Their role is to receive God’s light and flow it into the lower orders, through which individual and distinct duties are distributed to each. Some of these are "assistants" at the divine throne, continually praising God their Creator; others are "ministers" to Him and to us. Truly, the celestial or "Olympic" angels, beyond divine worship, are assigned to the planetary spheres. Their task is to entrust those influences they have received from the higher angels to the spirits <note>original: "daemonibus," used here in the older sense of "spirits" or "intermediaries" rather than necessarily evil demons.</note> of the lower order. These spirits use these descending lights in infinite tasks in the air, in the waters, and on the earth for the preservation and multiplication of creatures. Finally, all good angels in general are said primarily to revere, worship, and indeed see the face of the Creator, whether they are in the highest, middle, or lowest heaven.

The third duty of good angels toward God is to listen to His voice. Then, their obedience toward their Creator in bringing His commands to fruition is such that, through the fourth degree of their duty, they set about executing it immediately and willingly. Hence, the skilled theologians assert and agree that angels serve God without compulsion, and His commands...

# On the Efficient Cause of Meteors <note>In this context, "meteors" refers to all atmospheric phenomena, including wind, rain, and lightning, which were believed to be governed by spiritual forces.</note>

...they carry out His command suddenly and in an instant, and do not delay it. ->The duty of the good angels concerning creatures involves either:<-

*   **The Macrocosm** <term>Macrocosm</term> <note>The "great world" or the universe as a whole.</note>
    *   **The Whole:** The spheres of heaven, the world's axes, and the Elements.
    *   **The Parts:** Namely, the Earth and the Water.
    *   **Creatures:** Super-celestial, Celestial, and Elemental.
*   **The Microcosm** <term>Microcosm</term> <note>The "little world," referring to the human being as a reflection of the universe.</note>

Just as God first created angelic creatures for His divine worship and service in the world from the beginning, so in the second place He set them over creatures in general—namely, the Macrocosm and Microcosm—and then over those things made from the Macrocosm for the use of the Microcosm, so that they might watch over and care for them.

The angel, or that great and supreme Intelligence <term>Intelligence</term> <note>In medieval and Renaissance philosophy, an "Intelligence" was a pure spirit that moved a celestial sphere.</note> animating, inspiring, and moving the entire spirit of the Macrocosm from east to west (for he has command over the <term>Primum Mobile</term> <note>The "First Moved" sphere, the outermost sphere in the geocentric model which drives the motion of all others.</note>), is the one whom the Cabalists call *Metatron* <note>original: "Mittatron"</note>, the Sacred Page calls *Wisdom*, and the Platonists call the *Soul of the World* <note>original: "Animam mundi"</note>. All other angels in the world, both good and evil, are said to offer obedience to him; about whom we shall speak more specifically and fully below. 

There are also other Angelic Princes or Leaders who reign immediately under the leadership or command of this angel, who watch over the parts of the world. Some are rulers of the heavens and the ether; among these, some preside over the Zodiac, others over the <term>triplicities</term> <note>Groups of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water).</note>, and some over the <term>faces</term> <note>Ten-degree segments of the zodiac, also called decans.</note> or decuries, and even over the <term>quinaries</term> <note>Five-degree segments of the zodiac.</note>. Others are placed over the remaining stars of the firmament, for there is no star in heaven that does not have its own prefect. Others command the spheres of the planets by day and by night, etc. Others have their powers and seats in the Empyrean heaven <note>The highest, fiery heaven, believed to be the dwelling place of God.</note>, and others have both the regions of the world and the elements in their custody. 

Namely: **Michael**, the Eastern angel; **Gabriel**, the Northern; **Raphael**, the Western; and **Uriel**, the Southern (about whom we spoke before). There are also those who have command over the four elements: namely, **Seraph** <note>original: "Seruph"</note> over Fire, **Cherub** over Air, **Tharsis** over Water, and **Ariel** over Earth. Furthermore, 72 angels are called "Angels of Division" by the Cabalists, as it is their duty to divide the earth itself into as many distinct parts, which are called different kingdoms. Each of these said angels presides and spiritually reigns over the aforementioned kingdoms. This is not because they descend from heaven to dwell there (as the Cabalists claim), but insofar as they dwell in the super-celestial world, they nonetheless care for these lower things and govern earthly matters through their influences. 

This seems to be confirmed by <term>Ecclesiasticus</term> <note>Also known as the Wisdom of Sirach.</note>, where we read that an angelic ruler is set over every nation. Furthermore, Moses says in his song that when the Most High divided the nations, He set their bounds according to the number of the Angels of God. Our own view <note>original: "Nostra autem nos fert intentio"</note> suggests that these 72 angels (since the starry heaven is related by the wise to the Earth because of its stability) are those leaders who have primary force and power over the *quinaries* of each sign, which are the half-parts of the <term>decans</term> <note>original: "decurionum"</note>. For example, in every sign there are 30 degrees, and any group of ten is called a decan; hence the number five is half of a decan. Therefore, in every sign there are 6 quinaries, which, when multiplied by the twelve signs, produces 72. This is exactly the number of the 72 leaders whose task, according to the Cabalists, is to divide the earth into kingdoms. 

I have conceived this idea in my mind, and although it is to be found nowhere else in writing that I know of, the matter itself indicates it is probable. This is both because every kingdom is subject to the fate of change—which is seen even in the shifting of Empires—and also in that struggle held between Gabriel and the Prince of the Persians <note>A reference to Daniel 10:13, where an angel describes fighting the spiritual "prince" of the Persian kingdom.</note>. From this it is likely that such rulers are "Olympic" <note>In this context, meaning planetary or celestial, rather than from the highest spiritual realm.</note> and not at all Empyrean. This also seems more probable because, according to the observations of astrologers, the kingdoms and provinces of the earth are placed under particular signs of the Zodiac. These are the causes of change, both in the nature of places and the condition of inhabitants, which usually differs between one kingdom and another neighboring it. Furthermore, others are placed over the waters and have others under them...

...demons infinite in number; hence the sea gods Neptune, Thetis, Proteus, Nereus, and hence the river nymphs, the Nereids, etc. <note>The author is categorizing various pagan deities as types of elemental spirits or demons under the command of higher orders.</note>

Furthermore, so great is the order and harmony of these angels and even of their subjects, who are everywhere infused and dispersed throughout the world, that no order of theirs is permitted to take up or attempt a work destined for another.

Furthermore, in the ethereal heaven, every sign of the Zodiac, every triplicity <note>A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (fire, earth, air, or water).</note> of the same, every decan <note>A division of 10 degrees in the zodiac.</note> and quinarius <note>A division of 5 degrees.</note> of any sign, enjoys its own prince angel, by whom it is ruled and governed, who also has many legions and cohorts under him; indeed (as has already been said), no star is found in the whole firmament over which a Prince does not preside, and which is not inhabited by infinite angels of a lower order. Indeed, it is affirmed by some skilled in occult theosophy that angels not only agree with humans in many aspects of nature, but even in number, concluding that as many humans are to be saved as there were angels who fell from heaven in the battle between the dragon and Michael, so that those to be saved might fill the place of the angels expelled from heaven; and they say that as many are to be damned as there were angels who remained on Michael's side in heaven after the victory. From this they wish to conclude an equality in the number of humans and angels; if this were true, it would follow as a consequence that there are as many Saturnine angels as there are Saturnine humans <note>Those born under the astrological influence of Saturn.</note>, and as many Jovial, Martial, etc.

In the lowest part of the world as well, there are angels administering to every creature, as some are said to preside over animals, others over plants; indeed, the sages of the Kabbalists <term>Kabalistarum</term> <note>Followers of Kabbalah, a tradition of Jewish mysticism.</note> maintain that there is no herb or plant on earth that does not have an appropriated star in the firmament, and consequently an angel, who strikes it and says to it, as it were, "grow and multiply." Others are said to preside over precious stones, others over metals, and so on for the rest.

But since the ancient Jews attributed all things or species in creation to the holy letters, of which they made as many symbols of angelic orders as there are holy letters, they therefore assigned to these letters and the angels symbolizing them a particular office over creatures and a particular species to each one specifically. For example: for the outpouring of life into the world, handed down directly from God *Ehieh* <note>original Hebrew: אֶהְיֶה‎, "I Am," a name of God.</note>, the order called *Haioth*—that is, the living creatures of the sanctuary or of life <note>original: "animalia sanctuarii," referring to the Chayot Ha Kodesh.</note>—which symbolize with *Aleph*. For joining form with fluid matter, the order of *Aralim*—that is, the great, strong, and robust ones—who obtain that power from *Jehovah* by whom they are illuminated, with *Gimel*. The order through which God *Elohe* fashioned the shapes of bodies, the *Chachmalim* <note>Hashmallim</note>, is referred to *Daleth*. To the open *Mem* the sphere of the angel of Jupiter, to the closed *Mem* the sphere of Mars, and so on for the rest.

...it is also their role to receive Divine light and commend it to those below. The **Second Hierarchy** concerns the ethereal world and administers the heavens. Its first order, the **Dominations**, issues commands in heaven which the others execute; the second, the **Virtues**, administers the heavens and sometimes gathers together to perform miracles; the third, the **Powers**, wards off those things that might disturb the divine law. The **Third Hierarchy** contains the ministering spirits who descend to care for lower things. The first order of this group, the **Principalities**, cares for public affairs—namely leadership, magistracies, provinces, and kingdoms—and the princes of these are the seventy-two previously mentioned <note>Referring to the 72 nations or languages traditionally said to be overseen by specific angelic princes in Jewish and Christian mystical traditions.</note>. The second order, the **Archangels**, is present at sacred rites and is occupied with the divine worship of men, directing them in their ways and offering their prayers and sacrifices to God. The spirits of the third and final order are accustomed to arrange even smaller matters, and they are present as individual guardians to individuals. Some of these administer virtue to the smallest herbs, pebbles, and all lower things; nevertheless, these creatures do not receive these gifts from the angels themselves, but from God through the angels. Whence it was said by the Prophet Daniel:

> *God does according to His will in the army of heaven and among the inhabitants of the earth.*

And elsewhere in Job:

> *Do you know the laws of the heavens, or can you establish their rule <note>original: "praefectum seu praesidem vel exequutorem"</note> upon the earth? (Job 38)*

And it is for this reason that profound philosophers maintain that all lower things are representations of higher things, and as it happens below, so it is driven by what is above; in this, all **Kabbalists** <note>Followers of Kabbalah, a school of Jewish mysticism that influenced many Renaissance thinkers.</note> agree. This means the external appearance of any created thing made of elements appears according to the forms and acts of its internal agent, just as a scabbard is formed to the shape of the sword. Every such work is perfected by ministering angels. For an angel is defined as a "middle power" <term>virtus media</term> <note>A being acting as a bridge or intermediary between the Creator and the physical world.</note> between God and nature or a created thing, from which those operations arise that are visible, and even those which nature either would not do, or would do in such a way that others say they come from an "occult property" <note>An "occult property" refers to a hidden natural power that cannot be explained by the four elements (hot, cold, wet, dry).</note>; finally, all things are done and brought to their conclusion by God through the angels.

### Section I, Portion IV, Part II. Book IV. Member II.

...and dedicated to the custody of reason, it is governed by an angel of the highest order. Here, according to **Iamblichus** <note>A Neoplatonist philosopher (c. 245–325 AD) who wrote extensively on theurgy and the relationship between the soul and the divine.</note> and the doctrine of the **Egyptians**, this is called the **good spirit**, the **good genius**, or the **sacred intelligence**. According to Iamblichus, this spirit is not poured into a human from the stars or planets, but from a more exalted origin—namely, from the ruler of the world and of the angels. It is said to be destined primarily for the governance of the mind and the rational soul.

By the power of this spirit, it is granted to man—above all other creatures—to rule over the stars and to transcend the tyranny of fate. For it is the role of this spirit to direct the life of the soul and to continually offer good thoughts to the mind. It longs to illuminate our innermost parts and exerts itself at every moment, although we are often unable to perceive this very operation because of our own internal darkness. Only when we are cleansed and purified, and when we live calmly and peacefully, is it not only perceived by us, but it even seems to converse with us in its own tongue and speech. (As for what kind of language such an angel uses, or what voice it employs in its speech, we have explained this above.) Finally, its purpose is to lead us toward sacred perfection, to render us ready for divine worship, and to keep us safe from the snares and malice of the **Devil**.

The **second angel** is called the **spirit of birth** <note>original: "dæmon genituræ"</note>, also known as the **genius of life**. This one is believed to be from the order of the **Olympic** or ethereal spirits; therefore, it is said to descend from the regions of the stars at the time of birth as a natural influence. This is the guardian of life and the executor of its functions. Just as it provided the power of life to the body at the very beginning of birth, so it takes care to communicate that life and attract suitable nourishment for its preservation through a magnetic and hidden power from the heavens. This power is drawn daily—indeed, at every moment—from that star (whether planetary or fixed) in which it most participates. Ultimately, the health and happiness of the person born will be greater or more meager according to the "goodness" of this spirit—that is, according to the favorable influence of its presiding star.

As for the spirit of the lowest condition and place, we designate it as the **elemental spirit**. Some call this the **evil genius**. In truth, unless it is well-corrected in its ways by the **supreme spirit** (which we called the sacred intelligence), it will always be inclined toward the pleasures of the flesh and the vanities of this changeable world, according to the natural condition of its lowly place. This is because it comes from that region of the world in which the **prince of the power of the air** <note>A biblical reference to Satan, from Ephesians 2:2.</note> is accustomed to exercise his force.

Others say that a human's **third spirit** is the **angel of their profession**. They claim that when one's profession changes, the spirit changes as well. However, we can boldly contradict them in this, because a profession belongs to the realm of reason and intellect. Therefore, we leave the perfection of a profession to the direction of the **sacred spirit**. It is the role of this spirit, in its office, to share in the Holy Spirit and His gifts. It is also its role—as the Holy Scriptures testify—to distribute various sciences to men according to their varied capacities, as was done for **Bezalel** <note>The biblical craftsman (Exodus 31) endowed by God with wisdom and skill to build the Tabernacle.</note> and others whom the book of **Exodus** mentions more fully in chapters 28:3, 31:2, and 35:30. Therefore, we make the sacred angel the distributor of sciences and arts—since its role is to give art, science, and intellect—rather than another spirit of lesser condition. If, due to a person's darkened state, they choose or change one art for another, this is not the fault of their guardian and governor, but rather the error and depravity of their own blind and carnal will.

I am also aware that **Astrologers** attribute the trades and professions of men to the star of their birth, and consequently to the angel governing that star. For example, they attribute the mercantile art and mathematical sciences to **Mercury**, the arts of war and blacksmithing to **Mars**, and the arts of medicine and music to the **Sun**. But to these we reply that the **Olympic angel** at birth is always subject to the **sacred spirit**, just as the **elemental spirit** is subject to the **Olympic**. There is always a relationship of one to the other. First, God pours out His luminous property through a chosen gate into a specific order of angels in the **empyrean heaven**. This order immediately commits that influence to the **archangel** of the sphere or the star of the eighth heaven, or to a planet of the ether. This archangel, in turn, pours it into the elemental region and commends it to the spirit of its own sphere wandering in the air there. This spirit—along with the empyrean nature (which we call the sacred angel) and the celestial nature (which we call the spirit of life)—involves itself in the "spermatic mass" <note>A term for the biological matter or "seed" at the moment of conception.</note> for the procreation of the child.

But since we have spoken more fully of these three spirits in Treatise 1, Section 2, Portion 4, Book 3, Part 2, we do not wish to consume more time in this discourse on this subject. Instead, let us move more quickly to the numbering of the angels who are concerned with human affairs. Regarding the spirits that have power over the morals and faculties of the human body: beyond those spirits born with the person, we say that just as lower things represent higher things, so there are spirits in the elemental world that relate in condition to those celestial ones in the **Olympic world**. By natural inclination, they exercise their powers alongside the powers of the celestial souls—namely, the mind, reason, imagination, and the motive or life-giving power.

**Fiery spirits** follow the mind, where they join and assist in higher contemplations. **Airy spirits**, following the mind, favor the rational power and separate it, in a way, from the sensual and vegetative parts; these are said to serve the **active life**, just as the fiery ones serve the **contemplative life**. **Watery spirits** serve the imagination and the senses by natural inclination and contribute to a **voluptuous life**. Finally, **earthy spirits** favor the vegetative or natural faculty. These spirits are distinguished according to the natures and names of the Planets as **Saturnine**, **Jovial**, **Martial**, and so on.

### **On the Efficient Cause of Meteors.**

And here it must be carefully observed that, just as humans are found on earth who take on the nature of any given planet or star, so too do demons dwell in the world belonging to each planet, endowed with the condition of each element. From this, it happens that through the various **aspects** <note>In astrology, an "aspect" is the angle planets make to each other on the celestial sphere, believed to influence earthly events.</note> of the planets toward one another in the heavens, various effects are produced in the lower world. This is because the demons of both planets, being closer in nature at the point of the aspect, meet and join as if in a middle path if the aspect is favorable—namely, a **Trine** or **Sextile** <note>Trine (120°) and Sextile (60°) are considered harmonious astrological alignments.</note>—and thus, in the manner of an influence, they flow downward into the elemental world. But if the aspect is malevolent, especially from planets of contrary conditions, then spirits of contrary nature or elements clash at the point of the aspect—namely, in **Opposition**, **Square**, or **Conjunction** <note>Opposition (180°) and Square (90°) are considered tense or challenging alignments; Conjunction (0°) depends on the planets involved.</note>. In this way, they produce malevolent and turbulent effects, not only for human life but also for the spirit of the world. I would have you hold this as a secret mystery, for it is the reason why for some men life is more agreeable and healthy in condition, while for others it is turbulent, weak, and contentious; some excel in genius and intellect, while others are dull and devoid of good reason, and so on for others. Nevertheless, the **holy angel** holds command over the rest, both the Olympian and the Elemental spirits. For the bearer of the rational life who is a sinner is ruled by a pious and just spirit of rational life; moreover, the spirits of the just are the holy angels, for (as **Thomas** <note>St. Thomas Aquinas (1225–1274), the influential scholastic philosopher and theologian.</note> says) lower spirits are compelled by the higher. Indeed, this is evident in the command held by that angel who went out from **Zechariah**, ordering another angel to hasten to Jerusalem, and also in the spirits within the Apostles who cast out demons from the possessed, and the **Angel Raphael**, who put **Asmodeus** <note>A powerful demon mentioned in the Book of Tobit; Raphael is the archangel who binds him.</note> to flight, and in many other instances. For it is certain that those spirits who are more filled and intoxicated with the divine nectar of divinity are more powerful than those who are more destitute and in need of divine light, and thus dwell in darkness.

**Athanasius** <note>Likely referring to St. Athanasius of Alexandria (c. 296–373 AD).</note> says that it is the role of the order of the **Seraphim** <note>The highest order of angels, associated with light and fire.</note> not only to receive the divine outflow of light directly and to magnify God—as they are closest to Him—with unending hymns and restless praise, but also to pray to Him for our salvation. Thus we read it written in the **Apocalypse**: *And another angel came and stood before the altar, having a golden censer; and much incense was given to him, that he should offer it with the prayers of all the saints upon the golden altar which is before the throne of God.* (Revelation 8:2). Furthermore, it is intimately seen in **Job** that there are angels who make intercession for men. *If there be* (says **Elihu**) *an angel speaking for a man, to declare his uprightness, he will have mercy on him, and will say, "Deliver him, that he may not descend into corruption"; he will pray to God, and He will be favorable to him, and He will restore to man his justice.* (Job 33:23). This kind of angelic order is called **procuratorial**, because it is seen to ardently plead the cause of man before God.

There is also the office of a single angel, as the **Cabalists** <note>Followers of Kabbalah, a school of Jewish mysticism; the author integrates these views into a Christian framework.</note> maintain, who acts as a vicar in heaven, offering rational souls to God in the same way that common vicars or priests are accustomed to offer the body of Christ in the Mass on earth. They say this is **Michael**, who is that great prince (according to **Daniel**) standing for the people of God or the elect. They say he performs a perpetual priesthood as the great priest of God in heaven; hence, he is called by the more secret theologians in Hebrew **Cofhengadol** <note>original: "Cofhengadol"; from the Hebrew *Kohen Gadol*, meaning "High Priest."</note>, that is, the **High Priest**. Furthermore, this angel is appointed the prince of the militia of Christ over all souls to be received, as the **Archangel** <note>Likely referring to a specific commentator on Kabbalistic doctrine, possibly Archangelus de Burgonovo.</note> writes in his commentary on the dogma of the Cabalists.

There is also another order of angels who are immediately present to man in this life, which is called the **Doctrinal** order. The role of these angels is to instruct him in the truth of things—present, past, and future. Thus **Gabriel**, addressing the prophet Daniel, says: *I have come to teach you what things shall come to your people in the latter days.* (Daniel 11).

There are also angels of another condition present to man himself, who are called **Tutelary** <note>Guardian or protective spirits.</note>, such as was **Raphael**, who defended **Tobias** against evil spirits (Tobit 8). The royal prophet <note>King David, the traditional author of the Psalms.</note> speaks of these regarding the elect: *Fear not the terror of the night, nor the arrow that flies by day, nor the plague that wanders in the darkness or night, nor the destruction that wastes at midday or the midday demon; no scourge shall come near your tent, for He shall give His angels charge over you, and keep you in all your ways, etc.* (Psalm 91). Regarding such an angel, **Jacob** also spoke in his blessings: *The angel who redeemed me from all evil, bless these boys.* (Genesis 48). And those of whom it is written: *He has given His angels charge over you, and in their hands they shall bear you up, lest perhaps you dash your foot against a stone.* (Matthew 4:11).

There are others who are called **Ministral** or **Administering** angels, of whom the Apostle says: *Are they not all administering spirits, sent forth for those who shall receive the inheritance of salvation?* (Hebrews 1). Of this kind also were those who approached Christ on the mountain and ministered to Him (Matthew 4:11).

There is also the **Auxiliary** order, whose role is to assist the elect and the people of God against enemies and foes. Such were those angels of God who met **Jacob** on his journey; when he saw them, he called them the **army of God**, and through their mediation, he had victory over the malevolent spirit of his brother (Genesis 32:1). Such an angel was also sent by God in the time of **Hezekiah**, King of Judah, who slew 185,000 of the Assyrian enemies (2 Kings 19). Such also was the angel whom **Judas Maccabeus** sought from God for his help, by whose power he and his small band of men slew 35,000 of the enemy (2 Maccabees 15:22).

Section I. Portion IV. Part II. Book IV. Member II.

There are also others to whom the duty of consolation is attributed, such as the angel who was the consforter of Hagar <note>Referring to the angel who appeared to Hagar in the wilderness (Genesis 21).</note> in her great grief. And the angel who rescued Peter from Prison. And that angel seen by the grieving Apostles after the resurrection of Christ.

Others are **admonitory**: for these are accustomed to set before the eyes of the mind our sins, so that we may correct them; they also regularly advise us of the Divine will, instructing us on what ought to be done. Similarly, they often visit humans to warn them against sinning, and they rouse and stir them from the sleep of sin and vice.

Others are **assistants**, who assist humans in their ordinary business, like the angel who provided food and drink to Elijah and Daniel in their times of need.

Others are **leaders and conductors** on a journey, of whom Jehovah speaks, saying: *My Angel shall go before you on the journey, and elsewhere, Behold, I send my angel before you, to keep you in this way, and to bring you into that place which I have prepared, Exodus 32:34.*

Besides these, others have the duty to take the souls of the deceased into their custody, of whom we read in Luke: The soul of Lazarus was carried into the bosom of Abraham. Finally, the office of curing diseases and healing wounds is assigned to others; thus it is handed down by holy writ that Tobit was healed by Raphael; and that pool <note>The Pool of Bethesda (John 5).</note> stirred by an angel, which healed those who immersed themselves because of the angel’s touch, and so on in many other cases. But here, we think this should be noted above all: that although these orders seem to vary—since they receive names from their more specific duties—nevertheless, all these orders reported by us here are called by the Apostle Paul (in the place cited above) by a more general term, most fitting to their universal office: **Ministering Spirits** or angels, sent for the salvation and preservation of both the bodies and souls of men. Hesiod seems to intend this when he speaks to this effect: *Thrice ten thousand are upon the earth, many who nurture mortals, the guardians of mortal men from Jove* <note>original: "Iouis"; refers to Jupiter/Zeus as the supreme deity.</note>, who indeed watch over justice and pitiable deeds, clothed in mist, going everywhere over the earth. And these guardians mentioned by Hesiod are called **Spirits** by the Latins, each of whom (according to the sense of the Cabalists <note>Kabbalah: a Jewish mystical and esoteric tradition.</note>) is assigned to the care of lower business; and these are called **Mamon or Mammon** <note>original: "Mamona seu Mamon"; typically used for wealth, but here applied to spirits of earthly concerns.</note> by the Greeks, or **daemons**, not in a bad sense but a good one. We conclude, therefore, with a certain wise man in the *Revelation of the Divine Majesty*, who describes the more open and manifest offices of the angels thus: that first among all is that great spirit who holds apart the immense and widely extended water called heaven, and preserves it in its essence, and wonderfully grants motion to all growing and living things. In the second place are positioned the **Cherubim**, who guard and watch over the tree of life; other angels announce future things and teach men; others destroy Sodom and Gomorrah; others kill and repel enemies; others send down snow, rain, lightning, and thunder upon the earth, and so on, each one performing his own peculiar duty. Yet all serve God together, while they carry out His will in all things: in the heavens, in the air, and on the earth, and in every place whatsoever, and that in various and wonderful ways. Holy Scripture testifies to this: namely, that spirits and angels always indicated to those humans to whom they were sent that they had been dispatched and delegated by God to announce or command this or that to them, or even to carry out something among them according to the divine will. From this, the status and condition of the angelic offices can be gathered and perceived: there is the highest diligence, devotion, and greatest zeal, never neglecting anything, never delaying, but perfecting all things exactly and in the blink of an eye, and bringing back the report of their execution, by which God himself is praised, honored, and celebrated. In this execution, there is no respect of persons <note>meaning no favoritism or bias.</note>, no respect for wages, rewards, or gifts; nothing wicked, nothing perverse, nothing unjust is performed there. There, the words of God, His decrees and mandates, are not twisted, changed, or corrupted, but all things are carried out according to the divine standard without any depravation.

There is no one there who breaks, corrupts, or keeps the word of God in part while rejecting it in part, as the sons of men are accustomed to do.

### Section I. Portion IV. Part II. Book IV. Member II.
#### Page 246

It has been declared by us that a certain sage in secret **Theography** <note>original: "Theographia," writing concerning the nature of God</note>, in a certain treatise of his named the *Revelation of Majesty* (*Book on the Spirit, ch. 78*), breaks forth in these words: All things were created through the word of God, and therefore all things are also governed, moved, and led by that word. For this reason, the "wise men" of the world, or philosophers, are delirious when they refuse to concede that God works all things in all, and that His word moves, excites, and preserves all things. Instead, they ascribe these things to created nature, pretending that God works through "media"—namely, through secondary and tertiary causes. They are unwilling to understand that God works solely through His word and not through any other media or the aforementioned alleged causes, but only *within* them. The first body, namely water, God created as moist and humid through His word; thus, there appears to be no other cause in water that makes it wet and moist. Above and in the water, God created the hidden air so that it might float above the waters, and impel and move them, and preserve them in their liquid and flowing substance; this same thing happens even today. With the air, He also simultaneously created angels by His word, and spirits who carry out their duty and office in the air concerning the direction of storms, rain, snow, hail, frost, clouds, lightning, and the **ceraunian stone** <term>ceraunian stone: a "thunder-stone" or fossil once believed to fall from the sky during a lightning strike</term>, fire, **chasms** <note>original: "chasmatū," referring to openings or "gulfs" in the sky</note>, floods of water, heat, cold, warmth, humidity, dryness, and many other things of that kind. So says that author. From these things, it is clear that God does not work mediately through angels, but through the Word *within* the angels. This is also what Rabbi **Menahem Recanati** <note>A 13th-14th century Italian Kabbalist</note> says in his commentaries on *Exodus 14*: "The **flying characters** <note>original: "Characteres volantes," referring to the Hebrew letters as spiritual forces</note> hovering above in the foundation of spiritual wisdom are the administrative tools of the spirit, used to perform every thing through them, and their operations are known to the Kabbalists." But lest anyone, led by vain superstition, should think that all things are conferred upon human mortality from heaven by the angels alone, we therefore assert with **Reuchlin** <note>Johannes Reuchlin (1455–1522), a German humanist and scholar of Greek and Hebrew</note> (in the third book of *On the Art of the Kabbalah*) that all things are done by the Majesty of God itself through the angels as if through organs—even within the angels. The Prophet Daniel also testifies to this, saying to King Nebuchadnezzar: *He does according to His will in the army of heaven and among the inhabitants of the earth.* For the Word of God impressed His own character upon every angel; hence, concerning the Angel whom He placed at the head of the desert journey as a leader for Moses, Jehovah says: *He will not bear your transgressions, for my name is in him.* And it is from this that the names of angels end in *El* or *Iah*, such as Michael, Haziel, Hahaiah, Jehuiah, Habriah, etc. From this it is clear that it is God in the angel who acts and incites the angelic creature to perform this or that according to His will, and not the angelic creature itself; but indeed, insofar as the whole angel is considered—namely its internal and external—according to the worldly sense or the men of the world, this or that is said to be "done by an angel." Hence it follows that an angel, whether good or evil, can do nothing against the divine will, but is moved where and when it pleases God (or the Word marked within him) to lead him, so that he may execute his office in this or that place according to the Divine property leading or directing him.

Regarding the star of Christ, as the Magi intended when they said, "For we have seen his star" (*Matthew 2*), it was as if they had said it was led by His angel; and concerning the pillar of fire in which the angel was, whom Jehovah placed over the Israelites in their journey, it is said: *Wisdom was a covering for Israel by day, and a light of stars by night (Wisdom 10:17).* Regarding the whirlwind and the fiery chariot in which Elijah was snatched up into heaven (*2 Kings 2:1*); regarding the Angel having a face shining like the Sun, whose feet were like two pillars of fire (*Revelation 10*); regarding the 7 Angels by whose trumpet blast the stars fell and infected the sea and the earth (*Revelation 8*); regarding the horsemen running through the air (*2 Maccabees 5:2*); and other such fiery wonders in the air, the sacred letters make mention. Also regarding the **prester** <term>prester: a fiery whirlwind or "bellowing" storm-wind</term> or fiery whirlwind which God sent by means of angelic ministers (as history testifies) over Sodom and Gomorrah (*Genesis 19*), of which it is also said elsewhere: *He rained down upon the wicked coals of fire, fire, and sulfur, and a wind of various whirlwinds was the portion of their cup (Psalm 11:6).* Regarding the fire of God falling from heaven, and similarly concerning violent winds, concerning the whirlwind of the Lord, of which it is said: *Behold the whirlwind of the Lord, a fury going forth, a rushing storm rests upon the heads of the impious (Jeremiah 30:23).* And elsewhere: *Behold, a whirlwind came from the North, and a great cloud, and a fire infolding itself, and a brightness was round about it, and out of the midst of it was the likeness as of living creatures, etc. (Ezekiel 1).* And elsewhere: *Concerning all these things, we shall be visited by the Lord God of hosts, in thunder and earthquake, and with the great voice of whirlwind and tempest, and the flame of devouring fire, etc. (Isaiah 29:6).* And also that when Jehovah was angry with them, *the earth was moved and trembled, the foundations of the mountains were shaken: and that smoke ascended from his nostrils, and fire from his mouth, that coals were kindled by him, and that he bowed the heavens and came down, with darkness under his feet (2 Samuel 22:8)*; and that *he ascended upon the Cherubim, and that he flew, and glided upon the wings of the wind, and that he made darkness a hiding place round about him, sifting the waters from the thick clouds of the heavens, and that because of the brightness in his presence the clouds were kindled, coals of fire flew out, and that the Lord thunders from heaven, and that the Most High gives his voice and sends his arrows, and scatters the impious with lightning, and that he makes the effusions of the sea to appear, and the foundations of the world were revealed by the rebuke of the Lord, from the breath of his fury.* Elsewhere we have this in express words in the sacred source. In this we are taught that the attribute is given to Jehovah, even though He acts by means of the Cherubim and His windy spirits, of whom it is said: *Who makes your angels winds, and your ministers a burning fire (Psalm 103).* Thus, from this testimony, it is confirmed that God is the sole author and creator of these **meteors** <note>In this period, "meteors" referred to all atmospheric and weather phenomena, including rain and earthquakes.</note> which follow—namely, Earthquakes, Vapor or smoke, Lightning, the ceraunian stone, Clouds, Winds, Rain, Thunder, sea tempests, etc.—all of which He [manages] in His wisdom through His angelic organs, He Himself centrally through His word lea-

### On the Efficient Cause of Meteors.
<note>original: "De Causa Meteororum Efficiente." In early modern science, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomena, including rain, wind, lightning, and even earthquakes, rather than just falling space rocks.</note>

...is accustomed to produce; but this especially must be noted: that just as He produces good things—useful and advantageous to the earth, the waters, and their creatures—through good angels, so He sometimes employs His evil ministers, both in His wrath toward the ungodly and to test His chosen ones. This indeed seems to be clearly declared in the **History of Job**; for Satan said to Jehovah, *“Stretch out your hand, and touch whatever he has, etc.”* And Jehovah replied, *“Behold, let whatever he has be in your hand.”* With this said, it was in Satan's power (and not before) to move the spirits of the **Sabeans** <note>A people from South Arabia mentioned in the Bible as raiders who stole Job’s oxen and donkeys.</note> against Job's servants, to send forth fire from heaven which burned his sheep, and to send a great wind from the region of the desert, by whose force the four corners of the house collapsed upon Job's children. Again, coming into the sight of Jehovah a second time, he said to Him: *“Whatever a man has he will give for himself; but stretch out your hand, and touch his bones and his flesh, etc.”*

By these words, Satan seems to confess that none of the things inflicted upon Job should be attributed to himself, but to Jehovah—namely, whether it was the turning of the Sabeans' spirits, the calling down of fire from heaven, the stirring up of the violent wind, or finally the infliction of diseases. All this seems to have been done by God, as Satan says, *“Stretch out, I pray, your hand, and touch whatever he has, etc.”* and then later: *“But stretch out, I pray, your hand, and touch his bones and his flesh, etc.”* And yet, nevertheless, he himself was the minister of the divine temptation and execution; hence Jehovah said, *“Behold, he is in your hand.”* By these things it is clearly declared that whatever is performed by God, He is accustomed to execute by means of His ministers, whether good or evil. The Apostle speaks to this sense: *“There are those who are called gods in heaven and on earth; yet for us there is one God the Father, from whom are all things, and we in Him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, through whom are all things, and we through Him.” (1 Cor. 8:5-6)*. Where he says “gods,” he understands **angels**. Hence David says, *“The gods of the gentiles are demons, but the Lord made the heavens.” (Psalm 96)*. And in Job they are called the “sons of God.” (Job 1). Hence the **Platonists** <note>Followers of the philosopher Plato, whose later interpreters developed complex hierarchies of spirits or "daemons" inhabiting the natural world.</note> said, “All things are full of gods.” We have already spoken abundantly above, with many testimonies brought forth from the sacred page, concerning the overflowing snow and the harmful hail, and concerning the cold, ice, frost, and frozen ground proceeding from the breath of Jehovah.

Finally, just as the protection of the **East Wind** is assigned to the good angel **Michael**, that of the **South Wind** to **Uriel**, the **West** to **Raphael**, and the **North** to **Gabriel**, who affect the air with favorable and propitious breezes and produce meteors beneficial to the world; so indeed, from the malignant spirits, **Samael** blows malevolently from the East, and likewise his other companions, namely **Mahazael, Azael, and Azazel**.

Furthermore, God also, through and in His windy spirits, is accustomed to bring forth floods and deluges—either fatal or very advantageous to mortals—on account of men's disobedience and sins. As in the flood of **Noah**, it is said that He dried up the waters in no other way than through the winds; and elsewhere it is said, *“He turns the desert into a pool of water, and the dry land into springs of water.” (Psalm 107:35)*. That this is so is proven by these words: *“With a strong East wind Jehovah drove back the sea all that night, and turned the sea into dry land.” (Exodus 14:21)*. And in another place: *“By the blast of your nostrils the waters were heaped up.” (Exodus 15:8)*. Then afterward: *“You blew with your wind, and the sea covered them.”* And the **Cabalists** <note>Scholars of Jewish mysticism (Kabbalah) who often analyzed the names of God and the hierarchies of angels.</note> said that 72 angels were present at the division of the sea, counting the angel of the pillar of cloud and the angel of the pillar of fire, which 72 angels are called the “angels of division,” as **Reuchlin** <note>Johannes Reuchlin (1455–1522), a German humanist and scholar who introduced Christian audiences to the study of the Hebrew language and Kabbalah.</note> has it in his third book *On the Cabalistic Art*. But however it may be, it is certain that just as floods of this kind are produced with the greatest intemperance and disturbance of the air, so indeed in the fulfillment of such a divine will and command, the action of a turbulent spirit of God is required, whose role it is to carry out the word and pleasure of God. We have this confirmed also by the sacred page, which says *“that the stormy wind fulfills the word of God.” (Psalm 148:8)*. Furthermore, that this spirit is the cause of restlessness and of storms at sea and the disturbance of lakes is to be drawn from these words of the Prophet: *“He speaks and makes the spirit of the whirlwind blow, and lifts up its waves; they mount up to heaven, they go down to the depths, etc. Then He makes the whirlwind stand in silence, and their waves are still, etc.” (Psalm 107)*. By which it is clear that God acts to disturb the sea, lakes, and rivers through angels or "windy ministers," whom the Prophet calls **stormy spirits**, fulfilling His word or will. As He spoke and made the spirit of the whirlwind blow—that is, the stormy spirit. So it is said elsewhere, *“With the East wind you break the ships of the ocean.” (Psalm 48:7)*. And elsewhere, *“He drove the East wind in the heavens, and by His power He brought in the South wind.”* Or as **Jerome** <note>Saint Jerome (c. 347–420 AD), the translator of the Bible into the Latin Vulgate.</note> translated it, *“He transferred the East wind from heaven, and by His strength He brought in the African wind [Southwest wind], and rained upon them.”* Whence he seems to have understood by those angels the ones mentioned in the **Apocalypse** <note>The Book of Revelation.</note> who held back the winds so they would not blow, and made them blow again to harm the sea, the land, and the fruits. The sacred page also makes mention of corrupt waters in various places, and experience denotes that in many places of any region the air is infected with evil breaths, from which arise for the most part intermittent fevers, and where the breath is more poisonous, it brings on pestilential diseases, as in **Scanderoon** <note>Iskenderun (formerly Alexandretta) in modern-day Turkey, historically known by European travelers for its "unhealthy" air and malaria-ridden marshes.</note>, a place in the East.

Finally, **Psellus** <note>Michael Psellos (1017–1078), a Byzantine monk, philosopher, and politician whose work "De Operatione Daemonum" (On the Operation of Demons) was a standard text on demonology.</note> testifies that the subterranean kind of demons causes openings in the earth and shakes foundations, and even stirs up flame-vomiting winds. We see also that a great earthquake is said to have occurred *“because (it is said) an angel of the Lord descended from heaven, and his appearance was like lightning.” (Matthew 28:2)*. It is as if the Evangelist had said that by the appearance of that great angel, the demons, moved by terror, stirred up and shook the earth, because the Creator was angry. Just as in the greater world <term>Macrocosm; the universe as a whole</term> three regions of spirit are found, differing from one another in nature, dignity, and purity—namely the empyrean, the ethereal, and the aerial (or elementary)—so too are just as many species of spirit found in man, the lesser world <term>Microcosm; the human being as a reflection of the universe</term>. These are derived from those of the Macrocosm: the intellectual or rational spirit corresponds to the **empyrean** <note>The highest, most spiritual heaven of pure fire or light.</note>, the vital spirit to the **ethereal**, and the natural spirit to the **elementary**. Truly, that aerial spirit is the vehicle for the other two, just as the mundane air is the vehicle for influences—both the angelic ones sent from the empyrean heaven and the stellar ones falling from the ethereal—since without this medium, it would be impossible for them to be carried down to the earth. 

This communication of spirits, and the duty of the air in that work, is best described by **Hermes Trismegistus** <note>A legendary Hellenistic figure associated with a collection of mystical and philosophical texts known as the Hermetica.</note> in these words: *“The human soul,”* he says, *“is carried in this manner: the mind in reason, reason in the soul, the soul in the spirit, and the spirit in the body; where, diffused through the veins, arteries, and blood, it moves the living creature in every part, and sustains and carries the suspended mass of the body.” (Trismegistus, Pimander, Book 10)*. It is as if he had said: the trace of the Divine Word is in the empyrean spirit; the empyrean spirit descends, as if through a medium, into the ethereal spirit, which is the food of life (for the **Soul of the World** breathes through its veins); this vital spirit, along with the rational spirit—at whose center is the Divine Mind itself—descends into the air. Since the air is the vehicle for the others, it transfers them into the human body, in which it is disseminated everywhere through the blood (*Genesis 5:9* <note>original: "Gen. 5.9." The author likely refers to the concept found in Genesis 9:4 or Leviticus 17:11 that the life/soul is in the blood.</note>). 

God Himself seems to acknowledge this same thing, affirming that the soul of man is in the blood. From this we see that in the internal fabric of man, three spirits are found: the lowest is the air, the highest is divine, and the intermediate seems to participate in both. Hence it is that **Plotinus** and all the **Platonists**, following Hermes Trismegistus, placed three things in the internal part of man, which they call the highest, the lowest, and the middle. They establish the highest as that divine thing which they call the **Mind**—that is, the illuminated intellect, which **Moses** calls the very "breath of life" <note>original: "spiraculum vitae"</note>, namely inspired into us by God or His Spirit. And that part is never damned or suffers. The lowest they made the sensitive and natural soul, which they named the **Idol** <note>original: "Idolum," here meaning the phantom or lower reflection of the soul</note>, and the **Apostle Paul** calls the "animal man," of whom he speaks thus: *“I see another law in my members, taking me captive in the law of sin.”* The intermediate is the middle spirit, governed in a certain way by reason, which is a participant in both extremes; they say that by means of this, the animal soul is joined with the mind. 

But we also have this confirmed by Holy Scripture, for in one place we have: *“The spirit of the strong God made me, and the breath of the Almighty gave life to me.” (Job 33:4)*. God Himself also speaks of this spirit: *“My spirit shall not remain in man forever.” (Genesis 6:17)*. In this speech, He intends the "breath of life" which He breathed into the first man—that is, the super-celestial spirit, full of the Divine Mind, breathed out from the solar tabernacle in an ethereal spirit most full of life. Furthermore, mention is made of another spirit which is more familiar to beasts than to men, whence the wise man says: *“The spirit of man and of the beast and their outcomes are the same in all; as this one dies, so dies that one.” (Ecclesiastes 3:19)*. In this speech, he seems to intend the aerial and sublunary spirit, which alone is subject to mutations, corruption, and infirmities; about which **Solomon** understood when he spoke in this way: *“The spirit of a man sustains and will bear his sickness.” (Proverbs 18:14)*. And the Royal Psalmist, intending the same, says: *“My soul is saturated with evils.” (Psalm 88:4)*.

Therefore, these things being known and most carefully weighed, it is worthwhile to consider that just as **Lucifer** with his angels (full of pride, malice, and envy) was cast down from the kingdoms of heaven into the lowest region of the world (filled everywhere with common air), so indeed his malice and violence avail nothing against the supreme or middle spirit in man. Rather, his whole force, power, and dominion are in the air—both the Macrocosmic and Microcosmic. Whence he is called by the Apostle: *“The prince of the power of this air, who works in the children of distrust.” (Ephesians 2:2)*. And elsewhere: *“You must contend not with flesh and blood, but with princes and powers, with the lords of darkness in this world, with the spirits of wickedness under heaven.” (Ephesians 6)*. By which he seems to argue that just as the malignant demons, the enemies of men, were banished from heaven into the region under heaven (according to that passage in the Apocalypse: *“The devil, the dragon, the ancient serpent was cast out, who seduces the whole world,” Revelation 12*), so indeed their force and effort are occupied in the air under heaven, and not in that of the starry or angelic heaven. For just as the good angels have their chief power in the good spirit, both of heaven...

### On the Efficient Cause of Atmospheric Phenomena <note>original: "De Causa Meteororum Efficiente." In the 17th century, "meteors" referred to any phenomenon occurring in the air, including wind, rain, and lightning.</note>

...of both the middle and the highest regions, just as evil spirits (whom Paul calls the lords of darkness) exercise their powers in the air and the sublunary <note>The region "below the moon," which in ancient science was the realm of change and decay.</note> or sub-celestial parts.

For since the element of demons is air, and insofar as they are spirits of darkness, it is necessary that they have a very close relationship both with the thicker air of the lowest order within man, and with the air of the world. Thus, they are able—and quite often accustomed—to join their aerial bodies with the thick spirit in man most easily, producing in him such weaknesses and diseases as are of the same nature and condition as the wind from which they are sent, or the element in which they more gladly rejoice and delight to dwell according to the disposition of their nature.

Concerning this communion of the demon with the aerial spirit, that wise man Artefius <note>A legendary medieval alchemist and philosopher often cited in esoteric works.</note> also testifies when he speaks in this manner, understanding it to refer to fiery demons (as it seems): *There are certain infirmities to which the Devil joins himself—namely, when a humor departs from its proper temperament and disturbs health itself—and this happens especially from infirmities arising from yellow bile <term>cholera; one of the four bodily humors, associated with heat and dryness</term>. The cause of this is because the nature of yellow bile is hot and dry like fire, while the substance of the Devil is composed of two things: fire and air. His visible part, therefore, is air, but his hidden part is fire; and for this reason, he most easily joins himself with the aerial spirit of man when a fiery humor holds dominion beyond what is natural.* With these golden words, he seems to clearly declare what we have already set forth. But since we have spoken more broadly and fully on this subject in the chapter *On the mystical Anatomy of the blood*, I refer you to Section 1, Portion 3, Part 3, Book 3, chapters 5 and 12 of our *Triple Anatomy*.

We conclude, therefore, that those spirits who have power solely over the air (or over the spirit in man which is subject to imaginative changes) are either fiery or aerial. For the property of fiery spirits is to inflame the air with sensible heat, exciting anger, fury, quarrels, contentions, and disputes without any other manifest bodily hindrance. And just as fiery angels of a holy condition are said to follow the mind of celestial souls (insofar as they assist in contemplating higher things), so indeed these [evil] spirits kindle a fire in the human air to darken the rays of the mind; they strive with great effort to carry the whole man headlong against the laws of reason. Aerial spirits also play their parts very subtly within the human spirit to deceive it more easily. For just as it is the nature of the celestial order of aerial spirits to follow true reason, to favor the rational faculty, and to separate it from the sensual and vegetative faculties (likewise serving the active life, just as the fiery spirits serve the contemplative life), so indeed aerial spirits of the worst condition are accustomed to deceive men with tricks and deceptive illusions, insinuating themselves into their spirits in such a way that they change their reason like Proteus <note>A Greek sea-god capable of changing his shape at will; here used to describe shifting, deceptive thoughts.</note>, making those things appear rational and approved by reason which are, in truth, fictional and false phantoms.

The manner by which they deceive men, and how they act secretly within the aerial spirit of man to seduce him from the true path or the sincere contemplation of God, is described best by Psellus <note>Michael Psellus, an 11th-century scholar whose writings on demons were highly influential in the Renaissance.</note> from the revelation of Marcus:

> They do not (he says) act upon the imaginative spirit of man (which they approach insofar as they themselves are spirits) by making a sound, but they secretly remind us and whisper words of disturbances and pleasures to us. They do not send forth a voice with a certain pulse or sound, but emit their speeches without sound; for they speak by whispering in a hidden manner. Since they can be joined with the aerial spirit due to the proximity of their natures, they need no sound at all in their hidden speech; rather, their speech, conceived as if by will, creeps into the listener with no sound at all.

In this way, therefore, demons of this sort are accustomed to converse with men secretly—so much so, in fact, that one cannot even perceive from where the war is being brought upon us. Furthermore, just as air, in the presence of light, receives various colors and forms and transmits them into those things which can naturally receive them (as clearly appears in mirrors, in water, and other such reflective surfaces), so also the demonic bodies—receiving imaginative figures, colors, and whatever forms they themselves wish from the essences that are within—transmit them into our animal and vital spirit. From this, they provide us with much trouble, alluring us toward various desires and suggesting various plans, showing various forms, stirring up memories of pleasures, and inciting phantoms of passions, both while we are awake and while we sleep. Sometimes, indeed, by tickling the thighs and groins of men, they incite them to lust, and they suggest and sharpen insane loves—especially if they sense the humors of the body are agreeable to this. But these, putting on the helmet of Pluto <note>The "Cap of Invisibility" from Greek mythology; the author uses it as a metaphor for demonic concealment and deception.</note>, disturb the soul with a certain art and Sophistical fraud. Over such cohorts of demons are several princes, of whom St. Paul speaks in this manner in the place cited above: *You must struggle not against flesh and blood, but against Princes and powers, and the lords of darkness in this world, against the spirits of malice under heaven; Ephesians 6.* That is, against the aerial demons and their legions, whose commander is that supreme prince of this air who is accustomed to work in the sons of disobedience.
