...he is specifically called **Beelzebub**, that is, the **Ancient God** <note>original: "Vetustus DEVS"</note>, under whose dominion are those demons called the **False Gods** <note>original: "Pseudothei"</note>, inasmuch as they wish to be considered and worshiped as Gods; from this, they scatter the seeds of **Idolatry** in the human spirit. The sixth is called **Meriris**, that is, the **"Furious and Boiling Spirit,"** to whom are subjected those spirits who produce storms in the air and infect the spirits of men with plague and corrupted air.

The seventh is called **Apollyon**, or **Abaddon** in Hebrew, which is to say, **"The Exterminator"** and **"The Destroyer."** Under his governance are the demons called **Furies**, who are the sowers of evils, discords, wars, devastations, and so forth.

The eighth is **Astaroth**, that is, the **"Scout"** or **"Spy,"** called in Greek **Diabolos**, which is to say, the **"Slanderer"** and **"Accuser."** In the Apocalypse, he is called the **"Accuser of the Brethren,"** accusing them day and night in the sight of our God.

The last is **Mammon**, which is interpreted as **"Greed"** <note>original: "cupiditas"</note>. He has under him the **Ambushing** and **Tempting** demons, and these are present to every human being.

By these types of **Evil Demons** <note>original: "Cacodæmonum"</note>, therefore, as they are the powers of the air, the human spirit (or "aerial breath") is afflicted in various ways. For they do not know how to actually reach the higher ether or the intellectual spirit of man, as they have been expelled from heaven. The Devil is said to act upon the spirit alone, or generally, and this from the beginning as the producer and author of sin. He produced this in Adam through his lies, by which all the human race has been contaminated even to this day. For (as the Wise Man says), *God created man for an incorruptible state, and made him in the image of His own very nature, but by the envy of the Devil, death entered into the world* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:23). By "death," he means the sin that was the cause of death; hence it is said, *The Devil was a murderer from the beginning, and stood not in the truth, because there is no truth in him* (John 8). And elsewhere: *The Devil sins from the beginning* (1 John 3). And the Apostle says: *Sin entered into this world through one man, and death through sin, and so death passed upon all men, in whom all have sinned* (Romans 5). But the author of this kind of sin was that spirit, seducing with his lies.

<meta>This page continues the catalog of demonic hierarchies and their influence on the human condition. Following the previous page's introduction of Beelzebub, Python, and Belial, it now details how these "aerial spirits" physically and psychologically infiltrate the human body through the act of breathing and the manipulation of the senses.</meta>

### On the Efficient Cause of Meteors.

Since, therefore, there is such a proximity in nature between the **human aerial spirit** <note>The "aerial spirit" refers to the "pneuma" or vital breath that early modern thinkers believed circulated through the body, mediating between the soul and the physical flesh.</note> and the **external demonic spirit**, it is very easy to believe that from the slightest cause, this demonic nature—by means of the air, constantly drawn in through breath—can enter the human body. It joins itself with the air naturally enclosed within the body and, even by penetrating through the ears and nostrils, mingles with the **phantastic spirit** <note>The "phantastic spirit" was the part of the soul responsible for imagination and mental imagery.</note>. Thus, it allures and inclines the nature and condition of that air toward its own will through secret apparitions and persuasions.

<margin>Ephesians 2:2</margin>
Hence, it is said by Saint Paul: *You walked according to the Prince of the power of this air, who now works in the sons of diffidence* <note>original: "Ambulastis secundum Principem potestatis aeris huius, qui nunc operatur in filios diffidentiæ"</note>. For where faith is present, he has no power; thus it happens that this prince, with his angels, tries in every way through secret whisperings and persuasions to induce "diffidence" (or lack of faith) primarily into the human spirit, so that he may afterwards have force and power over it.

In the Sacred Scriptures, it is expressed everywhere into what great indignation against GOD this Prince of Malice led the Israelites, by seducing them from the true worship of GOD to the adoration of himself. Indeed, by his crafts, he even enticed Solomon, the wisest of all men, to the adoration of **Astaroth**. Furthermore, by his crafts, **Beelzebub** was held to be an ancient God among the Heathens.

<margin>1 Kings 22</margin>
False imaginations and apparitions are also introduced to the human spirit by his primary minister, **Python**, along with his subjects. By these, not only common men but even the Prophets of God themselves are deceived, as is declared in the history of King Ahab: *A certain spirit, coming forth into the sight of the Lord, said to him: I will go forth and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets, etc.* <note>original: "Spiritus quidam prodiens in conspectum Iehouæ dixit ei, egressus ero spiritus mendacis in ore omnium prophetarum, &c."</note>

<margin>Wisdom 5:15</margin>
This kind of demon also imprints a **false hope** upon the human spirit, not unlike how we see a false and fictitious image fixed superficially in a mirror. Regarding such Hope, the wise man speaks thus: *The hope of the impious is like down carried by the wind, and like thin foam driven by a storm, and like smoke dissolved by the wind.* <note>original: "Spes impii est vt lanugo delata à vento, & tanquam spuma tenuis à procella impulsa, & tanquam fumus a vento dissolutus"</note> Therefore, the effect of this vain hope is that it makes the soul sick, as Solomon testifies: <margin>Proverbs 13:12</margin> And this is the reason why the demon imprints vain hope into the aerial spirit of man: so that the spirit, through its contact with the "heaven of man" (or the ethereal spirit within him), can mark it with false reflections of the thing expected.

<margin>Job 13:4</margin>
He is also accustomed to inflate **fury and wrath** into the human spirit, by which the mind is evilly affected and reason is covered with a veil of error. Thus, while that state lasts, great crimes are usually committed. Concerning this kind of passion, the Patient One <note>A traditional epithet for Job.</note> says: *The fool tears his soul in his fury.* <note>original: "Animum suum laniat stultus furore suo"</note> In this diabolical passion, Cain was stained with his brother’s blood, and his soul was miserably defiled by brotherly slaughter.

<margin>Genesis 3</margin>
How much evil and how much misery did the disobedience of Adam toward GOD bring upon himself and his posterity? You have it very well explained by Moses how much affliction of both soul and body the obstinacy and disobedience of the Israelites caused during their journey through the desert. <margin>Exodus 33</margin> Indeed, **disobedience** is the fountain and origin of all sins.

Furthermore, he stamps deceitful, disguised, and treacherous imaginations like false **Idols** into the aforementioned spirit, and from there he renders hearts treacherous and weak. Thus, **Satan** is said to have entered into Judas and burned him with his hostile spirit so that he would betray his lord.

Sometimes he even agitates human spirits toward discord, contention, and the desire for arms or war. This he performs sometimes through the **infection of the air** (as occurs after the appearance of a comet) and sometimes through secret whisperings and agitations.

<margin>Ephesians 6</margin>
Therefore, we must struggle, according to the admonition of the Apostle, against those spirits of malice under heaven. Regarding this, the wise man gives us these lessons: *He loves falls who loves quarrels,* <margin>Proverbs 17:19</margin> and elsewhere, *It is a glory for a man to rest from strife.* <margin>Proverbs 20:3</margin>

<margin>Proverbs 22:10</margin>
And elsewhere: *When contention ceases, he shall cease from disgrace.* His first and principal minister in this action is called **Abaddon**, or **Apollyon**, under whom there are infinite specific spirits ordained for this business.

And sometimes there are evil demons who are ordained by God to strike **fear and terror** into the human aerial spirit, so much so that men are suddenly struck with a great stupor.

<margin>2 Kings 19:7</margin>
Concerning this kind of spirit, the sacred page speaks thus: *Behold, I will put a spirit in him, that he may hear a rumor and return to his own land.* Furthermore, in another place it is said: *Be amazed and wonder, fluctuate and waver; be drunk, but not with wine; stagger, but not with drunkenness, for the Lord has mingled for you a spirit of deep sleep.* <note>original: "spiritum soporis"</note> <margin>Isaiah 29:9</margin> The Archangel <note>Likely referring to a specific esoteric or kabbalistic source common in this era's literature.</note> says that the name of God, **Elohim**, denotes dread and terror; hence the angels who respond to Him are called **Bene Elohim** <note>Hebrew: "Sons of God/the Powers."</note>, to whom he assigns the **Northern place**, as it is the place from which all evil comes. Thus, it is likely that the office of terrifying and stupefying is assigned to these kinds of angels or demons.

Hence, those who are struck by sudden stupor and dread seem to grow stiff as if with cold and are seen to shake as if with trembling.

### Section I. Portion IV. Part II. Book IV. Member II.

Furthermore, they afflict the soul with sadness, sorrow, desolation, and grief, as we see in those suffering from **melancholy** <note>In the early modern period, melancholy was seen as both a physical ailment of "black bile" and a spiritual state where the mind was vulnerable to demonic shadows.</note>. This disease is said to be caused primarily by demons creeping into the human spirit and deluding it with false ideas; from this, they induce painful symptoms worthy of pity in the aerial spirit of man. Hence Job says (since his spirit was contaminated by Satan): *My face is fouled with weeping, and it swells; finally, a lethal shadow sits upon my eyelids, Job 16.* And elsewhere: *My spirit is narrowed within me, Job 21.* And the Royal Psalmist <note>Refers to King David, traditionally credited with the Psalms.</note> says: *A breaking of the soul brings sickness, and when I look for someone to grieve with me, no one is there; I am greatly weakened and worn down, I roar with the groaning of my heart; my sighing is not hidden from you, my heart palpitations, and my strength has left me, etc.* And elsewhere more clearly: *Wasting of the soul, indignation, and sorrow make the mind fail, and groans fill my years.* And elsewhere: *My spirit is overwhelmed within me; in the midst of me, my spirit seems desolate in itself. My spirit is consumed by your spirit; lead me into a level land—that is, into the right way, etc. Psalm 143.* 

But nevertheless, to a spirit so afflicted, he shows the way by the direction of his own mind, by which he may snatch himself from the power of the evil spirit, saying in another place: *Why are you cast down, O my soul, and why do you stir within me? Hope in God, for I shall yet praise him, etc. Psalm 42:6.* By these words, he clearly teaches that there is another spirit in man <note>The author distinguishes between the "sensitive/lower spirit" (subject to emotions/demons) and the "intellectual/higher spirit" (the soul's rational part) which remains under human or divine control.</note>, which stands above his lower spirit and commands it, against which the malignant demons can prevail neither by force nor by craft; this is what Job also indicated in all his afflictions by his firm hope and patience.

Sometimes the demon drives the human spirit with the spurs of **despair**, so that he may snatch the whole man into a "bad death" <note>Usually referring to suicide or a death without repentance.</note>, which we read indeed happened to Judas, the betrayer of the Savior of the world, and also to Saul.

As for the remaining hindrances of the spirit—namely pride, gluttony, avarice, and other such things—the deceitful aerial spirits are accustomed to bring these impressions in a pleasurable manner and path, as if by flattering and subtly persuading, as was declared above.

Finally, among all the impressions of the **evil demons** <note>original: "Cacodæmonum"</note> upon the human spirit, blasphemy is the most dangerous to both soul and body. Those of whom David spoke in *Psalm 139* were obsessed by this spirit of blasphemy, as was that blasphemer born of an Egyptian father and a Hebrew mother who cursed the name of **Jehovah** in the camp of the Israelites, *Leviticus 24.* Thus, when this spirit has insinuated itself into the lowest spirit of a man, it renders him not only hateful to men but also rebellious and reprobate before God himself.

We conclude, therefore, that the malignant spirits who have power only over the human spirit—without manifest contact with the body—are very thin, subtle, and of a high condition in their aerial disposition. For those who are of a grosser consistency—whether vaporous, aquatic, or earthly—these are accustomed to strike the spirit in the body, and the body along with the spirit, by manifest and more sensible contact. Hence, spirits of a grosser consistency and fiery nature produce fiery diseases in both the spirit and the body that are perceptible to the senses, such as **fevers**; but if they are more earthly, then they bring inflammations of the body and its solid parts, and so on for the rest, as described more broadly below. It should be known in the meantime, however, that those spirits which act primarily on the <term>phantastic spirit</term> <note>The "phantastic spirit" or "imagination" was thought to be a physical vapor in the brain that processed images; demons were believed to manipulate this "vapor" to cause hallucinations.</note>—that is, in the higher region of the human spirit—are spirits of a subtle consistency. Those, however, who operate on the **sensitive spirit** are somewhat grosser in their constitution, etc. For such as the differences are in the sublunary air <note>The atmosphere between the Earth and the Moon, which according to Aristotle was the realm of change and corruption.</note>, such also are the angels; according to their nature in their disposition, they are said to be either thicker or thinner.

Just as the power of the thinner aerial spirits is chiefly occupied with the "fantastic spirit" <note>The part of the soul responsible for imagination and mental images.</note> of man, resulting in the perturbation of the soul alone (as has been said), so indeed some of a lower order have the task of afflicting both the body and the spirit simultaneously with plague and sickness. Thus we see that just as the upper portion of the air differs from the middle, and the middle from the lowest, so also we perceive that the "meteors" in these three regions differ from one another in both consistency and quality. And yet, nonetheless, just as we have fiery meteors in the upper region, we also find them in the middle and lowest regions, which communicate by natural reason with earth and water. Therefore, the more a "meteor" is created high up in the air, the less it is observed to have commerce with earth and water, and the more with air and fire; and all these things are governed by the spirit of the place.

It is therefore no wonder if some fiery spirits act only upon the human spirit, inciting fury, lycanthropy <note>The delusion of being transformed into a wolf.</note>, anger, and heat within it; others disturb the spirit and, through the spirit, the humors and the body simultaneously; and likewise others are observed to rule over and afflict the humors in the limbs of the body alone, while the aerial spirit remains untouched and free from febrile heat. For these are all, without doubt, angelic ministers through whom God afflicts the spirits and bodies of sinners, just as the Fountain of Truth testifies that He acts beneficently with men through good angels. Whence it is written: *He wounds and He heals; He strikes, and His hands shall make whole; Job 5:17.* And elsewhere it says: *That God speaks by rebuke through pain in the bed, and makes all the bones waste away, Job 33.* And yet this is certain: that although this office is attributed to God, His striking angel nevertheless performs it. Even Satan himself confessed this, saying, *Put forth your hand against him, etc.* and nonetheless Satan himself afflicted Job with a most grievous ulcer from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head, *Job 1.* Whence God is called, as it were, the "Ordainer" who brings on this or that disease, and yet He uses avenging ministers to bring His decree into action.

It is therefore within the Divine will to afflict man with "aerial diseases," in which manner Job was also vexed, as if by a hypochondriac wind <note>Vapors or "winds" believed to rise from the organs below the ribs, causing physical and mental distress.</note> along with that demonic plague. Whence he was forced to say: *You have lifted me up into the wind or the blast; you set me upon it and cause me to melt away in substance, Job 30:22.* This is as if he had been distended either by a windy bloating or by a blast on every side, which also most frequently happens in fevers where diseases are complicated. And Albohali <note>Abu 'Ali al-Khayyat, a famous 9th-century astrologer and physician.</note> boldly says that windy and melancholic diseases are caused by evil spirits. But—

The Royal Psalmist <note>Referring to King David, the traditional author of the Psalms.</note> seems to assert that these "aerial" diseases <note>Diseases thought to be carried through or composed of the element of air, such as vapors or winds.</note> proceed from wicked spirits, with these words: *He cast upon them the fierceness of his anger, indignation, and trouble, by sending evil angels.* <note>Psalm 78:49; the Latin text cites it as Psalm 78. 74.</note> And elsewhere in the Holy Scripture, we read that by the prayer of Elisha, a multitude of those following him were struck with <term>Scotomia</term> <note>From the Greek *skotos* (darkness); a medical term for dizziness accompanied by dimmed or darkened vision.</note>, as seen in 2 Kings 6. It is also recorded that this same thing happened by angelic power to the Sodomites before the door of Lot's house. Mention is also made of the torment of the bowels along with painful colic, where it is written: *You shall be plagued with a disease of the intestines, until your intestines fall out because of the sickness.* <note>2 Chronicles 21:15, referring to the punishment of King Jehoram.</note> Does the Holy Scripture not intend to speak of these types of flatulent or "windy" spirits when it says: *A wind of the power of God, and justice pursuing the wicked*? <note>Wisdom of Solomon 11:20.</note> And elsewhere: *A spirit of power and a spirit of strength shall stand against them, and like a storm and a whirlwind it shall scatter them.* <note>Wisdom of Solomon 5:23.</note> For the spirit of "windy" epilepsy, of vertigo and dizzy-darkness, and of the <term>suffocation of the womb</term> <note>Known historically as *suffocatio intellectus* or "hysteria," believed to be caused by "vapors" moving through the body.</note> is of this nature; it is accustomed to disturb and toss the suffering patient in the manner of a storm in the <term>Macrocosm</term> <note>The great world or the universe at large.</term>.

But to come to the effects of the "burning" spirits—namely plagues, fevers, rages, and madnesses, and others of this kind—these are undoubtedly produced by malignant spirits of an aerial and fiery nature. Hence Job says: *The arrows of the Lord are within me, the poison whereof drinks up my spirit; the terrors of the Lord set themselves in array against me.* <note>Job 6:4.</note> Here, by "terrors," he understands the evil angels who induce terror, according to that which was cited from the Psalm: *He cast upon them the fierceness of his anger... by evil angels.* <note>Psalm 78:49.</note> And elsewhere: *You shall not be afraid for the terror by night; nor for the arrow that flies by day; nor for the pestilence that walks in darkness; nor for the destruction or demon that wastes at noonday.* <note>Psalm 91:5-6.</note> Elsewhere it is said: *Jehovah shall strike you with a consumption, and with a hot and burning fever, and with drought, and with blasting.* <note>Deuteronomy 28:22.</note> Here, when Jehovah speaks, it is understood as Jehovah commanding, and the angelic ministers executing the command. Thus, when God afflicted the Israelites with a plague, David saw the angel striking between heaven and earth; similarly, it is said: *Jehovah shall strike you with madness, and blindness, etc.* Even <term>Phrenitis</term> <note>Inflammation of the brain or "brain fever."</note> and <term>Lycanthropia</term> <note>A delusion where a person believes they have been transformed into a wolf.</note> arise from a hidden cause of this kind—namely, from the stirring up of a malignant demon, as is evident from the man possessed by a legion of demons who lived among the tombs, driven by a tumultuous rage, in Mark 5.

The Sacred Scriptures make ample mention of the afflictions of paralytics, epileptics, lunatics, the discharges of the bowels and of women, as well as gonorrhea; likewise the leprosy of Miriam, Naaman, Gehazi, and that on the forehead of King Uzziah. Concerning the gout of Asa, the hemorrhoids [of the Philistines], the "Royal Disease" <note>Usually referring to scrofula or jaundice, depending on the period.</note>, ulcers, scabs, itching, and many other such things expressed in the Holy Scripture, we shall speak more abundantly, God willing, in the appropriate place in the following volume. See concerning these: 2 Kings 2; 2 Chronicles 26; 2 Chronicles 16; 1 Samuel 5.

We conclude, therefore, since in this "Member" <note>A subdivision of the book's structure.</note> you have a description of the ministers of God—both the benevolent who do good, and the malevolent who afflict with malicious disease—acting upon the world and its creatures, and upon man, who is the end and perfection of all creatures. For this reason, the <term>Cabalists</term> <note>Followers of Jewish mysticism (Kabbalah) which was studied by many Renaissance scholars.</note> assign to man as his appropriate symbol the last of the holy letters, namely **Tau** <note>The Hebrew letter ת; in this context, it symbolizes the completion of creation or a mark of divine protection/judgment.</note>. If these ministers are good, God uses them in clemency, goodness, and kindness toward the world and man; but if they are evil, He conversely uses them in His severity, wrath, and vengeance as a whip for both the Macrocosm and the <term>Microcosm</term> <note>The "small world," referring to the human being.</note>.

Indeed, it must also be understood in this place that even His good angels sometimes execute the vengeance of God and His people upon men and the world; in this respect, they are nonetheless regarded as "evil angels" by those who suffer their whip. Hence Jehovah said: *Behold, I send my angel before you... for he will not pardon your transgressions: for my name is in him.* <note>Exodus 23:21.</note> But we shall speak more abundantly of these matters in the following volume, where we shall treat the causes of health and disease.

### CHAPTER VI.

->*Concerning the orders of Angels, into whom the radiant influences are poured and showered from the luminous gates appropriate to each Divine Name: and concerning those great Archangels to whom such influences are committed from each order of angels, so that they may subsequently carry them down into the celestial spheres.*<-

Although we have already made clear mention of the nature of the ten <term>Sephiroth</term> <note>The ten emanations or attributes in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself.</note> or divine numerations—which are various lights descending from a single root, by whose favor all things are created, and once created are either nourished or changed from one state to another according to the property of God—in Tractate 2, Section 1, Portion 2, Part 1, Chapter 3 of the *Theosophical, Cabalistic, and Physiological Discourse*; nevertheless, since they seem to pertain primarily to our present subject of the nature of both good and evil angels (seeing as they seem to have received their offices from these properties of God), it has come into my mind to discuss a few things about them here and to revisit that discourse.

<meta>This page continues the exploration of spiritual and celestial influences on the physical world. While the previous page categorized diseases within the human "Microcosm" as being caused by demonic or elemental forces, this page shifts to a higher perspective: the "Macrocosm." It details the hierarchical descent of divine energy from the Sephirot (the ten attributes of God in Kabbalah) through various ranks of angels and archangels, finally manifesting in the movements of the planetary spheres and the elements of our world.</meta>

# On the Efficient Cause of Meteors

The influxes of the first **Sephirot** <note>In Jewish Kabbalah, the Sephirot are the ten attributes or emanations through which the Infinite (Ein Sof) reveals itself and creates the universe.</note>—namely those which descend from the bright gate of **Cheter** <note>Keter</note> or the "Crown," over which the name **Ehieh** <note>Hebrew: "I Am"</note> presides (said to represent God the Father)—glide and flow downward into the first order of Angels, the **Seraphim**. From there, they are guided further down by that great Angel **Metattron** <note>Metatron</note> into the *Primum Mobile* <note>The "First Moved" sphere, the outermost sphere in the classical geocentric model of the universe</note>. They grant it the strength and vigor by which it turns the celestial orbs from east to west in the space of a single day. For this reason, Metattron is established as the governor of the *Primum Mobile*, from which he liberally rains down the essence and the faculty of motion upon the lower spheres. According to the Kabbalists, *Ehieh* bestows the gift of "being," and thus it is Metattron’s office to flow vitality into all creatures. This is why he is regarded as the **Soul of the World** <note>Anima Mundi</note>. In this action, the property of God signifies clemency and kindness toward the world.

The outflows of the second **Sephirot**, or "lucid gate," called **Hochma** <note>Chokmah</note> or "Wisdom"—over which the divine name **Iah** or **Jehovah** presides—fall into the order of the **Cherubim**. From that order, they are entrusted to the guardianship of the Archangel **Jophiel** (or, as others prefer, **Ruziel** <note>Raziel</note>), so that through him they may be introduced into the eighth sphere <note>The sphere of the fixed stars, beyond the planets</note>. From this sphere, they are poured out into lower realms, both celestial and elementary. By their power, the operations of the fixed stars—both within the Zodiac and outside its belt—are observed in the lower world. They produce various forms of life, especially animals; hence the "Zodiac" is named from the Greek word *Zoon*, which means "animal." Because of this, Cichus Esculus <note>Cecco d’Ascoli, a 13th-century astronomer and poet</note>, in his book on the sphere, asserted not ineptly that every animal on earth and in the sea symbolizes and agrees in nature with some sign of the Zodiac of the same name. Likewise, Moses the Arab <note>Maimonides, the famous Jewish philosopher</note> says that every living thing has a star in heaven flowing into it to protect and preserve its essence.

Indeed, since every heaven or sphere—and consequently all its stars—has its own great angel to move and govern it and to conduct the influences sent from God through the "intellectual heaven," and since many principal leaders are subject to each of these royal Archangels, having many legions of lower spirits under their command, we say that each of these spirits has its own peculiar office in both the heavens and the elements. Mercury Trismegistus <note>The legendary Hellenistic figure associated with the Hermetic writings</note> seems to partly confirm this in *Pimander 3* with these words: <note>original: "Dii in astrorum ideis cum signis conspiciebantur, Dinumerata sunt stellæ secundum eos qui inhabitabant Deos"</note> "The Gods were seen in the ideas of the stars with their signs; the stars were numbered according to the Gods who inhabited them," where by "Gods" he seems to mean these spirits or demons.

The influx of the third **Sephirot**, which is **Binah** or "Prudence" <note>Understanding</note>—over which the name of God **Elohim** presides—passes through the order of **Thrones** and is received by the Archangel **Zaphkiel** (or, as others will, **Jophiel**), who leads it into the sphere of **Saturn**. From this, Saturn derives its peculiar power and property, distinct from other planets. Thus, this planet rains "Saturnine influxes" or "Saturnine spirits" upon the earth, especially at the time when it holds dominion in the sky; for then its effects in the elements appear most clearly. These effects are for the most part gloomy and not at all favorable to the world or the human spirit, which is why astrologers call it the "**Greater Misfortune**."

The influxes of the fourth numeration or "lucid gate," called **Chesed** or "Clemency"—over which the name of God **El** presides—descend into the order of **Dominations**. Through them, they are carried downward by the Archangel **Zadkiel** into the sphere of **Jupiter**, mercifully tempering its nature. Consequently, the flows sent down from it are benevolent and gracious to both the air and the human spirit, as they are said to nourish and cherish natural strengths. For this reason, astrologers call it the "**Greater Fortune**."

The bright influences of the fifth gate or numeration, called **Geburah**—that is, "Punishment," over which the name of God **Elohim Gibor** presides—penetrate through the order of **Powers**. They are led by the Archangel **Camael** (or **Samael**) into the sphere of **Mars**, where they animate the fiery spirits of Mars with a burning and inclement severity. Therefore, this planet is not without reason called by astrologers the "**Lesser Misfortune**." For just as Saturn’s influence acts harshly upon the world’s elements and creatures by way of extreme cold and dryness, so do the Martial spirits, bearing arms under the leadership of Samael, afflict the fiery air of the world with conflagrations, lightning, comets, and many other troubles, and infest the human spirit with heat, fever, plague, and inflammations.

The sixth "lucid gate," called **Tiphereth**—that is, "Grace" <note>Beauty</note>, over which the name of God **Eloah** superintends—flows through the order of **Virtues**. The Archangel **Michael** is, by office, the receiver of its influxes, translating them into the sphere of the **Sun**. From its golden world, gracious, splendid, and life-giving virtues are rained upon the lower regions. These are called "Solar spirits," which never act maliciously unless they are corrupted by the spirits of the wicked planets.

The seventh, called **Netzeth** <note>Netzach</note> or "Triumph," presided over by the name of God **Jehovah Zabaoth**, sends its benevolent breaths into the order of **Principalities**. From there, they are led down into the sphere of **Venus** by the Archangel **Hanael**. It follows that the Venerean spirits emit favorable breaths into these lower parts; thus, Venus is called the "**Lesser Fortune**" by astrologers, being closer to the human race in nature and condition after Jupiter.

The eighth, called **Hod**—that is, "Praise," over which the name of God **Elohim Sabaoth** presides—emits and transfuses its influxes through the order of **Archangels**. These are received by the Archangel **Raphael** and applied to replenish the powers of the orb of **Mercury**, which again pours its spirits into the lower world, imparting the stated property of the Creator everywhere.

# On the Efficient Cause of Meteors.

Finally, the tenth numeration, called **Malkuth** <note>Hebrew: *Malcut*, meaning "Kingdom." This is the final Sephirah in the Kabbalistic Tree of Life, representing the physical world.</note>, which is presided over by the name **Adonai** <note>Hebrew: *Adonai*, meaning "Lord."</note>, sends down its influences into the order of holy souls. As the **Kabbalists** <note>original: *Cabalistæ*; practitioners of Jewish mysticism.</note> say, they imagine these souls are committed to the power of the soul of the **Messiah**. This order communicates those influences to these lower regions. From these things, therefore, it is right to see and notice that whatever exists in this world—whether it be supracelestial or angelic, or celestial and starry, or finally elementary—it is clear and evident that all of this arises from an immediate emanation from God. For it is His power, or His **fiery breath** <note>original: *spiraculum igneum*</note>, by means of which (and not otherwise) all things in this world are made, produced into action, and endowed with motion. This is according to the Sacred Page: *God fills all things.* And elsewhere: *God the Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in us all (Ephesians 4:6).* And elsewhere: *From God are all things (1 Timothy 6).* And elsewhere: *God works all in all (Ephesians 4:6).* And elsewhere: *The incorruptible Spirit of God is in every thing (Wisdom 12).* But this is also explained best and with a clearer thread in another place, where the Apostle seems to declare in plain words (2 Corinthians 5) that neither the Angels, nor the stars over which they preside in heaven, nor spirits, nor men, nor any other creatures on earth—no matter what title of "Gods" might be attributed to them—can perform anything by themselves or in themselves. Rather, it is only He who created heaven and earth, who is all in all. The words of the Apostle are these: *There are indeed those who are called Gods in heaven and on earth, yet for us there is one God the Father, from whom are all things, and we in Him, and one Lord Jesus Christ, through whom are all things, and we through Him (1 Corinthians 8).* Whence John says: *By the Word all things were made, etc. (John 1).* Concerning which the Prophet also says: *Thus says God, creating the heavens, stretching them out, establishing the earth and the things that spring from it, giving breath to the people who are upon it, and spirit to those who walk upon it (Isaiah 42:5).*

By these things it is clear that by this divine emanation or "breath of God"—to which the angels serve as ministers according to the will of Him who sent it forth—heaven, earth, and all things were made, and without it, nothing. Wherefore also these primary angels are called by the royal Prophet "the angels of God, most mighty in strength," *performing His word, doing His pleasure or His will (Psalm 103).* But even these are not said to "make" anything themselves, but rather God does so by means of His Word or emanation. Whence the wise maintain that all operations—the good according to their benevolent influences, as well as the bad according to the disposition of malevolent influences—are usually performed by God, as the immediate actor, through the angels acting as the organs in which God works.

For as was said before, the Name, or the Word, or the divine light is within the angels, and it drives the angelic composition to execute the divine will. They cannot move to perform this or that without His act, any more than we can move or act except by the impulse of the divine act, according to that in the Book of Acts: *In God we live, and move, and have our being (Acts 17).* *From Him, in Him, and through Him (says the Apostle) are all things, to whom be praise and honor.* And this is the reason why philosophers call Him the "center of every thing, whose circumference is nowhere"—that is, outside of all things. And this Prince or disposer of created nature was called by Zeno, along with Saint John, the **Logos** <note>original: *Logon*; the Greek term for "Word" or "Reason."</note> or the Word, which creates understanding of itself and is not dependent on any other. The Hebrews call Him **Shaddai** <note>original: *Sadai*</note>, that is, "sufficient unto Himself in every business." This Word, insofar as it is diffused throughout the entire nature of things, is called by the Platonists the **World Soul** <note>original: *mundi anima*</note>.

But here perhaps some may wish to object that if God or this divine emanation does all things, then God is also the author of evil and sin. To this we answer with **Elihu** <note>A character from the Book of Job who defends God's justice.</note> to the patient man: *Far be wickedness from the strong God, and iniquity from the Almighty; the strong God does not act wickedly, nor does He pervert judgment (Job 34:11).* And yet it is said by the wise man that *God does whatever He wills, and no one is to ask Him, "What or why do You do so?" (Wisdom 12:12).* How then can we judge the divine act, so as to say of it that He has acted either well or ill with the world or with man? *The secrets of God,* says the Holy Bible, *no one knows, but they are in the power of God.* And yet elsewhere we find *that good and evil, life and death, poverty and honor are from God (Ecclesiasticus 11:14).* And in another place we find this: *Consider the works of God, that no one can correct him whom He has despised; in the good day enjoy good things, and beware of the evil day; for as He made the one, so He made the other, so that man may not find just complaints against Him (Ecclesiastes 7:14).* And elsewhere it is said, *Is there evil in the city that the Lord has not done?* And elsewhere, *God has power over life and death, who leads down to the gates of death and brings back again (Wisdom 16).* And in another place this same thing is explained more brilliantly: *Wisdom is with Him, and His are counsel and understanding. Behold, He holds back the waters so that they dry up, and He sends them forth to overturn the earth; with Him is strength and power, His is the wanderer and the one who leads into error; He who makes counselors behave like madmen and makes judges fools; He looses the bond of kings; He who makes leaders behave like madmen and perverts the most crafty. He who increases nations and destroys them; who expands nations and leads them away; who removes the heart from the chiefs of the earth, who makes them wander like a drunkard, and grope in the dark where there is no light (Job 12).*

Finally, since the cause of **original sin** was unbelief, and that unbelief was introduced by God from the beginning, it would certainly be difficult (it seems to me) to deny that God Himself introduced the origin of that sin into the world for the exaltation of His name and glory. For that ancient serpent could not have enticed Eve to disobedience by her unbelief without divine incitement and will, since (as the Apostle says) all things are moved by God. Indeed, the Devil can in no way act or move without the divine will and permission, which he himself confesses in these words: *Extend...* <note>A reference to Job 1:11, where Satan asks God to "extend" His hand against Job.</note>

Sect. I. Port. IV. Part. II. Lib. IV. Membr. II.

...a little your hand, and touch all that he possesses, *Job 1:11.* And elsewhere, *Put forth your hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, etc.* <note>The author is quoting the Book of Job, where Satan challenges God to test Job's righteousness by taking away his blessings.</note>

Satan says these things to **Jehovah**, and yet it was nevertheless Satan who brought the wind from the desert, and who called down the fire of **GOD** from heaven, and who stirred up the hearts of the neighboring **Sabeans** <note>A group of people from Sheba, mentioned in Job 1:15 as those who raided Job's livestock.</note> against Job; and it was he who afflicted him and struck him with a malignant ulcer from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head. Therefore, when he says, "put forth your hand, and touch him," he seemed to imply that God should incite the Devil himself—as if he were His minister whom He uses as a scourge against men—or that He had granted permission to do this. For from the effect, it appeared to be so; but Jehovah also seems to acknowledge this same thing in express words, as is held in the Prophet **Isaiah 54:16-17**: *Behold, I have created the smith that bloweth the coals in the fire, and that bringeth forth an instrument for his work; and I have created the waster to destroy.* By these words, He seems to intimate that the Devil was expressly created by God to lead us into sins and to be a destroyer for us.

Furthermore (says the **Apostle** <note>Referring to St. Paul.</note>), if there were no law, there would be no sin; but the disobedience of man was the cause of the external and severe law. The Spiritual Lawgiver longs to heal the wounds of this law in His mercy through faith (which is the anchor of the internal law, or of Christ) and to wipe away the scars. If He had not given the law, sin would not have been introduced. But **GOD**, insofar as He is not subject to the law, cannot sin, nor act unjustly, since He gave the law not to Himself but to man. Consequently, He cannot be called the author of sin; hence, whatever He wills, He does, and yet in Him there is no iniquity. We say with Job (as above): *Far be it from the mighty GOD to do wickedness, and from the Almighty to commit iniquity: for the mighty GOD will not act wickedly, nor will He pervert judgment, Job 34:11.*

And yet, for no sin of his own, but solely to fulfill His own will (which in the eyes of men could appear to be injustice), He laid His hand upon Job. But so that the wise **Elihu** <note>One of the figures in the Book of Job who justifies God's actions.</note> might nonetheless demonstrate that there is no real injustice in GOD in all of this, he broke forth into the aforementioned words for the consolation of Job. God certainly holds in His hidden counsel what must be done; yet His actions are not to be judged according to the imaginations of men. For sometimes He seems to act severely, and occasionally—indeed, most often—He appears to act mercifully with the world and man; yet all His actions are consistent and uniform within Himself. The whole difference lies in their effect in respect to men. Whatever He does, He does indeed so that He may celebrate His name among men, and so that He may be rightly known and celebrated by them. And so that they might acknowledge His final mercy, He placed unbelief and sin among men, so that He might finally extend His mercy to them when they sin anew: *For GOD does whatever He wills, and no one is to ask Him, "What or why do you do so?" Wisdom 12:12,* as has been said. But the Apostle seems to signify all of this to us in the clearest words, in these truly golden words to be contemplated with a clear eye: *GOD hath concluded all in unbelief, that He might have mercy upon all.*

> O the depth of the riches of the wisdom and the knowledge of GOD! how unsearchable are His judgments, and His ways past finding out! For who hath known the mind of the Lord? or who hath been His counselor? Or who hath first given to Him, and it shall be recompensed unto him again? For of Him, and through Him, and in Him, are all things: to whom be honor and glory for ever. Amen. Romans 11:32-36.

What could be more brilliant than these words of the divine Apostle? In them, he seems primarily to assert that GOD has placed and concluded all things in unbelief—or as the interlined testament <note>original: *testamentum interlineatum*; likely referring to a polyglot Bible or a specific annotated version common in the 17th century.</note> puts it better:

GOD has concluded all men in unbelief that He might have mercy on all. The reason is that He might make men obligated and grateful to Him for His mercy. Furthermore, lest this or that man should say and object that this is impossible and against the sense of the Holy Scriptures (which seem to pronounce that many—indeed, the greater part of men—are to be damned, and the smaller part saved, wherefore this speech might seem harsh and improbable), the Apostle responds to such inconsistency, saying: *O the depth of the knowledge of GOD! how unsearchable are His judgments! For who knows the mind of GOD? or who has been His counselor? or who first gave to Him? etc.*

By these things, he seems to argue that the meaning of Holy Scripture is so profound that it is not within human sense to comprehend what GOD intends for Himself. Does not the Apostle confess elsewhere that *the letter kills, but the spirit gives life*? And Christ Himself confessed that He spoke in mystery and in the manner of parables, and warned His disciples that they should do the same. And yet, we ourselves wish to be the judges and expositors of divine counsels and judgments. But let us proceed to the final clause of the conclusion: *Since from Him, through Him, and in Him are all things, etc.*

From this, therefore, he concludes that neither this—whether it be some stigma of unbelief or an act of the Devil—nor that—whatever it may be of goodness—exists except from God, as one from whom, through whom, and in whom are all things. Although, in respect to human consideration, we refer those things which happen to us badly and perversely to the Devil or the Prince of Darkness, while we attribute those things which happen kindly and mercifully to God. And yet the Holy Scriptures show that GOD brings evils <note>original: *mala*; in this context, "evils" refers to calamities, punishments, or trials rather than moral sin.</note> upon men in His heat and wrath, just as, conversely, they confirm that all benefits to men proceed from GOD in the property of His mercy.

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the divine as the ultimate source of both creation and destruction. While the previous page touched upon the role of Satan and the Law, this page shifts to a Cabalistic and Neoplatonic framework, explaining how God’s various names and "gates" (Sephirot) channel different qualities—from mercy to severity—into the world.</meta>

->### On the Efficient Cause of Meteors.<-

The Cabalists <note>Followers of the Jewish mystical tradition who seek to interpret the hidden meanings of the Bible</note> also wisely signified all of this through the differences of the various titles attributed to **GOD** in the sacred text. Just as these names are varied, the wise have observed that they produce various effects in the places cited in the Bible. For this reason, they assigned to them various luminous properties, which they believed descended through as many bright gates, differing in quality, as there are names.

And they called these gates **Sephirot**, or the "enumerations" of the Cabalists. They describe some of these as inclining toward severity and others toward mercy, according to the nature of the matter being treated in that part of the sacred page where those divine names are recited. From these properties of God, they observed Him to be either severe—and thus inclined toward the cursing of the world and man—or inclined toward the blessing of those creatures. Therefore, they attribute to Him the name and the office of both "Destroyer" and "Preserver." Do we not also see that this spirit, creating and working all things, is the author of both corruption and generation? In corruption, the form is taken away and the thing is destroyed—and what can happen to a creature more grave than death and the deprivation of life? Yet in generation, it acts in the opposite way, namely by adding and preserving the nourishment of life, and not destroying it at all.

Hence it was that the mystic poets, who were well-versed in the deep mystery of nature—namely Orpheus, Hesiod, Euripides, Aeschylus, etc. (with whom Proclus <note>A Greek Neoplatonist philosopher who influenced medieval theology</note> also seems to agree)—called **GOD** by the name **Apollo** or **Phoebus** during the day. They say he carries grace in his right hand and a bow in his left. Yet they call Him **Dionysus** during the nighttime, whom they say tears things apart, and even himself, into seven pieces. Then, in the daytime state (insofar as he is called Apollo), he is said to assemble again those things which he tore apart at night. For this reason, he is called the leader of the <term>Septenary</term> number <note>The number seven, considered by ancients to represent the harmony of the universe</note>, which results from the unity, the dual, and the quaternary added together. From this arises the <term>Diapason</term> <note>The interval of an octave, representing perfect musical harmony</note>, which is perfect harmony. Thus, the Septenary number is attributed to him insofar as he is the author of life and also of dissolution. These are composed of the first odd number, namely three, and the first even number, which is four. For the number two is called the "number of confusion" by the Pythagoreans. From the even and odd number or proportion—as if from the passive and the active—all things are generated, and they are also dissolved by that same path. But generation comes from the supernal light, which partakes of the number three, while corruption belongs to the lower regions and the "tearing night." In this act, he is called Dionysus the Tearer, and in the daytime, Apollo the Uniter, for by his presence all evils are scattered. For this reason, he was called *Appellin* <note>original: "Appellin" - a wordplay on the Greek 'apellere', meaning to drive away</note> instead of Apollo by the ancients. And the Athenians called him *Alexicacon* <note>original: "Alexicacon" - literally 'Averter of Evil'</note>, that is, the scatterer and repeller of evil; and by Homer he was called *Paion* <note>The text reads "Plion," likely a transcription error for "Paean," the physician of the gods</note>, that is, the author of health, since by his unity all things are preserved in perfect consonance. But as he undergoes division, he is referred to the even number and is the God of darkness, deprivation, and destruction. It is in this sense that David seems to speak:

> *You take away their spirit, and all things fail and return to their own nature. But we also read it written more clearly by him: When God sends forth his spirit, the creatures are recreated; when he hides his face, they are troubled; when he takes back their spirit, they expire and return to their dust. Psalm 104:29-30.*

From these things, therefore, we see that it was the opinion of the Pagans that the same God, in respect to contrary properties (namely severity and mercy), was sometimes the Prince of Darkness, destroying all things, and sometimes the Prince and Commander of Light, generating and quickening all things. But in the resolution of this doubt of ours, I most willingly submit myself to the most learned theologians of this age. Indeed, I would not have cast myself headlong into the sea of such a controversy, unless the necessity of rendering an account of the subject at hand—namely the Cabalistic Sephirot and the two contrary properties contained within them—had compelled me. But now I shall hasten with a light step to the history of the Angels who hold offices concerning the Sephirotic influences.

Sect. I, Port. IV, Part. II. Lib. IV. Membr. II.

# CHAPTER VII.

## On the Angels of the Sephiroth, and especially on that great and imperial Angel of light called Metatron, and then afterwards on that great Angel of darkness, who is opposed to him in nature and disposition.

From the dual arrangement of the divine properties poured out from the Sephirothic <note>The Sephiroth are the ten attributes or "emanations" in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself</note> parts, two orders of Angels arise, opposed in nature and condition. One of these is occupied with beneficence, while the other deals with malice toward the human race, which is the goal of creation. This is the foundation upon which those philosophers stood who placed two principal powers in the world, namely strife and friendship; the latter of these reconciles things, while the former disperses them. Hence it happened that, according to the intention of the Poets, just as it was the role of Apollo to compose and unite with the bonds of harmony, so it was the property of Dionysus to destroy what was composed through the antipathy of discord and to scatter what was united. And yet, both Apollo and Dionysus represented nothing but a single essence of divinity, emitting the operation of its acts in a dual form according to its will—namely, either in clemency and piety, or in its severity and indignation toward creatures. For just as we see in the same fire—unchanged in both form and quality—a nature both beneficent and life-giving, as well as destructive and harmful (inasmuch as it tends to burn if a combustible thing is brought too near, yet from a distance it warms an animal creature sweetly and kindly), so God acts either kindly or destructively regarding these things, always remaining the same and immovable according to the various modes of his rays or emanation to be sent forth, according to his will and pleasure.

For this reason, therefore (insofar as he is accustomed to act immediately through his angelic ministers, who are called the intermediaries between God and creatures), he created and made them as vessels fit for receiving his flows—some benevolent, and others malevolent and tending toward severity. It follows, then, that in respect to these two properties, some angels are called good, others evil; some friends of men, others enemies; some preservers, others exterminators, wasters, and destroyers; some of life and health, and again others of death and diseases. But truly, since all angels whatsoever, insofar as they are intelligences, terminate in the one spiritual Christ <note>Fludd identifies the "Spiritual Christ" with the Logos or the universal soul of the world</note> as the royal, greatest, and primary angel, who contains the nature of both the angels and **GOD** within himself, in whom also all things terminate (for from him, in him, and through him are all things, as the Apostle and Plato in his letters say), so those skilled in the hidden Theosophy <note>Divine wisdom</note> called this Messiah of the world the good, royal, and greatest angel, predominating over the others. He primarily receives his flows of life and essence from *Ehieh* <note>Hebrew: "I Am," the name of God associated with the highest Sephirah</note>, and directs them through the *Cheter* <note>Kether, meaning "Crown," the first Sephirah</note> or crown into the *Primum Mobile* <note>The "First Moved" sphere, the outermost sphere of the universe in traditional cosmology</note>, from which he then imparts motion, act, and existence to both celestial and inferior creatures—indeed, even to the demons and spirits wandering everywhere through the world. <margin>☩</margin> The Cabalists <note>Mystics following the Jewish tradition of scriptural interpretation</note> considered this primary Angel to be the Angel of Christ, as will be explained more widely below, whom others have also called Michael, the one presiding over the Sun itself. But since it may seem uncertain to the reader how the wise understood one for the other and accepted them without folly, we shall briefly reveal our opinion on this matter. They called this great Angel *Mitattron* <note>Metatron, often described in mystical texts as the "Prince of the Countenance" or the celestial scribe</note> insofar as he was the first emanation of the life and existence of the world, by whose presence all things in the cavity of the world are illuminated, and the darkness is driven toward the center. And as an emanation or beneficent flow of this kind was made from the first Sephirah *Cheter* or crown, he is therefore related to the guardianship, office, and indeed the existence of the greatest angel, **Metatron**. But truly, insofar as this primary light was so dilated through the mundane spirit and, on the fourth day of creation, was contracted into the mass of the Sun by the power of the influx of *Tiphereth* <note>The sixth Sephirah, "Beauty," often associated with the Sun and harmony</note>, so this great name Metatron passes into that of Michael, as will be discussed more widely below, so that in this the Cabalists seem not to have wandered far from the truth. Therefore, I have proposed to speak significantly in this place concerning the imperial virtue of such a great angel considered under both names, since he is the great distributor of life, form, and existence both to the world and its creatures, and especially to man; the cherisher and sustainer of souls, the nourishing favorer of health and salvation, and the benevolent author of position and generation; and insofar as he is opposed by the malevolent prince of this world, who is contrary to him in all things by nature and condition, being the destroyer of life, the enemy of health, and the leader and author of privation and death, as in the following chapter.

The nobility of this angel with respect to his primary lineage is so great, and the dignity with respect to his office so great, that he is considered prior not only to every creature in origin and place, but also superior to all spirits of his kind in position and duty, and richer in gifts. As for what pertains to his origin and lineage, he is said to be Wisdom herself, who came forth from the mouth of the Most High before all things. *Wisdom was created before all things (says the Wise Man), and the understanding of prudence from everlasting; the source of wisdom is the word of GOD on high, etc. Ecclesiasticus 1:4–5.* <note>original Latin: "Prior omnium... creata est sapientia, & intellectus prudentiae ab auo, fons sapientiae verbum DEI in excelsis"</note> For when the will existed, he immediately flowed out through the bright gate of *Cheter* or crown,

...the **crown** <note>original: "corona"; referring to the Sephirah Kether, the highest point of the divine emanations</note>, that primary emanation, by whose power all things were brought from nothingness into being and actuality in the blink of an eye; and this very emanation is called **Wisdom** <note>original: "sapientia"; referring to the Sephirah Chokmah</note>, from which later a second outflow issued through the "bright gate" <note>likely referring to the Sephirah Tiphereth, often called the gateway of light</note> directly from the secret bosom of the Almighty. But the Wise Man <note>referring to the author of the Book of Wisdom in the Apocrypha</note> also seems to confirm this elsewhere, saying: *Wisdom is a pure emanation or flow of the brightness of almighty God, or the splendor and whiteness of eternal light. Wisdom 7.* And from this it follows that this God-like Angel, that emanation or flow of divine majesty, is taken for the spiritual **Christ**, as mentioned before; inasmuch as the angels—as if he were their king, who contains and embraces the nature of both angels and of God—are finalized in him, in whom all other things exist. 

Hence it is that the Kabbalists say the angel **Metattron** <note>Metatron is the highest angel in Jewish mystical tradition, often described as the celestial scribe or the "Prince of the Countenance"</note> is the **Prince of Faces**, because he is the mediator who introduces souls before the face of God; this is the office of the spiritual Christ himself, who is the true Wisdom, which proceeded first from the mouth of the Father like a son. And the Prophet seems to understand this Angel when he says: *And his name shall be called the Angel of Great Counsel, Isaiah 9* <note>The text cites "Esa. 6" but the "Angel of Great Counsel" phrase is famously from the Septuagint version of Isaiah 9:6</note>; for in this respect, this angel is seen to be taken for Christ in many places of the Sacred Scriptures. 

Therefore, the more secret Theologians hold this to be the angel under whose guardianship God committed Moses and the Israelites, to lead them through the desert, in whom the name of **Jehovah** was present. They say he has dominion in the world no differently than the Mind (which is the Intellect) is said to rule in the human spirit. To this point regarding his power—namely, his expanded and universal authority—a certain man profound in occult **Theosophy** <note>Theosophy here refers to divine wisdom or the study of God's inner workings</note> breaks out into these words: *First among all is that great spirit, who governs the immense and most widely extended water which is called "heaven," and preserves it in his essence, and marvelously grants motion to all growing and living things.* Thus he spoke. 

And this is the reason that he is held by the Platonists and other wise men to be the **Soul of the World** <note>original: "anima mundi"; the concept of an animating spirit that permeates all nature</note>, which the Kabbalists understood by the **green line** <note>original: "lineam viridem"; in Kabbalah, this "line" often refers to a boundary or the "Tohu" that surrounds the world</note>, which is said to encircle the entire spirit of the world. From this, some would have it that this Angel **Metattron** is the final **Middah** <note>term: Midah (plural Middot); a Hebrew word meaning "attribute" or "measure," used to describe the Sephiroth</note> or property of the Archetypal world, which is called by others **Cheter Elion** <note>term: Kether Elyon; Hebrew for "Supreme Crown," the highest Sephirah</note>, that is, the supreme crown. Hence, **Metattron** has for its meaning "The Gift of God": for the life and form of the world was the greatest of God's gifts, which includes all other gifts. Therefore, all those more skilled in mystical Philosophy seem to fall into this opinion, agreeing with the saying of Ecclesiasticus: that just as this Metattron (or this Soul of the World) is the first thing created among all creatures, so he is said to contain in himself the perfection of all creatures, since they are accustomed to receive their forms from him as from a universal fountain. 

And this is the reason why this Angel **Metattron** is said by Rabbi Moses <note>likely referring to Moses Maimonides</note> to be the Prefect of the Universe, or the primary **Agent Intellect**, from whom all forms flow, and consequently by whom all singular virtues in the world—and especially human ones—are governed. **Rabbi Bereshit** <note>likely a reference to the author of Bereshit Rabbah or a similar midrashic commentary</note> called all these virtues "angels," and others called them "forms." Those who wish the mystery of the Angels (concreated with natural things) to be contained under the common name of **Michael**—as a name for the angelic species—seem to suggest the same thing, by which we are taught that all angels are of the same species. 

We say, therefore, that whether the angel be **Metattron** or **Michael**, he is nothing other than the white and pure emanation or power of God, which we previously called **Wisdom**, clothed as if in a garment by the worldly spirit illuminated by his presence. This is held by the Kabbalists to be the power of the **Tetragrammaton** <note>term: Tetragrammaton; the four-letter holy name of God (Y-H-W-H)</note> involved in the worldly spirit from the world's origin, not otherwise than the Messiah himself was led about in the middle age of the world. Hence it is that Metattron is called an "Angel" insofar as there is "otherness"—that is, from the created worldly spirit as something external, and the uncreated divine spirit (the pure clarity of God or the emanation of clarity) which is his internal part, present everywhere in the world, filling, permeating, and producing all things, as it is the **Word of God** creating all. And for this reason, he is held by the more secret Theologians to be the spiritual Christ, or the Messiah, or the power of the Tetragrammaton, as said before. This is what the wise man in Ecclesiasticus understood when he said that Wisdom was created before all things—that is, mixed into the worldly spirit in the manner of a creature. In this state, expanded everywhere, he established the heaven with its regions and the earth, gave them life, and brought them into being; and this occurred in the first three days of creation, according to the opinion of Moses. Wherefore we also have it written by the royal Psalmist: *By the Word of the Lord the heavens were established (and elsewhere: by His wisdom), and all their power by the spirit from His mouth.*

When the third day was completed, **Metattron** (whom for the aforesaid reasons the Platonists called the Soul of the World) contracted his rays, which were dispersed everywhere, into one polished mass of the world—namely, into the **Sun**. This was done by the divine outflow of **En Soph** <note>term: Ein Sof; the Infinite, the unknowable Godhead before emanation</note> (or Infinity) working through the gate of **Triphereth** <note>term: Tiphereth; the Sephirah representing Beauty, Harmony, and the Sun</note>. This is according to that saying of the royal Psalmist: *He set his Tabernacle in the sun.* Therefore, just as Metattron now somewhat changed his quality, so also the name **Michael** was given to him, as was related before—as if one had said, "Who is like God?" arguing from this that he is God himself putting on a garment of light, who animates the sun. For this reason, the sun is called the father of life and multiplication. Hence also God was said by David to be *clothed in light as with a garment*; in which respect he is sometimes called an "angel," and sometimes **Jehovah**. Jehovah himself gave the reason for this, saying: *Behold, I send my angel before you; do not provoke him, for my name is in him.* For all Kabbalists agree on this: that this angel was Metattron or Michael. #### Section I. Portal IV. Part II. Book IV. Member II.

We observe that its property was to animate the entire mundane spirit, to arrange the regions of the heavens and the elements according to the design of the **Archetype** <note>The "Archetype" refers to the original divine blueprint or the mind of God from which all creation is modeled</note>, and to dispose them in harmonious peace. Thus, after three days had passed, it chose a denser **tabernacle** <note>original: "tabernaculum"; here referring to the Sun as a dwelling place for the divine light</note>, from which it might more easily look upon elemental creatures—namely animals, as well as plants and minerals—and rain down the gifts of quickening, germination, and generation upon them. Similarly, the structures of the entire world which **Metattron** created in the beginning, **Michael** intends to preserve until the very end, just as he looks after the things created after the fourth day. Therefore, we see that both **Metattron** and **Michael** agree as one—namely in the nobility of their lineage, as they proceed from the mouth of the Most High, and in their office and duty, namely in the quickening of the world and the distribution and preservation of souls or forms. Furthermore, just as it is the duty of the angel **Metattron** to introduce souls (as the occult theologians maintain) before the face of God—whence he is called the **Prince of Faces**—so too is it the duty of **Michael** (as the Archangel <note>Likely referring to the Archangel in the writings of Pico della Mirandola</note> has it in the *Commentary on Kabbalistic Dogma*) to offer souls in heaven. For he says:

> *Michael is the high priest, sacrificing the immaculate souls of men to the blessed God in the upper world;* <note>original: "Michael est sacerdos magnus, sacrificans in mundo superiori animas hominum immaculatas Deo benedicto"</note>

And elsewhere it says:

> *Michael performs a perpetual priesthood in heaven as the great priest of God;* <note>original: "Fungitur perpetuo Michael sacerdotio in cælo tanquam magnus Dei sacerdos"</note>

For just as a high priest on earth offers the souls of animals to GOD, so **Michael**, the spiritual Priest, offers rational souls to Him in heaven. By the same reasoning, **Metattron** is said to have been the guide of **Moses**, through whose mediation it is handed down that Moses achieved the grace of speaking with GOD face to face, as mentioned above:

> *I speak to him mouth to mouth,* <note>original: "Ore ad os loquor ei"; a reference to Numbers 12:8 where Jehovah speaks to Aaron and Miriam regarding Moses</note> says Jehovah.

Finally, just as it was the duty of the great Angel **Metattron** to drive back the darkness, to strike down the horrific shadows, and to cast everything impure out of heaven into the earthly abyss, so too is **Michael**, that great angel, said to fight for the souls of all against the ancient serpent, who continually seeks to devour them. In this battle, having cast the Dragon out of heaven, **Michael** prevailed; he reigns and flashes in glory in heaven, and he always holds the dragon, or the prince of darkness, under his command and authority. Therefore, we read in Daniel that **Michael** is always helping the people of God. The words are as follows: *Michael, the great Prince who stands for the children of your people, that is, for the elect.* **Daniel 12.** Led by these and other points, philosophers skilled in the divine mysteries teach that the angel **Michael** is that same one who is **Metattron**, and that **Michael** (whom the Kabbalists make the guardian of the **Sephirah Tiphereth** <note>term: Sephirah Tiphereth; the sixth emanation on the Kabbalistic Tree of Life, representing Beauty, Balance, and the Heart</note>) is the great angel of **Christ**, the **Messiah of the World**, or the power of the **Tetragrammaton** <note>term: Tetragrammaton; the sacred four-letter name of God (YHWH)</note>, the Soul of the World, and the fountain of light and life. He not only gives life to both celestial and earthly creatures but also preserves and defends their lives against the Prince of Darkness. 

But we also have all this confirmed from the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation</note>, namely that this Angel is the spiritual **Christ** and the **Messiah** of the entire world, or the Word of God, which, according to John, is the light of the world, from which all things were made and without which nothing was made, as in it is life, etc. **John 1.** For first, we read that John himself, caught up in the spirit, proclaimed and sounded forth with a loud voice as if from a trumpet:

> *I am the Alpha and the Omega, the Beginning and the End; who was like the son of man, whose eyes were like a flame of fire, and his feet like the purest molten brass glowing in a furnace; his belt was gold, and in his right hand he held seven stars; his face shone like the sun, and his voice was like the murmur of many waters, etc.* **Apoc. 1.**

By these words, that thrice-great Angel **Michael** seems to be most clearly and plainly described. According to **Trithemius** <note>Johannes Trithemius (1462–1516), a German abbot, polymath, and occultist</note> and others most well-versed in true magic, Michael is the prefect and leader of the celestial sun, who placed his seat and **Tabernacle** in the sun. This is also declared by his appearance, which is most similar to the sun; for just as a man's face claims its place in his upper part, while his feet rest on the earth, so indeed this Angel's face is likened to the sun in heaven, while his feet are likened to brass glowing and flashing in a furnace, thereby signaling the solar rays that strike the earth and the elemental region everywhere. 

And just as we observe the sun to be the lord and, as it were, the emperor of the whole sky, giving life and light not only to its own spirit but also to all its stars—which are said by the more eminent philosophers to have received their luminous power and their act of existence and essence from it, not unlike an earthly Emperor who grants dignity and the power of acting to the rulers, princes, or magistrates subject to him—so indeed we see here that this imperial angel, bearing a solar figure in his countenance, holds seven stars in his right hand. By this, John seems to signify that the seven stars and the Angels presiding over them are under his power. For as the material Sun is accustomed to impart its light and power to the other stars, so indeed **Michael**, who is the spiritual or internal Sun in heaven, is accustomed to attribute power and lucid vigor to the other seven angels, as he is superior to them in office and order. For **Dionysius**, **Basil**, **Origen**, and others testify that Angels of a superior order receive light more abundantly than inferior ones, and they also admit that inferior ones receive their light and power from the superior ones by way of influence. Therefore, it is clear that this Angel is the most powerful of all in heaven. For this reason, secret Theosophists say (as has already been mentioned) that the mystery of the angels created together with natural things is encompassed under the common name **Michael**, as the designation for the angelic species. By this (they say), we are taught that all angels are of the same species, but individual bodies, whether celestial or earthly, have their own rulers of virtues and prefects of operations. These are their words. But that **Michael** is a great Prince, and more eminent in place and dignity than the other 57 angels, is clear from these passages of Holy Scripture: *Michael...*

"The great Prince," (says Daniel) "who stands for the children of your people," <note>original: "Princeps magnus, qui ſtat pro filiis populi tui"</note> Daniel 10:13. And elsewhere the Angel Gabriel said, "Behold, Michael, one of the chief Princes, came to help me by fighting for the people." And that this great Prince is the Superintendent leader in the heavenly militia, John narrates in these words: "And there was a great battle in heaven: Michael and his angels fought with the dragon; and the dragon fought and his angels," Revelation 12:7. By this discourse it is indicated that Michael is not only the primary leader in the heavenly militia, but also that he is a confessed friend to men and to the life and health of mortals—inasmuch as he is the most direct adversary of the Dragon, or Satan, or the Devil—and consequently the author of life and health. This is in contrast to the Devil, who is the public enemy of life and health, and is therefore called the "destroyer," "waster," and "exterminator" <note>original: "deſtructor, atq; vaſtator atq; exterminator"</note> in the Holy Scriptures.

But since Michael triumphed over him and gained the victory with his angels, the Dragon or Devil is subjected to him with all his company. Thus, he and his angels are made subject and obedient to Michael and his angels, so that they cannot exceed his command by even a hair's breadth. This we have confirmed from the Holy Scriptures: "I saw," (says John) "four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth, so that they should not blow on the earth, or on the sea, or on any tree. And I saw another Angel ascending from the East, who had the seal of the LIVING GOD, and he cried with a loud voice to the four angels to whom it was given to hurt the earth and the sea, saying: 'Hurt not the earth, nor the sea, nor the trees, until we have sealed the servants of GOD in their foreheads,'" etc. Revelation 7. From these things it is quite clear that by the Angel ascending from the rising of the sun, Michael is understood; for to his custody is assigned the Eastern region of the world, as was demonstrated before. Furthermore, he is the prefect of the Sun, to whom the eastern corner is also attributed. 

Finally, he is that great Leader in the militia of GOD, who subjected the Dragon or Satan and his followers to his dominion. This obedience of the harmful angels is declared in this: that he said, "Hurt not the earth," etc., and they made themselves obedient in a moment. Lastly, Michael is the keeper of the seal of the great GOD; he is called by the **Cabalists** <note>Followers of Kabbalah, a school of Jewish mysticism</note> not only **Cohegadol** <note>Hebrew: Kohen HaGadol, meaning "High Priest"</note>, that is, the Great Priest of GOD, but also the vice-regent of the Supreme, whose name, seal, and office he possesses. For, as someone very learned in divine mysteries says: "Michael" signifies nothing else than "Who is like unto God?" as mentioned before. Moreover, Jehovah himself proclaimed that His great name was in him. Furthermore, that he is the High Priest who is accustomed to offer the prayers of the saints to GOD Himself, he seems to declare in these words: "Another Angel stood before the altar, having a golden censer in his hand; and there was given unto him much incense, that he should offer it with the prayers of all saints upon the golden altar which was before the throne. And the smoke of the incense, which came with the prayers of the saints, ascended up before God out of the angel's hand," etc. Revelation 8 <note>The text incorrectly cites Rev 7 here.</note>.

Finally, those more skilled in **divine magic** <note>The study of spiritual hierarchies and their roles in the cosmos</note> maintain that the seven angels who preside over the seven planets are those seven angels who are said to stand before GOD: namely **Zaphkiel** or **Oriphiel**, the angel of Saturn; **Zadkiel** or **Zachariel** of Jupiter; **Samael** of Mars; **Michael** of the Sun; **Anael** of Venus; **Raphael** of Mercury; and **Gabriel** of the Moon. Concerning these, the Holy Scripture makes mention both in general and in specific: "And I saw," (it says) "the seven Angels who stood before God, and to them were given seven trumpets," Revelation 8. And elsewhere: "I am Raphael, one of the seven angels who stand before Jehovah," Tobit 12:15. And elsewhere: "I am Gabriel, the Angel who stands before God, and am sent to speak to thee," Luke 1:19. And elsewhere: "Behold, Michael, one of the Princes, came to help." Here, therefore, we have the great gift of God—namely the bearer of divine light (the effects of which are life, generation, and health) in this world. Just as he obtained victory over the rebellious troop of the Devil, so he inclines God Himself toward granting lives and forms, and consequently toward being more prone to mercy and clemency than to punishment, severity, and indignation. However, it is certain and justified by Holy Scripture that God uses the Devil and his angels as ministers in His severity, just as He uses Michael and his followers in His clemency. We thus descend to a brief description of the prince of malice, death, and sickness.
