### CHAPTER IX

->**On the evil Angel created by God, whom He uses along with his associates in His severity and wrath.**<-

Just as it belonged to the Creator of the world, through the efflux of His **denary** <note>The number ten, often representing perfection or the completion of a cycle in mystical thought</note> from the gates of light, to act as severely with the world on account of man's sin as He acts mercifully in His grace; so indeed it pleased Him to procreate two leaders of angels most opposite in nature and condition. One of these contends and fights with the other for the safety and conservation of souls, lives, and things created and generated. This Prince, who has innumerable angels subject to him and agreeing with his nature in goodness, we have called **Metattron** or the great Angel Michael, of whom we have spoken so many words in the preceding chapter. The other, however, strenuously resists the impulse of the Archangel, and with every effort seeks to try by what violence and what snares he may bring open war upon the creatures made by God—and especially upon the human race—or produce fatal effects in the world for the ruin of man. Whence it is that Michael is the preserver and helper of lives and bodies, the promoter of nature and generation, and the diligent intercessor for souls before God,

<meta>This page continues the contrast between the celestial and infernal hierarchies. Sect. I. Port. IV. Part. II. Lib. IV. Membr. II.

Thus indeed, Satan, or the dragon—against whom we read Michael acted manfully and with triumph in war—is the devastator of lives, the exterminator, the open enemy of salvation, the foe of generation, and the constant accuser and slanderer of souls before God. From this it is clear that just as Michael is observed in his condition to be most full of piety, goodness, and affability toward men, so on the opposite side Satan abounds in all iniquity, malice, and cruelty against the human race. In the execution of his most wicked will, he has many legions of evil demons under him, all of whom are said to be most ready to perpetrate every kind of crime. He also has under his dominion, or in his army, leaders and standard-bearers, imitating in this business of his the government and disposition of God the Best and Greatest, whose seat and place he dared to usurp (carried away by violent ambition). Therefore, just as four standard-bearers are counted in the army of God—namely Michael, Gabriel, Raphael, and Uriel—so in the army of Satan, the avengers Samael, Azazel, Azael, and Mahazael carry the widest sails <note>The author uses a nautical metaphor ("wide sails") to describe the reach and influence of these demonic leaders.</note>. Under them are gathered great crowds of demons and the legions of Tartarus <note>original: "tartari"; referring to the deepest abyss of the underworld.</note>, all fugitives and outcasts, having their portion from the scapegoat <note>original: "capra emissoria"; a reference to the ritual of Leviticus 16, here associated with demonic exile.</note>. But leaving aside these particular angels, I shall now chiefly turn the thread of my discourse to their Emperor, the Prince who is supreme in malice and in the office of violence and iniquity.

Many names have been imposed upon this head and leader of malignant spirits by the Sacred Scriptures, encompassing great hidden mysteries concerning his condition. In the first place, he was called ***Lucifer***; for such was he made in his origin by the Creator—namely, clearer and more splendid than the other angels, as Gregory <note>Likely referring to Pope Gregory the Great (c. 540–604 AD), a major authority on the hierarchy of angels.</note> seems to assert. For this reason, he is said to have surpassed the other angels in dignity and power, but at last, puffed up by pride and ambition, he is said to have lost his beauty and brightness, and for this reason to have put on a foul and dark appearance, and thus he was cast down from heaven. The Prophet describes this in plain words: *How you have fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, who rose in the morning! You have fallen to the earth, you who did wound the nations, who said in your heart: "I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God, I will sit on the mountain of the covenant, on the sides of the North; I will ascend above the height of the clouds, I will be like the Most High." Isaiah 14:12.* <note>original: "Quomodo cecidisti de cælo Lucifer..."</note> And the Book of Revelation clearly indicates the manner of this expulsion after his change from a bright to a dark disposition: *A great red dragon, his tail drew a third part of the stars of heaven and sent them to the earth. Michael and his angels fought with the Dragon, and the dragon fought, and his angels; and they prevailed not, neither was their place found any more in heaven. That great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, who is called the Devil and Satan, who seduces the whole world; and he was cast unto the earth, and his angels were thrown down with him. And a loud voice was heard in heaven saying: "Now is come salvation and strength, and the kingdom of our God and the power of his Christ, because the accuser of our brethren is cast out, who accused them before the sight of God day and night," etc. Therefore rejoice, O heavens, and you that dwell in them; woe to the earth and to the sea, because the devil is come down unto you, having great wrath,* etc. *Revelation 12.* <note>original: "Draco magnus rufus..."</note> In this discourse, John best describes, first, the dark and foul disposition of Lucifer once he was intoxicated by pride, whence he assigns him the name of Dragon and Serpent (which of all animals in the world are the most hostile to the human race).

Then he describes the manner by which he was cast out of heaven, namely, by the unconquered pursuit of the great Angel Michael. Furthermore, his tumultuous restlessness is noted in that the heavens and all their inhabitants were filled with wonderful joy because of the exile of such a rebellious and dangerous enemy. Finally, the misery of the earth, water, and the other elements, and their inexplicable calamity, is judged to be because of the presence of this implacable Dragon, who with his spirits circles the earth and seas, greedily and constantly seeking whom he may devour. A certain unknown author, yet one very deep in the mysteries of creation, seems to explain the whole history of Lucifer—both in his happiness while he was good and his unhappiness when he was turned to evil—in this manner, as we have found it expressed in a certain old manuscript:

> God created the air from the dust of the first matter <note>term: "first matter" (original: "prima materia") - the formless, chaotic substance from which all things were created in ancient and alchemical philosophy.</note>, both good and evil in the same or equal quantity of weight in all places. It was created eternal by the perfect and uncreated God. And from the bright air, God created Lucifer with his companions or fellowship, so that he himself was a certain shining air, and brighter than the rest of the air, and that light shone where Lucifer was. Thus, all the darkness of the evil air was created or rendered good and bright without sin, and for that reason, in the beginning, evil was restrained, or subdued, or corrected under the good; for indeed evil air can best be corrected and mended by good air. But truly, that did not happen in Lucifer and in his fellowship; for when that Angel Lucifer saw that it would come to pass that the light hidden in the first matter of the waters would shine and be separated and raised above the angelic creatures, he was then inflamed with hatred and envy against the human creature. And then that dark air, which was hiding in the bright air, went forth and opened itself in Lucifer, and that dark and impure air overcame and conquered that bright and pure air. Thus, therefore, in the beginning, this angel Lucifer was offended. For when he saw the Holy Trinity painting and sketching a certain bright mirror, he wondered whom it concerned; for there was formed a kind of circle surrounding this most Holy Trinity on every side, in which was the Sun of that bright mirror, containing in itself all the virtues of the Trinity itself. Therefore he thought to himself: "If God has all these remarkable virtues enclosed within Himself, surely I, Lucifer, on the opposite side, have all great vices in me, and so I am not inferior to Him by that which is contained in me. ### On the Efficient Cause of Atmospheric Phenomena <note>original: "De Causa Meteororum Efficiente." In this period, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, including wind, rain, and lightning, rather than just space rocks.</note>

...and established him in his place; for he is God and flees my malice. Thus Lucifer, by an entirely free will, conceived of or introduced vices, and therefore even then fell from there through all the choirs of Angels with all his companions. For the heavens could no longer hold him, as they rightly recognized him along with all his associates who favored or adhered to him. Lucifer and his companions were ignorant of the strength or power of divine omnipotence, from which nothing at all remains hidden; likewise, they did not know that all things are compelled to serve and be subject to God—namely, the good and the bad alike—for no forces prevail against Him. In this manner, therefore, the first sin was produced and committed in heaven. 

Nevertheless, GOD had created Lucifer without sin, with a clear and pure air; but sin was a "dark air." For Lucifer and his company fashioned from the elements of the air—which were impure and mixed with the clear and pure elements of the air—an impure air that covered, subdued, and restrained them. But Lucifer, of his own accord and through his free will, produced and, as it were, brought forth into the light the impure air of sin while he was still in heaven. For Lucifer was the impurity of the air, and heaven was purged as soon as Lucifer and his company were excluded and cast out from it. Lucifer fell before Adam was created. 

Thus says that author <note>original: "Hæc ille"; a standard phrase indicating the end of a cited passage.</note>. In this history of Lucifer (which this Author undoubtedly saw inscribed in the secret and mystical book of nature and observed in the new creation), he clearly denotes that Lucifer was established from both clear and dark air together. He suggests that his pure air was his external part, shimmering with a wonderful brightness, which so illuminated and tempered the wicked or dark air that the whole of Lucifer, as created by God, was originally good and devoid of sin. Truly, however, his malice and envy were the cause that his hidden darkness gradually overcame his external Light, and thus he obscured his external self with his own shadows, repressed it, and darkened it everywhere in a manifest way with dark air. 

Because of this sin, he was banished into exile from that place of light, by the mediation of the spirits of light, into a place of darkness—namely, into this very air. Hence, while he was previously called *Lucifer* <note>"Light-bringer"</note> because of his clarity and was exalted in dignity above all the bright angels, he is now called by some *Lucifugus* <note>"Light-fleer"</note>—that is, one who flees the light of God and the good angels. Nevertheless, in this light of shadows, he holds empire over all the angels of his company. For this reason, he is called by the Apostle in one place the *prince of the power of this air, who works in the children of disobedience (Ephesians 2:2)*. And elsewhere, the *Prince, power, and lord of the darkness, the spirit of malice under heaven (Ephesians 6)*. 

John, in the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation</note>, called this Prince the *great and red dragon, the ancient serpent, because of his poisonous nature and subtlety (Revelation 12)*; the *Devil*, as if rushing downward; and *Satan*, as if a contrary one or an adversary. Elsewhere he is called *Behemoth*, like an ox or a terrible beast in the likeness of an ox; and elsewhere *Leviathan*, signifying an "addition" or "apposition" *(Job 40)*. For, as Gregory <note>Pope Gregory the Great</note> holds, he is accustomed to add and, as it were, sew together evil to evil, sin to sin, and grief to grief. He is also called the *Accuser* <term>original: "criminator"</term>, whence it is written in the Apocalypse, *The accuser is cast down.* Furthermore, he is named the *Lion* because of his open and manifest violence; hence Peter says, *As a roaring Lion (1 Peter 5)*. In the Apocalypse, he is called *Apollyon*—that is, the Destroyer or Devastator—for not only does he attempt to destroy men and other creatures, but he also tries to turn virtues into vices. Hence we also read what is written in the Prophet Isaiah:

> *Behold, I have created the smith that bloweth the coals in the fire, and that bringeth forth an instrument for his work; and I have created the waster to destroy. No weapon that is formed against thee shall prosper; and every tongue that shall rise against thee in judgment thou shalt condemn. This is the heritage of the servants of the Lord, etc. (Isaiah 54:16-17)*

By these words, the Prophet clearly teaches that the Devil was expressly created by God to lead men into error and to make them sin, so that he might afterward destroy them. For this reason, he calls him a "smith blowing the coals of fire" and "bringing forth his vessel." Just as a blacksmith, by means of fire, is accustomed to shape and adapt iron for his purpose into this or that form—so that he may more easily perfect the work he proposed to do—so indeed the Devil is accustomed to prepare his instruments, both for deceiving the human spirit with flattering whispers and, in an open manner, for harming the bodies of men and other creatures. It is for this reason that he sometimes stirs up the winds to injure and destroy men and beasts. Hence it is written in Job:

> *suddenly a vehement wind rushed from the region of the desert, and shook the four corners of the house, and falling, it crushed his children (Job 1:19).*

Sometimes he calls forth fire from heaven and uses it to perpetrate his deadly deeds; whence we read in the same chapter, *the fire of GOD fell from heaven, and having touched the sheep and the servants, it consumed them (Job 1:16).* Sometimes he afflicts the body with sores and plagues; thus it is said *that Satan struck Job with a most grievous ulcer from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head (Job 2:7)*. Sometimes he stains the air with corruption and is accustomed to introduce pestilence to fulfill the pleasure of his creator. For we read in the prophecy of Habakkuk: *GOD shall come from the South, his glory covered the heavens, death shall go before his face, and the Devil shall go out before his feet (Habakkuk 3:3-5)*—or, the pestilence or wasting plague shall go before him at noon. 

From this it is clear that the Devil is a minister of God, always ready at His feet. He contaminates the air with plague, and in this specific property, he is called by the Hebrew Mages *Meriris*, or the demon burning at noon. Agrippa <note>Heinrich Cornelius Agrippa, a famous Renaissance philosopher and occultist.</note> says this is that great Prince of malice who is said by the Apostle to have power over the air of this world—that is, the sublunary air <term>The atmosphere between the Earth and the Moon</term>, which is a dark air and quite subject to changes compared to that empyrean or ethereal air, which is far clearer and purer. Sect. I. Port, IV. Part. II. Lib. IV. Membr. II.

In the same way that the internal man <note>The "internal man" refers to the soul or the spiritual essence of a human being.</note> is said to be made in the image of God and holds superintendence over all other things—just as the Sun is given the chief place in heaven as the highest and first in dignity among all planets—so the angel of the East, being dedicated to the sun and for this reason preferred in dignity and place over the others, is said to be Michael, who belongs to the side of mercy. The Archangel Raphael rules the region opposite to him and governs the spirit of that wind, namely the *Favonius* <note>The West Wind.</note>, just as Gabriel rules the Northern region and Uriel the Southern. 

We also find this same point confirmed among the Hebrew Teachers: For Rabbi Todros Levi <note>original: "Rabi Tædacus Leui"; likely referring to the 13th-century Kabbalist Todros ben Joseph Halevi Abulafia.</note> in his *Book on the 10 Numerations* <note>The ten Sefirot or divine emanations in Kabbalah.</note>, after explaining the four winds—North, South, East, and West—finally proceeds thus: *From those four winds He created four Angels who are set over them by day and by night. Then Gabriel, by the power of judgment and severity, is set over the North wind during the half of the night and two measures of the world; Noriel <note>Another name for Uriel.</note> presides over the South.* So says the Rabbi. 

Furthermore, each of these has beneath him an Angel of the nature of the "Prince of the Air," <note>A biblical term for the leader of the fallen spirits inhabiting the atmosphere.</note> each of whom has several species under him, which the *Book of Secrets* <note>likely referring to the *Sefer HaRazim*.</note> contains. This also seems to be confirmed by what is read in the *Porta Lucis* <note>original: "Porta lucis"; *The Gates of Light* by Joseph Gikatilla.</note>: *From the earth,* it says, *all the way to the firmament, there is no empty place, but everything is full of forms. Some of these are pure, capable of grace and mercy; but below there are many false, harmful, and tempting images, all dwelling and flying in the air. Some are for peace, some for war; some for good, some for evil; some for life, some for death; and consequently some for safety and health, and some for disease and infirmity. And all this is in the lower habitation in which we are,* as Joseph of Castalia <note>Joseph Gikatilla.</note> asserts. From this it is clear that good Angels are mixed with foul and evil ones, so that the actions of wicked demons (who hold God and men in ineffable hatred) may be tempered, repelled, and mitigated.

Bartholomew <note>likely Bartholomaeus Anglicus, author of a famous medieval encyclopedia.</note> seems to agree with our assertion when he speaks thus: *The entire effort of demons or wicked spirits is to do harm, and to disturb and infest men with malice. For this reason, they very often disturb the elements, stir up tempests in the air and water, and corrupt the fruits of the earth, as is explained in the Apocalypse; and they would bring far greater evils upon the inhabitants of the earth if the good Angels did not blunt the edge of their violence.* 

From this, therefore, it is clear that they can do nothing except by divine permission, as the good Angels act as their bridles. But once permission is given, the good Angels themselves not only cease from their protection, but are even accustomed to contribute to the punishment of creatures, as we read everywhere in the sacred scriptures. Concerning the protection of the good Angels against the assaults of the evil Angels, the Royal Psalmist <note>King David.</note> speaks thus: *Fear not the terror of the night, nor the arrow that flies by day, nor the plague that invades in the darkness, nor the assault of the noonday demon; no plague shall approach your tent, for He shall give His Angels charge over you in all your ways,* Psalm 91. By this speech, he clearly seems to intimate that God has ordained to defend good men from the assaults of wicked demons through angels whose natures are contrary to them. This was elegantly demonstrated through the protection of the Archangel Raphael in the story of Tobias, who, by repelling the assaults of the demon Asmodeus, preserved Tobias himself immune from his rage.

We conclude, therefore, that it is most certain that just as Lucifer (now called Satan) was made the universal Prince of this air after his fall and exile from heaven, according to the saying of St. Paul, his primary effect is from the South. This is the place from which rot is sent out, along with plagues, wasting diseases, and very often thunders. Hence, he was called *Meririm* by the Hebrews (as was declared before); that is, the demon burning and raging at noon. Or, as Habakkuk and the Royal Prophet say in the places cited before: the pestilence or the demon wasting at midday or in the South. 

Similarly, just as this Prince of the Air divides his aerial kingdom into four quarters—namely East, West, South, and North—and assigns a prefect to each part by divine command (whose duty it is to make the winds blow perversely), so great was the mercy toward the creatures in the sublunary heaven, and especially toward man, that in place of this Prince of great wrath and malice in the air or this world where we live, God placed a Prince even greater and full of grace and mercy. This Prince also has three other angels joined to him as companions, similar in property and goodness, who have power and authority over those spirits acting as Satan’s lieutenants, who have power over the winds. 

Hence, just as Meririm with his spirit is accustomed to rage in the South, so Michael the Great Prince, who has superintendence over Meririm, claims for himself the Eastern quarter of the world, in which he manages the actions of Samael (or as others say, *Oriens*), as has been said more often. For these are the words of Cornelius Agrippa in Book 3 of *Occult Philosophy*, chapter 24: *Among the evil spirits, four most powerful kings preside over the others according to the four parts of the world, whose names are Uriens (or Oriens), King of the East; Amaymon, King of the South; Paymon, King of the West; and Egyn, King of the North. The teachers of the Hebrews perhaps more rightly call them Samael, Azazel, Azael, and Mahazael, under whom many other princes and presidents rule, along with innumerable demons of private duties.* 

Thus he speaks. And yet, in his *Scale of the Number Four*, he says there are four Angels presiding over the corners of heaven: Michael in the East, Raphael in the West, Gabriel in the North, and Uriel in the South. He says there are four Prince demons harmful in the elements: Samael, Azazel, Azael, and Mahazael. And four are the Princes of demons over the four corners of the earth: Oriens, Paymon, Egyn, and Amaymon. From these, it is clear that this author is not consistent with himself, since he makes a distinction here between the four princes harmful in the elements and those over the four corners of the globe, who have the care of the winds

But to show our mind's opinion on this matter, we say indeed that it is more probable to consider that, since the entire sublunary <term>sublunary: the region of the universe below the moon, subject to change and decay</term> region is filled as much by the goodness of God as by the malice of the Devil, it seems likely that every element has its own good and likewise its own evil Prince. Both, clearly, are ministers of the divine character: for He uses the former for doing good in His mercy, and the latter for punishing and doing harm in His severity. Therefore we say that just as there are four good princes—*Seraph, Cherub, Tharsis, Ariel*—so indeed there are evil and vengeful ones—*Samael, Azazel, Mahazael* <note>These names are drawn from Kabbalistic traditions regarding the fallen angels or spirits of the wilderness</note>—in those same elements. And since the Winds share in the nature of the Elements—namely, the East Wind in fire, the North Wind in earth, the West Wind in water, and the South Wind in air—the elementary Spirits, both evil and good, receive their strengths from the Spirits of the winds, whether they blow for good or for ill. Hence it is certain that the East Wind <note>original: "Eurus"</note> shares as much in the heat as in the violence of Samael, and so it is with the others. We also affirm that the royal spirits on the side of Satan who have power over the Winds—namely *Oriens, Paymon, Ægyn, and Amaymon*—are subjected to the commands of those good angels who preside over the four corners of the world, namely *Michael, Raphael, Gabriel, and Uriel*. This is especially true of that imperial Angel of goodness and life, *Michael*, who has force and power over the Prince of darkness or of the dark air, because of the victory won over the Dragon; wherefore under his supreme command are all demons, both of the Winds and of the elements, whether they be good or evil.

Here it must also be considered in passing that according to the position of the gates in the Heavenly City (of which three were situated toward the east, three toward the west, and just as many toward the North and South), the matter also holds true with the winds. For in any given quarter of the world there are three winds: namely, the East Wind <note>original: "subsolanus"</note> with its two wings, the South Wind <note>original: "Auster"</note> toward the south, and the Northeast Wind <note>original: "Cæcias"</note> toward the North, and so with the others, as you have clearly depicted in the demonstration above. And since, in the likeness of the gates of the heavenly Jerusalem, you have the Zodiac of the starry sky divided—namely into four triplicities <term>triplicities: groups of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element</term>, the Fiery and Eastern, the Airy and Southern, the Watery and Western, and the Earthy and Northern—and to each of these triplicities three signs are assigned: namely Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius to fire; Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius to air; Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces to water; and finally Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn to earth. Similarly, because a proper prince of the Angelic nature is assigned to each triplicity, and a specific angel is likewise assigned to each sign under him, so indeed (as it seems to me) it is likely that not only is a Prince Angel ascribed to the cardinal point, but also to each wind-gate in that quarter, which ought to have a relation to its own sign, under whose power it falls. We have made mention of the demons of the triplicities and the peculiar spirits of each sign before, where we spoke of the demons of the Zodiac; we could indeed compile great volumes on this subject, but since we shall discourse more openly on these things elsewhere, we will not speak further of them in this place.

You have here, benevolent Readers, how clearly described and almost vividly depicted are the two great Princes of the intelligences, differing expressly in character and nature. The first, who is the most powerful of all, is the Angel of light: merciful, good, the author of health and life, the solace and rest of the world, the driver-away of death and diseases, who holds evil in hatred and fosters and nourishes good benevolently. We have declared him to be the dispenser of divine mercy, benevolence, and kindness, the guardian of souls and indeed of bodies; from his region come those good angels of men, whom we have called sacred and good. He is the author and agent of the world's salvation and human resurrection, as one who has obtained victory against the Devil and Death. But the other Prince is most opposite to him in condition and will; for as the Angel of darkness, he is accustomed to seethe with severity and impiety, delights in evil actions, is the author of diseases, pains, and destruction, the scourge and unrest of the world, the destroyer of life, and the introducer of death into the world, who holds good in hatred and fosters and nourishes evil strenuously. And we have declared him to be the dispenser of severity and malevolence—indeed, of universal impiety—the destroyer of souls and indeed of bodies; from his rule come those evil and wicked demons who are called "evil geniuses" <note>original: "mali genii"</note>. He is the author of the world's ruin and man's damnation. And so you see these two Angels are entirely contrary to each other in quality. Regarding these, therefore, we shall treat particularly in the following volume, where we shall discourse copiously on health and disease.

->Greatest and Best) to do so with a more polished and clearer thread of speech.<-

### Of Part II.

# THE THIRD MEMBER

## BOOK ONE.

->*On the celestial efficient cause of meteors, as the Astrologers say.*<-

### CHAPTER I.

->*Whether there is in truth any celestial efficient cause or not. That the cause of the idolatry of mortals is their ignorance, from which arise so many errors in the world, and so many judgments in divine severity justly issued against men.*<-

Since in the preceding sections it has been most aptly and clearly declared by us that it is God alone, who through His various emanations with various powers and properties works in various ways—both in the heavens and on the earth—by means of His Angelic organs <note>original: "organis Angelicis"; instruments or tools through which a higher power acts</note>; which organs we have said are those in which God primarily acts in this world; and since the other creatures of the world are merely the vehicles of the said Angels, it follows by consequence that it is a monstrous error among creatures to attribute any essential act in the world to mundane creatures—whether they be angelic, celestial and stellar, or finally elementary—and not to GOD alone. This is also lawful to gather from these passages of the Holy Scripture, for in it we read it written: *He ascended upon the Cherubim, and flew or glided upon the wings of the wind, and He placed darkness around Him as His hiding place, sifting the waters from the clouds of the heavens, and from His brightness He gave forth His voice, He sent His arrows, and the lightning scattered them, etc. 2 Kings 22:11-15.* <note>In the Latin Vulgate, 1 and 2 Samuel are titled 1 and 2 Kings; this passage is from David's song of praise</note> In this speech it is denoted that God is present first in the Cherubim Angels, in whom He sits as if in a vehicle, and then the Cherub flies (driven by divine light) upon the wings of the winds, and then that spirit in the Cherubim and the winds gathers the dense clouds, and then from them He emits His voice or His thunders, and also sifts the waters from the clouds of the heavens. It is not said that God sat upon the Cherubim, and the Cherub flew upon the wings of the wind, and the wind gathered the clouds, and the stars—and especially the Sun—attracted the vapors and exhalations, and finally the coldness of the middle region of the air condensed them, and the stars liquefied the clouds thus collected and sent down rain. Rather, the Sacred Letters strive to attribute all these works together to the one God. Therefore, those have acted in vain who have attributed any acts in nature to either Angels or stars, for these things do nothing, but only God acts through them; they act as organs, and not from their own value or existence. Reuchlin <note>Johann Reuchlin (1455–1522), a pioneering German humanist and scholar of Hebrew and the Kabbalah</note> seems to express this best in this manner: *Book 3, On the Art of the Kabbalah. Lest anyone, led by vain superstition, should think that all things are conferred upon human mortality from heaven by Angels, and not rather that all things are done by the majesty of God Himself through Angels, we are taught even regarding the angels from the fountain of all truth: That God does according to His will in the army of heaven and the inhabitants of the earth. Daniel, to the King.* <note>Daniel 4:35</note> And in another place we find: *There are indeed those who are called Gods in heaven and on earth, yet for us there is but one God the Father, from whom are all things, and we in Him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, through whom are all things, and we through Him. 1 Corinthians 8:5-6.* By which the Apostle seems to declare that although the mundane Angels and demons may appear to be Gods—nay, indeed, and even some men are held for Gods in a superstitious manner, to whom divine honors are usually applied in the extreme degree of idolatry, while they falsely attribute all actions, both good and bad, to them and even to the stars of heaven—nevertheless (he says) for us, that is, for true Christians, there is only one God the Father from whom all things come at the root, namely from the immense fountain of *Ensoph* <term>Ensoph: (Hebrew: Ein Sof), meaning "The Infinite," the divine origin of all things in Kabbalah before any manifestation</term>, and one Lord Jesus Christ containing the nature of both all angels and of GOD in Himself, seeing as He is that great Angel of the world, and the true wisdom emanating from God from the beginning, namely the *word through which all things are, and we through Him:* whence also the Apostle says elsewhere, *From Him, through Him, and in Him are all things. Romans 11:36.* And elsewhere: *GOD the Father of all, who is over all and through all, and in us all. Ephesians 4:6.* And in another place, *From God are all things, but God is one. 2 Corinthians 5:18.* But the Apostle strives to declare this more expressly in these words, *GOD works all in all. 1 Corinthians 12:6.* Arguing from this that there is in truth no operation, not even by the mediation of angels, demons, or stars, except that which is essentially from God. For as rays are by no means to be divided or segregated from the Sun, so indeed the rays or emanations emitted from the fountain of all actions are not to be separated from their source, the unique and individual divine essence, which cannot be divided or distinguished into parts; for it is a pure unity, which does not suffer any separation, even though it immerses itself into the multitude of the material world, even to the center of the entire abyss.

<summary>The author argues that God is the sole "efficient cause" of all natural phenomena, such as rain and thunder, using angels and stars only as instruments. He warns that attributing power to the stars themselves leads to the error of idolatry, emphasizing the absolute unity of the divine essence acting through all things.</summary>

<margin>Deuteronomy 32:17</margin>
The ancient Magi <note>original: "Magi veteres"; here referring to ancient Persian or pagan wise men and sorcerers</note>, therefore, vainly attributed the actions of the one God to demons; these things are the works of the Lord *Jehovah* alone and are by no means to be regarded as gods. And this is the reason for the idolatry of the nations, which is mentioned in the source of truth <note>referring to the Bible</note>, where it is read: <margin>Leviticus 17:7</margin> "They sacrificed to demons and not to God, to gods whom they did not know," Deuteronomy 32:17. And this is the reason why an express law was given against the worship of demons at the beginning of the Mosaic Decalogue <note>The Ten Commandments</note>: and elsewhere we are warned that sacrifices are not to be offered to demons, as in *Leviticus 17:7.*

<margin>Jeremiah 43</margin>
Vainly also have the astrologers attributed the movements, powers, and operations of "influences" <note>original: "influentiarum"; the medieval belief that "virtue" flowed down from stars to earth</note> to the stars or planets, and especially to the Sun and Moon, which are the works of the Wisdom or the Divine Word; without His life-giving gift, they could not exist at all. For that error was also an occasion for notable idolatry among the gentiles and heathens. For example, the Egyptians worshipped the Sun, whose temples and statues the King of <margin>2 Kings 13</margin> Babylon is said to have shattered, *Jeremiah 43.* <note>The Latin text cites "4. Reg. 13," which corresponds to 2 Kings in modern English Bibles.</note> Furthermore, the Jews also fell into this damnable error, whence it is said that *the chariot and horses of the sun were removed from before the temple of the Lord, 2 Kings 13.* And in another place the Bible testifies that God created the Sun, Moon, and other things for service to all nations under heaven <margin>Deuteronomy 4</margin>, and therefore He forbade them to be adored or worshipped: and He commands the Israelites that they should not look upon the Sun, Moon, or stars, or any part of the heavenly host, so as to bow down and worship them, *Deuteronomy 4.*

By these things we are taught that just as God is the sole author and actor in this world, so to Him alone and not to a created thing is praise, honor, adoration, and worship to be offered. Whatever can happen to us or to the world, we should believe that it is not derived from the creature, but proceeds from the power of the Creator and the act of His emanation, sent into the creature and through it as if from a vehicle; for the creature itself, without His act, is plainly dead, having no value or esteem in itself.

But since it is the custom of the world to affirm that celestial influences and their virtues are derived from the stars according to the doctrine of the ancient astrologers—and consequently to say with the heathens that Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Orion, Corvus, Cassiopeia, and the rest among the fixed stars, and Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, etc., among the planets, are the causes of this or that alteration in the air, earth, and water—we, for the better understanding of our readers, will follow in their footsteps. We shall name and speak of the planets and fixed stars as the causes of storms and meteors <note>In this period, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomena, including rain, wind, and lightning.</note> in the air. We do this, however, under the condition that we always hold in our memories that it is not the star named by us, but the divine influx emitted from the <term>divine Sephirotic gates</term> <note>referring to the ten Sephirot or attributes of God in Kabbalistic philosophy</note> into the sphere and body of the planets. This influx is poured down into lower things by its Angelic minister according to the will of <term>Ensoph</term> <note>Ein Sof; the Infinite or Divine Essence in Kabbalah</note> or the Paternal Infinity, whether for the punishment or the benefit of mortals; this is the fountain and origin of effects of every kind procreated in the air, water, and earth.

These things having been first considered by the true Christian, we shall hasten to the description and living explanation of the triangle in our <term>meteorographic mirror</term> <note>original: "Catoptro nostro meteorographico"; likely a complex diagram or tool used to predict weather based on planetary positions</note>. In this, meteorological prognostication is clearly expressed through the "aspects" <note>the relative angles between planets</note> of the planets among themselves—namely, the conjunction, figured thus: ☌; the opposition, ☍; or the square, ☐—in relation to the moon. The image of the triangle will be depicted below.

## CHAPTER II.

->On the changes of the air, on the rising of a comet, and then afterwards, on the various changes of the air according to the aspects ☌, ☍, and ☐ of all the planets, both to the moon and among themselves.<-

Astrologers say that the efficient cause of all species of Comets are the stars, both fixed and wandering <note>planets</note>, and they warn us generally that meteors of this kind imitate the natures of Mars and Mercury. Whence they say it happens that they signify war, heat, and tumult. Similarly, Ptolemy in the second book of the *Quadripartitum* <note>A foundational 2nd-century text on astrology</note> wishes us to consider the stars which are accustomed (as he says) to stir up the matter and draw it along by their motion; he also teaches us to observe the place or the sign of the Zodiac under which it is ignited.

Now, as for what pertains to the various changes of the air in winds, clouds, rains, snows, hail, thunder, lightnings, and other things—and also what pertains to the exposition of the meteorological triangle depicted in our meteorographic mirror—receive this:

# On the Efficient Cause of Meteors.

### CHAPTER III.

->**An explanation of the wheel depicted in the right-hand empty part of the region of our Meteorological Mirror, as well as the openings of the gates, floodgates, and great valves.**<-

**W**e have depicted this wheel in this place for your better understanding, so that by looking at it you may more easily grasp the things contained within. In this wheel, taken from our Meteorological Mirror <note>original: *Catoptro nostro Meteorologico*. A "mirror" or *catoptrum* in this context refers to a diagrammatic representation of the heavens or a specific instrument for observation.</note>, one may see a two-fold description: namely, the openings of the **great valves** of heaven, which are described in the upper sphere; and then the openings of the **gates** of heaven, which are revealed in the parts rotating around the center of the sphere. 

As for what pertains to the openings of the **great valves** of heaven, it should be known that the floodgates <note>original: *cataractæ*</note> and great valves of heaven are said to be opened when the **Moon**, moving away from a conjunction, a square aspect, or an opposition with the **Sun**, **Jupiter**, or **Mars**, is led and passes directly toward **Saturn**, **Mercury**, and **Venus**, or vice versa. That is, if the **Moon**, moving away from a conjunction $\delta$, square $\square$, or opposition $\rho$ with **Saturn**, **Mercury**, or **Venus**, is carried toward the **Sun**, **Jupiter**, or **Mars**, then according to the opinions of all astrologers, rains in abundance and consequently great floods are to be expected.

Similarly, from the observation of the lower sphere, the **openings of the gates** are to be gathered. For where you observe in the order of the sphere a square line marked with $\square$ <note>a 90-degree angle</note> between the **Sun** and **Saturn**, or the **Moon** and **Saturn**, or **Venus** and **Mars**, or finally **Mercury** and **Jupiter**: Likewise, either a diametrical line or line of opposition marked with $\rho$ <note>a 180-degree angle</note> between the **Moon** and **Saturn**, or between the **Sun** and **Saturn**, or between **Jupiter** and **Mercury**, or finally between **Mars** and **Venus**: Lastly, where you see the **Moon** $\leftmoon$ with **Saturn** $\hbar$, or **Jupiter** $\text{\jupiter}$ with **Venus** $\text{\venus}$, or **Venus** with **Mars** with this sign $\delta$ <note>conjunction, or 0 degrees</note>, that is, in conjunction—in these cases they say the gates of heaven are open or about to be opened immediately, so that copious rains and showers are to be expected. 

For this is a secret observation among astrologers, and a science not much published by them. However, Aomar <note>Likely referring to Abu Ma'shar (787–886 AD), a Persian astrologer known in the West as Albumasar, whose works on the "Great Conjunctions" were foundational to medieval and Renaissance astrology.</note> has in his observations that if the **Moon** moves away from **Venus** and, after its departure, applies its rays to **Mars**, or if it moves away from **Mars** and applies itself to **Venus**, then it unbars the floodgates of heaven. But if it moves away from **Jupiter** applying to **Mercury**, or rather having separated from **Mercury** proceeds to **Jupiter**, it opens a gate here again. These are his views. 

But that which was previously condensed and reduced by us into the aforementioned sphere (as it has been proven by long-lasting experience), we hold in the highest esteem; consequently, we think it is to be preferred by far over the precepts of others. However, I advise you to use your own judgments and follow what seems more probable to you in this matter. Concerning the remaining celestial signs regarding changes in the air <gloss>weather</gloss>, we have spoken more fully in our Astrological treatise described in our **Technical History**, therefore I think you should be referred to that place.

### CHAPTER IV.

->*On the celestial efficient cause of Winds, where incidentally our opinion on Winds is introduced and sustained by strong reasons.*<-

After Fregius <note>Thomas Freigius (1543–1583) was a German scholar who wrote on natural philosophy and followed the method of Petrus Ramus.</note> made mention of the causes of winds, he immediately spoke thus (led by better reasoning and departing from the opinion of Aristotle): *Although the entire dispute concerning the winds, just like other meteors, is full of the wonderful works of God—for which no firm and sufficient efficient causes in nature can be brought forward—nevertheless it is profitable to see how far human reason can progress. Indeed, the Sacred Scriptures say that GOD produces the winds from his treasures, from whence we hear their blasts, but we know not from whence they come or whither they go.* <note>This is a reference to Psalm 135:7 and John 3:8.</note> Thus he spoke. And indeed, both the Peripatetics <note>The Peripatetics were followers of Aristotle, who taught that winds were "dry exhalations" drawn from the earth by the sun.</note> themselves and Pliny <note>Pliny the Elder, author of the encyclopedic *Natural History*.</note>, that accurate investigator of causes, are so involved in the mists of obscurity and ignorance that when they perceive themselves caught in the mire of ignorance, they subtly attempt to excuse themselves in part with vain distinctions. They say that some winds are "miraculous"—those, namely, for which no cause in nature can be given. Of this kind is the one described by Pliny, who says there is a certain cave on the coast of Dalmatia <note>A region in modern-day Croatia.</note> with a vast, sheer opening; if even a light weight is thrown into it, even on a day that is otherwise calm, a stormy wind like a whirlwind is observed to arise immediately. They also judge those winds to be of this sort which break forth from the rocks of the province of Cyrenaica <note>An ancient Greek and Roman province in modern-day Libya.</note>; for this reason, they hold those rocks to be so sacred that they believe them to be profaned by the touch of human hands, for if they are touched even once, the South Wind <note>original: *Auster*</note> is immediately stirred up, churning the sands, which is why they consecrated these rocks to the South Wind.

But truly, regarding those winds for which they could devise some cause within the possibility of nature, these they called "natural," and they judged their efficient cause according to their own custom. From this, anyone may see how uncertain is the opinion of men engaged in vain philosophy concerning such profound matters, and how inconstant is the judgment of human wisdom. Furthermore, even among the fathers of the Astrologers, there seems to be great hesitation and instability in their opinion regarding the efficient cause of winds. For just as the Peripatetics divide their natural winds into "fixed" and "sudden"—and the fixed ones again (which they say begin and end at fixed times) into "general" or "principal" winds, namely those which usually blow from the four cardinal points, and "particular" and "less principal" winds, which are observed to blow in certain provinces—so indeed the Astrologers look deeper into...

# I. On the Efficient Cause of Meteors.

Ascending in the investigation of these causes, some claim that impetuous winds—whether sudden or general, and especially those which tend from the North toward the West—stem from the influence of Mars, and they say such winds are subject to him. Yet others claim the winds are the "infant children of Titan, Astraea, and Aurora," <note>In Greek mythology, the winds were often said to be the offspring of Astraeus (a Titan) and Eos (the Dawn, or Aurora).</note> insofar as they are generated by the heat of the sun, which renders the air subtle and rare; this occurs especially at dawn. Indeed, even Aristotle admits that winds are brought forth by the heat of the Sun. However, all winds are said to receive the commands of Juno, because they do not blow except in the air, which is called Juno. <note>original: "Iuno dicitur." In Renaissance natural philosophy, the goddess Juno was frequently used as an allegory for the element of Air.</note> Others say that among the fixed winds are those they call *Prodromos* (as they precede the Etesian winds) <note><term>Etesians</term>: Strong, cool, seasonal Mediterranean winds that blow from the northwest. <term>Prodromos</term>: Literally "forerunners," referring to the winds that signal the coming of the Etesians.</note> during the most burning time of summer, around the time the Dog Star rises; they precede the Sun as it enters the first part of Leo by about 8 days. Furthermore, the Etesians, which are Northern winds, are observed to blow constantly for 40 days, preceded by these forerunners. Ptolemy is eager to attribute these winds to Jupiter, saying that Jupiter stirs them, which is why he says they are more fruitful and healthy than others. These begin to blow immediately after the solstice and the rising of the Dog Star, as Aristotle says; but Pliny says the Etesians blow two days after the rising of the Dog Star, while the sun stays in Leo, and so on for the rest.

From these things, you see that there is such great difficulty in finding the causes of the winds that the Philosophers themselves could judge nothing certain or firm about them. Instead, whatever they do, they gather from the outcome and from long experience and practice; thus, they see things entirely *a posteriori* (from the effects) and not *a priori* (from the first causes).

But we, as becomes a Christian, do not cease to scrutinize the mystery of the winds and other meteors in a more profound way. We do this neither from Aristotle, nor from any other book of the Pagan authors, who were ignorant of the acts of the Divine Word (through which, as the Bible—the fountain of all truth—testifies, all things were made). This is especially true of the majority of them (though the Divine Plato is always to be excepted). Rather, we have immersed ourselves (not without great delight) into the most internal cause of these creatures, guided by the instruction of the Sacred Page, as well as by the infallible reason and demonstration of philosophical probability. We have sought with all effort the opinion of the Hebrew Doctors in this matter, as they were more practiced in the mysteries of the Jews, and especially in the exposition and interpretation of the Holy Bible. Truly, from Rabbi Tedaco Levi, <note>Likely referring to Tzadok Ha-Levi, a Jewish scholar or a specific kabbalistic source used by the author.</note> who in his book *On the Ten [Numbers]* says:

> *Speaking of the four Cardinal Winds: From those four winds, God made angels as prefects over them by day and by night. Michael, who is of the side of mercy, is appointed over the East wind, and Raphael rules the West wind. Then Gabriel, in the power of judgment and severity, is appointed with the North or Boreal wind, and Noriel or Uriel presides over the South. Thus he says; and in the Book of Secrets we have it that each of these has many legions under him, which they employ in their business to obey the will of the Creator.*

However, we are compelled to disagree with that Doctor in certain respects, considering the matter down to its core. For it is certain and beyond all doubt, as proven by the experience of sailors, that the Frigid Zone of the Antarctic region of the world is no less stiff with cold and cold effects than the Boreal (Arctic) one—namely with frost, snow, and constant ice. These effects are procreated from the wind blowing from the Antarctic pole no differently than the cold effects from the North or Northern winds. Hence, it seems least probable that a "fiery spirit" such as Uriel—which name means "Fire of God"—or Meriris—which means "the demon burning at noon"—should have dominion or power in that region: namely, where the pole star of the Antarctic hemisphere has its seat. For this is certain, and to be denied by no one: just as the Northern hemisphere is divided into its temperate and frigid land zones, which extend all the way to the pole star, so it is apparent that the opposite hemisphere is distinguished into just as many regions of similar condition. Specifically, the space of the Torrid Zone is that which is located between the equinoctial line and the Tropic of Capricorn, and the temperate space extends in latitude from the Tropic of Capricorn to the Antarctic circle. Finally, they measure the Frigid Zone from the Antarctic circle to its own pole star.

By these things it is clearly established that the wind blowing from the Antarctic pole is governed neither by Meriris nor by Uriel or Noriel, since in nature and condition it is contrary to fire, being instead most cold. Therefore, we must consider, and that seriously, that a more suitable seat for the aforementioned angels is in the center of the Torrid Zone—that is, around the equinoctial region—since 그 place best agrees with the natures of Uriel the good Angel and Meriris the evil demon. <note>In traditional demonology and occult philosophy, Meriris was associated with the "Noonday Demon" mentioned in the Psalms.</note> Therefore, it should rather be understood that when it is said that Uriel or Meriris are the presiding Angels of the South, this is said with respect to us and the Jews, who are North of the Equator. Hence, the guardianship of the South is ascribed to the planet Jupiter, as its climate passes between Ethiopia and Judea. The Angel Uriel serves Jupiter and has dominion over him; just as when Saturn is dominant near the Equator, Meriris has greater power in the air. We say, therefore, the reason why the wind proceeding from the Southern region is so pestilential to us, and usually renders the air so corrupt (and this happens when the wrath of Jehovah is kindled against the Northern world), is because the most cold and dry blasts from the Antarctic pole, passing through the torrid or burning seats of the prefects Uriel and Meriris, mix with the natures of those blasts. Thus, cold is mixed with hot, and dryness with Jovial [Jupiter-like] moisture and even with fiery dryness; which incongruous mixture, being blown toward the Northern parts, causes a contention of hot with cold and...

### Section I. Post. II. Part II. Book I. Member III.

When the combination of moisture and dryness gathers clouds, it produces rain through natural liquefaction, sometimes mixed with lightning and thunder. But if *Meriri* <note>In Cabalistic tradition, Meriri is a "bitter" demon or spirit associated with the pestilence of the midday heat.</note> is accustomed to raging in his region, then the air is rendered more corrupt and becomes more pestilential; likewise, the thunder sounds more unnatural, or rains are poured out in excessive abundance. This can be very easily discerned from these words of the Prophet Habakkuk: *God will come from the South, his glory covered the heavens, and the earth is full of his praise, his splendor shall be as the light, there his strength is hidden, death shall go before his face, and the Devil shall go forth before his feet*, or, as others interpret it, a plague precedes him, with a wasting destruction in the south (Habakkuk 3:3). <note>original: "Iehoua veniet ab Austro... ante pedes eius." The author interprets the Hebrew word *Resheph* (flame/pestilence) as "Devil" or "Plague."</note> 

A similar situation exists with our North Wind (*Boreas*), which produces snow, hail, ice, and frost when it blows. But truly, this wind, penetrating through the equinoctial region <note>The Equator.</note>, breathes such a temperate climate to those of the Antarctic hemisphere—and especially the Temperate Zone—as the wind of the Antarctic pole breathes to us: namely, a cloud-bearing, rainy, contagious, moist, and hot wind. For a wind of that sort, because of its diverse mixture, participates in different natures, and it is the most mixed and composite of all the winds of heaven. It behaves like a crude and undigested chaos, consisting of qualities that fight against each other. The cause of its greater or lesser wickedness depends on whether it is led and directed by the good Angel *Uriel* (or *Noriel*) or by the evil spirit called *Meriri*.

We see that in both hemispheres, the final climate toward either pole is ruled by the Moon. Similarly, the North (*Boreas*) or the Northern axis is governed by the Cabalists, and consequently, the Moon holds dominion there among the stars—though not without the great power and operation of Saturn. In every celestial motion, we see a circle, both in the hours of the day and in the counting of months in childbirth; thus it is in every other thing, so that where the Moon ends, Saturn immediately begins. Therefore, in the furthest regions where the distance from the sun is longest, these two planets are observed to be joined in their operation. Hence, not only from the Cabalists but also from the effect itself, we see that the Moon (over which *Gabriel* presides) and then Saturn (from which proceeds a "constricting" quality, speaking in the Astrological manner) have dominion at the poles. 

But Saturn especially looks toward the Antarctic pole, although he works his effects in both. The intermediate place—namely, that through which the axis of the poles passes, where the meridian circle cuts the equinoctial line at right angles—is the place where Jupiter is said to have his seat. From there, the spirit breathing from that region is moist and warm, and is likened to the air. Furthermore, the Sun claims for itself the point of the East wind (*Subsolanus*), specifically that exact part in the east where the equinoctial circle cuts the Horizon; thus Michael, who is the "Intelligence" <note>In Renaissance philosophy, an "Intelligence" is a celestial spirit or angel that directs the motion and influence of a planet.</note> of the Sun, is appointed over this quarter. 

But the point from which the East-Southeast wind (*Eurus*) blows—namely, that place where the Tropic of Capricorn cuts the Horizon in the eastern region—is governed by Mars. Consequently, an evil Angel of a fiery condition called *Samael* (who is the prefect of Mars) presides over that region; thus this wind is said to blow with such violence, such ardor, and fiery heat. We also have this confirmed from the Holy Scripture: *With an East wind you break the ships of the Ocean* (Psalm 48:7). <note>original: "Euro perfringes naues Oceani."</note> Furthermore, we are taught elsewhere that the East wind scorches the fruit and herbs of the field (Genesis 41:6). And in Jonah it is said, *God sent a strong East wind which, with the sun, greatly scorched Jonah, etc.* (Jonah 4:8). <note>original: "DEVS emisit fortem Eurum..."</note> 

But this wind is a little more damp for us than the Northeast wind (*Caecias*), because it blows through the region of Jupiter and also, in the path of its motion, it carries with it and condenses the Northern air. However, the closer one gets to its source, the drier and more turbulent its blasts are found to be; for this reason, its blasts are more furious in the Mediterranean and Indian seas than they are here, and they also dry things out more there. Conversely, the Northeast wind (*Caecias*), which blows from that point of the east where the Tropic of Cancer intersects the Horizon, participates in the dryness of the North. For this reason, it is governed primarily by Mars, and it also has something of the astringency of Saturn; thus it is considered the worst, driest, and most impetuous wind. From its malice, wickedness, and inconstancy, it earned this name *Caecias*. This wind is therefore ruled primarily by the angel *Samael* and, in a smaller portion, by the spirit or demon named *Azael* who is appointed over the North. Thus it is occupied with malice, the gathering of clouds, and constant violence. Mars rules that entire side of the eastern world through his Angel, yet in such a way that he is subject to the command of Michael, who benevolently causes the wind to blow from the western equinox.

So also Mercury extends his dominion through the entire western region. In the "African cave" <note>Likely referring to the direction of the wind *Africus*, the Southwest wind.</note> he is governed mostly by the Angel of the South (whether good or evil) and joins with him. For Mercury is inconstant; he is accustomed to being "good with the good and evil with the evil." Furthermore, in the *Africus* wind, which is between the South-Southwest and the West wind (*Favonius*), he joins himself with the tumultuous Angel of the South. From this, he usually stands in a furious manner; indeed, this wind is the strongest of all, because Mercury is the most "windy" among all the other planets.

But from that point where the equinoctial line cuts the western part of the Horizon at right angles, we say the West wind (*Favonius*) blows—called *Zephyrus* in Greek. Over this wind *Anael* presides, along with the good Angel *Raphael*. For this reason, it emits healthy, though temperately cold and moist, blasts (after the manner of the female sex), which the solar spirit makes healthy, generative, and fruitful by meeting them. ->On the elementary Efficient cause.<-

### CHAPTER I.

->**How the regions of the world are compared to the visions of human sense, and how the more the divinity immerses itself into the multitude, the more its rays are covered and hidden from human sense.**<-

Just as three visions are observed to exist in man—one of which is corporeal, concerned with bodily objects in which the outer sense is most often deceived by judging as true those things which are actually fabricated and false images, such that this is the most uncertain of all human visions; the second is in the imagination or phantasy <note>original: "phantasia"</note>, which is the first degree of spiritual vision, in which the likenesses and, as it were, shadows of bodies are seen (for to the phantastic spirit, bodily objects sometimes appear no differently than an image in a mirror); and this vision, being a middle ground between the external sense and the intellect, sometimes sees false things and is deceived, but looking toward the intellect it can hardly be deceived, wherefore this species of human vision is more certain than the corporeal one; finally, the third species of vision is the intellectual one, which is accustomed to gazing upon things that are neither corporeal nor have the forms of bodies, and the objects of this kind of human vision are the Mind itself, GOD, justice, wisdom, and every good affection of the soul. In a similar way, the matter holds true in the inspection of the efficient cause of meteors among men. For those to whom it is given to look into and gaze upon the marrow of meteors with the vision of the intellect see indeed that God himself, the supreme mind, the word or divine Wisdom, is the sole and infallible agent in their production; and that vision is truly intellectual. There is also another vision, which is phantastic, by which men see and gaze upon the cause of meteors; and by this vision, a man determines that the Angels or demons themselves are the causes of meteors, and in this kind of inspection, a man sometimes errs—namely, by having regard for the created nature or human spirit (which has the closest proximity with corporeal things); for in attributing the efficient cause of a meteor to a created thing, he errs and seems to fall into the crime of Idolatry. But if he looks to the internal part of the Angel, which is light or divine emanation, which it received immediately from the source of the Infinite <note>original: "Ensoph" (Ein Sof), the Cabalistic term for the Infinite God.</note>, he is to that extent not deceived in his vision, as it is intellectual. Finally, if we look back at the celestial bodies through corporeal vision of the first order with the Astrologers, or if we look at the bodies of the elements and elemental things of the first degree with the Peripatetic <note>Followers of Aristotle’s philosophy.</note> Philosophers, it is necessary that we fall into great error and immerse ourselves in a deep sea of Idolatry,

Specifically, by attributing that wondrous work to coarse creatures—those visible to the senses—which are truly dead in themselves and of no significance: namely the sun, the other stars, the elements of fire and air, the heat of the earth, the cold of the middle region of the air, exhalations, vapors, and so on. Therefore, I advise all who are curious about philosophy not to attribute the work and act of such great and miraculous procreation—and consequently the honor and glory—to the elements or things made of elements, nor to the stars, nor indeed even to the Angels insofar as they are considered merely creatures. Instead, attribute it to God the Creator alone, who produces all these things (and indeed far greater things) in the world, in and through the angelic creatures. These angels are in the closest state of proximity and nearness to the Divinity, insofar as they immediately receive the impressions of light or divine emanations, which they then, led by divine command, desire to impart to creatures that are both perfectly and imperfectly mixed. 

Let me place before your considerations a most fitting comparison for this matter. A certain man wounds another with a sword. The question is then asked: Who among men wounded him? One will answer (in the manner of the **Peripatetics** <note>Followers of Aristotle’s philosophy, who focused on immediate physical causes.</note>, who attribute the efficient cause of atmospheric phenomena to fire or air) that "the sword did this." But another (following the **Astrologers**, who attribute the acting cause to the stars or atmospheric events) will say that the hand of the striker is the producer of that deed. A third, coming closer to the truth (like the **Magi** <note>Practitioners of "high magic" or spiritual wisdom who sought the hidden causes behind nature.</note>, who say that the authors of atmospheric phenomena are spirits), will say it is the spirit in the man who did it. Finally, one skilled in **theographic mysteries** <note>The study of God’s direct "writing" or actions in the world.</note>, looking with eyes somewhat sharper into the very center of both things, will say that God did both this and that. 

By this example, the error of the world is clearly explained. However, in this place, we shall make mention of the winds only in the common manner, under which name we shall nonetheless understand the **Angels of God** <note>original: "Angelos DEI"</note>, who are accustomed to animate them. But since in this book of the third member we intend to act in a physical manner and concern ourselves with the elements, we shall therefore treat the winds in this place after the manner of common philosophers.

### CHAPTER II.

->***On the correct division of the winds, and that they are the efficient causes (speaking in common language or according to common philosophical fashion) of any meteor whether in the Air, Water, or Earth.***<-

Winds—whose souls we have previously said are the angels, either openly and manifest or hiddenly bright—we categorize either as invisible and perceptible only to hearing, or as visible and bright. Examples of the latter include lightning, fire-whirls, flashes, and similar visible **meteors** <note>In this era, "meteor" referred to any atmospheric event, such as wind, rain, or lightning, not just falling stars.</note> which are driven through the air with violent motion, no differently than those winds which are visible. 

From these kinds of winds, therefore, as the primary movers in the elementary world, all other meteors—both bright and dark—are produced and procreated. These include **Comets**, **chasms**, **beams**, **lightning**, **flashes**, **fire-whirls**, **leaping goats** <note>original: "capræ saltantes"; a historical term for a type of streaking atmospheric light or aurora.</note>, **will-o'-the-wisps** <note>original: "ignis fatuus"</note>, and **sulfurous flames** which the earth might vomit, and other such things from the bright winds that are manifested as fire (which in their nature are nothing but the most subtle air, animated and agitated by a fiery soul). On the other hand, clouds, mists, vapors, snow, hail, stones, hoarfrost, and ice come from the hidden and less manifest winds acting as the efficient causes, with the hidden and dark air contracted into such dark forms. We shall now say some words regarding the hidden and least visible winds, and we shall do so in the common manner.

### CHAPTER III.

->***On the East Wind, and on its two collateral winds.***<-

The hidden wind blowing directly from that place of the east where the **equinoctial line** <note>The celestial equator.</note> intersects the Eastern horizon is called **Subsolanus** <note>Literally "under the sun."</note>, as it arises under the Sun in the **Torrid Zone**—specifically in that place where the equator passes. Furthermore, it is called **Apeliotes** <note>A Greek term for the East wind.</note> by the Greeks. This wind, along with its two other collateral winds, is said to be hot and dry. 

But this wind, being the Prince of the eastern winds between the two aforementioned, stands like a Virtue in the middle; it is most temperate in its fiery disposition, like the celestial sun. For this reason, it is a "clearer of the skies" for the **Macrocosm** <note>The great world or universe.</note> and healthy for the **Microcosm** <note>The "little world," or the human being.</note>. Its right wing, which blows from that point of the Eastern horizon which the **Tropic of Cancer** intersects—that is, from the summer sunrise—is called **Caecias** <note>The Northeast wind.</note> because of its malice, and the **Hellespontic** wind, from the place from which it blows. This wind is very inconsistent in its disposition: for sometimes it is cold, sharing the disposition of the North, and sometimes scorching with the nature of the east; but for the most part, it exceeds all winds in dryness, and this is from the nature of its location, insofar as it partakes of the dryness of the North or the earth, and that of the east or...

...participating in fire. Yet, by accident, it is also observed at times to be imbued with a certain moisture. The reason for this is that it is not its nature—after the manner of the North wind—to drive clouds away, but rather to eagerly attract them to itself. This happens, if I am not mistaken, because of its intense dryness, which acts as an attractor of moisture. The left wing, or the companion wind to the East wind toward the south—which blows from that point where the Tropic of Capricorn intersects the eastern Horizon (that is, from the winter sunrise)—is called in Greek the South-East wind <note>original: *Eurus*</note>. By some, it is also called the *Vulturnus* <note>A Latin name for the South-East wind, likely derived from Mount Vultur</note> because of its rapid nature; for it is accustomed to blow violently and fly high, observed to behave much like a vulture. In its condition, this wind is stormy, hot in itself, and dry, though it does not abound in dryness as much as the North-East wind does. This is because on one side it faces the damp South wind <note>original: *Auster*</note>, from which it is seen—at times, or rather quite often—to gather clouds. Yet, because of its own dryness and heat, it is also sometimes observed to scatter gathered clouds through the air and fill the space everywhere with smoky mists and thick vapors. For this reason, it often deceives the sight, making visible objects appear larger than they truly are.

For a fuller explanation of the qualities of these winds, I refer and direct you to the following volume which, God willing, will treat the relationship between health and disease.

## CHAPTER IV.

### *On the description of the West wind with its wings or collateral winds, and on the meteors which they are accustomed to produce in the air.*

That general wind blowing from the corner of the west—whose middle point is intersected by the equinoctial line—is called in Latin *Favonius* and in Greek *Zephyrus*, which means "carrying life and vigor." This is the prince of those winds that blow from the west. In its nature, this wind is cold and moist in a most temperate degree. It has to its right, as its wing or collateral wind, the South-West wind <note>original: *Aphricus*</note>, and to its left the North-West wind <note>original: *Corus*</note>.

The collateral wind *Aphricus* <note>The South-West wind</note> is that which blows from that point of the western Horizon intersected by the Tropic of Capricorn (namely, from the winter solstice). Its disposition is to incline somewhat toward the Southern heat, but the western coldness chiefly abounds in it. This wind is accustomed to blow impetuously in turns, and thus it is stormy and sometimes accompanied by clouds.

The other wing of the West wind <note>original: *Fauonii*</note>, turning toward the North, is that wind which blows from that point in the west which the Tropic of Cancer intersects (namely, from the summer solstice). This is called in Latin *Corus* and in Greek *Argestes*, meaning impetuous and stormy. In its condition, it inclines somewhat from the moisture of the West wind toward the dryness of the North. From this, it is naturally inclined to produce hail, snow, and cold, and is moist by turns. While it blows, the clouds in the sky are observed to be dark, although for part of the day it may be serene, dry, and finally moist. Furthermore, because of its more intense moisture, it sometimes brings hailing or snowing rains; and occasionally—more frequently in summer—it brings the most vehement thunders, lightnings, and horrendous storms.

Concerning the production of these qualities—whether leading to disease or health in both worlds <note>Referring to the Macrocosm (the universe) and the Microcosm (the human body)</note>—we shall speak copiously in the following volume, with God’s assistance.

## CHAPTER V.

### *On the North wind with its two companions and their effects in the air.*

The North wind, called *Boreas* in Greek, is the principal wind of the North, and it usually blows directly from the pole star. In its condition, it is exceedingly cold and dry. Its role is to cleanse and purify the air of the thick humors produced by the South wind. According to the testimony of Holy Scripture, it is accustomed to drive away rains; yet sometimes it produces hail and snow, specifically at those times when the South wind blows strongly against it. This occurs when a louder noise is heard; for then it condenses the clouds in the air, and occasionally—especially in the summer time—it is observed to produce thunder.

Its left wing is called *Aquilo* <note>The North-North-East wind</note>, which blows from that point of the eastern region where the polar or arctic circle intersects the Horizon. This wind is very cold and dry in its condition, but truly somewhat...

### CHAPTER VI.

<image-desc>A manicule (pointing hand) points toward the following subheading</image-desc>

->***On the three Southern Winds, along with their conditions in the production of meteors.***<-

Finally, the Cardinal wind that reigns principally in the south, which is said to breathe from the Antarctic pole, is called **Auster** <note>The South Wind</note>—from "drawing up waters" <note>original: *ab hauriendo aquas*</note>, as some would have it. This wind is hot and moist in its nature, whereby it is accustomed not only to gather thick and persistent clouds, but also to pour out heavy rains. It tends to produce lightning, to make the air thick and dense, to nourish mists, and also quite often to flash with lightning and give forth great peals of thunder. Furthermore, just as the North wind is a hard wind that hardens humors, so the South wind is soft and softening.

The right wing of this wind blows from the place of intersection made by the antarctic circle on the Eastern Horizon, and it is called **Euro-Auster** <note>The South-Southeast wind</note>. In its quality, it is hot and moist, but indeed, because of its aspect toward the Eastern corner, it is somewhat hotter and not quite as moist as the South wind; it is a cloud-bearer and occasionally a producer of thunder.

Its left wing is the **Austro-Africus** <note>The South-Southwest wind</note>, which blows from the point of the western Horizon where the antarctic circle cuts it; this produces stormy winds, which sometimes accompany thunder and clouds.

From this, therefore, you see what those learned in common observation and experience perceive: that almost all meteors proceed from the winds. However, the heathens <note>original: *Ethnici*</note> seemed to us to be truly ignorant of the internal nature of these winds, as they quite imprudently made their internal agent to be nothing but exhalations gushing out of the earth and animated by solar heat. But we are taught by Saint John that it is not known where the winds arise or where they go, and that the spirit tends to blow where it wills. And the Prophet says that Jehovah "made his Angels winds, and his ministers a burning flame" <note>A reference to Psalm 104:4</note>. By this speech, he clearly seems to explain that there are two species of winds after the manner of Angels: those that are heard and not seen, being hidden; and those that are seen and are bright, but are not heard except by their effect, as are the lightning-flashes and coruscations in a thunderstorm.

And so, nearly exhausted and fatigued by the weariness of such great labor, we gladly place an end to this volume—not without perpetual grace and blessing to God our Creator for such great favor and illumination.
